Hereinafter, the results show that photovoltaic density, module width, and actuation strategy strongly govern crop-relevant light conditions. The proposed workflow provides quantitative support for selecting greenhouse photovoltaic layouts that balance energy integration with spatially uniform crop light availability.

title: Inferring wind-energy inflow spectra from height and stability: A cumulative-energy log-normal model with operator-learned compensation
abstract: Accurate inflow turbulence spectra for wind turbines and wind farms should vary with height and atmospheric stability while preserving the correct total energy, here defined as the integrated streamwise velocity variance σu2, for load prediction and large-eddy simulation inflow forcing. Guided by Monin–Obukhov similarity and wall-turbulence scaling, this study presents an energy-conserving framework for reconstructing the one-dimensional streamwise velocity spectrum from two routinely available descriptors: relative height within the boundary layer and the neutral-to-unstable stability coordinate. The cumulative energy fraction is represented by a two-parameter log-normal distribution in ξ=ln(kxz), where the fitted mean μ gives the logarithmic location of the energy-containing ridge and the fitted standard deviation σ gives its spread over wavenumber space. Analytical inversion of this cumulative form then yields a baseline spectrum constrained by a stability-dependent velocity-variance model. The remaining mismatch in the energy-containing range is corrected by a compact compensation followed by variance-preserving renormalization. Two implementations are considered: a compact empirical parameterization and a lightweight operator-learning surrogate. Validation against high-Reynolds-number wind-tunnel boundary-layer data and long-term atmospheric surface-layer measurements shows that both approaches reproduce the premultiplied spectral peak, low-wavenumber shoulder, inertial-range behaviour, and integrated energy partition across neutral to unstable conditions. Under near-neutral conditions, the characteristic spectral location varies approximately logarithmically with relative height, whereas increasing instability shifts energy towards larger streamwise scales with only weak changes in spectral breadth. The resulting model gives fast, interpretable and variance-consistent one-dimensional streamwise spectra for the tested neutral-to-unstable boundary-layer datasets, and provides a practical basis for wind-energy inflow specification, LES inflow generation and preliminary aeroelastic-load studies within this validated range.

title: A tool for economic assessment of investment decisions for multi-energy systems
abstract: Renewable Energy Communities (RECs) enable collective participation in local renewable generation, storage, distribution and consumption. However, optimal design is shaped by electricity settlement and compensation schemes. These regulatory mechanisms are often represented exogenously in planning tools, limiting transparent comparison of transition pathways. This paper presents a regulation-aware planning tool based on an integrated optimisation framework for community-scale energy systems. Electricity settlement and compensation rules for local self-consumption schemes are embedded within a mixed-integer linear model, with photovoltaic (PV) generation considered as primary application. The framework enables techno-economic assessment of individual and collective investment configurations under net billing (NB), net metering (NM) and feed-in tariff (FiT) schemes, with monthly and annual settlement horizons. Electricity system optimisation is coupled with low-carbon heat supply options, including biomass-based cogeneration and individual heat pumps. The framework is applied to a real-world case in Ispaster (Spain). Results show that regulatory design and aggregation level drive optimal sizing and economic performance. Collective configurations and annual settlement consistently outperform individual and monthly alternatives, while battery storage adds limited value once annual settlement is available. The proposed approach supports community-level planning and investment decisions through regulation-aware comparison of alternative energy transition options.

title: Reducing the number of wind turbine prototype measurement campaigns for power curve model validation using a model-validity predictor
abstract: Prototype turbine measurement campaigns are required for turbine type certification and the associated validation of aero-elastic wind turbine models when wind turbine designs slightly differ from previous measurement campaigns. Small changes in the turbine design are allowed without additional testing campaigns being required. We propose a model-validity predictor that is able to conservatively predict the validation results on new turbines before a measurement campaign is carried out. This predictor is trained based on previous measurement campaigns and uses a set of variables to describe the wind turbine design space. The model-validity predictor demonstrates the potential to reduce the number of prototype campaigns required to validate a model, and it is shown that a change of variables can expand the predicted safe domain by 72%. Detailed uncertainty propagation is carried out for each wind turbine measurement campaign using Monte Carlo simulations. We separate aleatoric uncertainties and parameter epistemic uncertainties. This separation enables us to quantify the degree of validity of a model with respect to the measurements. This study demonstrates the potential benefits of calibration, with the qualification that the ideal workflow will separate data used for validation and calibration, perhaps using a sophisticated cross-validation routine.

title: Method based on optimized tendencies to evaluate the impact of the introduction of solar and wind energy sources in energy systems
abstract: Fossil fuels continue to dominate global energy use but are a major source of GHG-emissions driving climate change. This makes the transition to clean, carbon-free energy sources increasingly urgent. The introduction of solar and wind sources is an essential step toward decarbonization not only because their costs are steadily falling but also because they are among the most widely available local energy resources in many regions around the world. However, these energy sources cannot always meet demand, as their production depends on the intensity of solar radiation and wind. Due to this intermittency, they must be supplemented by energy storage systems or/and by conventional, controllable sources that can adjust their output to follow fluctuations in demand. The characteristics of the backup energy needed to compensate for the intermittency of solar and wind energy vary considerably depending on the share of these sources in the grid, both in terms of average load and peak load. This article analyses how these shifting needs impact the cost and distribution of generation technologies, especially in systems that lack energy storage. It presents the development of a method capable of accounting for this while managing many scenarios of increasing introduction of intermittent energy into the mix, and several indicators of interest for stakeholders are needed. The energy mix for each scenario is determined by minimizing energy production costs. Two regions—Grand-Est in France and Cuba—are examined.

title: Improved modeling, parametric analysis, and experimental validation of freestanding rotary electret nanogenerator
abstract: Electret nanogenerators have emerged as a promising technology for harvesting vibration energy to power low-consumption electronics. This study develops two improved equivalent-circuit models for freestanding electret nanogenerators featuring eccentric and centripetal electrode layouts of equal spacing. Unlike conventional simplified models neglecting detailed electrode configurations, the proposed models explicitly incorporate geometry-dependent overlapping-area evolution, thereby improving the prediction accuracy of output characteristics, particularly for high electrode-number configurations. Analytical expressions for the output current, voltage, and average power of both configurations are derived using Kirchhoff's Current Law. Parametric analyses quantify the effect of key structural variables, and the models are validated through laboratory experiments. Results demonstrate good agreement between theory and experiment when the net charge density is adopted. The proposed models provide higher accuracy in predicting the effects of structural and electrical parameters on freestanding electret nanogenerator outputs. A smaller inner radius, shorter electrode spacing, reduced generator capacitance, higher rotational speed, and increased surface charge density could enhance the average power output of the freestanding electret nanogenerators. The measured maximum power is 1.14 mW with an optimal load resistance of 2.9 MΩ. The rotation-frequency response of the freestanding electret nanogenerators exhibits an ultra-high sensitivity of 13.4 rpm/Hz with a good linearity coefficient of determination of 0.93. The proposed models can effectively describe the charge transfer behavior and provide useful guidance for geometry optimization and performance prediction of the freestanding electret nanogenerators. The proposed analytical framework may facilitate future applications in self-powered sensing systems, distributed energy harvesting devices, and structural health monitoring technologies.

title: Effect of alkali metals on gasification reaction characteristics of pine sawdust and kinetic analysis in dielectric barrier discharge
abstract: Biomass gasification is a technology that transforms biomass into combustible gas, holding significant implications for energy, environmental sustainability, and economic development. In this paper, dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) was employed to investigate the gasification reaction characteristics and kinetics of pine sawdust(PS) with different alkali metal content. The results showed that the total gas yield of PS in CO2 (275 mL/g) atmosphere was the highest, and the reaction rate of syngas increased with higher alkali metal content. By Inductively Coupled Plasma Optical Emission Spectrometry (ICP-OES), Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) and Fourier Transform Infrared Spectrometer(FT-IR), PS and pine sawdust char (PSC)was characterized and analyzed. Increased alkali metal content notably inhibited tar formation. Notably, the activation energy decreased gradually with the increase of alkali metal content (CH4: from 56.50 kJ/mol to 3.49 kJ/mol, CO: from 17.74 kJ/mol to 2.61 kJ/mol, and H2: from 30.42 kJ/mol to 0.69 kJ/mol), indicating that alkali metals enhance reaction efficiency and feasibility. This research provides valuable insights for the application of DBD in biomass gasification for power generation, heating, liquid fuel production, or chemical feedstock synthesis. It presents a promising method for enhancing the efficiency of biomass conversion, which is crucial for advancing sustainable chemical production technologies.

title: Preliminary investigations on the evacuated PVT-driven methanol electrolysis for enhanced solar hydrogen production
abstract: Methanol is a promising liquid fuel and hydrogen carrier. Its electrolysis requires both electrical and thermal energy for efficient operation. Although the theoretical electrolysis voltage is extremely low, the process still requires coordinated electrical and thermal inputs to satisfy the overall energy demand. To address this challenge, this study proposes an integrated system coupling methanol electrolysis with an evacuated photovoltaic-thermal (PVT) collector, which can simultaneously and sustainably provide electricity and medium-/low-temperature heat from the same solar aperture. Owing to vacuum insulation, the evacuated PVT collector can significantly suppress thermal losses, thereby increasing the attainable thermal output temperature and providing a thermal supply well matched to the energy requirements of methanol electrolysis. A thermodynamic analysis was first conducted to clarify the partitioning of the overall energy demand between electricity and heat in methanol electrolysis. A coupled opto-electro-thermal model, validated by experimental data, was then developed to evaluate the integrated PVT-electrolysis system. The results show that the useful thermal output recovered from the evacuated PVT collector can meet part of the heat demand of methanol electrolysis, thereby reducing the electrical input to the electrolyzer. Consequently, the PVT-driven methanol electrolysis system decreases electricity consumption by more than 40% and achieves a daily hydrogen output 3.62 times higher than that of the PVT-driven water electrolysis system. These results highlight the potential of synergistically integrating methanol electrolysis with evacuated PVT technology to advance efficient and practical solar-driven hydrogen production.

title: Novel hydrogen fuel cell vehicle-to-grid strategy for peak shaving in renewable-powered residential microgrids
abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy sources in residential microgrids introduces challenges for peak load management and grid stability. Hydrogen-powered fuel cell electric vehicles offer a promising solution by combining mobility with distributed energy storage. This study investigates vehicle-to-grid operation of hydrogen fuel cell vehicles that can efficiently alleviate short-term peak demand occurrences, providing targeted flexibility and reinforcing microgrid resilience. A Matlab/Simulink simulation model of a residential microgrid with 6.5 MW of solar power and 4.5 MW of wind turbines was developed, considering a fleet of 15 vehicles. Results demonstrate a peak load reduction capability of 100%, with the entire fleet delivering 484 kWh, with a peak of 520 kW, in 95 minutes, while the hydrogen utilization ratio varied between 21% and 37%. The paper demonstrates that fuel cell vehicle fleet can fully eliminate overloads, confirming the potential role of hydrogen-based mobility in enhancing renewable-powered microgrids.

title: Solar-assisted heating of a medium-deep U-type borehole heat exchanger system: Improved operational performance and mitigated subsurface thermal attenuation
abstract: Integrating medium-deep geothermal energy and solar thermal energy in buildings can enhance renewable energy utilization and coordinated multi-energy management while reducing carbon emissions. The long-term operation of medium-deep U-type borehole heat exchanger (MDUBHE) systems may lead to performance degradation and rock-soil temperature attenuation, especially in severe cold regions. Solar-assisted heating is an effective measure to mitigate these problems. However, design methods for such coupled systems remain underdeveloped, and the mechanisms by which solar assistance affects long-term system performance are still not fully understood. In this paper, a coupled simulation platform for a solar-assisted MDUBHE heating system is established, an operation control strategy for the coupled system is developed, the accuracy of the platform is validated, and the effects of solar-assisted measures are investigated. The results show that solar-assisted heating effectively alleviates the attenuation of MDUBHE water temperature, with the inlet and outlet water temperatures in the 15th year increasing by 18.7% and 11.1%, respectively. The operational efficiency of the coupled system is also improved after the integration of the solar collector system. Furthermore, solar-assisted heating reduces the thermal impact of the coupled system on the rock-soil and alleviates its temperature attenuation, with the thermal attenuation rates at depths of z = 1600 m to z = 2000 m reduced to 8.85%, 9.20%, 9.51%, 9.79%, and 10.03%, respectively. This study provides useful guidance for the design and implementation of solar-assisted MDUBHE systems.

title: LLM-CECM: A simulation framework for strategic generation behavior in coupled electricity-carbon markets
abstract: The deep integration of electricity and carbon markets creates a coupled decision environment in which generators must coordinate energy offers, quota positions, and expectations about policy shocks. Traditional market simulators often either simplify strategic cognition or incur prohibitive computational cost when richer reasoning is introduced. This paper proposes LLM-CECM, a rolling multi-agent simulation framework in which carbon-order submission, carbon-cost feedback, and electricity dispatch interact at every time step. The framework combines: (1) LLM-enabled agents with persona, memory, and belief modules; (2) an Adaptive Decision Frequency (ADF) mechanism that allocates expensive reasoning only to informative periods; and (3) a fixed-depth Iterated Belief Revision with Counterfactual Reasoning (IBR-CR) heuristic for anticipating rival responses. In the reported IEEE 118-bus/AEMO-based experiments, ADF reduces LLM calls by 80.5% and runtime by 81.5%, while IBR-CR lowers the rolling price-volatility proxy from 5.49 to 2.69 CNY/MWh. Event-window diagnostics further show that thermal agents increase markups and quota purchases during a pre-announced multi-event stress sequence involving demand tightening, coal outages, and later renewable relief. These results should be interpreted as empirical evidence from a rolling simulation framework rather than a proof of equilibrium existence, uniqueness, or Nash convergence in the underlying coupled market game.

title: Transformer prediction decomposition dual-driver for maximum power point tracking under partial shading conditions of photovoltaic power generation systems
abstract: Solar power, as a form of environmentally friendly and sustainable energy, has attracted considerable attention in the field of renewable energy power generation. However, the power curves of photovoltaic arrays are highly complex due to the inherent nonlinear characteristics of photovoltaic modules. To address the challenges of global maximum power point tracking under complex conditions, this study proposes a Transformer prediction decomposition dual-driver algorithm. The Transformer prediction decomposition dual-driver algorithm first utilizes a Transformer network to rapidly and accurately predict global maximum power point values of photovoltaic systems. Subsequently, the proposed algorithm integrates complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise mode decomposition, fractional order proportional-integral-derivative control, and deep Q-network technology to achieve dual-mode control, thereby enhancing the stability of the control process. This study compares the Transformer prediction decomposition dual-driver algorithm with conventional algorithms and intelligent optimization algorithms under various shading conditions through simulation and hardware-in-the-loop experiments. Compared to other algorithms, the Transformer prediction decomposition dual-driver algorithm achieves a minimum increase in mean tracking efficacy of 0.1034% while concurrently reducing the mean tracking duration by no less than 0.0371 s. In physical experimental results, the proposed method exhibits minimal power disturbance compared to the reference algorithms.

title: Algae extract-delaminated molybdenum disulfide functionalized with glycidyl methacrylate and polyaniline for enhanced hydrogen, oxygen evolution reaction and Lithium-ion batteries performance
abstract: A green synthesis strategy was developed to fabricate a novel MoS2/PGMA@PANI 2D conducting polymer composite. MoS2 nanosheets were synthesized using ammonium tetrathiomolybdate, algae extract, and sulfurization, followed by GMA functionalization and in-situ PANI grafting. The successful formation of the composite was confirmed by SEM, TEM, EDX, FTIR, XRD, XPS, and AFM analyses. In 0.5 M H2SO4, the MoS2/PGMA@PANI catalyst demonstrated outstanding HER activity, delivering a Tafel slope of 50.8 mV dec−1 and requiring overpotentials of 108, 164, and 266 mV to reach current densities of 10, 50, and 100 mA cm−2, respectively. These values were significantly better than those of MoS2 and MoS2/PGMA. For the OER process, the composite achieved a Tafel slope of 54.7 mV dec−1 and an overpotential of 153 mV at 100 mA cm−2, surpassing the electrocatalytic performance of pristine MoS2, MoS2/PGMA, and commercial IrO2. The catalyst exhibited remarkable long-term stability, sustaining consistent electrochemical performance over 60 h of continuous operation. When employed as a lithium-ion battery anode, MoS2/PGMA@PANI achieved a reversible capacity of 268.3 mAh g−1 and retained 79% of its initial capacity after 60 cycles at a current density of 100 mA g−1. This improved electrochemical behavior arises from the synergistic integration of conductive PANI, functionalized PGMA, and porous MoS2 nanosheets, which collectively facilitate rapid charge transport, enhance ion diffusion, and reinforce the structural integrity of the electrode.

title: Optimization of power capture performance of heaving buoys based on the Taguchi method
abstract: To enhance the energy capture performance of heaving point absorbers in the South China Sea, classic cylindrical-conical and cylindrical-semi-ellipsoidal buoys, as well as a novel cylindrical-concave semi-ellipsoidal buoy, were selected for design optimization based on the Taguchi method and ANSYS AQWA numerical simulations. The optimization process takes into account buoy geometry, draft ratio, PTO system type (a spring-damper system and a mass-damper system), and PTO parameters. The primary factors influencing the power capture of the buoy systems were investigated using signal-to-noise ratio analysis, and a secondary optimization was performed specifically targeting these primary factors. The results indicate that, for both types of PTO systems, the most significant factor affecting the power capture of the three buoy types is the ratio of draft depth to buoy height. The PTO mass-damper system effectively reduces the natural frequency of the system and enhances the resonance effect with the incident waves, resulting in an optimal absorbed power of approximately twice that of the spring-damper system. Moreover, the secondary optimization of the most influential factor with reference to the signal-to-noise ratio results further improves the energy harvesting performance of the buoy systems. After optimization, the difference in power capture among the three buoy types is small. The novel cylindrical-concave semi-ellipsoidal buoy has power capture performance comparable to the best-performing cylindrical-conical buoy, thus can serve as an important option for buoy systems in different sea areas.

title: Enhanced pre-cooling for underground pipe gallery ventilation via a hybrid borehole heat exchanger-capillary ceiling system
abstract: The underground pipe gallery ventilation system effectively provides pre-cooling during the cooling season. However, its shallow burial depth limits the long-term stability of heat exchange. To overcome this limitation, a novel hybrid ventilation system was developed, integrating a borehole heat exchanger with a capillary mat–coupled radiant ceiling cooling system. A full-scale experimental platform was constructed to evaluate its climate adaptability and cooling enhancement mechanisms under real operating conditions. Results showed that the radiant ceiling cooling system compensated for the limited cooling capacity of the shallow overlying soil, reducing vertical temperature stratification from 5.1 °C to 3.7 °C compared with a system without ceiling cooling. Fan-assisted ventilation effectively suppressed reverse airflow. The integrated system achieved a maximum outdoor air temperature reduction of 10.8 °C and a peak total heat transfer rate of 6.4 kW, representing a 68.7% improvement over mechanical ventilation alone. In addition, the vertical temperature difference was further reduced to 2.1 °C, leading to a 41.8% increase in heat exchange efficiency compared with non-integrated operation. The system maintained lower indoor temperatures for at least 36.9% of the summer operating period, demonstrating a practical, energy-efficient, and scalable retrofit strategy for existing underground pipe galleries.

title: Modeling and coordinated control optimization of the focused flux distribution for a discrete solar-simulator concentrator
abstract: To meet the requirements for peak-flux regulation, improved uniformity, and increased target-region energy fraction for a high-flux solar simulator in thermochemical heat supply, this study proposes a discrete concentrator based on angular stratification of source emission and a multi-objective coordinated optimization method. First, an ideal geometric-optics model is established using Monte Carlo ray tracing, and a calibrated model is constructed by applying a point spread function to the ideal flux prediction and validating it against experiments. This dual-layer framework combines ideal prediction with system-error-aware verification. Second, a composite objective combining target-region non-uniformity and energy fraction is formulated under a unified criterion and solved using an adaptive genetic algorithm. Compared with the conventional genetic algorithm, the adaptive genetic algorithm reduces the final objective by approximately 35%. Independent optimization over receiver-plane position and target-region radius is then used to construct response surfaces, revealing the coupled effects of geometric parameters on non-uniformity, peak flux, and energy fraction. Finally, guided by response surfaces, geometric flux shaping and input-power scaling are coordinated to meet the prescribed peak-flux target bands under the upper power constraint. The calibrated-model results show this strategy reduces the target-region non-uniformity factor to 0.13 and increases the energy fraction to 59.80%.

title: Synergistic parametric optimisation of gas–liquid interaction with valve lift and liquid column in an ionic liquid hydrogen compressor
abstract: Ionic liquid hydrogen compressors serve as vital components for hydrogen refueling stations, where gas valves act as core elements. The self-acting valve in the compressor chamber has several control parameters, and the characteristics of the ionic liquid column also affect the two-phase flow within the cylinder. The self-acting valve and the fluctuations of the liquid column jointly exert an influence on the compression process. This study investigates the influence of three critical design parameters on isothermal efficiency, valve delay closure time, and liquid discharge volume. Among these, valve lift predominantly governs the valve delay closure time. Subsequently, a multi-objective optimization analysis integrating these three performance metrics is conducted. By adopting grey relational analysis (GRA), the study derives the optimal design parameter configuration. Results show that the optimized parameters are: valve lift of 2 mm, ionic liquid density of 1800 kg/m3, and initial liquid piston height of 30 mm. This work uniquely targets valve lift and ionic liquid density to balance valve dynamics and liquid carryover, which lays a foundation for gas valve design in ionic liquid compressors and ionic liquid selection while offering extendable insights for exploring other influencing factors and design considerations under diverse operating conditions.

title: Reducing market risk in run-of-river hydropower: The economic value of improving predictions of day-ahead production
abstract: Accurate streamflow forecasts are essential for optimizing hydropower production and reducing market imbalance costs, particularly for small-scale hydropower plants with limited storage capacity. This study evaluates the potential of an LSTM neural network for hourly streamflow prediction at operationally monitored hydropower systems with limited historical observations and assesses its economic value in a hydropower production context. The effect of two aspects on prediction accuracy is investigated: (i) including back-calculated streamflow data from 110 run-of-river hydropower plants during training, and (ii) implementation of a data assimilation (DA) approach using back-calculated streamflow as input. The performance of the model is assessed in a perfect weather forecast context using regional reanalysis data and compared with both a persistence model and the operational model currently used by the largest small-scale hydropower operator in the Nordics, Småkraft AS. The results show that including data from hydropower plants in training provides the model with valuable information, while data assimilation yields the greatest performance gain. The proposed model has the potential to decrease annual imbalance fees for Småkraft AS by 23.6% (143 kEUR) compared to the model currently used and reduces exposure to extreme prices in the balancing market by reducing the CVaR 75 with 16% (380 kEUR). The findings demonstrate that enhanced hydrological forecasting reduces imbalance cost and market risk, while supporting more stable grid operations.

title: Performance enhancement of concentrated photovoltaic/thermal systems using water cooling and phase change materials under outdoor conditions
abstract: Rising photovoltaic operating temperature remains a major barrier to efficient solar-energy conversion because it lowers electrical output and accelerates thermal degradation. To address this limitation, the present work experimentally investigates a water-cooled concentrated photovoltaic/thermal system integrated with phase change material under outdoor conditions. The novelty lies in the direct comparison of three configurations—conventional photovoltaic, water-based photovoltaic/thermal, and concentrated photovoltaic/thermal with phase change material—under identical irradiance and coolant-flow conditions, enabling the separate and combined effects of optical concentration, active cooling, and latent heat storage to be evaluated. Experiments were conducted at water mass flow rates of 0.015, 0.025, and 0.035 kg/s with solar irradiance ranging from 210 to 1350 W/m2. The integrated concentrated photovoltaic/thermal–phase change material system achieved the best overall performance, reducing photovoltaic surface temperature by up to 40.91% compared with the conventional photovoltaic module. This thermal regulation increased average electrical efficiency by 117%, while maintaining useful heat recovery with a maximum thermal efficiency of 36% at the highest flow rate. The results demonstrate that optical concentration can provide net performance gains only when the associated thermal penalty is controlled through active cooling and thermal storage. Therefore, the proposed hybrid system offers a practical route for simultaneous electricity generation, heat recovery, and temperature stabilization in solar-energy applications.

title: A novel distributed model predictive control-based optimal energy management of islanded multimicrogrids with renewable energies and hybrid storage
abstract: Interconnected multimicrogrids operating in islanded mode face significant challenges in maintaining energy balance, mitigating battery degradation, and ensuring effective coordination among neighboring microgrids. These challenges are particularly critical in off-grid and remote areas, where ensuring energy security and sustainability is essential for long-term viability. Existing energy management strategies often struggle to optimize energy scheduling, prolong battery lifespan, and maintain a reliable power supply across multiple grids simultaneously. This study proposed an advanced energy management strategy based on a novel distributed model predictive control (DMPC) framework. This approach formulates the mixed-integer quadratic programming to solve DMPC optimization problem and introduces a slack variable to constrain the state of charge of batteries within an optimal range, thereby minimizing battery degradation. Furthermore, a decentralized coordination mechanism utilizing the accelerated distributed augmented Lagrangian (ADAL) technique is proposed to enhance power supply reliability and optimize energy exchange among interconnected microgrids. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed strategy leads to a 48.26% improvement in the state of health retention of storage systems and a 76.42% extension in their cyclic life compared to conventional methods.

title: Thermal depletion patterns of CO2 and water in closed-loop coaxial geothermal systems with vertical and L-shaped wells
abstract: Closed-loop coaxial geothermal systems offer a fracturing-free approach for heat extraction from hot dry rock formations, yet the thermodynamic behavior of CO2 as a working fluid—particularly the Joule–Thomson effect—remains insufficiently understood. This study presents a systematic numerical investigation of transient heat-exchange mechanisms, well configuration effects and fundamental differences between CO2 and water in coaxial borehole heat exchangers. Four distinct operational stages are identified, revealing that the Joule–Thomson effect governs the early injection transient, during which near-adiabatic compression of the descending CO2 can briefly raise the annulus temperature above the local formation temperature. Comparison of vertical and L-shaped wells shows that the horizontal section functions as a thermal insulator for the return flow, eliminating radial heat loss during vertical ascent and increasing the outlet temperature by approximately 5 K. An L-shaped well penetrating 900 m shallower than a vertical well of equal total measured depth achieves nearly equivalent thermal output. Three-dimensional depletion analysis reveals that CO2 produces a characteristic inverted-nail morphology—a slender rod along the wellbore capped by a broad disc at the annulus-to-tubing transition—driven by its near-critical heat-capacity peak and Joule–Thomson-induced cooling, whereas water exhibits a quasi-cylindrical depletion column, consistent with its negligible Joule–Thomson coefficient. The L-shaped architecture partially mitigates localized thermal exhaustion by relocating the depletion front to the horizontal toe. Sensitivity analyses confirm diminishing marginal returns of increasing geothermal gradient and greater flow-rate sensitivity of CO2 owing to its lower thermal inertia.

title: Experimental performance of solar-assisted water source heat pump system coupled with convection-radiation terminals: operational behaviors and energy-saving potentials
abstract: Solar-assisted heat pump (SAHP) systems combined with intermittent heating are effective strategies for improving building energy efficiency. However, most existing studies focused primarily on either the cascaded utilization of energy at heat sources or the coupling of different terminals, leaving a gap in the systematic evaluation of series-coupled terminal systems. To address this, this study experimentally investigated a solar-water source heat pump system integrated with convection-radiation terminals. Results demonstrated that combining radiant and convective terminals enabled a rapid thermal response during startup and enhanced the thermal persistence after system shutdown. Among all configurations tested, the combined radiator-fan coil-radiant wall (RAD-FC-RW) mode delivered the best overall performance, achieving the largest heat storage capacities (31.2%), the shortest time constant in the heating process (0.18 h) and the longest time constant in the non-heating process (0.39 h). In terms of energy performance, it achieved the highest system energy efficiency ratio (7.01), the highest solar contribution ratio (74.0%) and the highest exergy efficiency (23.5%), with the shortest payback period (4.3 years). The proposed system successfully demonstrated cascaded thermal energy utilization and synergistic operation across convection-radiation terminals. This offers valuable insights for the design and operation of efficient building heating systems.

title: Field investigation of diurnal boundary layer effects on wind farm wake evolution and power performance
abstract: Wind farm wake effects play a critical role in wind resource utilization and power generation efficiency, especially in large-scale wind power bases. However, systematic field studies that simultaneously characterize inflow conditions, wake evolution, and power response under different diurnal atmospheric conditions remain limited. In this study, the Jiuquan wind power base in the Hexi Corridor of China was investigated using a combination of Doppler LiDAR measurements and wind farm operational data. A comprehensive analysis was conducted from the perspectives of wind resource characteristics, wake behavior, and power generation performance. The results show that wake-induced velocity deficit and power output strongly depend on inflow wind speed. Under low to medium wind speed conditions, downstream turbines are more sensitive to wake interference, and the dispersion of the capacity factor among turbines increases markedly. When the inflow wind speed exceeds the rated wind speed, the influence of wake interference on downstream power output gradually becomes negligible. Diurnal comparisons further indicate that wake recovery is significantly suppressed under stable nighttime conditions, which leads to much larger downstream power losses than those observed during daytime. Under unstable daytime conditions, enhanced turbulent mixing accelerates wake recovery and reduces the impact on power loss. Based on field measurement, this study quantitatively elucidates the modulation effects of diurnal boundary layer variations on wind farm wakes and power characteristics. The results provide robust observational support for wind farm micrositing, turbine layout optimization, and operational control strategies.

title: Feasibility of boosting single-step biohydrogen production from sugarcane bagasse mediated by RSBA-biochar
abstract: This research offers a novel approach by utilizing the solid residue of biomass left after fermentation and examining the effects of producing biochar from this residue. Specifically, it investigates biochar derived from the solid residue of sugarcane bagasse, with biochar initially added before fermentation (RSBA-biochar), to boost single-step biohydrogen production through dark fermentation of sugarcane bagasse. RSBA-biochar II (RSBA II), added before fermentation, significantly boosted H2 yield, reaching 2706.05 mL/L (180.18 mL/g) at 7 g/L, with an increase of 2.82 times compared to the biochar group and 3.21 times compared to the control without biochar. The H2 production rate was 126.88 mL H2/L/h with a 7.27-h lag time, and the substrate utilization yield of 52.65% was tripled compared to the control. Overall, the unique physicochemical properties of RSBA II demonstrated improved pH buffering capacity due to its initial high pH and alkalinity, enhanced the NADH-dependent H2 production pathway with a higher NADH/NAD+ ratio of 0.76, and increased electron conduction efficiency during the fermentation process. This research provides an in-depth insight into the role of RSBA-biochar supplementation in improving the efficiency of single-step biohydrogen production from sugarcane bagasse, promising to facilitate the efficient utilization of inexpensive biomass for low-cost bioenergy production, contributing to the development of waste valorization and the circular bioeconomy.

title: Low-Carbon Operation Mode of the wind-photovoltaic-thermal-hydro-pumped storage hydropower combined generation system
abstract: Pumped storage hydropower plants (PSHP) have emerged as a fundamental component in the consumption of wind and photovoltaic(PV) resources and the reduction of carbon emissions. To address the challenge of coordinating PSHP with wind, PV, cascade hydropower, and thermal power plants, multiple PSHP scenarios are established to quantify the carbon reduction effect and the differences in reducing residual load fluctuations. A coordinated optimization model combined wind, PV, hydropower, PSHP, and thermal power plants is constructed, and the life cycle assessment (LCA) methodology is used to quantify the carbon emissions. Multiple operation scenarios are established by considering seasonal variations in the residual load, operating modes of PSHP, and dispatch objectives. By comparing the differences in carbon emission reductions and residual load fluctuations across various scenarios, an optimal operating mode for PSHP is declared. Results indicated that after incorporating carbon reduction into objectives, the carbon emissions decreased by 6.3% to 22.6% while maintaining overall output. It means that low-carbon energy replaces high-carbon energy. The output and water level changes indicate that the coordinated operation effects of the combined generation system are related to the reservoir's reserved storage capacity, residual load process, available water volume, number of pump-discharge cycles, and duration of pump-discharge flow. For scenarios characterized by multiple peaks in residual load with significant variations and limited available water volume, the one-pump and one-discharge operation mode is adopted. Conversely, for scenarios where residual load peaks show minimal variation and sufficient water volume, the one-pump and two-discharge scheduling mode is more appropriate.

title: Editorial Board
Framework for circular economy strategies in wind turbine end-of-life management
abstract: This study develops an integrated decision-support framework to evaluate circular economy (CE) strategies for wind turbine generator (WTG) end-of-life management. The proposed framework combines economic, environmental, and circularity indicators to assess alternative pathways including repair, refurbishment, reuse, remanufacturing, recycling, and repowering. A circularity metric based on the 9R framework is introduced to quantify the relative circular performance of different scenarios. Through scenario-based analysis, the framework evaluates the impacts of lifetime extension strategies on annual energy yield, emissions savings, and economic performance. The results highlight the significant potential of second-hand WTG markets, particularly under favorable wind conditions at new installation sites. The findings further demonstrate that increased circularity can simultaneously improve resource efficiency, reduce environmental impacts, and create additional economic value. The proposed framework provides a transparent and adaptable tool to support decision-making toward more sustainable and circular practices in the wind energy sector.

title: Ultra-short-term PV power forecasting under complex sky conditions using all-sky imaging and physically informed dynamic features
abstract: Accurate 5-min-ahead PV power forecasting remains challenging under complex sky conditions, where rapid cloud evolution and background scattering/turbidity variations jointly disturb irradiance and induce nonlinear power fluctuations. This study proposes an ultra-short-term forecasting framework based on synchronized all-sky imaging and grid-connected PV data. After quality control and temporal alignment, physically informed features are constructed — cloud-fraction and sky-optical descriptors, an image-derived background-optical proxy (HCF), and dynamic-gradient and interaction terms describing cloud–background co-evolution — and organized into three progressively enriched feature sets (M1–M3). Representative algorithms are evaluated under a unified protocol, with feature contributions quantified through ablation analysis. XGBoost with the full feature set (M3) achieves the best overall performance (RMSE, nRMSE, R2). Static descriptors provide only limited improvement, whereas dynamic-gradient and interaction features yield directionally consistent but modest aggregate gains; during ramp events, this advantage is confined to reduced peak error and improved phase alignment, without corresponding gains in ramp RMSE or MAE. Feature-importance analysis confirms the value of background-optical and evolution-sensitive representations. The framework operates entirely on instrument-derived, image-extracted features rather than raw image tensors or sequences. These findings indicate that explicitly incorporating cloud evolution and background-optical modulation can improve the accuracy and robustness of ultra-short-term PV forecasting, supporting more reliable short-term operation of PV-based renewable energy systems.

title: Study on wellbore flow and heat transfer characteristics in a surface-well-reservoir coupled compressed CO2 energy storage system
abstract: Compressed CO2 energy storage has emerged as a promising solution to accommodate the intermittent nature of renewable energy. The wellbore serves as the critical link for transporting working fluids to subsurface reservoirs, experiencing pronounced temperature and pressure fluctuations that significantly impact overall energy storage performance. Consequently, a detailed analysis of CO2 flow and heat transfer within the wellbore is essential to ensure effective coupling between surface and underground, which has not been adequately addressed in previous studies. The novelty of this study lies in the development of a surface-well-reservoir coupled energy storage model, which was used to investigate unique temperature variations caused by wellbore pressure work. This work identifies the complex trade-offs among storage temperature, energy efficiency, and turbine power output induced by heat storage. Accordingly, differences in performance under various charge-discharge strategies and wellbore depths are examined, and ultimately an effective optimized design scheme is proposed. The results indicate that wellbore pressure work leads to compression heating of CO2 during injection and expansion cooling during production, with effects varying by depth. Accounting for this effect reduces the calculated energy efficiency by 23% compared to previous estimates, yielding a more accurate assessment. Lower turbine outlet pressure, higher compressor inlet temperature and pressure that matches turbine outlet pressure, moderately high flow rate, and greater wellbore depth collectively enhance energy storage performance, achieving an energy efficiency of 64% and a turbine power output of 123 MW. These findings provide important insights for the design and performance optimization of underground energy storage systems.
keywords: Wellbore fluid flow and heat transfer

title: Pyrolysis-catalytic steam reforming of sewage sludge for the production of hydrogen/syngas over Ni-Fe/Al2O3 bimetallic catalysts prepared by the redox method
abstract: Pyrolysis-catalytic steam reforming over Ni-Fe/Al2O3 bimetallic catalysts represents a highly efficient strategy for simultaneous sewage sludge disposal and hydrogen-rich syngas production. Ni-Fe active-site interactions influence the catalytic process, which is effectively determined by the synthesis methodology. This study investigates a novel redox preparation method to enhance interactions at the Ni-Fe active site. Experimental work involved steam reforming of sewage sludge pyrolysis volatiles at 650 °C over catalysts prepared via redox, precipitation, and impregnation methods under identical conditions. Gas and liquid products were characterized via GC and GC×GC-TOFMS, respectively. Comprehensive catalyst characterization employed multiple techniques, including BET, SEM-EDX, XRD, XPS, NH3-TPD, H2-TPR, and TGA. Results demonstrated that the redox-prepared catalyst exhibited superior hydrogen production (5.30 mmol/g) compared to catalysts prepared by precipitation and impregnation. Characterization revealed that the redox catalyst possessed an optimal surface area and pore structure, uniform Ni-Fe active-phase dispersion, and abundant, strong acidic sites. The enhanced Ni-Fe interaction facilitated an effective redox cycle, promoting the steam reforming of volatiles. Based on these findings, a comprehensive reaction mechanism for the reforming process over this novel catalyst was proposed.

title: A model predictive control approach to dual-axis agrivoltaic panel tracking
abstract: Agrivoltaic systems--photovoltaic (PV) panels installed above agricultural land--have emerged as a promising dual-use solution to address competing land demands for food and energy production. In this paper, we propose a model predictive control (MPC) approach to dual-axis agrivoltaic panel tracking control that dynamically adjusts panel positions in real time to maximize power production and crop yield given solar irradiance and ambient temperature measurements. We apply convex relaxations and shading factor approximations to reformulate the MPC optimization problem as a convex second-order cone program that determines the PV panel position adjustments away from the sun-tracking trajectory. Through case studies, we demonstrate our approach, exploring the Pareto front between i) an approach that maximizes power production without considering crop needs and ii) crop yield with no agrivoltaics. We also conduct a case study exploring the impact of forecast error on MPC performance. We find that dynamically adjusting agrivoltaic panel position helps us actively manage the trade-offs between power production and crop yield, and that active panel control enables the agrivoltaic system to achieve land equivalent ratio values of up to 1.897.

title: Bifacial photovoltaic-micro agriculture integrated system for urban distributed energy applications: Optical-thermal coupling, realizable rear-side gains, and parallel carbon offsets
abstract: Micro agriculture provides environmental cooling via evapotranspiration and substrate buffering while providing storm water retention and carbon sequestration. Integrating micro agriculture with photovoltaic systems can enhance per-area value in urban low-carbon distributed energy systems, but existing composites are often simple stacked configurations with limited mechanistic coupling. This study develops and evaluates a bifacial photovoltaic and micro agriculture integrated system using a rooftop-adapted tall edible Sedum-type micro-agricultural vegetation layer on a full-scale test platform. The results show that rear-side gain in bifacial photovoltaic systems under rooftop validation conditions is governed by the balance between reflected irradiance and thermal penalty. Highly reflective surfaces enhance rear-side light input but also increase module heat accumulation and efficiency loss, so high power gains are not necessarily realized. In contrast, the micro-agricultural vegetation layer mitigates module overheating through evapotranspiration, shifts rooftop heat dissipation toward latent heat, and stabilizes reflection-driven gains. Over 20 consecutive experimental days, the bifacial photovoltaic-micro agriculture integrated system achieved a 4.58% increase in total power generation relative to a conventional concrete-roof bifacial photovoltaic system. Meanwhile, photovoltaic-mediated shading and microclimate regulation reduced evaporative water loss in the micro-agricultural subsystem by 57.9%. Further, biomass carbon sequestration and soil organic carbon sequestration were incorporated into a scenario-based life cycle assessment framework to quantify the carbon balance of the bifacial photovoltaic-micro agriculture integrated system. Under the defined 15-year composite-system LCA scenario, the micro-agricultural module provided an additional 6.8 kg CO2-eq/FU reduction, and the modeled net carbon balance of the system was −6625.91 kg CO2-eq/FU.

title: Hydrothermal conversion of lignocellulosic biomass using deep eutectic solvents and iron salts for solid biofuel and chemical recovery
abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrothermal carbonization (HTC) of lignocellulosic waste (hemp oil cake) was investigated using a thermally stable choline chloride–glycolic acid deep eutectic solvent (DES) as an alternative reaction medium, in combination with iron salts (FeCl 3 and FeSO 4 ), to assess their synergistic effects on product properties. DES significantly enhanced biomass hydrolysis and solubilisation, while Fe salts modified reaction pathways and nutrient distribution. Compared to water-assisted HTC, DES-assisted HTC resulted in reduced hydrochar yields (50–72 wt%), particularly at higher temperatures and DES dosages, but promoted carbon enrichment. Carbon content increased from 49.6 wt% for water-derived hydrochar to 53.1–59.7 wt% for DES–Fe derived hydrochars, accompanied by a substantial reduction in nitrogen content. The combined DES–Fe HTC resulted in a notable improvement in fuel quality, with heating values reaching up to 26.6 MJ/kg. SEM showed increased porosity and spherical carbon structures. XPS and NMR confirmed enhanced aromatisation and nitrogen stabilisation in heterocyclic and graphitic forms, with Fe salts accelerating graphitic-N formation. DES-assisted HTC enriched process liquids in organic carbon, phenolics and furfural, indicating enhanced extraction but also increased ecotoxicity. No genotoxicity was detected in the Vicia faba assay. This work introduces a novel DES–Fe-assisted HTC approach to tailor hydrochar properties for renewable energy applications.

title: Bitcoin mining and renewable energy: Navigating sustainability, profitability, and electricity market dynamics
abstract: Bitcoin mining's substantial electricity demand has raised environmental concerns, yet its operational flexibility offers potential alignment with surplus renewable generation. Using source-tagged nodal Locational Marginal Price (LMP) data from the California Independent System Operator (CAISO) for the pre-halving period (January 2018 – May 2020), this paper introduces and empirically quantifies the colocation premium—the realized electricity price advantage of renewable-tagged relative to fossil-tagged nodes. The results show that this premium is concentrated in the lower tail of the price distribution: at the 5th percentile, wind LMP reaches –$33.48/MWh, versus –$15.33/MWh for natural gas, while the difference largely vanishes at the median. A profit-maximizing model calibrated with two ASIC generations (Antminer S9 and MicroBT Whatsminer M31S+) demonstrates that wind-colocated mining achieves a substantially lower break-even Bitcoin price of $3200 than gas-colocated mining $5,800, but only under threshold-based dispatch. Post-halving dynamics approximately double break-even prices, narrowing profitability margins. Seasonal robustness checks confirm that renewable sources consistently offer lower LMPs. These findings suggest that Bitcoin mining can operate as a flexible demand-side resource that absorbs surplus renewable energy, although its economic and environmental benefits depend on tail-driven price advantages, selective operation, and enabling policy frameworks.

title: A multi-stage leaf-shaped solar distiller inspired by plant guttation for near-zero liquid discharge
abstract: Achieving near-zero liquid discharge and maximizing freshwater recovery from highly saline brines remain significant challenges in solar-driven interfacial desalination. This paper presents a multi-stage leaf-shaped solar interfacial membrane distiller with a back-side configuration. Inspired by the plant guttation process, this design leverages gravitational potential energy to create a non-contact dripping mechanism at the leaf tip that effectively prevents salt crystallization on the evaporator. The periodic detachment of brine droplets physically disrupts the continuous hydraulic connection, fundamentally suppressing back-diffusion of salt ions and reducing parasitic heat conduction between the evaporator and brine reservoir. A steady-state energy-balance model was established to elucidate the relative contributions of various heat-loss pathways. Through indoor steady-state experiments, the relationships between evaporation temperature and water production rate as functions of petiole thickness, leaf inclination angle, and seawater salinity were systematically characterized. Notably, a four-stage leaf-shaped distiller achieved a water production rate of 2.08 kg/m2/h with 3.5 wt% seawater salinity. After five consecutive desalination cycles of the concentrated brine, a cumulative recovery ratio of 84.7% was attained. Due to increasing brine salinity, the gain output ratio decreased progressively from 1.35 to 0.7 across successive desalination cycles. Under real weather conditions, the four-stage leaf distiller yielded a daily freshwater production of 6.06 kg/m2/d with an average solar irradiance of 831.6 W/m2. This work provides a valuable strategy for solar desalination and the treatment of highly saline brines.

title: Continuous direct solar-driven thermochemical energy storage via funnel-shape falling-particle reactors
abstract: Direct solar-driven thermochemical energy storage offers a promising pathway to bridge the mismatch between intermittent solar availability and continuous thermal energy demand, owing to its high energy density and long storage duration. However, existing thermochemical energy storage reactors are usually constrained by intermittent operation, limited controllability, and low solar-to-chemical conversion efficiency. Here, we demonstrate continuous and efficient direct solar-driven thermochemical energy storage via a funnel-shaped falling-particle reactor. By dynamically regulating particle residence time, the reactor enables optimized matching between solar energy transport, reaction kinetics, and particle flow, providing a flexible operating window to balance conversion and throughput. Under direct solar irradiation, the reactor achieves a system efficiency of 26.63%–34.20% and a calcium carbonate conversion of 74.4%–95.5%. Numerical analysis further suggests that a 25% reduction in thermal losses, which is a reasonably achievable target through insulation upgrades and optical optimization, could increase the system efficiency to 40.72%. This work opens new routes for the design of direct solar-driven thermochemical energy storage reactors that enable continuous, efficient, and tunable operation, and promotes their scalable applications.

title: Nanoparticles–functionalized kaolinite-based composite materials for multimodal energy conversion
abstract: Multifunctional composite phase change materials (CPCMs) capable of photothermal, electrothermal, and magnetothermal energy conversion have garnered considerable attention for advanced thermal energy-storage applications. Herein, a simple chemical deposition–surface lamination strategy is proposed to uniformly load Fe3O4 nanoparticles onto kaolin as the carrier, yielding such CPCMs. Owing to the remarkable photophysical properties of the nanoparticles and the surface plasmon resonance effect, endowed kaolinite-Fe3O4/stearic acid (SA) achieves excellent photothermal conversion performance and electrical thermal conversion performances (90.9% and 86.5%, respectively). Graphene provides a continuous channel for electron transfer and requires only 1.4 V for electrothermal conversion. In the presence of a magnetic field, the Nair and Brownian relaxation effects of the nanoparticles endow kaolinite-Fe3O4/SA with a heating rate of 0.19 °C/min. In addition, after multiple phase transformation processes, the CPCMs remain leak-resistant and thermally-stable. These findings demonstrate that simplified design processes can feasibly obtain multifunctional CPCMs for multienergy conversion.

title: Defrosting control strategy optimization of superhydrophobic air source heat pump aimed at minimizing defrosting duration and energy consumption
abstract: Superhydrophobic coatings have demonstrated excellent defrosting performance. However, its defrosting performance when used in air source heat pumps (ASHPs) is still unclear. To promote its application in ASHPs, two ASHPs with same configuration were manufactured, one superhydrophobic and the other hydrophilic. Through the microscopic observation and experimental analysis, its defrosting performance under the different frosting conditions were revealed. Then, the effects of compressor speed and defrosting termination conditions on defrosting performance were quantitatively analyzed, respectively. Finally, according the analysis results, a new defrosting control strategy suitable for superhydrophobic ASHPs was proposed and validated. Experimental results showed that the superhydrophobic ASHP exhibited excellent defrosting performance under different frosting conditions. Compared to those of hydrophilic ASHP, its defrosting durations at 2/1 °C and −3/-4 °C were 75 s and 165 s shorter, and the defrosting energy consumption was reduced by 62.8% and 64.5%. However, as the defrosting control strategy of hydrophilic ASHP was used, the superhydrophobic ASHP encountered the excessive defrosting issue. When adopting the proposed defrosting control strategy, i.e. the compressor speed was 46 rps and defrosting terminated when the surface temperature reached 2 °C and lasted 30 s, the goal of minimizing the defrosting duration and energy consumption was realized.

title: Inhibiting the formation of slag derived from K–Ca carbonate melts in gasifiers by tuning the ash fusion characteristics of woody biomass fuels through blending
abstract: Efficient biomass conversion is essential for achieving carbon neutrality by 2050. Small-scale decentralised gasification combined heat and power plants are promising owing to their high efficiency; however, their operational availability in Japan remains limited (∼50%), primarily due to slag formation from salt melts in biomass ash. This study proposes a practical additive-free strategy in which Japanese cedar (JC) is blended with selected Pinaceae species to increase ash fusion temperatures (AFTs) and suppress slag formation. Several Pinaceae species—red pine (RP), black pine (BP), white pine, larch, and Todo fir—were evaluated to identify those with high AFTs. The blended ash samples were characterised using ash fusion tests, thermogravimetric–differential thermal analysis, and thermodynamic equilibrium calculations to elucidate the underlying mechanisms. Blending JC with BP or RP significantly increased AFTs, with optimal mass ratios of BP/(JC + BP) ≥ 88% and RP/(JC + RP) ≥ 37%. BP blending reduced K and increased Ca contents, thereby suppressing the formation of low-melting K2CO3–CaCO3 phases and inhibiting slag formation. RP blending produced similar effects while supplying Si and Mg, promoting the formation of high-melting Ca–Mg–Si compounds. Furthermore, CaCO3 decarbonation and subsequent CaO formation improved melting behaviour. These findings demonstrate that controlled biomass blending, without external additives, can effectively modify ash chemistry and phase equilibria, providing a cost-effective and sustainable strategy for mitigating slag formation in gasification systems using alkali-rich woody biomass.

title: Financing renewable energy projects in Latin America beyond resource quality, levelized cost of electricity, project feasibility, and the role of the weighted average cost of capital
abstract: Evaluating renewable energy in emerging markets requires accounting for the interaction between resource quality and financing conditions. Traditional Levelized Cost of Electricity assessments apply uniform discount rates, overlooking cross-country differences in the cost of capital. This omission conceals a fundamental trade-off: a project with excellent resource quality may be less competitive than one with inferior resource but cheaper financing. This study quantifies that trade-off by estimating the Weighted Average Cost of Capital for utility-scale renewable generation projects in Latin America. Using bond data, adjusted equity costs, tax, and leverage ratios, the analysis constructs country-specific financing environments. Results reveal capital costs divergences driven by debt costs and sovereign risk. These financial disparities have stronger effects on project valuation than variations in electricity generation. In America Latina, a 150–200 basis points increase in the cost of debt has a larger impact on net present value than a 5–7 percentage-point improvement in resource availability. Sensitivity analysis shows that increasing leverage reduces the cost of capital, reinforcing the primacy of financing conditions over marginal resource advantages. Findings demonstrate that cheaper capital outweighs resource quality in determining competitiveness. For investors and policymakers, improving access to low-cost financing becomes a more effective lever than resource-driven strategies.

title: Interface inclination in partially filled metal-foam/PCM thermal buffers for solar-facing renewable-energy applications
abstract: Solar-facing thermal interfaces may experience intense transient heat loads that increase peak temperature and produce local temperature non-uniformity. Phase change materials provide passive thermal buffering, but their low thermal conductivity limits charging performance. This study investigates a passive internal-geometry strategy for partially filled copper-foam/paraffin thermal buffers without changing the external module orientation. Visualization experiments were conducted, and a local thermal non-equilibrium model was validated against melting-front evolution and infrared temperature patterns. The validated model was then used to vary the inclination of the interface between the pure-paraffin and copper-foam/paraffin regions at a fixed filling ratio and constant foam volume under a controlled heat flux. Relative to a horizontal interface, a +60° inclination reduced complete-melting time by 18.0% but increased the peak heated-wall temperature indicator by 4.0%. Redistributing a small fraction of foam to a top layer occupying one-eighth of the cavity height reduced the peak heated-wall temperature and hotspot indicators by 14.6% and 61.6%, respectively. The refined configuration retained comparable charging performance, with complete-melting time reduced by 2.8% and the time to 90% melting advanced by 8.8%. These results demonstrate that interface orientation and targeted foam redistribution can coordinate buoyancy-driven convection and foam-assisted conduction in compact solar-facing thermal buffers.

title: Potential effect of different PV cell structures on CPV electrical performance enhancement
abstract: Concentrated photovoltaic (CPV) technology plays a pivotal role in the progression towards a zero-carbon built environment (ZCBE). The incorporation of CPV technology within building designs not only enhances the energy output of PV cells but also facilitates photovoltaic thermal applications. Nonetheless, the non-uniform irradiance field produced by the concentrator results in a corresponding non-uniform temperature distribution, which adversely impacts the electrical performance of the PV cells. To address this issue, a model of a non-uniform composite physical field PV cell has been developed, and the model's reliability has been established through a comparison of experimental data with simulation outcomes. Following the validation of the model, the effects of different PV cell surface structures (different PV cell distributions, busbar distributions and numbers) on the power output of CPV is investigated. Furthermore, the analysis encompassed the radiation distribution within the emitter region and the series losses occurring in the finger and busbar regions under varying surface structures of the PV cells. The results show that the difference in the electrical efficiency of the CPV for different PV cell distributions is 0.30%; the maximum difference in the electrical efficiency of the CPV for different busbar distributions is 0.98%; and the maximum difference in the electrical efficiency of the CPV for different numbers of busbars is 0.37%. Consequently, optimizing the structural design of PV cells to accommodate the specific non-uniform composite physical field generated by concentrated light may represent a viable strategy for enhancing the efficiency of photovoltaic energy generation.

title: Utilizing water turbines for cathodic protection of pipelines
abstract: — Cathodic protection (CP) using the impressed current method is widely employed in the water transmission industry to prevent or mitigate corrosion of metal structures and pipelines, thereby reducing associated costs. Powering CP stations is a crucial aspect, and traditional methods often incur high expenses due to the distance from power generation and distribution centers. This paper presents a novel approach utilizing the energy of the flowing water within the pipeline to power CP stations, distinguishing it from conventional grid-based, solar, and wind-based supply strategies by exploiting the pipeline's internal hydraulic energy for self-sustained operation. An efficient and practical method for generating the electrical energy required for impressed current cathodic protection (CP) stations is introduced through a detailed modeling of a water turbine, a proposed generator, and the design of power electronic converters. To comprehensively evaluate operating conditions, this research employs an accurate electrical model of steel pipelines. The generator's output power fluctuates due to variations in fluid flow within the pipeline. However, the power electronic converter maintains a steady injected current by continuously monitoring the pipeline voltage relative to the half-cell electrode. By addressing both corrosion risks and power supply challenges, this study presents a self-sustaining solution for cathodic protection in remote pipeline installations.

title: Enhancing solar energy conversion via a coupled colloidal photovoltaic with thermally regenerative electrochemical conversion system
abstract: Efficient use of solar energy is limited by unavoidable heat losses during electricity generation, which reduces overall system performance. To address this challenge, this study introduces a hybrid solar energy system that combines a colloidal photovoltaic (CPV) with a thermally driven electrochemical unit capable of both power generation and cooling. A comprehensive numerical model is developed to describe the coupled electrical, thermal, and electrochemical interactions within the hybrid system, accounting for key irreversible losses. The effects of operating temperature, absorber thickness, regeneration efficiency, material properties, and internal resistance on system performance are systematically analyzed. Under optimal operating conditions, the hybrid system delivers a power density of 209.86 W m-2 and an energy efficiency of 20.99%, corresponding to improvements of 24.2% and 24.3%, respectively, relative to standalone CPV. The analysis further reveals that appropriate thermal management and parameter matching between subsystems are essential for fully unlocking the performance potential of the system. These findings demonstrate the viability of integrated solar-electrochemical systems to enhance solar energy utilization while simultaneously providing cooling, offering a promising pathway for advanced solar energy applications.

title: Techno-economic assessment of salt hydrate-based solar water heating systems under different climate scenarios
abstract: Large energy storage capacity and low cost of salt hydrates make them ideal candidates for integration into solar water heating systems. In this work, the phase-change performance and system reliability of the sodium acetate trihydrate–acetamide-based system and the sodium acetate trihydrate-based system were experimentally compared. The former system achieved a 5.6% higher efficiency. The system performance was further investigated numerically under varying setpoints and climate conditions to determine the optimal operating conditions for each material. Due to its more efficient use of latent heat, the sodium acetate trihydrate–acetamide-based system achieves a reduction of approximately 3.0% in annual cost compared to the sodium acetate trihydrate-based system at a setpoint of 40 °C in Hong Kong. However, the former system shows a longer payback period of approximately 4.9% in Denmark, and both phase-change materials showed negative net present values in France. The sodium acetate trihydrate–acetamide-based system exhibited lower energy use and operating expenditure under solar radiation of around 350–700 W/m 2 in Hong Kong. Nevertheless, after accounting for degradation, the higher replacement cost offset its operational savings, leading to a slightly higher lifecycle cost than the sodium acetate trihydrate-based system. This study highlights the importance of climate-specific material selection to balance energy performance and cost-effectiveness.

title: A novel combination of water-washing pre-treatment, varying briquetting techniques, and oxidative microwave torrefaction for the production of low-ash empty fruit bunch-based briquette with improved performance
abstract: This study aimed to produce low-ash empty fruit bunch (EFB)-based briquettes with improved physical and fuel properties as well as thermal decomposition and combustion behaviors. This study was established through a novel combination of multiple optimized methods. The methods consisted of water-washing pre-treatment, various briquetting techniques, and oxidative microwave torrefaction (OMWT). 60-minute optimized water-washing pre-treatment of EFB with EFB-to-water mixing ratio of 1:20 (by weight) and stirring speed of 180 rpm was performed. Subsequently, non-heated (with starch binder) and heated (binderless) briquetting techniques were employed. Ultimately, 10-min optimized OMWT of the produced briquette was carried out at microwave power level of 300 W and oxygen concentration of 6 vol%. Comparative analysis was then performed to evaluate the effects of the proposed novel method on the briquettes’ performance. Results showed the excellent performance of the washed EFB-starch binder briquette that satisfied the aim of this study. It produced low ash (4.75 ± 0.57%) and moisture contents (3.36 ± 0.25%), satisfactory higher heating value (22.14 ± 0.29 MJ/kg), and acceptable physical properties. It also had competitive thermal decomposition and combustion behaviors. Ultimately, this study contributes to the effective utilization of biomass-based materials as a sustainable and renewable energy source.
keywords: Washed empty fruit bunch-starch binder briquette

title: Cepstral coefficients for real-time recognition of known and unknown wind turbine damage and power-generation states
abstract: This work presents a methodology for real-time recognition of wind turbine damage and power-generation states. By linking structural response features to altered or degraded operating behavior, the framework connects vibration-based monitoring with renewable energy generation performance. The methodology combines Linear Discriminant Analysis for dimensionality reduction with Probabilistic Linear Discriminant Analysis for adaptive classification under changing conditions. A key innovation is the model’s ability to recognize both known and previously unseen classes, despite being trained only on known nominal operating conditions in a semi-supervised learning setting. This capability addresses a critical challenge in wind turbine monitoring, where faults are difficult to anticipate and labeled data are often limited. The framework also adopts the Confusion Flow matrix, an extension of the traditional confusion matrix that incorporates temporal dynamics, enabling classification behavior over time. The method is validated using vibration and Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition data from the Aventa AV-7 research wind turbine, organized into four nominal operating classes and multiple off-nominal states associated with pitch-system malfunction and aerodynamic imbalance. The identified classes correspond to distinct changes in operating behavior, including the transition from nominal to degraded power production before emergency shutdown during pitch failure. The framework achieves average binary and multi-class performance indices of up to 0.89 and 0.67, respectively, with best-case results above 0.94 and 0.91 for selected sensors. The proposed Confusion Flow matrix further highlights temporal trends in misclassification, class stability, and state separability, providing interpretable insight into model adaptability over time.

title: HetWECs: Experimental heterogeneous wave energy converter arrays
abstract: Wave energy converter arrays are necessary to provide grid-scale power production. However, array hydrodynamic interactions are commonly ignored and rarely experimentally investigated, leaving a gap in numerical multi-body model validation. Additionally, no previous work has evaluated a multi-architecture (heterogeneous) array to quantify the potential power extraction symbioses and increase in array response bandwidth. This study provides a rigorous experimental dataset for system identification of a heterogeneous wave energy converter array consisting of both heaving point absorbers and oscillating surge wave energy converters. Heterogeneous array interactions increased the point absorber heave response by up to 30% compared to their homogeneous counterparts while the oscillating surge device response remained relatively unchanged. Additionally, the heterogeneous array interactions smoothed the point absorber heave response, providing consistent dynamic responses across a range of regular wave frequencies. Traditional theoretical estimations of viscous damping for oscillating surge devices produce a trend line slope opposite of the observed viscous damping, pointing to a need for improved linearization of this term. The boundary element method solver over-predicts excitation force and does a poor job predicting the off-diagonals of the radiation force interaction matrix. Superimposing the empirical isolated radiated, diffracted, and incident wave fields over-predicts wave elevation between 2 and 25%, and the boundary element method solver produced 10%–15% error in wave elevation prediction nearest to the array. Overall, heterogeneous arrays show complimentary response and power extraction trends, suggesting they may enable developers to broaden the bandwidth of wave energy converter arrays.

title: Optimization of wind-PV-storage aggregated inertia coefficient using physics-informed neural network to suppress frequency oscillations in hydropower-dominated power systems
abstract: Low-frequency oscillations can severely threaten frequency stability of hydropower-dominated power systems. Although such oscillations can be mitigated by adjusting the proportional-integral-derivative parameters of hydro turbine governors, this adjustment compromises the primary frequency regulation capability of hydro units. Wind, photovoltaic and energy storage systems are increasingly being integrated into hydropower delivery networks, and the fast regulation capabilities of these renewable sources offer an alternative solution to suppress both hydro unit power swings and system frequency oscillations.
