To make use of these capabilities, this paper proposes a novel coordinated control strategy for wind-photovoltaic-energy storage systems to suppress frequency oscillations in hydropower-dominated power grids. The key innovation of the proposed strategy lies in the use of a physics-informed neural network to dynamically optimize the aggregated virtual inertia coefficient of the wind-photovoltaic-energy storage system. This enables adaptive allocation of active power among wind, photovoltaic and energy storage units under different frequency deviation deadbands. Importantly, the proposed method achieves effective oscillation damping without modifying the existing hydro turbine governors. The performance of the proposed strategy is validated through real-time simulations on an RTLAB-based wind-photovoltaic-hydro-energy storage delivery system model. The corresponding results demonstrate that the proposed approach effectively suppresses power oscillations in the multi-source system and significantly enhances the primary frequency regulation performance, confirming its potential for practical implementation.

title: Synthesis mechanism and combustion behavior of hybrid bio-coal synfuels from biomass and coal via synergistic co-carbonization technology
abstract: In this paper, a synergistic co-carbonization technology for cleanliness and environmental protection has been reported, which has successfully produced eco-friendly carbon-based synfuels from bituminous coal (BC) and agricultural corn stalks (CS) for use in eco-friendly ironmaking sintering processes. The experimental results indicate that the mixed powders of CS and BC with 4 wt% CaO were carbonized at 550°C for 30 min, and the higher heating value, solid yield and bulk density of the synfuel reached reasonable basic parameters of 29.16 MJ kg−1, 63.87% and 462 kg m−3, respectively. Moreover, the decrease in the initial temperature of the pyrolysis process by 78°C resulted in an increase in the activation energy of the active devolatilization stage by 39.85 kJ mol−1, whereas that of the secondary cracking stage decreased by 19.90 kJ mol−1. Additionally, the dissociation of the aliphatic side chains in the crude materials increased the proportion of the carbon microcrystalline structure, resulting in an increase of the biochar by 0.09 with the addition of 4 wt% CaO. The content of C=C increased to 6.85, which proved that CaO promoted the transformation from biomass to carbonaceous material. Such structural upgrades boost thermal stability and combustion efficiency. This work clarifies multi-level CaO mechanisms covering crystal growth, volatile inhibition, activation energy balance and graphitization, laying a solid scientific framework to convert biomass into high-grade sintering fuel.

title: Multimodal wave energy conversion: Modal coupling effects and power capture
abstract: Multimodal wave energy converters offer theoretical performance advantages over single-mode devices, yet optimal design is hindered by limited understanding of modal interactions. This research study investigated modal coupling and veering phenomena across six configurations. The configurations employed pendulum geometries with symmetrically inclined power take-off tether systems. Their geometries, mass distributions, and draft were optimized to achieve target natural periods in heave, pitch, and surge. Modal analysis across various tether angles and power take-off stiffness revealed modal interaction and veering effects associated with surge-pitch coupling. These effects were linked to annual energy production metrics to identify optimal configurations for beneficial modal coupling. Results indicated that optimized multimodal wave energy converters can achieve superior energy production compared to equivalent single-mode heave absorbers. Combining modal analysis and power capture results, this paper demonstrates that characterizing coupling effects is a critical step in the system’s design.

title: An improved wake steering optimization method for enhanced wind energy production using realistic yaw behaviour
abstract: Wake steering is widely regarded as an effective strategy for mitigating wake losses and enhancing wind farm energy production through active yaw misalignment. However, most existing wake steering optimization methods implicitly assume ideal yaw execution without accounting for turbine yaw control logic and execution dynamics, leading to systematic performance deviations when deployed in real wind farms. This study develops a wake steering optimization framework that explicitly accounts for realistic turbine yaw behaviour. By integrating data-driven identification of yaw control characteristics with a probabilistic yaw response representation and a two-level optimization scheme, the proposed method captures uncertainty-induced, multi-modal, and directionally coupling effects in yaw execution. Gaussian-Hermite Sparse Grid Quadrature is employed to efficiently propagate these effects within the optimization process. Simulation results based on a commercial wind farm demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves higher overall energy production than conventional wake steering optimization methods. Overall, the proposed framework provides a systematic and customizable approach for wake steering optimization under realistic yaw execution, supporting more reliable long-term operational improvements in real-world wind farms.

title: Operative performance of helical borehole heat exchanger with shape-stabilized phase change material: borehole array analysis
abstract: Although shape-stabilized phase change materials are widely studied as borehole heat exchanger backfill, their long-term performance in large-scale arrays under realistic conditions remains unclear, hindering practical deployment of such enhanced exchangers. A ground source heat pump model with three borehole heat exchanger configurations evaluated a two-year operation of an office building in Chongqing under annual loads: a traditional U-tube (Case 1), a single-helix exchanger with shape-stabilized phase change material (Case 2), and a double-helix exchanger also with the material (Case 3). Case 2 showed lower summer outlet temperature (28.13°C vs 30.64°C) and higher annual energy efficiency ratio (5.39 vs 5.11) than Case 1. The double-helix configuration utilized more phase change material (reaching higher summer temperatures) but suffered from borehole heat accumulation, limiting long-term performance. Case 2's optimal performance balances phase change material benefits and increased heat transfer area against thermal accumulation. Helical designs improve land efficiency, needing only 73.0% (Case 2) and 56.8% (Case 3) of the conventional area. Increasing borehole spacing partly alleviates heat accumulation but cannot prevent long-term ground temperature rise under land constraints. This work provides a basis for selecting and optimizing helical borehole heat exchangers in engineering applications.

title: Long-term field performance of twin thin-film PV systems: A 14-year comparative study across two Spanish climatic zones
abstract: ABSTRACT Using 14 years of operational data, this study compares four small grid-connected thin-film photovoltaic systems installed as twin setups in Madrid and Jaén, Spain: a-Si (0.90 kW) and a-Si/μc-Si (0.88 kW). This configuration enables a controlled comparison between a more continental climate and warmer southern Mediterranean conditions. The a-Si systems were the best performers in terms of energy production, with average annual final system yields of 1537 kWh·kW -1 in Jaén and 1438 kWh·kW -1 in Madrid, and average annual performance ratios of 0.73 and 0.71, respectively. For a-Si/μc-Si, the corresponding values were lower: 1449 and 1361 kWh·kW -1 , and 0.68 and 0.67, respectively. Jaén generally outperformed Madrid, especially in winter, due to higher irradiance levels and slightly more favourable spectral conditions. However, a-Si/μc-Si showed slightly greater long-term stability. When regular cleaning was applied only in Jaén during a subperiod, the Madrid systems exhibited a more pronounced performance decline, revealing the role of soiling-related losses. Over the full analysis period, representative performance loss rates remained moderate, ranging from about −0.75 to −0.96 %·y -1 . Overall, this study provides a rare long-term field benchmark for legacy thin-film technologies, supporting PV lifetime modelling, performance-decline assessment, and the evaluation of emerging thin-film concepts under real operating conditions.

title: Improvement of the combustion model for a biomass stove: Validation with experimental measurements
abstract: In this work, two enhanced combustion models are used to study the overall performance of the Portable Patsari (PP) biomass stove. The 6R and 10R chemical mechanisms feature six and ten reactions, respectively, along with two values of the excess air ratio ( λ = 2 and 3). The main goal is to validate both models using experimental measurements by comparing key variables. The ANSYS Fluent software was used to build the following numerical configuration to simulate transport phenomena in the stove. The results showed that a better and more accurate assessment for the thermal and combustion performance was achieved by implementing 10R model than the 6R one. In general, there is good agreement between experimental measurements and simulations with λ = 3 . Also no significant differences in global efficiency and in most mass flow rates (MFR) were reported. The average contribution of the stove for 6R_L2 and 10R_L2 was found to be 0.63 ± 0.04 kgCO 2 e/kg (5%, p = 0.41) and 0.54 ± 0.05 kgCO 2 e/kg (11%, p = 0.11), respectively. This means that both models correctly predicted CO 2 e emissions. Finally, the insights constitute a substantial advance in the understanding of the combustion process in biomass plancha-type stoves. Given that the one-reaction combustion model is still in use, the results provide a more comprehensive study based on two upgraded combustion models.

title: 3D urban solar potential assessment using data-efficient deep learning in Lhasa (City of sunshine)
abstract: Low-carbon energy transitions are essential for climate change mitigation, yet urban solar potential assessments often emphasize rooftop photovoltaic (PV) systems. Consequently, façade solar potential, solar-thermal (ST) yield, and solar supply–demand contributions are underexplored. It is an acute gap for Lhasa, China (“City of Sunshine”), where solar resources are abundant, but potential remains unquantified. The study proposes a three-dimensional assessment method integrating geographical potential (rooftop and façade solar radiation), technical potential (PV and ST outputs), and comprehensive potential (solar contribution to building energy consumption) to address this gap. A deep learning model for building height estimation was developed, reducing training images by 72.1% while cutting errors by 18.2%. A 3D urban model was derived, and three-tiered solar potential was calculated. The results highlight notable facades and ST potential. During the heating season, roofs and south facades receive comparable solar radiation. With an optimal PV-ST configuration, annual electricity production covers Lhasa’s residential demand, and thermal energy meets 69.5% of heating requirements. Solar energy supply proportion varies significantly across land use types and block forms. Transportation Land exhibits the highest solar energy supply proportion (54.5%), while Industrial and Mining Land shows the lowest (29.6%). High floor area ratio blocks can effectively utilize facade solar energy. The work extends solar potential analysis to include facades and thermal systems, providing an evaluation method adaptable to cities globally.

title: Machine learning model of hydrokinetic energy harnessing for tandem cylinders in flow-induced oscillation based on limited systemic data
abstract: The vortex-induced vibration for aquatic clean energy converter with two tandem cylinders, on elastic end-supports, can extract marine hydrokinetic energy into electricity through synergistic flow-induced oscillation. Its performance depends strongly on the spacing ratio of tandem oscillators and other flow and system parameters. In this paper, the energy harvesting potential at a high spacing of 4.57 diameters is explored, compared with the previous values of 1.57, 2.0, and 2.57. To achieve rapid parameter optimization for power and efficiency harvesting, we propose an efficient optimization framework combining an accurate machine learning prediction model with a levy flight particle swarm optimization algorithm. The main conclusions are: (1) A spacing ratio of 4.57 improves the harvested power and efficiency from flow-induced oscillation owing to wake interference. (2) By refining parameter resolution, particularly by capturing the optimal spacing ratio of 3.5, the optimization framework improves vortex-induced vibration power by 1.09-3.28 times compared to experimental optima from limited parameters. (3) The tandem-cylinder system outperforms a single-cylinder system, achieving 2.09-8.25 times higher optimal power and 37%-288% greater optimal efficiency based on the Betz Limit. (4) The global maximum power efficiency occurs at the end of galloping with a high spacing ratio of 4.57, low spring stiffness, and damping ratio. Global optimization reveals novel synergistic parameter effects on energy harvesting—patterns not discernible through conventional methods—and offers direct design guidance.

title: Improving the overload performance of a Francis turbine by means of a passive vortex control device
abstract: The increasing demand for flexible operation of hydropower plants forces Francis turbines to operate frequently under off-design conditions, where draft-tube flow instabilities can severely limit performance and structural integrity. In particular, overload operation is associated with strong residual swirl at the runner outlet, leading to vortex-induced pressure pulsations and reduced pressure recovery. Despite its growing relevance, effective mitigation strategies specifically targeting overload conditions remain limited. This study proposes a novel passive vortex-control concept based on a bladed runner cone, inspired by boss-cap fins commonly used in marine propellers. The device is conceived as a minimally invasive retrofit solution aimed at reducing the tangential velocity component at the draft-tube inlet during high-discharge operation. Unsteady numerical simulations are performed on a medium–specific-speed Francis turbine over its entire operating range, from deep part load to overload conditions. The results show that the proposed device effectively suppresses overload vortex structures and significantly reduces draft-tube pressure pulsations, while improving diffuser pressure recovery. At the highest investigated discharge, an increase in hydraulic efficiency of up to approximately two percentage points is achieved, with only minor efficiency penalties at nominal and part-load conditions.

title: Data-driven temporal recursive thermal response model for borehole heat exchangers based on sum of exponential approximation
abstract: Accurately predicting borehole temperature responses is critical for the long-term simulation and optimization of ground-source heat pump systems. However, traditional methods based on convolution integration suffer from inherent historical dependence, requiring the storage and processing of complete load sequences, which results in high computational costs and memory demands. Existing acceleration techniques, such as load aggregation and the Fast Fourier Transform, can improve computational efficiency to some extent but do not fundamentally eliminate historical dependency. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel data-driven thermal response model based on the sum of exponentials approximation of the g-function. This method decomposes the thermal response into a local component that depends only on recent heat exchange and a historical component that can be computed recursively without storing the complete load sequence, thereby effectively reducing the computational burden and memory usage of long-term simulations. Theoretical analysis indicates that the temperature error introduced by this approximation method is strictly bounded by the error of the g-function sum of exponentials approximation, ensuring the model’s accuracy. Unlike existing non-history-dependent methods, the proposed method directly utilizes discrete g-function values obtained from numerical simulations or experiments to construct the sum of exponentials approximation, making it applicable to arbitrary wellfield layouts and complex boundary conditions. Numerical test results show that, compared to traditional load aggregation methods, the proposed method improves computational efficiency while increasing prediction accuracy by approximately two orders of magnitude.

title: In situ test of vertical ground source heat pump system for space heating in Tunisia: energetic, economic and environment assessment
abstract: This study presents the first field evaluation of a vertical ground source heat pump system for space heating in Tunisia. The experimental setup comprises a 50 m deep double U-tube vertical ground heat exchanger, a reversible ground source heat pump, and a radiant floor heating system. The results demonstrate that the ground heat pump achieves a peak coefficient of performance of 30 during start-up, which stabilizes at 17.53, while the overall system coefficient of performance averages 6.34, demonstrating substantially higher efficiency than conventional heating systems. Environmental assessment indicates a potential reduction of approximately 5.53 tCO2 emissions per dwelling per year compared with gas-based heating systems. Economic analysis further confirms significant energy savings and a favorable payback period, supporting the feasibility of vertical ground source heat pump deployment in semi-arid Mediterranean climates. The study also highlights the importance of borehole depth in maintaining thermal stability and system efficiency.

title: Comparing the sizing and costs of wind versus solar energy generation for a compressed hydrogen energy storage remote microgrid
abstract: Understanding the effects of renewable resource variation is critical to designing reliable and cost effective microgrid systems. Wind turbines and solar panels provide variable and intermittent generation of renewable energy due to the variable nature of the wind speed and solar irradiation. When combined with an energy storage approach such as hydrogen, a wind-hydrogen or solar-hydrogen microgrid system can be designed to reliably meet the energy demand of a remote installation. This study combines low‑order models of microgrid components to evaluate how different levels of renewable energy capacity relative to peak load affect system sizing and total cost. Representative wind speed and solar irradiance profiles over a one-week period are used along with load demand data from a naval base facility off the coast of southern California. Both the wind-hydrogen and solar-hydrogen configurations require the overbuilding of wind and solar power capacity relative to peak demand to achieve sustainability. The results indicate that for this location, the wind-hydrogen configuration can provide a cheaper sustainable solution compared to the solar-hydrogen configuration and to the current diesel-based energy infrastructure. Based on existing system economics and assumptions the model predicts the lowest upfront and long-term cost for a wind-hydrogen microgrid system is $8.94 million and 181.17 $/MWh respectively, compared to $10.94 million and 208.99 $/MWh for a solar-hydrogen microgrid system. This work provides important insight into the design and costs of wind and solar-based microgrids that can be applied at other locations.

title: Enhancing lipids deoxygenation for efficient sustainable fuel production over rapid Joule-heated MnFeCoNiCu/C catalysts
abstract: The production of sustainable biofuels via lipid deoxygenation relies heavily on efficient catalysts, but conventional tube-furnace calcination often leads to excessive metal grain growth and limited active sites, restricting catalytic performance. Herein, we report the synthesis of MnFeCoNiCu/C catalysts using a rapid Joule heating method to address these limitations, aiming to enhance lipid deoxygenation for efficient sustainable fuel production. Compared with the traditionally calcined catalyst (AC-900), the Joule -heated catalyst (AC-900 J) exhibits distinct structural advantages: smaller metal crystallites (23.31 nm vs. 41.91 nm), a higher specific surface area (1050 m2/g), and abundant moderate-strong basic sites, which are attributed to ultra-fast heating that suppresses grain growth and promotes uniform metal dispersion. Catalytic tests at 350 °C under atmospheric pressure H2 show that both catalysts achieve near-complete conversion of fatty acid methyl esters (FAME), while AC-900 J demonstrates superior bio-jet fuel selectivity (65.1% vs. 57.5% for AC-900). Its versatility is validated across diverse feedstocks (e.g., palmitic acid, oleic acid, soybean oil), maintaining 100% conversion and >94% hydrocarbon selectivity despite structural variations in substrates. Additionally, AC-900 J exhibits favorable cyclic stability, retaining 84.7% conversion and 49.2% bio-jet fuel selectivity after 4 cycles. This work highlights rapid Joule heating as a robust strategy to fabricate MnFeCoNiCu/C catalysts with tailored nanostructures, effectively enhancing lipid deoxygenation and enabling efficient production of sustainable biofuels.

title: Comparative analysis of biomass conversion routes for 2G bioethanol production process by two dehydration technologies in sugarcane biorefineries
authors: Mauro Antonio da Silva Sá Ravagnani
abstract: Lignocellulosic biomass is an abundant and sustainable feedstock for second-generation (2G) bioethanol production. This study evaluates bioethanol production from sugarcane bagasse at a processing capacity of 2.0 t/h. A comparative analysis of different fermentation modes and two dehydration technologies through process simulation in Aspen HYSYS V14 was considered. In the fermentation stage, simultaneous saccharification and fermentation (SSF) and simultaneous saccharification and co-fermentation (SScF) were implemented. For the dehydration process, extractive distillation (ED) and pressure-swing distillation (PSD) were evaluated. Co-fermentation of C5 and C6 sugars produced a higher ethanol concentration of 42.4 g/L. The lowest total energy consumption and lowest GHG emission factor were observed in the SScF-ED scenario, with values of 52,921 MJ/m3 of bioethanol and 0.28 CO2-eq/MJ of bioethanol, respectively. The economic assessment identified SScF coupled with extractive distillation (SScF-ED) as the most favorable configuration, with the following economic indicators: a net present value (NPV) of 1,302,440 US$, an internal rate of return (IRR) of 37.5%, and a payback period of 5.2 years.

title: Hydraulic disturbance characteristic of hybrid pumped storage hydropower under hydraulic short circuit mode
abstract: The hydraulic short circuit mode in hybrid pumped storage hydropower enables the simultaneous operation of generating and pumping units, offering advantages such as flexible overall input power regulation and rapid transitions between operating conditions. However, under this mode, pumping and generating flows coexist within the same hydraulic system, and the resulting circulating flow effect significantly intensifies hydraulic disturbances among units. The underlying mechanism is fundamentally distinct from that in conventional single-mode generation or pumping operations. To address this gap, a numerical simulation model of hydraulic disturbances under the hydraulic short circuit mode is established to elucidate the aforementioned mechanism. Both power and frequency regulation modes are considered to investigate the power response characteristics of the disturbed unit, and critical unfavorable operating conditions are identified for different water level combinations and initial operating power. Owing to the opposite flow directions between the generating and pumping sides in the hydraulic short circuit mode, the power response trend is completely reversed compared to that in conventional generation mode, with the maximum negative deviation increasing by approximately 25 %. Moreover, disturbances induced by the pumping unit are significantly stronger than those caused by the generating unit. The resulting high discharge variation rate substantially weakens governor performance, leading to power responses predominantly governed by the coupled effects of head and discharge. Finally, hydraulic disturbances are the most severe under the minimum head condition and low initial generating output power. Therefore, a lower limit on initial output is recommended to ensure operational safety.

title: Clean energy from algae: Tracing the sustainable biodiesel pathway through environmental impact, energy demand, and uncertainty assessment
abstract: Rising environmental concerns and reliance on fossil fuels make sustainable energy essential. Microalgae-based biodiesel is a promising option, but its environmental performance requires thorough evaluation. This study presents a comparative life cycle assessment of three harvesting and lipid recovery techniques: BD1 (hexane extraction), BD2 (dynamic cross-flow (DCF) microfiltration), and BD3 (flocculation/sedimentation with DCF), while maintaining a uniform downstream transesterification process across all cases. Using IPCC 2021, ReCiPe 2016, cumulative energy demand (CED), and water footprint, the study identifies clear differences in global warming potential (GWP), energy use, and resource efficiency driven solely by variations in harvesting and lipid recovery. Results show that BD2 has the highest GWP at 9.60 kg CO2 eq. and CED (130.5 MJ), due to fertilizer use and high electricity consumption throughout the production, and indicating significant fossil energy dependence. In contrast, BD3 had the lowest GWP (3.55 kg CO2 eq.), highest energy efficiency, and minimal toxicity and water use. BD3 also exhibited lower variability in environmental impacts, confirming its sustainable performance. The study shows that efficient harvesting and lipid recovery reduce environmental impacts and improve energy efficiency, stressing the need for optimal pathways to make biodiesel more sustainable.

title: Nickel availability governs autotrophic carbon distribution and methane selectivity in thermophilic hydrogenotrophic trickling biofilter reactors for renewable CO2-to-methane upgrading
abstract: Nickel is an essential trace metal for hydrogenotrophic methanogenesis, yet its role in regulating metabolic stability and carbon distribution under strictly autotrophic conditions remains unclear. This study investigated the impact of nickel concentration on thermophilic hydrogenotrophic methanation in two trickling biofilter reactors (TBRs) packed with Matala and MBBR carrier media. The reactors were operated with only CO2 and H2, allowing direct evaluation of trace–metal–controlled carbon flow without interference from organic substrates. Nickel deprivation caused delayed but significant inhibition of methane production without pH decline, indicating enzymatic limitation rather than acidification. Nitrogen profiles revealed suppressed microbial growth under nickel deficiency, while rapid recovery after nickel reintroduction suggested reversible metabolic inhibition. In addition to reduced methane yield, nickel imbalance led to increased soluble COD and volatile fatty acids (VFAs), suggesting altered carbon distribution behavior within the autotrophic system. Carbon recovery remained near unity under optimal conditions, suggesting internal carbon redistribution rather than substantial carbon loss. Although both reactors achieved high methane purity at appropriate nickel levels, under the operating conditions evaluated in this study, particularly at 1.36 mg/L, the Matala-packed system exhibited smoother transitions under deficiency and toxicity conditions than MBBR, which exhibited greater instability under 4.81 mg/L nickel conditions. These findings suggest that nickel availability plays an important role in influencing metabolic state, carbon distribution, and reactor stability in thermophilic autotrophic hydrogenotrophic TBR systems, highlighting the importance of trace metal management in biological biogas upgrading.

title: Effective path to realize the balanced development of China's regional economic growth and ecological environment in the construction of Ultra High Voltage project
abstract: The construction of Ultra High Voltage (UHV) project can promote regional economic growth, but the ecological environmental costs it brings have been ignored. To address this issue, this paper evaluates the impact of UHV project on the ecological environmental of counties, and evaluates effective paths to achieve balanced development between regional economic growth and ecological environment. The paper finds that although UHV project promote economic growth, they also significantly reduce the quality of local ecological environment. The main reasons for the decline of ecological environmental are the destruction of local forests and grasslands and the increase of rural land transfer. The increase of thermal power generation in power export zone is also an important reason for exacerbating the decline of ecological environmental. UHV project are faced with the realistic dilemma of economic growth and ecological environmental damage. Strengthening environmental regulation and paying attention to the layout of ecologically fragile areas are effective ways to achieve this. The research conclusion of this paper has important policy reference value for other countries and regions around the world to implement UHV engineering.

title: A smart energy systems planning framework for high-renewable transitions in emerging energy systems: Application to Ghana
abstract: This study addresses the challenge of planning high-renewable energy transitions in rapidly developing energy systems facing increasing energy demand, fossil-fuel dependence, structural constraints, and limited flexibility. To this end, it develops and applies an integrated planning framework grounded in the Smart Energy Systems concept to evaluate pathways towards high shares of renewable energy under realistic system constraints. Ghana is used as a representative case study to demonstrate the applicability of the proposed framework in a Sub-Saharan African context. The analysis combines the characterisation of the national energy system, assessment of renewable resource potential, analysis of socio-economic drivers, and construction of a validated reference model. Four baseline high-renewable scenarios and two cost-optimised scenarios were evaluated using cost minimisation subject to ε-constraint bounds on electricity imports and exports. This enabled the identification of feasible combinations of photovoltaic, wind, and hydropower generation, complemented by battery and flywheel storage, while maintaining realistic electricity exchange balances. The results show that the selected transition pathway can reduce carbon dioxide emissions by approximately a factor of three, decrease fuel consumption from 131.7 TWh to 75 TWh annually, increase the renewable share of electricity to 95%, and expand renewable generation from 7.7 TWh to 40.2 TWh per year. The findings provide practical insights for renewable integration, storage planning, regional electricity trade-offs, and low-carbon transition strategies in Sub-Saharan Africa and comparable contexts.

title: Quantifying off-design transfer-coefficient drift for regulation performance assessment and dispatch support in hydro–PV–wind hybrid energy systems
abstract: Hydropower units in wind- and solar-dominated grids are increasingly dispatched far from their best-efficiency point, yet how the small-signal governor transfer coefficients drift over the operating envelope, and how that drift affects regulation performance, remains unquantified across Francis machines of differing specific speed. This study analyses 69 off-design conditions on three medium-head Francis units (rated head 91–132 m, 12.0–20.6 MW) in one combined hydro, photovoltaic and wind network. For each condition the six transfer coefficients are evaluated from the unit hill chart, and a dimensionless off-design condition index (OCI) compresses their joint deviation into one scalar. Four results emerge. The coefficients drift widely—the torque-to-gate coefficient ey alone varies 2.2–4.1-fold within a unit—so the constant-coefficient assumption of conventional tuning is not supported. ey is the dominant predictor of the regulation time Ts; a pooled inverse-form model reaches an adjusted coefficient of determination of 0.71 with a fitted exponent of −0.92, consistent with Ts ∝ 1/ey. The speed overshoot σ is a machine-type signature, confined to a narrow within-unit band yet differing significantly between units (one-way analysis of variance F = 65.5) and governed by mechanical inertia. A three-tier envelope based on the index flags the high-head unit as the only one with a non-negligible high-risk area. Twenty-four grid-connected field step-change records provide directional support rather than independent validation. The framework offers a plant-calibrated dispatch rule and an operating-point-independent monitoring trigger.

title: Liquid air energy storage with high-grade molten salt heat recovery for enhanced round trip efficiency
abstract: The thermodynamic performance of standalone liquid air energy storage (LAES) is strongly governed by the temperature grade and utilization pathway of recovered compression heat. Conventional heat recovery media restrict the reheating temperature of the working air during discharge, limiting the round trip efficiency of many reported standalone systems to approximately 50%. To overcome this constraint, this study develops a novel standalone LAES system with high-grade molten salt heat recovery (termed as HH-LAES). A series-coupled absorption chiller is applied to utilize excess compression heat to provide deep precooling of the compressed air, thereby improving overall heat utilization. Results indicate that compared to conventional water and thermal oil, molten salt offers a significantly higher heat storage density of 639 MJ/m3. The round trip efficiency of the LAES is increased to 62.9%. Effective exergy management of the molten salt loop limits excess compression heat to only 4.3% of the total compression heat. This study contributes to the advancement of high-temperature heat storage solutions for LAES systems and promotes a broader development of LAES in the context of carbon neutrality.

title: High−performance silica nanosheet/carbon black supported platinum catalyst in high−temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells
abstract: Current catalysts for high-temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells (HT-PEMFCs) are challenged by limited three−phase boundaries and electrochemical active surface area (ECSA). In response, hybrid silica nanosheet (SN) and carbon black (CB) supported Pt catalysts were synthesized. To enhance the electrical conductivity of the SN, the surface was coated with zeolitic imidazolate framework−8 and then carbonized to prepare carbon coated SN (CSN). The hybrid catalyst with a SN: CB weight ratio of 2:3 (Pt/SN2−CB3) retained around 95% of the ECSA even after 18000 cycles of accelerated stress test. Furthermore, Pt/CSN2−CB3 showed a superior peak power density of 320 mW cm−2, compared with 283 mW cm−2 for Pt/SN2−CB3 and 237 mW cm−2 for Pt supported on CB (Pt/CB). Benefiting from their hydrophilicity and surface hydroxyl groups, SN and CSN could retain phosphoric acid (PA), thereby decreasing the PA absorption on catalyst surface, evidenced by improved ECSA and performance. Techno-economic analyses suggest a ∼30% reduction in cell production cost using the hybrid catalysts compared to bare CB case. This work demonstrates that the scalable, low-cost, and recyclable Pt/CSN2−CB3 catalyst can enhance HT-PEMFC performance and accelerate the integration of hydrogen fuel cells into renewable energy systems.
keywords: High−temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cell

title: The impact of energy security on green technology innovation efficiency: Importance of ecological innovation in facilitating renewable energy transition in MENA countries
abstract: Green technology innovation efficiency (GTIE) serves as a critical metric for evaluating the capacity of innovation systems which simultaneously delivers economic, technological, and environmental benefits. Despite growing recognition of the roles played by energy security (ES), ecological innovation (EIN), and renewable energy transition (RET), their integrated impact on GTIE remains underexplored particularly within Middle East and North Africa (MENA). This study fills this gap by examining the joint influence of ES, EIN, and RET on GTIE across 14 MENA countries during 2000–2023. A comprehensive multi-dimensional analytical framework comprising the novel super-efficiency ray slack-based measure (SR-SBM) model and the method of moments quantile regression (MMQR) approach is applied. The SR-SBM findings reveal that GTIE in the region is relatively low, with most inefficient countries requiring at least 61.5% improvement to reach the efficiency frontier. Considerable disparities are observed, with Israel exhibiting the highest efficiency and Iraq the lowest. The MMQR result indicates that while ES negatively influences GTIE in less efficient countries, EIN and RET exert a consistently positive effect across the distribution. These insights underscore the importance of prioritizing ecological innovation and accelerating renewable energy transition, even in energy-secure context, as essential strategies for enhancing GTIE in MENA region.

title: Fabrication and performance study of semi-transparent perovskite solar cells for photovoltaic windows
abstract: To accelerate energy-saving and carbon-reduction efforts in the building sector, semi-transparent perovskite photovoltaic windows, which combine power generation with indoor light and heat regulation, have emerged as a highly promising solution for building-integrated photovoltaics. However, most existing studies focus on the fabrication and optimization of small-area (<1 cm2) devices under standard laboratory conditions, while a systematic evaluation of their integrated “optical-thermal-electrical” characteristics under real and dynamic environments remains lacking. In this study, 15 cm2 series-connected semi-transparent perovskite solar cells are successfully fabricated. Under standard test conditions, these devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 3.57%, an average visible transmittance of 38.4%, and a color rendering index as high as 94. Indoor comparative experiments reveal that the devices in the “photoelectric mode” can achieve an average active-cooling effect of 1.81 °C compared to the “photothermal mode.” Further outdoor tests using a multi-tilt-angle platform (0°, 30°, 60°, 90°) show that the device at 30° tilt yielded the highest daily cumulative energy generation, reaching 1.211 MJ/m2. Performance analysis indicated that outdoor operation can be divided into two characteristic phases: a “normal stage” dominated by temperature-induced degradation, where the efficiency exhibits a negative true temperature coefficient; and a “degradation stage” where light-induced degradation occurs, leading to a positive true temperature coefficient. Moreover, during the “normal stage” under diffuse-light-dominant conditions, the power conversion efficiency of the devices generally exceeds standard test values. This study provides important experimental evidence for the fabrication, performance evaluation, and optimization of semi-transparent perovskite photovoltaic windows for practical building applications.

title: Valorization and bioconversion of food waste and post-hydrolyzed food waste via black soldier fly larvae for lipid-based biodiesel production in a circular economy
abstract: This study proposes a novel valorization pathway for post-hydrolyzed food waste (PHFW) via black soldier fly larvae (BSFL) bioconversion and evaluates its suitability as a feedstock for BSFL lipid-based biodiesel production compared with untreated food waste (FW). Three feed types were prepared: (1) FW (−), untreated FW mixed with rice bran (RB) as the control; (2) FW (+), FW (−) with pH adjustment using CaCO3; and (3) PHFW (+), PHFW mixed with RB and pH-adjusted using CaCO3. FW (+) achieved the highest larval performance, with a waste reduction rate of 66.41%, bioconversion efficiency of 31.43%, waste reduction index of 3.89, and feed conversion rate of 2.83, while FW (−) showed the highest lipid yield (39.33%). PHFW (+) exhibited the shortest development time (20.17 days) and the highest biodiesel yield (69.34%), producing biodiesel with an acid number of 0.40 mg KOH/g and a calorific value of 38.54 MJ/kg. Normalized biodiesel production reached 23.83 kg/ton PHFW (+), presenting a preliminary demonstration of biodiesel production potential. Its defatted larval meal also contained 38.27% protein, highlighting the additional value beyond biodiesel production. These findings highlight the potential of PHFW valorization via BSFL bioconversion within a circular economy framework for sustainable resource recovery and biodiesel production.

title: Cooperative wake steering for wind farm power enhancement under dynamic inflow conditions: An entropy-regularized multi-agent reinforcement learning approach
abstract: Wake interactions among wind turbines can significantly reduce wind farm energy production under dynamically varying inflow conditions. To improve wind farm power generation while mitigating wake-induced losses, this study develops a cooperative yaw-control framework for active wake steering under steady and time-varying wind conditions. The framework is based on a multi-agent reinforcement learning approach, enabling coordinated yaw-angle regulation among multiple turbines while accounting for wake interactions and changing inflow conditions. Simulation studies were conducted with a reduced-order wind farm flow model across steady and dynamic wind scenarios. The proposed strategy was compared with conventional greedy control, differential evolution optimization, and deep deterministic policy gradient control. The results demonstrate faster convergence, improved power generation, and more stable yaw-control behavior. Under dynamically varying wind conditions, the strategy effectively mitigates wake effects and achieves improved power performance with stable yaw control. Across multiple dynamic wind scenarios, it achieves an average power improvement of approximately 8.6% relative to greedy control and generally outperforms the comparison methods. Reduced cumulative yaw activity further indicates improved control smoothness and lower actuator utilization. A separate held-out generalization evaluation using stochastic wind episodes shows that the learned policy maintains robust performance on previously unseen wind realizations within the predefined scenario ranges. These results demonstrate the potential of cooperative wake steering to enhance wind farm energy capture and provide a promising framework for dynamic wind farm control.

title: Development of a system-efficiency-oriented offshore wind-hydrogen regulation framework for urban grid reliability
abstract: This paper develops an integrated wind-hydrogen regulation framework to effectively regulate urban power grid load using offshore wind energy, thereby improving grid reliability. To mitigate fluctuations in offshore wind power, this framework proposes a dual-path system model with hydrogen energy storage to enhance the system's wind power absorption capacity and regulation flexibility. Simultaneously, the framework also includes system capacity configuration optimization, aiming to find the optimal configuration using multi-objective mixed-integer linear programming (MOMILP) to maximize system efficiency. The framework is validated using real-world data from Hong Kong (2022). Results reveal distinct operational characteristics: under full-time regulation, the system achieves 95.4% system efficiency with minimal wind curtailment (0.7%); conversely, in peak-shaving mode, it prioritizes load satisfaction (32 GWh) but requires significantly higher capacity (197 GW) and results in lower efficiency (45.5%). Sensitivity analysis further highlights the dominance of conversion efficiency in peak-shaving scenarios. This work provides a critical technical reference for integrating offshore wind energy into the energy system and combining it with pure hydrogen energy storage to regulate urban power grid load and improve the overall reliability of the system.

title: Integrated solid oxide fuel cell–gas turbine and compressed air energy storage for multigeneration and renewable power stabilization with efficient waste heat recovery: Comprehensive 4E analysis and optimization
abstract: In this study, an integrated system is developed in which a topping solid oxide fuel cell–gas turbine is coupled with a compressed air energy storage system via a heat recovery exchanger. The compressed air energy storage is integrated as an energy storage technology for stabilizing intermittent renewable power and improving operational flexibility. The continuous power output of gas turbine 1 is supplied to a proton exchange membrane electrolyzer for hydrogen production. During compressed air energy storage charging, waste heat from the compressor stages is recovered to drive an absorption chiller for cooling. In addition, residual heat from the solid oxide fuel cell–gas turbine 1 subsystem and from the compressed air energy storage discharge in gas turbine 2 is recovered using a thermoelectric generator and a domestic hot water heat exchanger, respectively. During discharge, the combined power output of gas turbine 2 and the thermoelectric generator is used to operate a reverse osmosis desalination unit for freshwater production. Accordingly, the system operates as an integrated multigeneration configuration with enhanced waste heat recovery from both solid oxide fuel cell and compressed air energy storage subsystems. In the base case, intermittent renewable power supplied to the compressed air energy storage system of 51.7 kW is stored during the charging process and later recovered during discharge, producing 54.24 kW of power through gas turbine 2 and the thermoelectric generator for freshwater production of 3.167 kg/s. In addition, waste heat recovery during charging and discharging provides cooling of 8.89 kW and heating of 47.42 kW, respectively. Under full-time operation, gas turbine 1 output is used in the proton exchange membrane electrolyzer to produce hydrogen at a rate of 3.78 kg/h. A parametric study and multi-objective optimization are performed to evaluate energy, exergoeconomic, and environmental performance. The optimized results show a maximum exergy round-trip efficiency of 53.85%, a total cost rate of 134.53 $/h, and a unit product cost of 53.93 $/GJ. The system is finally compared with existing solid oxide fuel cell–compressed air energy storage configurations, demonstrating improved performance and multi-generation capability.

title: Efficient photothermal conversion of biomass lipids into sustainable diesel fuel enabled over a PdPtRuCuNi/TiO2 high-entropy alloy catalyst
abstract: Renewable diesel derived from biomass offers a sustainable alternative to conventional fossil fuels, yet its efficient production under mild conditions remains challenging. Herein, we report a PdPtRuCuNi high-entropy alloy/TiO2 catalyst synthesized via a facile one-pot solvothermal method for the photothermal decarboxylation of biomass-derived oils and fatty acids into diesel-range alkanes. Structural characterizations confirm the successful formation and uniform dispersion of multicomponent HEA particles on TiO2. The integration of PdPtRuCuNi alloy sites with oxygen-vacancy-rich TiO2 creates a cooperative metal–oxide interface that promotes light-induced charge separation, accelerates interfacial electron transfer, and suppresses carrier recombination. Meanwhile, the HEA/TiO2 interface facilitates H2 activation, hydrogen spillover, and the adsorption/activation of oxygenated intermediates, thereby enhancing the decarboxylation pathway under mild photothermal conditions. As a result, the catalyst achieves complete conversion of oleic acid with 98.8% selectivity toward renewable diesel-range alkanes at 100 °C and 0.4 MPa H2 within 3.5 h. Moreover, it retains 91.2% selectivity toward C15-C17 alkanes after ten consecutive cycles, demonstrating excellent stability. This work establishes a high-entropy-alloy/oxide interfacial strategy for efficient photothermal biomass upgrading to renewable fuels.

title: Derivation and validation of time-averaged and fluctuating integrated wake model for wind turbine considering blade rotation and wake's ground contact
abstract: To address the limitations of existing analytical wake models for wind turbines, including the neglect of rotation-induced turbulence asymmetry, wake's ground contact effect, turbulent fluctuation characterization, and fixed wake expansion coefficients, this paper establishes a blade rotation and ground contact corrected turbulence intensity model based on a double Gaussian turbulence intensity model. By adopting the modified Kaimal spectrum and frequency-domain synthesis, an integrated time-averaged and fluctuating wake model is constructed, together with a dynamic wake width model adaptively correlated with turbulence intensity. Validated against wind tunnel data, large eddy simulation data, unmanned aerial vehicles field measurement data, and Horns Rev offshore wind farm data, the proposed model accurately captures asymmetric turbulence intensity distribution in the near wake and turbulence variation near the ground. The predicted velocity profiles and wake width agree well with measurements. For horizontal wake velocity profiles, the overall root mean square error is 3.38%, while for vertical profiles is 5.59%. The wake width relative errors are consistently confined within 8% across all validated cases. Additionally, the time-averaged and fluctuating integrated analytical model achieves reliable fatigue load predictions, with its normalized blade root bending moment DEL aligning well with FAST.Farm benchmark results. Furthermore, the model exhibits improved power prediction accuracy compared to other analytical models in the Horns Rev validation, highlighting its utility for wind farm layout design, micro-siting and fatigue analysis.

title: Multi-energy liquid air energy storage powered by geothermal energy from an abandoned exploitation well – A techno-economic analysis
abstract: Liquid air energy storage is a promising thermo-mechanical electricity storage technology that can simultaneously deliver different energy streams, such as electricity, cooling, and heating. Yet, when operated in multi-energy mode, its commercial deployment remains constrained by limited round-trip efficiency and weak economic performance. This study proposes and techno-economically evaluates a novel integrated multi-energy LAES system coupled with 1) the low-grade geothermal heat from abandoned exploitation wells during discharging and 2) different industrial energy valorization pathways, including direct waste heat utilization during the dehydrogenation of liquid organic hydrogen carriers, organic Rankine cycle, absorption chiller and clean dry air supply. The results show that bidirectional heat recovery and multi-output operation significantly enhance system performance. While stand-alone LAES remains economically unfeasible under all electricity tariff scenarios, exhibiting high LCOS of 0.97 USD/kWhe and no viable discounted pay-back period, integrated configurations achieve LCOS values below 0.15 USD/kWhe and a discounted pay-back period of 13.7 years. Among the investigated options, the configuration integrating direct waste heat utilization and clean dry air demonstrates the highest robustness to electricity price uncertainty. Furthermore, exploiting the horizontal extension of abandoned wells enables zero-emission geothermal heat recovery, offering a viable pathway for both well revitalization and electrical energy storage utilization.

title: An experimental investigation on cooling performance of a nanofluid-based radiant cooling system
abstract: Enhancing the heat transfer efficiency of fluid-based radiative cooling systems is of great significance for the application of radiative sky cooling (RSC) technology in building energy conservation. To address the limitation of low heat transfer coefficients of conventional heat transfer fluids in fluid-based radiative cooling systems, this study proposes a novel and high-efficiency nanofluid-based radiative cooling panel by employing nanofluid as the heat transfer medium. A controlled experimental method was adopted to investigate the energy generation characteristics of proposed nanofluid-based radiative cooling panels (NRCP). The study identifies the response mechanisms and sensitivities of cooling performance for NRCP to nanofluid properties, operating conditions, and the incorporation of phase change materials (PCM). Results indicate that cooling performance of NRCP is superior to that of water-based radiative cooling panels (WRCP). Among various nanofluids, aluminium oxide-water (Al2O3-H2O) nanofluid exhibits the optimal heat transfer performance and is thus identified as the preferred working fluid for enhancing cooling performance of fluid-based radiative cooling systems. Furthermore, for Al2O3-H2O nanofluid, working conditions featuring smaller particle sizes (20 nm), higher volume concentrations (1.0 vol%), higher flow velocities (1.2 m/s), and higher inlet temperatures (40°C) contribute to an increased cooling power of NRCP. In addition, this study analyzes the energy-saving performance and application potential of both energy-storage and non-energy-storage types of fluid-based radiative cooling panels. The results demonstrate that proposed NRCP not only enhances cooling efficiency but also exhibits a strong power-saving capability and a short payback period. This research provides a theoretical basis for optimizing the design of fluid-based radiative cooling systems.

title: Energy loss mechanisms and hydraulic interference during pump-trip transients in one-penstock–two-unit pumped-storage plants
abstract: Hydraulic interference in one-penstock multi-unit pumped-storage systems during transient processes is not well understood, particularly when a normally operating unit is subjected to the pump trip of an adjacent unit. This study examines a one-penstock-two-unit pumped-storage power station using a coupled one-dimensional–three-dimensional (1D–3D) numerical framework. According to the external characteristic evolution of the tripped unit, the transient process is identified as successive transitions from pump mode to pump-braking mode and then to turbine mode. The results show that the pump trip of Unit 1# causes significant hydraulic interference in Unit 2# through the shared penstock, resulting in multiple rise–fall stages in total energy loss and an opposite variation in hydraulic efficiency. Clear phase differences are observed among the runner, double-cascade passages, and spiral casing, indicating asynchronous responses of different flow domains to the same transient excitation. Further analysis shows that the energy-loss evolution of Unit 2# is primarily determined by shear-related dissipation and mean kinetic-energy redistribution. The first rise–fall stage is dominated by flow evolution in the runner, whereas the second stage is primarily associated with increased flow separation in the guide- and stay-vane passages. These findings improve the understanding of transient hydraulic interference in one-penstock multi-unit pumped-storage systems and support transient safety assessment and coordinated operation.

title: Enhancing jet fuel production from catalytic co-pyrolysis of biomass and low-density polyethylene over sulfonated activated carbon catalysts
abstract: To mitigate climate change, developing bio-jet fuel represents a promising strategy. This study evaluates sulfonated activated carbon (SAC) catalysts in the co-pyrolysis of poplar sawdust (PS) and low-density polyethylene (LDPE) for bio-jet fuel production. We systematically investigated the effects of sulfonation temperature, acid-to-carbon ratio, and feedstock mixing ratio on catalyst performance and product distribution. The SAC catalysts were characterized by XRD, BET, SEM, FT-IR, and XPS. The results show that SAC catalysts possess high specific surface area, well-developed microporosity, and abundant strong acid sites, which collectively enhance both the yield and quality of bio-jet fuel. Detailed analysis of pyrolysis gases and bio-oil composition further reveals that SAC catalysts markedly improve the selectivity toward C8–C16 aromatics and alkanes. At an LDPE/PS ratio of 2, the 150-SAC-120 catalyst achieved the highest bio-jet fuel yield of 80.04%. Overall, SAC catalysts demonstrate excellent catalytic activity, high stability, low cost, and abundant protonic acid sites in biomass–plastic co-pyrolysis. This work not only provides technical insights for bio-jet fuel production but also offers guidance for future catalyst optimization and mechanistic studies.

title: Effect of carbon-based and mineral additives on biogas production yield and microbial distribution during anaerobic digestion of banana agro-wastes
abstract: In this study, granular-activated carbon (GAC) in two mesh sizes (4×8 and 8×20), powdered-activated carbon (PAC), and natural mordenite-type zeolite (MZ) were tested as additives during the mesophilic anaerobic digestion of banana peel and pulp agro-wastes. Automated biomethane potential assays, kinetic modeling, and 16S rRNA sequencing were performed to evaluate the impact of the additives on biogas production and microbial community structure. Results showed that MZ and GAC_4×8 enhanced the biogas yield by 25% for banana pulp, reaching 669.5 and 662.3 mL gTVS−1, respectively. For banana peel, maximum yields of 541.4 and 540.2 mL gTVS−1 were achieved with MZ and GAC_4×8, representing an increase of 16% over the control reactor. PAC and GAC_8×20 did not result in significant improvements. The highest biogas production rates were observed with GAC_4×8, reaching 54.4 mL gTVS−1·h−1 for pulp and 60.9 mL gTVS−1·h−1 for peel. Microbial analysis revealed a core fermentative phylum composition for all reactors, particularly Proteobacteria, Chloroflexi, and Euryarchaeota. MZ promoted the relative abundance of hydrogenotrophic methanogens (Methanothermobacter, Methanospirilum) and amino acid-degrading bacteria (Syntrophorhabdus). GAC_4×8 selectively enriched direct interspecies electron transfer (DIET) related taxa such as Methanothrix and Syntrophomonas. These results highlight the relevance of additive type in enhancing the efficiency of anaerobic digestion for agricultural waste.

title: Experimental and numerical study on a Darrieus vertical-axis wind turbine with a wind-concentrating and speed-accelerating device
abstract: To address the poor self-starting capability and low efficiency of Darrieus vertical-axis wind turbines at low wind speeds, this study designs an H-type Darrieus turbine integrated with a wind-concentrating and speed-accelerating device. Its aerodynamic and self-starting performance are systematically investigated through wind tunnel experiments and three-dimensional unsteady CFD simulations. Using a scaled model, parametric analyses are conducted under varying blade chord lengths, blade numbers, and inflow velocities to compare performance with and without the device. Results show that the device significantly improves the rotor inflow, increases blade windward velocity, enhances energy capture, and shifts the optimal tip-speed ratio to higher values. For two blades with a chord of 0.0516 m at 6.4 m/s, the raw peak power coefficient reaches 0.406, representing an increase of approximately 180 % over the baseline. After tunnel blockage correction using a Maskell-type method, the corrected peak Cp becomes 0.237, still approximately 120 % higher than the baseline. The device benefits low-solidity conditions more. Moderately increasing blade number or chord improves self-starting, whereas excessive solidity reduces efficiency due to wake interference. Numerical simulations further reveal that the device widens the operating range via Venturi acceleration, mitigating downwind wake shielding and dynamic stall, thereby enhancing cycle-averaged torque. This wind-concentrating design effectively improves Darrieus turbine performance in low-wind environments, providing guidance for optimal design and engineering application of distributed wind energy systems.

title: Mechanism-driven CFD simulation and experimental validation of natural soiling on BIPV façades
abstract: Building-integrated photovoltaic (BIPV) façade systems are vulnerable to natural soiling in urban atmospheres, which reduces transmitted irradiance and causes power losses under non-uniform shading. Existing soiling studies predominantly address rooftop or low-tilt PV, while mechanistic boundary-layer formulations that capture the detailed competition of forces on vertical surfaces remain underexplored. This study presents an integrated evaluation framework that couples micro-mechanistic deposition tracking, CFD simulation, indoor calibration, and multi-weather-field validation. A façade-specific boundary correction that accounts for aerodynamic wind shear and gravity-driven rolling-off is implemented in ANSYS Fluent via user-defined functions, combined with the SST k-σ turbulence model and a discrete phase scheme. Simulations reveal a stepwise, discretely triggered accumulation process: deposition increments occur in only 7.83% of time steps, whereas ∼92% exhibit zero increment; the times to reach 10%, 50%, and 90% of cumulative deposition are 197.8 s, 861.1 s, and 1499.7 s, respectively. To link deposition to power loss for engineering use, indoor calibration experiments establish an attenuation database across irradiance and areal dust mass density, demonstrating diminishing marginal losses at medium-to-high soiling (average reduction increases from 45.09% to 47.34% over 20–60 g/0.72 m2). Transient field validation across contrasting weather scenarios (Sunny, Dry-Windy, and Stagnant-Breeze) demonstrates strong chronological alignment, with a mean relative error of 9.21% against empirical cumulative mass measurements. The developed framework provides a reliable alternative for predicting vertical surface soiling boundaries and correcting associated power degradation, supporting cleaning schedules and yield-loss attribution in urban microclimates.

title: Influence of maldistribution match on thermal performance of printed circuit type recuperator in CSP plants considering fin conduction and heat capacity ratio
abstract: Printed circuit heat exchangers (PCHEs) are widely used in concentrated solar power plants because of their compactness, high-temperature and high-pressure tolerance, and corrosion resistance. However, manifold-induced pressure gradients can cause flow maldistribution in the core, making accurate prediction of the associated performance deterioration essential for PCHEs design and safe operation. This study numerically investigates the influence of maldistribution match on thermal performance of PCHEs, with particular attention to fin conduction and heat capacity ratio. Four inlet configurations and three fluid pairs with heat capacity ratios of 0.5, 0.8, and 1.0 were considered. Results show that the effect of inlet configuration on effectiveness depends on the degree of maldistribution match on two streams. Relative to uniform flow, well-matched configurations nearly eliminate maldistribution-induced degradation, with a deviation of only about 0.08%, whereas poorly matched configurations reduce effectiveness by up to 17.9%. Fin conduction improves temperature uniformity and overall effectiveness under both uniform and maldistributed conditions, but only marginally alters the effect of maldistribution matching. Moreover, the impact of maldistribution matching is insensitive to heat capacity ratio under well-matched conditions, while the effectiveness variation reaches 54.4% for poorly matched configurations as the heat capacity ratio decreases from 1.0 to 0.5. A simplified method incorporating flow maldistribution is finally proposed for predicting PCHE thermal effectiveness. These findings provide practical guidance for manifold configuration, flow-distribution matching, and system-level performance assessment of PCHEs in concentrated solar power applications.

title: Ground topology as a driver of solar chimney power plant performance: integrated thermo-fluid-dynamics and strategic geometry optimization
abstract: We numerically investigate the thermo-fluid-dynamics of a small-scale (chimney height = 3m, collector diameter = 3m) solar-chimney-power-plant (SCPP). To enhance the typically low performance of a conventional SCPP, we propose an innovative ground-topology for the collector, featuring polygonal protrusions. We vary the side count, height, and width of the protruded elements, and offer an optimal absorber shape to maximize collector performance. We divide the investigation strategically into two stages. First, we optimize the geometry of an axisymmetric reduced model, and then, we perform full 3D simulations to address discontinuous protrusions. As the discontinuous protrusions are fabricated, the azimuthal spacing (ϕ) between two consecutive discrete elements is also optimized. We obtain the best values of the overall performance parameter (η) for square elements with a height of 0.01m and ϕ=4˚. The seasonal variation analysis with discontinuous protrusions indicates that although the optimal ground-modified collector achieves its maximum performance in summer (η= 35.5%), it also maintains stable and consistent performance throughout the year. In contrast to the base configuration featuring a flat collector ground without protrusions, the optimal configuration achieves a maximum performance enhancement of 35%, observed during summer. The study highlights the impact of the complex 3D-structure of vorticity iso-surfaces, which is attributed to an additional tangential velocity, resulting in notable performance enhancements.

title: Experimental validation and performance analysis of an LNG integrated liquid air energy storage system with air purification
abstract: Integrating liquefied natural gas cold energy with liquid air energy storage offers a large-scale energy storage solution. However, models neglecting industrial constraints may overestimate performance. Specifically, the air purification unit imposes an energy penalty, and high-pressure liquefied natural gas supply temperatures of −145 °C to −135 °C lead to a thermodynamic mismatch. To address these challenges, a liquefied natural gas-integrated liquid air energy storage system with air purification is proposed and validated on a 50 kW full-process experimental platform. Experimental results indicate that a regeneration flow ratio of 0.2 enables effective air purification regeneration. Using the experimentally validated model, the 10 MW analysis shows that expanded-air regeneration reduces regeneration energy consumption by 65.0% and increases round-trip efficiency by 7.1 percentage points compared with electric heating. Under fluctuating liquefied natural gas temperatures, coordinated adjustment of the air split ratio maintains round-trip efficiency between 65.0% and 66.4%. Under optimal conditions, the system achieves an exergy efficiency of 57.1%, and an equilibrium energy factor of 0.2 indicates favorable peak-shaving capability. Economic projections show a static payback period of 7.8 years at a 4.5:1 peak-to-valley price ratio. This work supports the integration of liquid air energy storage with liquefied natural gas terminals.

title: Energy and exergy analysis of geothermal–ORC hybrid trigeneration system with a self-superheater using low-GWP working fluids
abstract: A single-flash geothermal and organic Rankine cycle (ORC) trigeneration system equipped with a self-superheater (SSH) is proposed. Under identical geothermal resource and operating conditions, four configurations, with and without the self-superheater using R245fa and the low-global-warming-potential fluid R1233zd(E), are compared through energy and exergy analyses. The results show that R1233zd(E) consistently outperforms R245fa, increasing the Energy Utilization Factor from 0.6137 to 0.6209 and the exergy efficiency from 0.6231 to 0.6449 in the basic configuration. With the self-superheater, the corresponding values are 0.6161 and 0.6472, respectively. The self-superheater also increases the net power output from 9460 to 9514 kW for R245fa and from 9836 to 9895 kW for R1233zd(E), while the cooling load increases from 3806 to 3855 kW and from 3850 to 3900 kW, respectively. These improvements are accompanied by a slight reduction in heating exergy from 1229 to 1207 kW for both working fluids. Among the two investigated dry working fluids, the R1233zd(E) configuration with the self-superheater achieves the best performance, with a net power output of 9895 kW, a cooling load of 3900 kW, and an exergy efficiency of 0.6472.

title: Integrated binary geothermal–LNG cold energy recovery multigeneration system for urban energy applications
abstract: The increasing demand for low-carbon energy solutions in the building sector has intensified interest in geothermal-based polygeneration systems capable of delivering multiple energy services from a single renewable source. This study proposes an advanced geothermal-driven polygeneration configuration integrating a Kalina cycle, a transcritical CO2 Rankine cycle, an organic Rankine cycle, liquefied natural gas cold energy recovery, multi-stage flash desalination, and a proton exchange membrane electrolyzer. The system is modeled in Engineering Equation Solver and evaluated through comprehensive energy, exergy, economic, and environmental analyses. A parametric investigation is conducted by varying the geothermal inlet temperature between 180 °C and 240 °C, and a multi-objective optimization approach is applied to examine trade-offs among thermodynamic performance, irreversibility, and cost. Under base operating conditions, the system produces 1966 kW of net power, 5818 kW of district heating, 10.55 m3/h of freshwater, and 2.727 kg/h of hydrogen, achieving overall energy and exergy efficiencies of 68.22% and 39.32%, respectively. Exergy analysis reveals that major irreversibilities originate from condensation processes and heat transfer interactions, highlighting the importance of thermal matching within the heat exchanger network. Increasing geothermal temperature enhances useful outputs while reducing the levelized cost of electricity and water, whereas the levelized cost of hydrogen shows only a slight increase due to electrolysis-related costs. The proposed system demonstrates strong potential as a flexible geothermal energy hub for building and district-scale applications requiring simultaneous electricity, heating, and freshwater production.

title: Kinetic and metagenomic exploration of uncoupling hydrolysis and methanogenesis in an enriched cellulose-degrading anaerobic digestion community
abstract: Cellulose degradation is the main limitation in biogas production from anaerobic digestion of lignocellulosic biomass. To improve this, a microbial consortium was developed by enriching an inoculum from a goat manure-fed biogas plant in consecutive 14-day batch cycles. Using a carbon-balance approach, the 37th enrichment cycle achieved over 90% of the estimated potential cellulose conversion within 6 days, a significant increase from 59% in the initial cycle. A gene-centric metagenomic analysis revealed that the microbial community shifted towards specialization, with endocellulase genes and carbohydrate-binding modules increasing 1.6- and 1.7-fold from the initial cycle, respectively. Reconstruction of 85 Metagenome-Assembled Genomes detailed the complete metabolic pathway from cellulose to methane. This analysis identified a core cellulolytic group reliant on secreted enzymes across dominant phyla like Fibrobacterota, Chloroflexota, Planctomycetota, and Spirochaetota. These effective cellulose degraders, such as Fibrobacter and the families Paludibacteraceae and Anaerobacaceae, accounted for 17.8% relative abundance. Although the enrichment process created a metabolic bottleneck where rapid volatile fatty acids production inhibited methanogenesis, this consortium holds high potential for bioaugmentation. Ultimately, this study highlights the highly efficient microbial community capable of rapid cellulose degradation, providing the essential genomic profile to optimize future lignocellulosic anaerobic digestion systems.

title: Synergistic effects of “Frog Skeleton” and cross-spiral flow fields designs on PEMFC performance
abstract: Effective water management is essential for improving the performance, durability, and efficiency of Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (PEMFC), which play a key role in hydrogen-based renewable energy systems. The design of the bipolar plate flow field plays a key role in regulating water distribution while ensuring adequate membrane hydration. In this study, two novel flow field geometries are proposed and numerically analyzed: the Frog Skeleton Flow Field (FSFF) and the Cross-Spiral Flow Field (CSFF). Both configurations employ an eight-channel serpentine design to improve gas distribution and enhanced water distribution. This work introduces a hybrid flow field strategy that combines different geometries at the anode and cathode, providing a novel design framework to exploit synergistic effects between flow orientation and channel architecture. The results show that the proposed flow fields enhanced hydration distribution by up to 18% and improve average current density by approximately 37% (achieving a uniformity index value of up to 0.93), leading to enhanced electrochemical performance and power density. These improvements contribute to more stable PEMFC operation and higher efficiency, reinforcing the role of advanced flow field design in supporting hydrogen-based renewable energy conversion systems.

title: Analysis of a building-integrated solar-driven multi-effect distillation system for Canadian Indigenous community applications
abstract: Many of Canada’s Indigenous populations depend on bottled water due to long-term drinking water advisories in their communities. Solar-powered multi-effect distillation has been demonstrated to be a sustainable solution for producing clean water for domestic use. However, there is a lack of research regarding its suitability for small-scale plants in northern climates. In this study, a building-integrated solar multi-effect distillation system is designed to meet the freshwater demand of a multi-unit residential building in a remote Indigenous community in Canada. Annual simulations carried out in TRNSYS assess the technical and economic performance using two types of solar thermal collectors: flat plate and evacuated tube. Simulations show that using a solar multi-effect distillation system with evacuated tube collectors can meet or exceed the water demand of a multi-unit residential building located in communities at or below a latitude of 59 degrees north in a cost-effective manner relative to current drinking water delivery options.

title: Wind-solar complementary hydrogen production strategy based on coordinated ratio and rotation optimization of heterogeneous electrolyzers
abstract: Power fluctuations in off-grid wind-solar-storage hydrogen production systems trigger unstable electrolyzer operation, frequent equipment start-stop cycles, and accelerated equipment performance degradation. To enhance the operational stability and durability of the system, this paper proposes a coordinated strategy combining capacity ratio optimization and rotational dispatching for arrays of alkaline electrolyzers (ALK) and proton exchange membrane electrolyzers (PEM). The cold-start sensitivity inherent to alkaline electrolyzers is fully integrated into system capacity allocation and global operational dispatching processes. First, a convolutional neural network-bidirectional long short-term memory (CNN-BiLSTM) model is constructed to conduct classified prediction of wind and solar power, delivering time-interval prior information to support electrolyzer dispatching. Afterwards, an optimization framework based on K-means-genetic algorithm (K-Means-GA) is developed. With comprehensive consideration of investment costs and start-stop losses, the optimal capacity ratio between ALK and PEM electrolyzers is solved, which realizes a balanced optimum among system economic performance, renewable energy accommodation capacity and equipment loss. In addition, a cooperative greedy optimal dispatching strategy (CO-GA) is designed by introducing the priority principle of hot-state operation range, anti-jitter judgment and local cost gradient decision-making mechanism. Simulation results verify that the proposed method effectively cuts down unnecessary equipment switching and cold-start behaviors, and raises the effective service time and hydrogen production power of facilities. The established optimization framework that accounts for cold-start characteristics can offer solid technical support for the safe, reliable, economical and efficient operation of off-grid renewable energy hydrogen production systems.

title: Enhanced solar dryer performance for Terminalia chebula: Energy, exergy, economic, and quality evaluation
abstract: This study provides a detailed assessment of an innovative solar drying system developed for Terminalia chebula, evaluating its performance across energy, exergy, economic, and quality dimensions. The dryer incorporates a canned solar air collector (CSAC) integrated with sensible heat storage to maintain stable drying conditions under variable solar radiation. Experimental results showed a 41.51 % reduction in drying time compared to open sun drying (OSD), achieving a final moisture content of 12.5 % (w.b.) within 31 h. The CSAC exhibited average energy and exergy efficiencies of 74.4 ± 1.41 % and 26.9 ± 2.50 %, respectively, while the dryer demonstrated energy and exergy efficiencies of 21.15 ± 2.04 % and 12.77 ± 3.01 %, respectively. Exergy-based sustainability indicators were evaluated to assess the environmental impact and thermodynamic performance of the system, confirming its suitability for sustainable operation.
