A comprehensive techno-economic evaluation highlighted the system's economic viability, with a short payback period of 0.94 years. Quality analysis revealed improved retention of polyphenols, flavonoids, and favorable color attributes compared to OSD. This design, integrating sensible heat storage with solar drying technology, demonstrates substantial improvements in both operational efficiency and product quality, positioning it as a sustainable and practical solution for agricultural drying needs in resource-limited regions.

title: Editorial Board
Governance and financing frameworks for hydrogen refueling stations under uncertainty: A hybrid MCDM analysis of the Northern Adriatic Hydrogen Valley
abstract: The decarbonization of road transport has positioned green hydrogen as a critical vector for sustainable mobility, particularly in hard-to-abate segments. Yet, the large-scale deployment of hydrogen refuelling stations (HRS) remains constrained by capital intensity, regulatory uncertainty, and demand volatility. Due to paucity of empirical evidence linking governance and financing models to HRS deployment pathways; this study develops a hybrid multi-criteria decision-making framework, combining Grey Relational Analysis and fuzzy-VIKOR, to prioritise ten operational, techno-economic and regulatory criteria and to determine the compartive ranking of five governance and financing models: Build–Operate–Transfer (BOT), Transfer–Operate–Transfer (TOT), Public-Private Partnership (PPP), Hydrogen-as-a-Service (HaaS) and Asset-Backed Securitisation (ABS). Given the early stage uncertanities the regulatory challenges, project risk, and demand uncertainty emerged as most prominent determinants with highest priority weights. HaaS and ABS appear effective as complementary mechanisms for smoothing capital requirements and diversifying investors when embedded in hybrid structures. Overall, the analysis underscores three key insights: (i) HRS deployment is constrained more by institutional design than by technological readiness; (ii) market-centric governance-framework and regulatory harmonization are essential for scalability; and (iii) PPP-based hybrid models offer a viable pathway to bolster the sustainable expansion of HRS infrastructure, particularly within transnational hydrogen valley initiatives.

title: Renewable hydrocarbon production via PPh3/NaI photoredox catalysis from derivatized fatty acid
abstract: Transitioning from fossil dependence toward sustainable fuel architecture requires green chemical pathways capable of generating drop-in hydrocarbon biofuels directly from biomass. Herein, we present a metal-free, visible-light-driven photoredox strategy employing a sodium iodide and triphenylphosphine (NaI/PPh 3 ) catalytic system for the selective hydrodecarboxylation of long-chain fatty acid-derived redox-active esters. Operating at room temperature (25 °C) and atmospheric pressure (1 atm) under blue LED irradiation (λ≈ 450 nm), and utilizing Hantzsch ester as a hydrogen donor, this protocol cleanly converts saturated fatty acid derivatives into linear n-alkanes C 9 –C 17 with yields up to 88%. The process eliminates the need for molecular hydrogen, noble-metal complexes, organic dye sensitizers, or high-temperature processing. The methodology was further adapted into a streamlined one-pot protocol directly from free fatty acids and successfully validated on mixed fatty acid feeds, yielding hydrocarbon distributions matched to sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and green diesel specifications. Mechanistic insights confirm the key role of an electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complex in driving radical cleavage. Overall, this work establishes a benign, highly selective, and low-cost photochemical platform for converting renewable lipid derivatives into drop-in fuels.

title: Toward optimal wide-area site identification and capacity assessment of wind and solar power: A data-driven GIS-MCDM framework with application in Northwest China
abstract: Deploying large-scale wind and solar power requires navigating complex trade-offs among resource availability, infrastructure, and ecological sensitivity-a spatial challenge particularly acute in vast, resource-rich, yet environmentally fragile regions like Northwest China. To address the limitations of traditional Multi-Criteria Decision-Making models in accounting for criterion interdependencies, this study proposes a novel spatial evaluation framework integrating Geographic Information Systems with a two-stage weight allocation method. By explicitly resolving structural interdependencies and synthesizing multi-source, high-resolution datasets under strict ecological redlines, this framework enables rapid suitability classification and high-precision capacity assessment for wind and solar power. Empirical application to Northwest China indicates that after excluding restricted areas (59.30% for solar and 63.75% for wind), the region possesses a massive technical installable potential of 4514.05 GW for PV and 264.28 GW for wind power. The assessment reveals pronounced spatial heterogeneity: Xinjiang dominates in dual-resource potential (holding 77.5% of the regional wind and 61.34% of the PV capacity); Qinghai excels in highly suitable photovoltaic clusters, contributing 19.86% to the regional photovoltaic total, with 44.42% of its provincial PV capacity concentrated in high-suitability areas; and Gansu demonstrates a balanced wind-solar profile, accounting for 11.94% and 14.68% of the regional wind and photovoltaic totals, respectively. Ultimately, this high-precision spatial blueprint provides crucial data support for addressing the insufficiency of flexible regulation resources and guiding the deployment of regional multi-energy complementary systems.

title: Bacillus licheniformis T13: A bifunctional strain for sequential lignin depolymerization and biohydrogen production from agro-wastes
abstract: Bacillus licheniformis T13, isolated from anaerobic digester sludge, exhibits dual metabolic capabilities for lignin depolymerization under aerobic conditions and biohydrogen (H2) production under anaerobic conditions. T13 achieved 72.1 ± 4% lignin decolorization and 58.4 ± 3% Azure B degradation over seven days aerobically, with release of ferulic acid (2.456 mg/L) and vanillin (0.907 mg/L). Genome analysis revealed genes encoding multicopper oxidases (mco, yfiH), AA10 lytic polysaccharide monooxygenases, AA3 oxidoreductases, and the [FeFe]-hydrogenase (hydA) coupled with pyruvate dehydrogenase (pdhA), supporting its metabolic versatility. Under anaerobic batch fermentation, T13 produced hydrogen yields of 0.042–0.089 mol H2/mol hexose equivalent from pure substrates and agro-wastes, with volumetric yields (mL H2/g VS) ranking as: xylose (228 ± 9), glucose (215 ± 9), food waste (213 ± 10), CMC (125 ± 8), and starch (115 ± 8). Co-fermentation of food waste and corn straw increased H2 yield by 53% (107 ± 6 mL/g VS) compared to corn straw alone (70 ± 5 mL/g VS). Gompertz modeling revealed maximum production rates up to 3.6 mL/g VS·h and lag phases <9 h. While lignin depolymerization and H2 production occur in separate phases, T13 offers a robust single-strain platform for consolidated bioprocessing through sequential valorization of lignin and fermentation of hydrolysates from untreated agro-industrial wastes.

title: Effects of torrefaction on the self-heating and subsequent combustion of biomass
abstract: Biomass poses self-heating and spontaneous combustion risks during storage, raising safety concerns. Torrefaction, a deoxygenation pretreatment, can mitigate these risks by altering biomass physicochemical properties. In this study, wheat straw was torrefied at 200, 250, and 300°C, then subjected to self-heating experiments at 25, 55, and 85°C. The objective was to investigate how torrefaction influences the self-heating behavior and combustion characteristics of wheat straw. Results showed that self-heating was most evident at 25°C. Torrefaction reduced the O/C and H/C ratios and volatile content, weakening the intensity of self-heating. Specifically, at 25°C, the untreated sample experienced an 8°C rise, while the sample torrefied at 300°C showed only a 3°C increase. Combustion kinetics analysis further revealed that torrefaction elevated the ignition and burnout temperatures, while decreasing weight loss and combustion indices. At 300°C torrefaction and 85°C ambient conditions, the ignition temperature reached 267°C, reflecting the lowest combustion reactivity. Additionally, at 25 and 55°C, torrefaction increased the activation energy of self-heated samples, with the highest value (93.48 kJ/mol) for the sample torrefied at 250°C at 25°C. These findings provide practical guidance for optimizing torrefaction and storage conditions to improve combustion performance and safety.

title: Probabilistic voltage forecasting of hydrogen fuel cells with a data-driven mean-guided model for performance assessment
abstract: Accurate voltage forecasting is essential for performance assessment and safe operation of Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (PEMFCs) in renewable hydrogen systems. However, PEMFC voltage exhibits strong stochasticity and nonstationarity under degradation and varying operating conditions, which limits deterministic forecasting methods and complicates predictive maintenance. In this study, we propose DMG-PVF, a data-driven mean-guided probabilistic voltage forecasting framework for multi-step PEMFC performance assessment. DMG-PVF first employs an Attention-based Feature Extraction (AFE) module to capture temporal dependencies and cross-series interactions from historical stack-voltage sequences and generate a structured mean prior. This prior is then incorporated into a modified conditional diffusion process, guiding both forward perturbation and reverse generation so that the model produces future voltage distributions rather than only point estimates. Experiments on two real-world PEMFC datasets show that DMG-PVF achieves relative error reductions of 19.51% and 23.33% over TimeDiff on FC1 and FC2, and 29.13% and 27.17% over D3VAE, while producing uncertainty-aware prediction intervals. These results indicate that probabilistic voltage forecasting can support predictive maintenance, risk-aware dispatch, and reliable performance assessment of PEMFC-based systems powered by renewable hydrogen.

title: Configuration selection and optimal flow design for medium-depth coaxial and U-type borehole heat exchangers
abstract: Coaxial and U-type borehole heat exchangers are widely used in medium-deep geothermal systems, but comparisons under equal drilling footage remain scarce. This study develops validated numerical models for a two-coaxial borehole system and a U-type borehole heat exchanger and evaluates their performance under a total drilling footage of 5000 m. Axial heat transfer intensity is introduced to characterize performance differences, while net heat exchange intensity is used for flow optimization. At identical flow conditions, system superiority varies with pipe configuration, flow regime, and geological conditions. The two-coaxial system with a stainless-steel vacuum pipe achieves 6–12% higher heat extraction than the U-type system but requires greater pump power, whereas with a PE-RT II pipe, heat extraction exceeds the U-type system only when total flow reaches a critical threshold of about 67.0 m3 h−1. Under net heat exchange intensity-based optimal flow rates of 38.5 m3 h−1 for the coaxial and 60.0 m3 h−1 for the U-type, their heat extraction becomes comparable, whereas the U-type exhibits higher net heat exchange intensity above a critical value of 45.0 m3 h−1. Both heat extraction-based and net heat exchange intensity-based critical flow rates vary among regions. Axial heat transfer analysis identifies upper 200 m of the U-type straight borehole as the key region limiting performance relative to the two-coaxial system. Regional results further indicate that lower stratum thermal conductivity and higher ground temperature reduce performance disparities between the two systems. These findings provide guidance for flow rate optimization and borehole configuration selection.

title: Methane production from acidic substrate furfural residue: Effects of fermentation conditions and microbial characteristics
abstract: Furfural residue (FR) is a biomass waste generated from the furfural industry. Rich in carbon and cellulose, FR represents a promising feedstock for bioenergy conversion. However, its high acidity and low pH pose challenges for anaerobic digestion (AD). This study investigated the effects of initial pH, total solids (TS) content, and pretreatment methods on methane production from FR via batch AD. Results showed that alkaline adjustment to pH 8.0 significantly enhanced cumulative methane production to 38.24 mL/g TS, representing a 34.18% increase over pH 7.3 (28.50 mL/g TS) and a 127.62% increase over the control group (16.80 mL/g TS). Raising TS content from 3% to 6% enhanced cumulative biogas production by 7.42%-25.10%. Alkali pretreatment (5% NaOH) outperformed water-washing pretreatment, increasing biogas production by 5.89%-23.33%. Microbial analysis revealed that alkaline conditions and higher TS content enriched Methanosarcina (relative abundance increased by 1.91%-4.86% and 0.44%-2.29%, respectively), a versatile methanogen capable of utilizing acetate, H2/CO2, and methylated substrates. Under optimal conditions (pH 8.0, 6% TS, alkali pretreatment), cumulative methane production reached 106.77 mL/g TS, with methane content of 55.21%-68.02%. This study demonstrates an environmentally friendly approach for valorizing furfural residue, offering a promising strategy for sustainable biogas production from acidic lignocellulosic wastes.

title: Resilient real-time operational planning of smart grids with electric vehicle battery swapping stations
abstract: The growing deployment of electric vehicle battery swapping stations, distributed generation, dynamic switches, and communication-based controllers, together with renewable generation variability, uncertain demand, network reconfiguration requirements, false data injection attacks, and communication delays, makes the operation of modern distribution networks a complex cyber-physical challenge. This paper proposes a real-time operational planning framework that integrates a multi-objective optimization method with a long short-term memory neural network for hour-ahead decision-making. The framework jointly considers battery swapping station operation, uncertainty modelling through fuzzy Monte Carlo simulation, cyber-physical disturbances, dynamic network reconfiguration, short-circuit level and loadability constraints, expected energy not supplied, environmental penalties, and dynamic security assessment based on a virtual synchronous generator model. Operational scenarios generated during the offline stage are used to train the neural network. During online operation, the trained model predicts near-optimal generation dispatch, power exchange at battery swapping stations, and dynamic switch states without repeatedly solving the optimization problem. Simulation results obtained from a modified 118-bus test system expanded to 124 buses for distribution-level operational studies and incorporating microgrids, renewable energy resources, battery swapping stations, energy storage systems, and dynamic switches show reductions in operating cost and expected energy not supplied, together with improvements in voltage security, reliability, resilience, loadability, and short-circuit level control compared with existing methods.

title: Heat transfer characteristics of an oceanic crust thermal reservoir under seawater cyclic thermal shock: optimization for geothermal energy extraction
abstract: Driven by global carbon neutrality goals, the development of hot dry rock geothermal resources in the oceanic crust has considerable potential, and using seawater as a heat exchange fluid can conserve freshwater resources. However, the dynamic evolution of heat transfer in hot dry rock under cyclic seawater thermal shock, as well as the critical temperature threshold remain unclear. To address this gap, this study used experiments and numerical simulations and, for the first time, constructed a temperature field model of the thermally damaged fracture network in hot dry rock to systematically evaluate heat transfer under cyclic seawater thermal shock. The effects of different temperatures (100-500 °C) and cycle numbers (0-20 cycles) were investigated. The degradation of thermophysical parameters was measured experimentally, and the transient temperature responses and the evolution of the heating/cooling rates were analyzed using the temperature field model. The results indicate that thermophysical parameters values decreased nonlinearly with increasing temperature and cycle number. Thermal conductivity and thermal diffusivity were 35.55% and 45.57% lower, respectively, after 20 cycles at 500 °C than during initial conditions. A critical thermal threshold was identified at 300 °C, above which the thermal barrier effect of the fracture network replaced the temperature gradient as the dominant heat transfer mechanism. This study elucidates the deterioration of heat transfer under coupled thermo-chemo-mechanical damage and provides a theoretical basis for thermal management and long-term performance assessment of reservoirs in the geothermal development of the oceanic crust.

title: Household adoption of small-scale renewable energy in Sierra Leone: An integrated behavioral and technological model
abstract: This study examines the factors associated with households' intention to use small-scale renewable energy (SSRE) systems in Sierra Leone by integrating the Theory of Planned Behavior, the Technology Acceptance Model, and the Diffusion of Innovations theory into a unified analytical framework, addressing a significant gap in understanding renewable energy use in developing economies. Using data from 341 households, the integrated model explains approximately 83% of the variance in SSRE use intention. The results indicate that perceived affordability, trust, perceived ease of use, perceived behavioral control, relative advantage, and social norms are positively associated with intention, with perceived affordability and trust showing the strongest associations. Indirect analysis further highlights perceived behavioral control as a key pathway linking these factors to intention, offering practical guidance for policymakers seeking to promote inclusive and sustainable household energy transitions in low-income settings.

title: Numerical analysis and structural optimization of PEMFC cold-start performance
abstract: Achieving reliable cold-start performance in proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) under subzero conditions remains a critical engineering challenge. A unified three-dimensional (3D) transient multiphase computational fluid dynamics (CFD) framework was developed to systematically quantify the structural trade-offs between shutdown purge efficiency and auxiliary ice-melting performance. Using rigorous CFD, we evaluated cold-start performance across four cathode flow-field geometries (straight, unidirectionally, bidirectionally, and periodically tapered) with heights varying from 0.3 to 0.7 mm. The 0.3 mm unidirectionally tapered channel reduced ice-melting time by 59.99% and purge time by 20.01% relative to the straight-channel baseline. A multi-objective evaluation matrix incorporating scenario-dependent weighting factors was formulated to resolve the competing demands of rapid startup and long-term durability. Under a weighting of 70% ice-melting and 30% purge efficiency, the 0.3 mm unidirectional channel achieved the highest overall improvement (48.00%). Under the reversed weighting (70% purge, 30% ice melting), the 0.3 mm periodically tapered channel was superior (36.04% improvement). These results indicate that passive flow-field tapering simultaneously enhances liquid water removal and ice melting without incurring additional auxiliary energy consumption, providing a structurally efficient design strategy for PEMFC systems operating in cold climates.

title: Superhydrophilic CuS/PDA@PI nanofibrous aerogel with efficient synergistic solar-driven interfacial evaporation for water purification
abstract: Solar-driven interfacial evaporators represent a promising approach to alleviate global freshwater scarcity. However, practical applications still face challenges such as low evaporation efficiency, salt scale accumulation, and unstable evaporation. Therefore, we polymerized and deposited polydopamine (PDA) and hydrothermally synthesized CuS nanoparticles onto a polyimide (PI) aerogel to prepare a superhydrophilic porous CuS/PDA@PI nanofibrous aerogel. The aerogel achieved >97% light absorption over 200-2500 nm and a water evaporation rate of 1.963 kg m−2 h−1 under one sun irradiation (1 kW m−2). The apparent total evaporation efficiency reached 119.8%, exceeding the theoretical limit due to additional environmental heat harvesting. Even after 1200 min of cycling, the aerogel maintained an apparent total evaporation efficiency of 116.6%. The evaporator maintained an apparent total evaporation efficiency of 88.7% under a salt (20%) environment and exhibited self-cleaning performance. Furthermore, the aerogel exhibited purification performance for dye wastewater, acidic and alkaline solutions, and seawater. This superhydrophilic evaporator provides a viable route for practical seawater desalination.

title: Rainfall effects on biogas production at wastewater treatment plants
abstract: In this study, we quantify rainfall effects on biogas production using regression models and long-term daily operational data from wastewater treatment plants. Of particular attention is what we denote “first flush”, where rain following dry days brings sludge deposited in pipes, allowing the examination on how this process affects sludge deposition and biogas quality. From a case study in Denmark, we find first flush events are typically triggered when there has been no significant rainfall for three to four consecutive days followed by a daily rainfall exceeding 2 mm. A significant negative effect of rainfall was only found in secondary sludge separation but not in primary sludge separation. Although rainfall directly dilutes wastewater, the first flush event can increase the deposition of sludge thereby also increase the methane in biogas. On-site, the resulting increase in biogas-based electricity generation partially offsets the additional energy demand caused by rainfall, highlighting a self-balancing mechanism of rainfall effects. Rolling average regressions showed that rainfall in general (i.e. not first flush) directly and significantly reduced biogas production within 9 - 12 days by 1.94%–5.50%, and the electricity consumption response to rainfall was more evident on the following day.

title: National assessment of renewable cold energy resources in China using an integrated cold quality and balance index
abstract: Cooling demand is a rapidly growing contributor to electricity consumption and carbon emissions, highlighting the need for renewable alternatives to conventional refrigeration. This study develops a dimensionless Integrated Cold Quality and Balance Index that combines cold-season duration, annual cold–heat balance, and freezing quality within a multiplicative, non-compensatory framework. Daily air-temperature observations from 771 meteorological stations across China during 1973–2024 were used for national-scale spatial assessment, zoning, sensitivity analysis, and station-specific time-series projection. The proposed index ranged from nearly zero to approximately 2.63 and exhibited a clear west–north high and east–south low pattern. The Abundant and Hyper-rich zones covered 50.29% of China, with major high-potential regions in Northeast China, the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau, and mountainous Xinjiang. The cold–heat balance component controlled the first-order spatial pattern (r = 0.9929), but rankings based on this component alone and on the complete index showed a five-group agreement of 92.9% (ρ = 0.9734), meaning that 7.1% of the stations changed rank-based group after duration and freezing quality were incorporated. Rankings remained stable under alternative operational thresholds (ρ = 0.9866–0.9875) and additive formulations (ρ = 0.9657–0.9746). Spatial comparison with freezing depth and cold-season temperature supported climatic plausibility. The national station-average index declined significantly during both 1973–1997 and 1998–2024. Time-series projections averaged 0.0882 during 2025–2034 and showed only a weak, statistically non-significant downward tendency (p = 0.100), while the broad national spatial pattern remained stable. The proposed index provides a physically interpretable first-stage tool for renewable cooling-resource screening and regional technology matching.
keywords: Integrated cold quality and balance index

title: Multi-year assessment of energy storage capacity for a carbon-neutral grid in Arizona and the impact of wind energy integration
abstract: The energy storage capacity for large, interconnected grids with high renewable penetration needs further evaluation to balance the intermittency while maintaining reliability. This study develops a multi-year, hourly resolution model of Arizona U.S.A., using synchronized electric load, solar insolation and wind data from 2019 to 2023 to quantify storage needs under high renewable penetration. Unlike prior studies, it explicitly sizes storage to achieve a carbon-neutral grid, decomposes requirements into daily minimum, seasonal peak, and multi-day components, and assesses the role of wind power in reducing storage demand. When solar PV is the only generation source replacing all non-renewables, Arizona's annual energy storage requirements range from 290 to 560 GWh, with 66 to 91 GWDC of installed solar PV capacity needed over the five years analyzed, reflecting substantial yearly variability. On average, daily minimum and seasonal peak storage account for 48 GWh and 155 GWh, respectively, but multi-day storage dominates at 350 GWh and exhibits the highest variability, driven by prolonged low solar insolation events. While Arizona's wind resources are modest, even limited deployments substantially reduces storage needs; adding 4 GW of wind turbine capacity lowers daily minimum, seasonal peak, and multi-day storage by 44.8%, 4.4%, and 21.3%, respectively, while 11 GW cuts multi-day storage by an average 48% for all five years. These results underscore the role of diversified renewable portfolios in reducing total storage requirements of a carbon-neutral grid, with a significant impact on lowering capital expenditure and enhancing the resilience of the infrastructure.

title: Effect of strut configuration on startup and steady-state performance of a crossflow turbine
abstract: The startup and hydrodynamic performance of crossflow turbines are strongly influenced by structural components such as struts; however, their role remains insufficiently understood. This study experimentally investigates the effect of strut positioning on turbine startup dynamics and steady-state power performance. Experiments were conducted in a towing tank at a fixed Reynolds number using three strut configurations: top-and-bottom, mid-span, and 20% from the blade tips. An electromagnetic brake was used to apply controlled resistive loading. Under the adopted startup protocol, the loaded startup response was classified into three operating regions, ranging from reliable self-starting to a regime requiring an off–on strategy to sustain rotation. The corresponding transition limits were identified using azimuthal adjustments restricted to approximately 20° from the reference blade orientation and therefore do not constitute a full static torque map. The 20% configuration demonstrated improved startup capability and higher load tolerance compared to the other configurations. The top-and-bottom and mid-span configurations exhibited narrower operating boundaries; under resistive loading, the mid-span configuration started faster but tolerated lower loads than the top-and-bottom configuration. Despite these startup differences, all configurations achieved similar peak power coefficients. These findings indicate that strut placement significantly influences startup behavior while exerting comparatively limited impact on peak efficiency.

title: Response-based scaling and design optimization of small-scale floating offshore wind turbine prototypes
abstract: Laboratory testing supports the modeling and design optimization of floating offshore wind turbines, yet full-scale testing is often impractical due to cost, safety, and limited flexibility for design iteration. Model-scale testing provides an alternative. However, conventional model-scale approaches face fundamental similarity limitations, as Froude and Reynolds similitude cannot be simultaneously satisfied at small scales due to wind tunnel velocity, blockage, and operational constraints. This study presents a numerical response-based dynamic similarity framework. It preserves selected system-level responses rather than enforcing strict classical similitude. Three metrics are used: (1) the ratio between excitation (i.e., from aerodynamic rotor loads and hydrodynamic forcing) and primary natural frequencies, (2) the damping ratio for the pitch motion, and (3) normalized platform pitch rotation and tower-tip bending deflection. A reduced-order coupled model, combining a linear six-degree-of-freedom platform representation, an Euler–Bernoulli tower model, and a Blade Element Momentum rotor formulation is developed. The NREL 5-MW turbine on the OC4-DeepCwind semi-submersible is used as a reference case for benchmarking. The framework is benchmarked against full-scale OpenFAST simulations. A constrained optimization determines rotor geometry, tower properties, and ballast distribution. Results show that the proposed approach reproduces the selected similarity metrics with deviations of approximately 4 − 12 % in frequency ratio, damping characteristics, pitch response, and structural deformation. The methodology provides a low-cost and manufacturable design pathway for response-matched model-scale prototypes. Physical testing of the optimized design is outside the scope of the present study and is reserved for future work.

title: A novel dual-bent-duct floating pneumatic wave energy converter for broadband energy conversion and wave attenuation
abstract: This study presents a theoretical investigation of a novel dual-bent-duct floating pneumatic wave energy converter designed for broadband wave energy conversion and wave attenuation. A hydrodynamic model based on linear potential flow theory is established and validated against published data and experimental results. Parametric studies examine the effects of forward duct length, front cabin draft, and forward water channel height on energy conversion efficiency and wave transmission. The results reveal a complementary energy capture mechanism: the forward bent duct dominates in short-period waves (3–7 s), while the backward bent duct governs in long-period waves (7–10 s), together broadening the effective frequency bandwidth beyond that of conventional single-duct designs. Over the 3–10 s period range, the proposed device achieves an average conversion efficiency of 0.81—compared to 0.56 and 0.23 for the backward-only and forward-only configurations—and an average transmission coefficient of 0.3, representing reductions of 26.8 % and 60 %, respectively. Parametric analysis identifies a channel-height-to-duct-length ratio of approximately 0.9 as favorable for long-wave attenuation. These findings provide insights into the design of multifunctional wave energy converters that combine energy extraction with offshore structure protection.

title: Coordinated rotor speed-pitch angle deloading control strategy of wind turbines based on LiDAR wind speed forecast for grid frequency regulation
abstract: This study proposes a LiDAR-based coordinated control strategy that integrates rotor speed and pitch angle deloading for wind turbine frequency regulation. The methodology employs a nacelle-mounted four-beam LiDAR system coupled with hub-height equivalent wind speed estimation to obtain high accuracy, hub height predicted wind speeds for feedforward control. Based on the predicted wind speed, an iterative algorithm for solving nonlinear equations is developed, incorporating dynamic wind speed zoning to effectively eliminate frequent switching between deloading modes. Furthermore, a multi-objective optimization framework is formulated with a cost function that simultaneously minimizes pitch angle variations and ensures rotor speed stability, thereby achieving an optimal balance between frequency regulation performance and mechanical system reliability. The controller is comprehensively evaluated in MATLAB/Simulink using field-measured nacelle-LiDAR data from a high-altitude wind farm in Yunnan Province, China, as model inputs. Results demonstrate that compared to Maximum Power Point Tracking control and conventional deloading strategies, the simulation results exhibit comprehensive advantages across all wind speed regimes. Specifically, under medium wind speeds during frequency abrupt events, when providing equivalent frequency response performance compared to traditional deloading methods, the proposed method achieves a 7.0% reduction in pitch angle variance, a 36.4% decrease in pitch rate standard deviation, and a 0.34% reduction in power fluctuation standard deviation. This research provides a technically feasible approach for wind turbine participation in primary frequency regulation.

title: Interfacial water evaporation performance of 3D printed inverted conical porous ceramic skeletons
abstract: Solar interfacial evaporation (SIE) provides a low-carbon pathway for desalination relative to traditional high-energy-consumption technologies. However, traditional SIE evaporators suffering from uncontrollable pore structures, random salt crystallization, and a trade-off between evaporation efficiency and salt resistance, which severely limit their large-scale application. Here, 3D ceramic-based SIE evaporator with controllable porous structure was fabricated via direct ink writing (DIW) 3D printing technology, and an integrated system for synchronous SIE and salt crystal recovery was further developed. The inverted conical structure of the 3D-printed evaporator induces targeted edge crystallization and spontaneous gravity-driven shedding of salt crystals, realizing robust and sustained salt resistance. In 15 wt% NaCl high-salinity brine, the evaporator with a pore diameter of 0.29 mm maintains an evaporation rate of 1.64 kg m−2 h−1. The integrated SIE-salt recovery system achieves a high and stable evaporation rate of 2.05 kg m−2 h−1 in 15 wt% NaCl brine and realizes synchronous automatic salt crystal recovery. The 3D printing-based controllable structure design, inverted conical structure-induced salt resistance, and evaporation-salt recovery system align with the sustainable development trend of renewable energy integration for decarbonization. It shows important practical value for promoting the large-scale application of SIE technology in desalination and sustainable water resource utilization.

title: Enhancing anaerobic co-digestion of organic wastes through targeted feedstock allocation based on biodegradability: Performance optimization and microbial regulation
abstract: To enhance the biochemical conversion efficiency of multiple organic wastes, the staged anaerobic co-digestion (SAcoD) featuring targeted allocation based on feedstock biodegradability was proposed. In this process, readily biodegradable feedstock was used for acid production, and the resulting acidic effluent was then co-digested with recalcitrant feedstock for methane production, thereby optimizing material flow. Using food waste and corn straw as substrates representing readily biodegradable and recalcitrant feedstocks, respectively, batch experiment results showed that the synergistic index of SAcoD reached a maximum of 1.20 at a volatile solids (VS) mass ratio of food waste to straw of 2:3, with a corresponding methane yield of 351.5 mL/g-VSfed. Microbial community analysis revealed that SAcoD could selectively enrich functional genera (norank_Bacteroidales, HN-HF0106, Syntrophomonas, Methanothrix, etc.) by regulating the VS ratio, promoting organic matter degradation and methane production. PICRUSt-based functional prediction suggested a potential enrichment of genes associated with both hydrogenotrophic and acetoclastic methanogenesis pathways. During the stable operation phase of the semi-continuous system, SAcoD achieved 7.5% higher methane production than that of conventional co-digestion under the tested system configuration, while contributing to a more stable methanogenic environment. This study provides theoretical insights and technical references for improving the anaerobic co-digestion of organic wastes.

title: Anaerobic co-digestion of lignocellulose and ammonia rich biomasses using advanced composite bioaugmentation inocula
abstract: Lignocellulose- and ammonia-rich biomasses are widely available and offer substantial potential for methane generation, yet their combined use often severely inhibits anaerobic digestion (AD) performance. This study explored bioaugmentation as a strategy to counteract the simultaneous inhibitory effects of lignocellulose and ammonia. Composite microbial inocula, consisting of hydrolytic bacteria and methanogenic archaea, were developed from mixed cultures and pure strains (i.e., Ruminococcus albus and Methanoculleus bourgensis ). These cultures were acclimated to elevated lignocellulose (3 g VS L -1 ) and ammonia (4 g NH 4 + -N L -1 ) concentrations. To assess long-term preservation methods suitable for practical future commercial use, the acclimatised inocula were either lyophilised or immobilised in gel. Their performance was then assessed in batch reactors operating under high lignocellulose and/or ammonia levels. The lyophilised composite inoculum containing acclimatised M. bourgensis and R. albus achieved the highest methane yield, reaching 195 ml CH 4 g -1 VS, which was sixfold higher than its gel-immobilised counterpart. In addition, the lyophilised composite inoculum derived from acclimatised mixed inoculum exhibited a rapid initial methane production response and produced 235.1% more methane than its corresponding abiotic control. This study demonstrated, for the first time, the successful development of composite bioaugmentation inocula combining hydrolytic and methanogenic microorganisms that are acclimatised to harsh lignocellulose and ammonia levels, while also being suitable for extended storage and on-demand use, offering promising potential for improving AD process stability and efficiency.

title: System interactions constraining offshore wind deployment in the Dutch North Sea
abstract: The Netherlands aims to deploy up to 70 GW of offshore wind by 2050 in its waters. As one of the busiest sea areas in the world, the Dutch part of the North Sea is shaped by spatial tensions and a degraded state of nature due to activities such as fossil fuel extraction, shipping and fishing. The interconnectedness of sectors and actors leads to various interactions with spatially demanding offshore wind, potentially enabling and constraining its deployment. We use systems thinking to explore the interactions which occur in the Dutch North Sea as a result of the offshore wind transition. We interview 22 stakeholders, organise one structured focus group discussion, and four follow-up workshops. Through our systems thinking approach, we elucidate on the interactions between different sectors and activities in the domains of the socio-technical system of offshore wind, spatial competition, and quality of nature, thereby broadening the scope of analysis. This allows us to identify a set of interactions which impact the deployment of offshore wind in the Netherlands, located in the domains infrastructure, society, space, and ecology. Overall, we find that the spatial and ecological interactions point to the need to build on synergies between different activities for a successful transition. As the expansion of offshore wind will lead to a variety of effects due to the interactions with other domains, there will likely be conflicts with other policy areas such as ecology and marine spatial planning.

title: Optimizing specific dark fermentation strategies for enhanced bio-hydrogen production from different agricultural wastes
abstract: The integration of the dark fermentation process into existing anaerobic digestion plants, leading to the implementation of two stage processes, may enable the sequential recovery of biohydrogen and biomethane from agricultural residues. This study evaluated semi-continuous dark fermentation of cattle manure, corn residue, and soybean residue at hydraulic retention times of 3–10 days, including co-fermentation and digestate recirculation strategies. Cattle manure did not support stable biohydrogen production under the tested conditions, producing no detectable hydrogen and rapidly shifting towards methanogenesis. CR showed only transient biohydrogen peaks, followed by process instability associated with pH decrease, nutrient limitation, and methanogenic competition. Soybean residue supported stable hydrogen production at HRT 3 d, reaching 4.7 NmLH 2 /gVS. The best performance was obtained by soybean/CR co-fermentation, which achieved 12.4 NmLH 2 /gVS, 67.8 NmLgas/gVS, and 0.32 gCODVFA/gVS. VFA production was strongly substrate-dependent, with CR at HRT 7 d reaching the highest VFA yield among single-substrate trials. Biomethane potential tests showed that fermented effluents retained relevant residual energy potential, with fermented CR increasing biomethane recovery by up to 34% compared with the untreated substrate. Overall, the results demonstrate that substrate selection and nutrients balance are key factors for implementing two-stage anaerobic digestion of agricultural residues.

title: Process simulation of green ammonia production plant and waste heat recovery system for integration into Finnish district heating networks and energy infrastructure
abstract: An integrated process simulation model is developed to study the utilization of waste heat recovered from an industrial scale green ammonia production plant in Finland. ASPEN Plus was used to simulate the steady-state production of green hydrogen via alkaline electrolysis and it´s subsequent synthesis into ammonia through the Haber Bosch process. The plant behaviour is simulated under varying power levels, hydrogen mass flow rates and district heating supply temperatures using a MATLAB code to estimate the annual hourly recoverable waste heat for two district heating networks i.e. Kokkola and Oulu in Finland. The simulations targeted an annual ammonia production of approximately 213kt and evaluated waste heat recovery potential and district heating integration feasibility. The study reveals that the plant can generate up to 115 MW of usable waste heat, confirming its potential as a significant thermal energy source. Dynamic simulations showed seasonal variation in waste heat availability. In Oulu, a 47.16 MW district heat (DH) production system caused only 0.2% DH curtailment, while in Kokkola a 23.58 MW system resulted in 12% curtailment, highlighting the importance of site-specific, moderately sized heat pump integration for stable operation. Results indicate that although waste heat is continuously generated, its high volume relative to demand particularly during summer is limited due to feasibility constraints.

title: Assessment of fuel property enhancement toward TRL advancement in biomass torrefaction
abstract: Coffee wood pruning residues constitute an abundant lignocellulosic feedstock with strong potential for thermochemical upgrading into sustainable fuels at pre-commercial scale. This study assesses the influence of torrefaction temperature (200–300 °C), nitrogen flow rate (200–600 mL min−1), and particle size (250–710 μm) on the physicochemical and fuel properties of coffee wood stems through response surface methodology combined with process simulation. Temperature was identified as the dominant operational variable, significantly affecting solid yield, proximate and ultimate composition, and calorific value (adjusted R2 > 0.90). Increasing torrefaction temperature from 200 to 300 °C reduced solid yield from 85% to 60%, while increasing carbon content up to 70 wt% and decreasing oxygen content below 30 wt%. Consequently, the calculated higher heating value (HHV) increased from 19.6 to 24 MJ kg−1, and the energy densification ratio (EDR) reached 1.35. Economic and environmental assessments revealed that plant capacity strongly influences process sustainability. At the current miniplant scale, electricity consumption accounted for more than 99% of the environmental burden and significantly increased production costs. However, scaling up substantially reduced both the carbon footprint and the cost of torrefied biomass. Overall, this study demonstrates the achievement of Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 5, validating torrefaction as an integrated miniplant technology for future biorefinery applications.

title: Unraveling the trade-off effects of catalyst layer cracks on proton exchange membrane fuel cell performance and corresponding optimization strategies
abstract: Proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) are key devices for converting renewable hydrogen into clean power for transportation, stationary power, and distributed energy systems. The catalyst layer (CL), where the electrochemical conversion of hydrogen occurs, strongly governs the efficiency and durability of this renewable energy conversion process. Yet the mechanism by which CL cracks affect performance remains unclear, making it challenging to effectively guide the design of CL and operational optimization. This study presents a comprehensive experimental approach to investigate the effects of CL cracks across various operating conditions and proposes an optimization scheme. Experimental results show that whether cracks in the CL are beneficial is highly dependent on test operating conditions, especially under high current density. Under low humidity, cracks cause a substantial 38.2% increase in ohmic impedance, thus functioning as defects in the CL. However, under high humidity, cracks reduce the mass transfer impedance by 43.4% and instead act as optimized structures that help the CL resist flooding. The experimental results uncover the synergistic coupling effect between CL cracks and operating conditions, breaking through the previous one-sided evaluation of CL cracks. Based on mechanistic analysis, this study proposes a phase diagram integrating cracks in the CL, humidity levels, and PEMFCs performance, thereby supporting efficient hydrogen utilization in renewable energy systems for practical applications.

title: A lifecycle review of sky eyes: A space-air-ground remote sensing for photovoltaic systems
abstract: Remote sensing (RS) technologies are increasingly recognized as important infrastructure for next-generation photovoltaic (PV) deployment. As solar expansion accelerates under global decarbonization targets, RS provides critical spatial intelligence for managing land constraints, environmental risks, and system performance. This review summarizes the spectral, spatial, and physical attributes most relevant to PV diagnostics and examines how different RS modalities have been applied across PV planning, construction, operation, and decommissioning. The reviewed literature shows that spaceborne, airborne, and ground-based platforms offer complementary capabilities, but their practical maturity differs across lifecycle stages and deployment contexts. Based on this synthesis, the paper synthesizes an altitude-based, lifecycle-integrated review framework that links RS modalities with key PV phases and clarifies their respective roles in site selection, ecological sensing, performance monitoring, and risk assessment. The paper also discusses a deployment-oriented typology of RS-enabled PV scenarios including various land types. The review further discusses frontier applications and remaining bottlenecks related to data resolution, multi-source fusion, validation, and deployment cost. Finally, it highlights the need for integration among geoscience, engineering, energy systems, and governance. These findings suggest that RS is moving from a reactive inspection tool toward a strategic evidence layer for more resilient and accountable solar development.

title: Multi-criteria decision-making for net zero transition in energy islands: A case study in South Italy
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving net-zero emissions in islanded and remote areas presents unique challenges due to energy supply limitations, high reliance on fossil fuels, and environmental constraints. This study applies Multi-Criteria Decision-Making methods to support energy planning for the transition to net zero on Favignana Island, Italy. Using real consumption data from the local community, it evaluates renewable energy deployment strategies, considering technical feasibility and socio-environmental implications. The novelty of the study lies in coupling HOMER Pro scenario optimization with Fuzzy AHP-TOPSIS to rank island transition pathways across technical, economic, environmental, and social criteria. LCOE, reliability, and social acceptance emerged as the most influential criteria according to pairwise comparisons developed by 3 experts, with weights of 0.2552, 0.2294, and 0.1864, respectively. Under the adopted assumptions, the grid-connection scenario ranked highest, achieving a TOPSIS relative closeness index of 0.7884, compared to 0.3104 of Rooftop PV, 0.1893 of Utility scale PV, and 0.2704 of Hybrid PV and Wind solutions. A sensitivity analysis confirmed the robustness of the ranking, showing that the grid-connection scenario remains the preferred option under a wide range of variations in criteria weights and key input assumptions. The study offers a replicable framework for energy decision-making in other insular or off-grid contexts.

title: Technical evaluation of bio-Fischer-Tropsch wax co-processing in industrial hydrocracking: a scalable pathway to lower-carbon fuels
abstract: The integration of renewable feedstocks into conventional refinery operations is a key pathway for accelerating decarbonization in the fuels sector. Among the available options, bio-based Fischer–Tropsch (FT) wax provides a chemically compatible and scalable route for refinery co-processing. In practice, such integration is most effectively implemented in hydrocracking units, which are highly sensitive to feedstock properties. A clear understanding of how renewable FT wax affects unit performance and product quality is therefore essential for reliable deployment. This study presents a rigorous evaluation of bio-FT wax co-processing in an industrial-scale hydrocracking unit using advanced simulations validated against operational plant data, ensuring high fidelity and practical relevance. A comprehensive set of blending scenarios was examined to quantify the influence of bio-FT wax on feed impurity mitigation, reactor thermodynamics, hydrogen consumption, and product distribution over the future implementation roadmap. The results reveal that increasing bio-FT wax content substantially reduces feed contaminants, lowers hydrogen demand, and moderates exothermic reactor profiles, while maintaining product yields and properties within specification limits. These findings demonstrate the technical viability and operational robustness of integrating bio-derived FT wax into existing hydrocracking infrastructure, highlighting its potential as a scalable, near-term pathway to produce lower-carbon fuels suitable for high-demand sectors such as aviation.

title: Mechanism of CaO-catalyzed tar steam reforming during biomass gasification: Experimental and simulation study
abstract: Tar is the principal impediment to the commercial deployment of biomass gasification technology. Tar steam reforming, which converts tar into syngas while enhancing gasification efficiency and ensuring cleaner operation, is considered the most promising tar removal approach. CaO-based materials have garnered significant attention due to their high efficiency and economic advantages. An understanding of their catalytic mechanism is therefore crucial. This study investigates the catalytic mechanism of CaO in the biomass tar steam reforming process by combining fixed-bed gasification experiments with ReaxFF MD simulations. Experiments demonstrate that the H2 yield increases 31%, while the yields of light hydrocarbon gases increase correspondingly. Furthermore, CaO catalyzed the cracking of large tar molecules into smaller compounds with lower molecular weights and more oxygen-containing functional groups. ReaxFF MD simulations demonstrated that CaO facilitates H2O dissociation through a hydration reaction (Ca + H2O ↔ H2CaO), generating highly reactive ⋅H and ⋅OH radicals. The ⋅OH radicals subsequently interact with tar molecules, inducing C–H bond cleavage to release ⋅H and form oxygenated molecules (e.g., CH2O2), thereby providing a crucial hydrogen source for syngas formation. DFT calculations further revealed that the coordination of Ca with the oxygen atom of oxygenated molecules triggers a reconstruction of the local electronic structure, generating an electrostatic polarization effect. This effect reduces the C–O bond dissociation energy from 114 to 21 kcal mol−1, thereby facilitating molecular dissociation. This work elucidates the role of CaO in enhancing syngas production via catalytic cracking, laying a theoretical groundwork for deploying CaO-based catalysts in tar steam reforming.

title: Thermal analysis and optimization of energy diaphragm walls with ground heat exchangers under groundwater seepage in the Chengdu Plain
abstract: The impact of groundwater seepage on the thermal performance of energy diaphragm walls has attracted increasing attention. This study develops a full-scale three-dimensional thermo-hydro coupled model for energy diaphragm walls based on the actual geological conditions of the Chengdu Plain in Southwest China. The long-term thermal performance under different seepage velocities and locations, including upstream, midstream, and downstream zones, is investigated. A novel adjustment factor method is introduced to evaluate and optimize the heat transfer among ground heat exchanger groups. The results show that the longer cooling season causes excessive heat accumulation around energy diaphragm walls, thereby weakening summer heat transfer. Groundwater seepage mitigates this deterioration, depending on seepage velocity and wall location. At 75.9 m/yr, the heat transfer energy per unit area in the upstream zone is 12.1% and 8.6% higher than that in the midstream and downstream zones, respectively. After optimizing the spacing of ground heat exchanger groups using the adjustment factor method, the overall summer heat transfer energy in the midstream and downstream zones increases by 2.4% and 5.2%, respectively. The present findings demonstrate the potential of the adjustment factor method for improving the thermal performance through effective geometric design.

title: Study on exergy loss governing and product distribution regulation mechanisms of biomass staged gasification system based on experiments and Aspen Plus
abstract: Biomass staged gasification technology (BSGT) is an effective approach to enhance syngas quality and energy utilization efficiency during gasification. By combining devolatilization experiments with Aspen Plus simulation and incorporating an improved kinetics model (RPM+) that considers AAEMs effects, this study developed a comprehensive process model of the BSGT system with enhanced accuracy. The interstage coupling relationships (devolatilization, gasification and reforming) were systematically analyzed, and quantitative optimal operating ranges were determined based on product distribution and exergy efficiency. The results indicated that CO2 production was primarily controlled by the gasification reforming stage, whereas H2 production was mainly influenced by the devolatilization temperature and S/B ratio. The overall system efficiency was most sensitive to the devolatilization temperature. Considering the combined effects, the optimal operating ranges for devolatilization temperature, gasification reforming temperature, and S/B ratio were 350–550 °C, 850–950 °C, and 0.5–0.7, respectively. Under these conditions, the system exergy efficiency reached 59.8–79.8%, significantly higher than that of conventional gasification. This study clarifies the interstage coupling relationships within BSGT, i.e., how the operating conditions of different stages affect the final product distribution and exergy efficiency, and offers valuable insights for optimizing high-quality, hydrogen-rich syngas production.

title: Economic potential of the energy transition: A regionalized input-output analysis of wind power in Lower Saxony, Germany
abstract: Wind power is crucial for the energy transition, but regional impacts are still underexplored. This study analyzes the impact of regional datasets for examining the economic footprint and multipliers of regional wind power, differentiating between technology type and lifetime phase. Additionally, the economic and environmental impacts of wind power expansion are evaluated. Lower Saxony, a pioneering wind power region in Northern Germany, is used as a case study. The methodological approach involves constructing a regional input-output table, integrating wind power sectors and developing scenarios consistent with policy objectives. Results reveal the significant economic footprint of wind power in Lower Saxony and emphasize the importance of detailed regional datasets. Onshore wind key component manufacturing and offshore wind installation generate the highest economic multipliers. Offshore wind has greater economic impacts per unit of electricity than onshore wind. Wind power expansion can create substantial gross economic gains, but outcomes strongly depend on regional supply chain integration. Net effects include job losses and substantial reductions in emissions and water use. Policy implications include strengthening upstream industries, coping with labor market dynamics, and enhancing regionalized data collection. The study highlights the need for spatially focused approaches to capture the regional dimension of the energy transition.

title: Critical roles of anion identity in activating potassium-modified Fe-based oxygen carriers in biomass chemical looping gasification
abstract: This study investigates the critical role of anion identity in optimizing biomass chemical looping gasification performance using potassium-modified oolitic hematite oxygen carriers. Agricultural waste, specifically corncob char, was treated to produce high-quality syngas, focusing on how potassium salt precursors influenced the reaction mechanism and material properties. Results show that K2CO3 modification enhances carbon conversion ratio to 94.3% and syngas selectivity to 88.6%, attributed to a highly active K2Fe22O34 phase and a stable porous architecture. Anion-induced phase evolution was verified: K2CO3 promoted gradual transformation of iron-silicate composite into K2Fe22O34, while KCl induced low-melting-point eutectics causing sintering, and K2SO4 formed stable complex sulfates restricting active site exposure. Furthermore, reduced activation energies were observed for lattice oxygen release; Fe-20K showed a second reduction peak at 838°C compared with 975°C for the unmodified carrier, indicating enhanced redox kinetics. CO32− donation created surface oxygen vacancies and electron-donating effects that weakened Fe-O bonds, whereas Cl− and SO42− introduced electron-withdrawing inductive effects stabilizing lattice oxygen. Optimal process conditions—950°C, oxygen carrier to biomass ratio of 0.5, and water flow rate of 0.03 mL/min—balanced reactivity and structural integrity. In conclusion, this work provides data support for rational design of cost-effective oxygen carriers, offering an efficient pathway to integrate biomass waste and minerals into chemical looping gasification systems.

title: Solar-driven tubular Co2(OH)PO4/carbon nitride S-scheme heterojunctions for renewable H2 production and CO2 reduction to solar fuels
abstract: The scalable synthesis of green chemical fuels via artificial photosynthesis represents a cornerstone strategy for buffering intermittent renewable energy and advancing global carbon neutrality. However, the practical engineering deployment of this technology is severely constrained by suboptimal solar-to-fuel conversion efficiencies at the catalytic interface. Herein, a tubular S-scheme Co2(OH)PO4@CN (CoHP@CN) heterojunction was fabricated via a pre-coordination-mediated in-situ growth strategy to facilitate solar energy harvesting. Characterizations reveal that a directional internal electric field (IEF) drives an S-scheme charge pathway, significantly reducing transfer resistance while preserving strong redox capabilities. Benefiting from these kinetic features, the heterojunction delivers exceptional solar fuel production performance, achieving a CO yield of 383.40 μmol g−1 (over 4 h) and H2 evolution of 4657.40 μmol g−1 (within 2 h). This study underscores the power of precise interface engineering in modulating charge dynamics, offering practical insights for scalable solar-to-chemical energy storage and renewable energy deployment.

title: Ruthenium nanoparticles embedded in Mn-doped Fe5Ni4S8 pentlandite with outstanding bifunctional electrolytic hydrogen and oxygen evolution reactions
abstract: Alkaline water electrolysis represents a pivotal route to scalable green hydrogen production, yet the rational design of bifunctional electrocatalysts that simultaneously boost hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) kinetics remains a fundamental challenge. Herein, we develop a hetero-structured electrocatalyst with Ru nanoparticles anchored on Mn-doped Fe5Ni4S8 (denoted as Ru/MFNS) via a one-step solvothermal strategy. Distinct from single-element modification, our design integrates dual regulation: Mn doping tailors the carrier morphology into an interconnected cross-linked nanoarchitecture to enlarge the electrochemically active area, and modulates the d-band electronic structure of Fe/Ni to optimize intermediate adsorption; subsequent Ru loading constructs a built-in electric field at the heterointerface driven by work function difference, which substantially lowers the water dissociation energy barrier in alkaline media. Benefiting from the strong interfacial synergy, the self-supported Ru/MFNS exhibits exceptional bifunctional performance: it delivers an HER overpotential of 90 mV at 10 mA cm−2 with a Tafel slope of 73 mV dec−1, and requires only 286 mV to reach 50 mA cm−2 for OER. When assembled into a symmetric alkaline electrolyzer, the catalyst achieves 10 mA cm−2 at a cell voltage of 1.56 V and maintains stable operation for 120 h at 50 mA cm−2. This work demonstrates that coupling heteroatom doping with noble-metal interfacial engineering is an effective pathway to construct high-efficiency, low-noble-metal electrocatalysts for practical water splitting.

title: Accurate installation angle determination for bifacial photovoltaics using hybrid parameter extraction and outdoor experiments
abstract: Bifacial photovoltaic modules achieve higher energy yield than monofacial systems by capturing irradiance on both surfaces, but accurately predicting performance remains challenging due to complex optical–thermal–electrical interactions. This study develops and experimentally validates a coupled optical–thermal–electrical model for bifacial photovoltaic modules under real outdoor conditions in Tehran, Iran. The framework integrates view-factor geometry for optical analysis, multi-layer heat transfer modeling, and a single-diode electrical formulation. A hybrid optimization procedure combining a genetic algorithm extracts electrical parameters, ensuring robust convergence and accurate identification. The model is validated against experimental measurements from a 580 W bifacial module, achieving a mean absolute percentage error of 4.61% for predicted power. Parametric analyses investigate the effects of tilt angle and azimuth orientation. Results show that at a tilt angle equal to site latitude (35°), annual energy yields of east–west and south-facing configurations are nearly identical (1286.3 vs. 1279.5 kWh)—a finding contrary to conventional monofacial behavior. The validated model provides a reliable tool for predicting bifacial photovoltaic performance, optimizing installation geometry, and supporting system design. This assessment framework offers practical guidance for maximizing energy yield in semi-arid regions and similar environments.

title: Quantification of building demand uncertainty on the operational performance evaluation and capacity optimizations in building microgrid system design
abstract: Building microgrid is an efficient system infrastructure to deliver energy flexibility in power grids. Building demand uncertainty is a major factor that affect the effectiveness of microgrid design and the stability of microgrid operations. Current studies have not comprehensively reflected the influence of demand uncertainty over long term microgrid operations and capacity design plans, limiting practical applications that account for uncertainty. This study proposed an analytical framework of assessing the building demand uncertainty and its impact on microgrid design optimizations. The research aims to answer two research questions: (1) How long period of simulation is required to evaluate the microgrid operation performance under different levels of demand uncertainty? (2) How will the optimal capacities of microgrid subsystems change with the increment of building demand uncertainty? The results from case study with repeated simulations on commercial, office and government buildings suggest that the required length of simulation period increases exponentially as demand uncertainty increases. With every 1% of increase on building demand uncertainty, the optimal PV and battery capacity decreases by 0.0260% and 0.0587% respectively. The results massively support the efficient and effective assessment of demand uncertainty in operation performance evaluations and capacity design optimizations in realistic building microgrid design practices.

title: An exergoeconomic exploration of a solar-driven humidification-dehumidification desalination
abstract: Solar-assisted humidification-dehumidification (HDH) systems offer potential for brine treatment in zero liquid discharge applications. This work presents a multi-objective exergoeconomic optimization of a solar-assisted HDH system. The system is modeled through component-wise mass, energy, exergy, and cost balances following the SPECO methodology under steady-state assumptions and coupled with an annual quasi-dynamic simulation (8760 hourly runs). Five performance metrics are evaluated: Gain Output Ratio, Freshwater Production, Exergy Efficiency, Levelized Cost of Water, and Exergy Cost of Water. The model identifies optimal design bounded by second-law feasibility constraints, across varying water-air mass flow ratios (0.694-0.857), top air temperatures (55-80 °C), and water inlet salinities (25-75 g/kg). Under the equal-weight multi-objective framework, the system achieves its best aggregate performance at 75 g/kg feed salinity, suggesting greater suitability for brine treatment than for conventional seawater desalination under the tested operating conditions. Valorizing the concentrated brine as a coproduct reduces the exergy-based water cost by 5.3-18.2 $/m3 relative to the levelized cost. Across six semi-arid Chilean locations, inland sites yield 39.2% more solar thermal energy and reduce boiler operation by 336 h per year, lowering both cost metrics. Results support application-specific optimization frameworks for future HDH system designs.

title: Advanced wind-cooling coordination by tensor train based higher order dynamic mode decomposition
abstract: The global transition to a carbon-neutral energy system faces a significant challenge due to the rapid increase in building cooling requirements. Integrating wind energy, which is cost-competitive but highly intermittent, into building cooling processes presents a promising way to achieve sustainable development. However, because of the significant temporal and spatial mismatch between supply and demand, it still encounters challenges. To address this issue, a new framework is proposed that combines tensor train decomposition and higher order dynamic mode decomposition. This framework starts by compressing high-dimensional temporal and spatial dynamics into a low-rank tensor train format. Then, higher order dynamic mode decomposition is applied to identify the dominant temporal and spatial modes, and their dynamic behaviors. This enables the implementation of an effective model predictive control strategy for real-time coordination. Compared with existed methods such as canonical polyadic decomposition and long short-term memory networks, the proposed framework reduces the amount of wind curtailment by 7.2% and operating costs by 21.4%–25.2% while maintaining thermal comfort violation rates below 3.5%. Furthermore, the framework achieves 95.1% prediction accuracy with an online computation time of only 0.45 s per control step, fully meeting real-time requirements.

title: Effect of steam-enriched CO2 atmosphere on the properties of biochar derived from food waste gasification
abstract: Agro-industrial residues (food waste) represent a significant source of feedstocks that possess, both material and energy potentials. This study examined the valorisation of sunflower husks, buckwheat husks, cherry stones, and tomato waste through gasification under CO 2 and steam-enriched CO 2 atmospheres at 900 °C. The biochemical composition of these feedstocks was characterised by 28–78 wt% lignocellulosic fractions content and from 0.6 to 17 wt% of lipids. Solid residue (biochar) yields ranged from 9.1% (sunflower husks, CO 2 + H 2 O) to 28.1% (tomato waste, CO 2 ), while carbon content reached up to 88 wt% for cherry stone. The introduction of steam reduced the yield by 35%, but significantly increased the specific surface area from 410 to 881 m 2 /g and from 224 to 823 m 2 /g for buckwheat husks and sunflower husks, respectively. Lignin-rich feedstocks produced more aromatic and thermally stable structures (R 50 > 0.45). FT-IR spectra confirmed the loss of hydroxyl and carbonyl groups and formation of condensed aromatic structures. These findings show that biochemical composition of food waste significantly influences carbonisation behaviour and surface functionality. Furthermore, they provide a framework for optimizing gasification conditions to produce biochars that can be used as bio-based materials in catalysis, adsorption, and carbon sequestration.

title: Hydrothermally synthesized sites of NiFe-LDHs anchored on the biomass-derived hydrochar for electrocatalytic performance
abstract: Oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is the rate-limiting step during the electrochemical water splitting, which hinders the sustainable production of hydrogen energy to a large extent. For this reason, we established a one-pot approach for the in-situ growth of NiFe-LDHs anchored on the biomass-derived hydrochar, and the activity caused by its structural features were systemically explored with the help of several techniques. Relevant results showed that the interlaced nanosheets consisting of metallic nanoparticles were clearly found with high crystallinity, suggesting that the carbonized substances only provided sufficient sites for the in-situ formation of NiFe-LDHs without interfering its surface porosity. Meanwhile, Ni2+ was transferred into Ni3+ (i.e., NiOOH) with the introduction of Fe atoms, functioning as the active sites for OER performance in 1.0 M KOH solution; among them, the sample with a ratio of Ni:Fe at 4:1 exhibited an excellent η10 and Tafel slope at 299 mV and 72.3 mV·dec−1, respectively. Then, the use of surfactants enabled precise control over the carbonaceous supports from microsphere to nano-flask sharp, whose specific surface areas accessible for the NiFe oxides could further improved the OER activity because of its smaller size as well as the well-dispersed distributions.As a result, this study provides new insights into the design and facile preparation of carbon-enhanced electrocatalysts from biomass, which is of great potential for the OER application in the near future.

title: Optimized design of periodic open cellular structure for enhancing heat discharging performance of metal hydride reactor for thermochemical heat storage based on entransy theory
abstract: The inherently low effective thermal conductivity of metal hydride (MH) beds significantly restricts the heat discharging performance of MH reactors for thermal energy storage systems. To address this challenge, a metallic periodic open cellular structure (POCS) can be integrated into MH beds to enhance heat transfer performance. In this study, a two-dimensional axisymmetric mathematical model was developed to simulate the reactors equipped with various POCS configurations, including single-layer and multi-layer discrete gradient designs. Using the entransy dissipation extremum principle via a simplified one-dimensional model, the radial effective thermal conductivity (λe) distribution was optimized by adjusting the volume fraction distribution of POCS within MH beds. Results indicate that the optimized POCS configuration significantly enhances the heat transfer performance by minimizing entransy dissipation through optimal alignment between the λe distribution and the radial heat flux distribution. Furthermore, increasing the number of discrete gradient layers from two to four yields better heat transfer characteristics, but exhibits a minimal effect on the reaction time and gravimetric exergy-output rate, with maximum differences of only 100 s and 0.5 W kg−1, respectively. Compared with the two-layer design, the performance-to-cost index for the four-layer design decreased by 13.4%. Therefore, the two-layer discrete gradient POCS configuration is recommended as a practical choice for balancing heat transfer performance and design simplicity in the MH-based thermal energy storage systems.

title: Carnot battery integrated with ultra-high-temperature heat pump and parabolic trough collector for hybrid PV-concentrating solar power plants
abstract: Integrating Carnot Battery (CB) with concentrating solar power (CSP) offers a promising pathway for large-scale photovoltaic (PV) electricity storage and dispatchable power generation. This work presented a CB integrated with a hybrid PV-parabolic trough CSP plant, where an ultra-high-temperature air heat pump and an sCO2 power cycle are employed for charging and discharging. Thermodynamic models, solar thermal models and Monte Carlo economic model are developed. Exergy analysis indicates that the upgrade effect of the heat pump allows a small solar exergy input to replace a substantial portion of electricity, resulting in average relative improvements of 42.4% in round-trip efficiency and 55.4% in overall solar utilization efficiency compared with the EH baseline. Parametric analysis shows that the maximum round-trip efficiency of 63.2% is achieved when solar thermal energy is used only as the low-temperature heat source of the heat pump under typical conditions. A techno-economic multi-objective optimization reveals trade-off between efficiency and the levelized cost of storage (LCOS), and identifies the optimal configuration in which solar heat is additionally used for molten salt preheating. Finally, seasonal operation analysis indicates that compared with conventional parabolic trough CSP plants, the proposed CB extends equivalent generation duration by 82.5%, with 24.7% of this gain attributed to the heat pump upgrade effect.

title: Sustainable biogas upgrading using renewable ammonia from pig slurry: integration of microbial electrolysis cells and hydrophobic membrane technology
abstract: Biogas upgrading is required to increase methane concentration and meet grid-injection standards. Conventional absorbents such as monoethanolamine (MEA) and synthetic ammonium hydroxide (NH 4 OH) provide high CO 2 removal but involve high costs, energy-intensive regeneration, and non-renewable resources. This study proposes an integrated approach coupling ammonium recovery from pig slurry in microbial electrolysis cells (MEC) with its reuse as a CO 2 absorbent in hollow fiber membrane contactors (HFMC). The recovered ammonium was evaluated against water, MEA, and synthetic NH 4 OH under different gas-to-liquid ratios and absorbent concentrations. Water achieved limited CH 4 enrichment (∼80%), whereas MEA and synthetic NH 4 OH provided >90% CO 2 removal. MEC-derived ammonium achieved >95% CH 4 and <2% CO 2 with real biogas, demonstrating its potential as a renewable absorbent. This dual valorisation approach enhances the economic and environmental sustainability of biogas upgrading, positioning MEC-derived ammonium as a viable alternative to conventional absorbents.

title: Assessing the potential for floating offshore wind farms in Irish waters: A comprehensive methodology and findings
abstract: ABSTRACT The potential of Irish waters to support floating offshore wind farms has not been fully recognised. A novel and robust methodology has been developed and implemented to address this research question and define the capabilities of floating offshore wind energy in Irish waters. This approach features a meticulous selection of hierarchically organised criteria aligned with legislation, policy, and best practices from the wind industry. The delineated area identifies locations where floating offshore wind farms could possibly be developed with limited technical and legal risk. Additionally, the study outlines key characteristics of the area, including bathymetry, wind conditions, total installed capacity, and energy yield. The identified area for potential development comprises only 13.7% of the initially surveyed section of the exclusive economic zone; nonetheless, it has substantial potential, capable of hosting a total power capacity of 246 GW or 307 GW, depending on the layout scenario. Remarkably, nearly 80% of this power can be developed in water depths up to 200 m. Furthermore, the capacity factor of the reference wind turbine ranges from 56.7% to 64.1%, with a gross annual energy output of between 53.1 and 59.9 GWh per year per wind turbine.

title: Novel anode catalyst layer design towards gradient catalyst distribution for boosting performance of PEM water electrolyzers
