abstract: To improve catalyst utilization of proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolyzers, the novel catalyst coated membrane (CCM) with gradient catalyst distribution with varied loading along the flow channel was designed. The effect of flow channel distribution among catalyst loading zones in the inlet and outlet regions on the performance of PEM water electrolyzers was systematically investigated. The results showed that the CCMs with gradient catalyst loading showed significantly better performance than the CCM with uniform loading. In particular, the CCM with 1.38 mg/cm2 catalyst loading at the catalyst loading area ratio of 5:8 (CCM-5:8) exhibited the lowest cell voltage with high catalyst utilization. At 5 A/cm2, CCM-5:8 achieved a cell voltage of 2.216 V@80 °C, 96 mV lower than the CCM with 1.5 mg/cm2 uniform loading (CCM-1.5). At 2.2 V, the current density of CCM-5:8 was up to 4.90 A/cm2. And the mass activity of CCM-5:8 reached 3.55 A/mg, 23.26 % higher than that of CCM-1.5, along with a lower average degradation rate for 100 h. These improvements are attributed to the optimized structure of the segmented catalyst layer, which ensures more uniform current density distribution and enhanced proton transport. The gradient loading design significantly boosts catalyst utilization by reducing catalyst loading and effectively reduces iridium noble metal catalyst loading and improves performance of PEM water electrolyzers. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of gradient catalyst distribution and offers practical guidance for developing high-performance, low-cost PEM water electrolyzers.

title: Energy pile thermal performance in saturated layered ground considering mixed convection: A numerical modeling and machine learning approach
abstract: Geothermal piles, serving as both structural and thermal elements, play a vital role in sustainable development by reducing energy consumption. These geo-structures exploit geothermal energy for building heating and cooling across different seasons. Careful consideration of the governing heat transfer mechanisms is essential for accurate design of energy geo-structures. Although many studies have examined the thermo-hydraulic behavior of geothermal piles, such simulations often involve high computational costs and are therefore less common in practical applications. However, recent advancements in machine learning and data science technologies suggest that trained machine learning models can provide a promising pathway to bridge the gap between research-oriented analyses of energy piles and practical design applications. In this study, a coupled thermo-hydraulic finite element model was developed to assess the thermal performance of a geothermal pile embedded in saturated layered soil, accounting for heat conduction and mixed convection. The results indicate that thermal performance is primarily controlled by the effective thermal conductivity of the surrounding soil. Accordingly, sandy soil exhibits the highest thermal performance, with values 59.6% higher than clayey soil and 22.1% higher than layered soil. Four machine learning models were developed to predict outlet fluid temperature, with the random forest model achieving the highest accuracy across five sensor placement scenarios. Optimal prediction accuracy was achieved when the sensors were positioned downstream of the groundwater flow at a radial distance of 0.6 m from the pile center. These findings provide valuable insights into energy pile site selection and the design of temperature sensor placement strategies.

title: Developing response surface methodology and machine learning for analyzing the continuous biodiesel production in a controlled ultrasonic micro-channel
abstract: A controlled ultrasonic micro-channel was introduced for increasing biodiesel production through waves’ irradiation and cavitation phenomenon. Two oils of flax and sesame seeds were analyzed, alone and mixed. Flaxseed oil with methanol played an important role in producing the biodiesel in the presence of potassium hydroxide as catalyst. Response surface methodology (RSM) designed the experiments by Box-Behnken approach. Results revealed that maximum fatty acid methyl ester (FAME %) of 99.66 % was attained in optimum independent variables (reaction temperature of 64 C°, catalyst amounts of 1.352, methanol to oil ratio of 8.472:1, and 5 piezoelectric sets), and a residence time of 350 s. Ultrasonic waves not only increased the FAME % but prepared the energy of the reaction (specialized power and frequency). Moreover, a quadratic model was developed and the variables were examined due to analysis of variance. The reaction temperature and interaction between catalyst amount and number of piezoelectric presented a significant degree of importance in the experiments. To further evaluation of modeling and obtaining a general model, machine learning was employed through artificial neural network (ANN). The outputs confirmed that the ANN was powerful in predicting the experimental data with a higher agreement in comparison with the RSM.

title: Technical assessment of Agave sisalana leaves as feedstock for integrated first- and second-generation ethanol production
abstract: Agave sisalana , widely cultivated in northeastern Brazil, holds great socioeconomic importance, although its leaves remain underutilized. This study evaluated their potential as feedstock for integrated first- (1G) and second-generation (2G) ethanol production. In the 1G route, leaf juice underwent acid hydrolysis and fermentation, yielding 40.70 g/L ethanol with 74.00% efficiency using Ethanol Red®. In the 2G route, a fractional factorial design optimized bagasse pretreatment; the best condition (30 min, 180°C, 15% solids, 0.5% acid) achieved 60.31% cellulose and 80.32% hemicellulose conversion. Although inhibitors were generated, detoxification enabled efficient fermentation, resulting in 27.44 g/L ethanol with an 83.59% yield using the GMO strain Celere2L. Overall, 80.90 L of ethanol per ton of leaves was obtained, demonstrating A. sisalana 's potential as a sustainable feedstock for integrated 1G–2G ethanol production and reinforcing its relevance for biofuel development and energy diversification in semi-arid regions.

title: Performance analysis of a distributed renewable energy system integrating ground source heat pumps and fuel cells with controlled hybrid energy storage
abstract: Battery integrated with hydrogen storage has emerged as a potential way for improving energy utilization and reliability of solar-driven distributed energy systems. However, solar intermittency often forces electrolyzer to operate under low-load conditions, which reduces energy conversion efficiency and hydrogen production. This work develops a hybrid energy storage control method by considering the electrolyzer operational status. The short-term storage capability of the battery is used to suppress low-load operation of electrolyzer while absorbing surplus power. A distributed energy system integrating photovoltaic/thermal, ground source heat pump, electrolyzer, battery and fuel cell is developed to provide cooling, heating and power for an integrated building, which is established in TRNSYS. Furthermore, a multi-objective optimization framework is formulated, considering energy efficiency, economic performance, environmental impact and electrolyzer operational characteristics. The optimal system configuration is determined using TOPSIS–EWM decision-making method, and comparative analysis is conducted for cases with/without battery and electrolyzer control method. The results indicate that compared with the case without battery and control method, high-load operating time ratio of electrolyzer under high-load condition increases by 79.73%, accompanied by a 1.31% improvement in energy efficiency. And battery-assisted control shifts electrolyzer operation toward higher-efficiency regimes under fluctuating renewable conditions while the battery regulates short-term power fluctuations and hydrogen storage enables long-term energy balancing. The proposed hybrid energy storage control method based on electrolyzer operation status provides an effective pathway for the coordinated utilization of hydrogen storage and battery in renewable energy systems and improves the development of hydrogen-based technology in integrated parks.

title: Hydrazine enhanced seawater electrolysis using a highly efficient Pd-Ni(OH)2 catalyst for green hydrogen production
abstract: Direct seawater electrolysis offers a sustainable route for large scale green hydrogen production but suffers from high energy requirements due to the sluggish OER. Here, we report a Pd-doped Ni(OH)2 catalyst supported on nickel foam that enables efficient hydrogen generation by coupling HzOR with HER. The optimized Pd-Ni(OH)2 catalyst delivers an exceptional current density of 1100 mA cm−2 at 0.9 V and 500 mA cm−2 at only 0.4 V vs RHE. HER measurements revealed that Pd-Ni(OH)2 in hydrazine-free seawater exhibited a higher current density of 610 mA cm−2 at - 0.8 V compared with 296 mA cm−2 in seawater containing 0.3 M hydrazine hydrate. Computational investigation reveal the Pd synergistic role in Ni(OH)2, where Pd 5d to N 2p electron transfer facilitates hydrazine activation and lowers the potential-determining step. The catalyst exhibits remarkable durability, maintaining 0.6 A for 120 h without degradation, highlighting Pd-Ni(OH)2 as a promising platform for low voltage, energy efficient seawater electrolysis.
keywords: Hydrazine oxidation reaction (HzOR) and green hydrogen production

title: Reactive molecular dynamics of hydrogen production from hydrothermolysis of ammonia borane with water supply
abstract: Ammonia borane (AB) is a potential hydrogen storage material with a high hydrogen mass fraction. The effect of water supply on hydrogen evolution from AB is studied with different initial water/AB molar ratios (0, 3.1, 4.0, and 5.0, being notated as SAB, S155, S200, and S250, respectively). The SAB system corresponds to the pyrolysis of pure AB, the S155 and S200 systems correspond to the hydrothermolysis of AB with limited water supply, and the S250 system corresponds to the hydrothermolysis of AB with sufficient water supply. Comparing the three situations of hydrogen production from AB, the decomposition pathway of AB is investigated by reactive force-field molecular dynamics simulations (ReaxFF-MD), and product distributions are obtained. In contrast to pyrolysis, water accelerates the hydrogen release rate from AB and promotes the formation of H2. The simulation results show that in S200 with the limited water supply, there is slight polymerization, high H2 yield, and fewer NH3 by-products. The calculated apparent activation energy of the S200 system is 60.2 ± 8 kJ/mol. The effective H2 release is achieved by hydrothermolysis of AB under water supply and heating without any catalyst. These studies are significant for evaluating the potential application of AB in stationary systems for high-temperature fuel cells.

title: Design and operation of fully renewable integrated energy system (FRIES) coupling multiple forms of energy using two-stage optimization method
abstract: With the continuous deterioration of environmental issues, renewable energy has attracted significant attention. However, renewable energy may not be able to meet diverse load demands due to intermittency and singularity uncertainty. The integrated energy system (IES) can couple multiple forms of energy, achieve multi-energy complementarity, and meet users’ diverse demands. This work presents a full renewable integrated energy system (FRIES) with solar, wind, and geothermal energy (GE) as input energy. A two-stage optimization method is used to obtain the optimal capacity configuration and operation strategy in three load scenarios. The system performance of multi energy complementary modes was analyzed, and the effects of capacity changes in renewable energy conversion equipment on system performance were evaluated. Results show that compared to wind energy, GE and solar energy have better universality and efficiency. Multi energy complementarity can significantly improve the environmental friendliness of the system, but slightly reduce its economic efficiency. In high-single-load demand scenarios such as resident and industry, increasing the input of renewable energy can not only reduce carbon emissions, but also lower the cost of the system.

title: Experimental investigation of a pyramid solar still incorporating pulsating heat pipe and phase change material-filled cans
abstract: Solar stills are gaining attention due to their simple operation and environmentally friendly nature; however, their productivity remains significantly lower than that of conventional desalination technologies. To address this limitation, phase change materials (PCMs) have been explored for their superior thermal energy storage capabilities, while pulsating heat pipes (PHPs) offer enhanced heat transfer performance. The novelty of the present work lies in the systematic and synergistic integration of PCM-filled recycled aluminium cans with a pulsating heat pipe in a pyramid solar still. The PHP rapidly transfers thermal energy to the basin water during daytime, enhancing evaporation, while the PCM stores excess thermal energy and gradually releases it after sunset, sustaining evaporation and freshwater production during off-sunshine hours. Unlike previous studies that examined PCM or PHP independently, this study experimentally demonstrates their combined effect on evaporation enhancement, energy–exergy performance, and freshwater yield through a comparative investigation of four configurations: a conventional solar still (CSS) and three modified solar stills (MSS + PCM, MSS + PHP, and MSS + PCM + PHP). The freshwater yield was found as 2.93 L/m2 in CSS, and it was increased by 44%, 38% and 77% in MSS + PCM, MSS + PHP, and MSS + PCM + PHP, respectively. The superior enhancement in MSS + PCM + PHP is mainly attributed to enhanced evaporation due to PHP integration and night-time production due to PCM. The maximum yield in MSS + PCM + PHP was also justified by maximum energy and exergy efficiencies of 41.96% and 3.88%, respectively. The evaporation heat transfer coefficient was found significantly higher than other heat transfer modes, and it was increased by 47.6% in MSS + PCM + PHP, compared to CSS. The economic analysis indicated MSS + PCM + PHP as the most economical with a cost per litre of 0.0115 $/L, and a minimum payback period of 133 days. The environment analysis suggested a maximum of 64.28% CO2 savings in MSS + PCM + PHP.

title: Increase in corn ethanol production in Brazil: Examining changes in dynamic interconnectedness
abstract: Brazil is a major producer of ethanol in the world. Traditionally, this type of production is derived from sugarcane. However, in recent years, the increase in corn production in the country has directed part of this surplus toward corn-based ethanol. This movement has changed biofuel production dynamics to new areas in the country’s Center-West, where grain production is dominant. Therefore, this study examines the dynamic connectedness between regional ethanol and corn prices in Brazil. A TVP-VAR model was applied, considering the specifications proposed by Antonakakis et al. (2020). First, we examined the transmission between the major sugarcane-based ethanol region in the southeast and the new corn-based ethanol region in the Center-West. Second, we examined the regional interconnectedness between ethanol and corn in the Center-West production spots. DCC-GARCH and wavelet coherence analysis were also applied to complement the regional analysis. The results indicate an increase in ethanol volatility connectedness between producing states after the corn-based ethanol outbreak in 2019/20. At the regional level, our findings suggest a slight increase in the connection between ethanol and corn prices, especially in the state of Mato Grosso, where significant co-movements were observed in the recent period. These findings are important to show that the new ethanol feedstock in Brazil can potentially affect ethanol price volatility dynamics at the country level as well as the contagion between corn and ethanol at the regional level.

title: Quantifying microbial, enzymatic, and acid-driven pathways of lignocellulose degradation and their impact on methane production in Sudangrass silage
abstract: Lignocellulosic biomass represents a promising feedstock for the sustainable circular bioeconomy. However, its recalcitrant structure necessitates efficient pretreatment. Converting lignocellulosic biomass into renewable energy via anaerobic digestion (AD) often exhibits low degradation efficiency and thus requires optimization to enhance conversion efficiency. Ensiling is a promising, low-cost, and environmentally friendly biological pretreatment method, yet the individual contributions and interactive mechanisms of microbial-, enzymatic-, and acid-driven pathways during lignocellulose degradation have not been fully elucidated. In this work, gamma-ray sterilization, high-temperature enzyme inactivation, and organic acid simulation were employed to isolate and quantify the effects of enzymatic-driven (ED), acid-driven (AD), microbial-driven (BD), and synergistic (SYN) pathways on lignocellulose degradation and methane production during Sudangrass ensiling. Results demonstrated that the BD treatment, driven by synergistic microbial activity and organic acids, achieved the highest lignocellulose degradation rate (LDR, 24.5%) and methane yield (295.20 mL/g VS). The absence of active microbiota in the AD and ED treatments significantly decreased LDR (13.6% and 4.36%, respectively) and reduced methane production (275.50 mL/g VS and 274.40 mL/g VS). The SYN treatment had moderate performance with LDR of 20.3% and methane yield of 284.20 mL/g VS. Structural equation modeling (SEqM) revealed that enzymatic and acid pathways affected methane yield only indirectly via water-soluble carbohydrate release, while the microbial pathway exerted dual direct and indirect effects by simultaneously promoting lignocellulose degradation and sugar metabolism. Furthermore, the potential synergy between microbes and endogenous enzymes was inhibited by rapid acidification. These findings confirm that microbial-driven processes are the dominant mechanism enhancing lignocellulose biodegradability and methane production. This work provides mechanistic insights for optimizing ensiling-based pretreatment to boost the efficiency of anaerobic digestion of lignocellulosic biomass.

title: Alkaline thermal treatment of algae for hydrogen production: Insights into the effect of biochemical components
abstract: Alkaline thermal treatment is a promising route for H2 production from algal biomass, offering high H2 yields under mild conditions, in situ capture of CO/CO2, and direct processing of wet algal biomass. However, the H2 formation pathways of the major biochemical components during alkaline thermal treatment are still poorly understood, which hinders the rational optimization of this process for hydrogen production. In this study, carbohydrate-rich, protein-rich, and lipid-rich algae were used as representative feedstocks to elucidate how the major components govern hydrogen production. The results showed that lipids were the most favorable fraction for H2 production, with the lipid-rich feedstock achieving the highest H2 yield of 35.90 mmol g−1 at 600 °C. The three major components exhibited distinct temperature-dependent H2 release. Carbohydrates contributed mainly to the earliest H2 release through dehydration, cleavage, and dehydrogenation of oxygen-rich structures. Proteins showed the most intense H2 release between 330 and 350 °C, accompanied by significant CH4 formation, which was mainly attributed to cracking and dehydrogenation of protein-derived intermediates. In contrast, lipids showed a delayed main H2 peak at 410 °C. Above 450 °C, lipids further dominated H2 formation through the stepwise conversion of unsaturated intermediates, long-chain intermediates, and residual char. These findings offer mechanistic guidance for feedstock selection, process optimization, and the rational design of efficient algal alkaline thermal treatment systems.

title: Experimental and numerical characterization of a large-stroke winch-based power take-off for wave energy converters
abstract: Point absorber wave energy converters face critical survivability and efficiency challenges due to limited stroke constraints and destructive end-stop collisions in extreme seas. This study presents a 1 kW-scale winch-driven power take-off system with a 10 m active stroke, designed to geometrically decouple the internal drivetrain from constrained motion rails. To evaluate the drivetrain without hydrodynamic uncertainty, land-based crane trials imposed repeatable 10 m tether displacements, while the prescribed 1 m/s line velocity was selected to be broadly consistent with a 1:6 Froude-scaled representation of full-scale extreme vertical motion. The controlled actuation isolated the internal energy cascade and enabled stage-wise separation of speed-dependent mechanical losses from load-dependent electromagnetic losses across resistive loads of 4.5 to 45 Ω. Experiments identified an optimal internal conversion efficiency near 18 Ω, beyond which high-current effects degraded performance. Diagnostic analysis further showed that constant-parameter generator predictions failed when stator current exceeded the 5.16 A rated limit, causing over-predictions of current, torque, and electrical power due to armature reaction and magnetic saturation. To capture this behavior, a multi-domain physics-based model combined a no-load-calibrated viscous rotational damper with a current-dependent back electromotive force coefficient roll-off profile. This correction eliminated high-current prediction bias and restored agreement across the mechanical-to-electrical energy cascade. These findings demonstrate that single-point static tuning is insufficient under transient overloads. The validated model supports future upscaling and parameter-scheduled load control to maintain optimal operation, mitigate saturation, and maximize wave-to-wire energy extraction in irregular seas.

title: Sequencing batch high-rate algal ponds: An alternative approach to sustainable biodiesel and ALE production with microalgae-bacteria consortia cultivated in domestic wastewater
abstract: High-rate algal ponds (HRAP) are cost-effective systems for producing microalgal-bacterial aggregates from wastewater, forming a consortium rich in alginate-like exopolymers (ALE) and lipids suitable for third-generation biodiesel. However, the effects of sequencing batch (SB) operation in HRAP remain unknown. Therefore, the present study evaluated the dynamics of algal genera, sewage treatment, ALE and lipid contents, and biodiesel quality of an HRAP (2400 L) operated in SB over 134 days. After the consortium formation (d0-d20), the pond reached a stability period between days 66 and 128, demonstrating a relative abundance of >80% of Cyclotella sp. and nitrogen, phosphorus, and chemical oxygen demand removals of 90.1 ± 3.7%, 40.1 ± 7.3%, and 66.6% ± 7.6%, respectively. ALE content reached 87.4 ± 19.3 mg/gTSS. The most efficient extraction (Soxhlet + chloroform: methanol 2:1) yielded an average lipid content of 11 ± 2 %, and the most abundant methyl esters were C16:0 (35.74%), C18:0 (21.01%), and C16:1 (12.08%). The biodiesel produced met international standards for cetane number, iodine value, kinematic viscosity, and density, while also exhibiting a higher heating value consistent with other renewable energy sources, such as soybean. These results imply increased flexibility in the use of HRAP-MABA systems through SB operation and demonstrate the production of high-quality biodiesel from predictable biomass, even under the adverse conditions of open systems.

title: High-fidelity numerical simulation and performance analysis of Magnus-effect vertical axis wind turbine
abstract: Recent advancements in wind energy have introduced the Magnus-effect vertical axis wind turbine, a turbine design utilizing rotating cylinders with rectifier plates to generate unidirectional torque via the Magnus effect. Despite successful prototypes, detailed numerical studies on the aerodynamic interactions within this configuration remain limited. This study investigates the performance of multi-bladed Magnus-effect vertical axis wind turbines in turbulent flow and explores various rotor configurations. High-fidelity, time-dependent three-dimensional numerical simulations were conducted using the direct-forcing immersed boundary method coupled with a large eddy simulation turbulence model. The in-house code was accelerated through general-purpose computing on graphics processing units and coupled with an improved volume-of-solid algorithm for efficient fluid–structure interaction modeling. Dynamic simulations of two- and three-bladed rotors at constant tip speed ratios show that both designs perform effectively when properly configured. At a tip speed ratio of 0.7, the three-bladed rotor has a higher peak power coefficient of 0.443 than the two-bladed rotor, which has a peak power coefficient of 0.393. In addition, the three-bladed configuration demonstrates superior performance at low tip speed ratios, indicating enhanced aerodynamic efficiency. Blade spacing is optimal at R=2D for the three-bladed rotor and R=1.5D for the two-bladed rotor, demonstrating the critical impact of wake interactions.

title: Ultrasound-enhanced selective fermentation improves lipid recovery from microalgae
abstract: To enhance microalgal cell disruption and multitargeted product recovery, this study combined pretreatments with selective anaerobic fermentation, using microalgae as sole substrate. Comparative analyses showed NaOH pretreatment favored biogas and VFAs production, while ultrasonic pretreatment improved lipid extraction efficiency (yield and concentration) with minimal degradation, balancing energy and material recovery. Optimal ultrasonic-assisted fermentation conditions (4.4 min, 60 μm amplitude, 10 h) via response surface methodology gave ∼80% lipid extraction based on total lipid content. Continuous-flow evaluation showed reduced residence time increased daily gas to 4.4 L, with 83.36% lipid rate at 10 h. The prepared biodiesel presents a cetane number > 60, satisfying EN (≥51) and ASTM (≥47) standards, with qualified kinematic viscosity, iodine value, and higher heating value. The mechanism was demonstrated by high-throughput sequencing of 16S rRNA gene to characterize microbial community succession. Biodiesel met international standards. Microbial analysis confirmed Firmicutes and Bacteroidetes as dominant phyla; they synergistically hydrolyze carbohydrates/proteins and drive acidogenesis, favoring lipid retention and boosting energy (H2) yield. These findings show targeted pretreatments improve lipid and bioenergy yields, addressing low substrate use, providing a pathway for large-scale microalgal biorefineries for biodiesel and value-added biochemicals.

title: Pyrolysis and combustion of crude glycerol-based de-oiled yeast: analyses and kinetic modeling
abstract: Biomass is essential for the production of both energy and high-value products, making the diversification of sources necessary. De-oiled yeast is a waste obtained after oil extraction from oleaginous yeast. The study investigates the pyrolysis and combustion behaviors of de-oiled yeast biomass (G-DYB) under heating rates of 5, 10, and 15 °C.min -1 , the oleaginous yeast being cultivated with crude glycerol as carbon source. Kinetic modeling is performed applying the Extended Independent Parallel Reaction model with eight constituents, or other tools. The optimal values of the activation energy lie between 38 and 106 kJ.mol -1 for pyrolysis and between 35 and 155 kJ.mol -1 for combustion, which are relatively low compared to those obtained for conventional biomass. A deconvolution procedure specifies the contributions of the eight constituents which are identified considering the chemical composition of G-DYB. The calculated values of conventional indices indicate potential slagging and fouling issues. The study also analyzes the main gaseous emissions occurring during pyrolysis and combustion at 5 °C.min -1 . The results of the study will contribute to optimizing the thermal degradation of G-DYB at an industrial scale.

title: Oxidative torrefaction of brewers' spent grain: Fuel property enhancement and substantial energy efficiency improvement
abstract: Torrefaction has emerged as a promising pretreatment technology for enhancing the fuel properties of biomass. By introducing controlled oxidation reactions that supply in-situ exothermic heat, oxidative torrefaction significantly improves both fuel properties and overall energy efficiency. In this study, oxidative torrefaction of brewers' spent grain was performed, where the influences of torrefaction temperature (200-300°C), residence time (15-30 min), and oxygen concentration (0-21 vol.%) on torrefaction performance were systematically investigated. Results show that oxidative torrefaction yields superior fuel properties, doubling the Energy-Mass Co-benefit Index at 250°C for 30 min. FTIR and TG-MS analyses confirm intensified deoxygenation. Oxidative conditions accelerate torrefaction rate and extent, significantly reducing processing time and improving energy efficiency. When EMCI exceeds 10, electrical energy consumption is reduced by over 40%. TG-DSC analysis reveals that inert torrefaction at 250°C requires heat equivalent to 3.82% of the final product's calorific value, whereas oxidative torrefaction (13.5 vol% O2) supplies 37.66% of its own heat demand. Overall, high temperature (300°C), short duration (15 min), and moderate oxygen concentration (13.5 vol%) achieve the best comprehensive performance. This work provides systematic insights into fuel performance and energy efficiency of oxidative torrefaction, offering new directions for process optimization and industrial application.

title: Bioinspired nano-arrays for broadband and wide-angle anti-reflection in solar PV modules
abstract: Fresnel reflection from the glass cover is a key bottleneck limiting both power generation and sky radiative cooling performance of solar photovoltaic (PV) modules. Existing approaches reduce reflection through surface roughening, yet they still struggle to deliver broadband and wide-angle anti-reflection. To address this gap, this study introduces bioinspired nano-arrays that achieve omnidirectional ultra-low reflectance across the solar spectrum (average reflectance < 0.01 for incident angles from 0° to 50°) and the atmospheric window (8 to 13 μm). By clarifying the angular- and spectrally selective properties of the designed nano-arrays, a transient numerical model was developed to evaluate its enhancement in solar PV generation and sky radiative cooling performance. In Hong Kong, the nano-arrays enhance the monthly power generation and daytime sky radiative cooling energy by 8%-17% and 17%-22%, respectively. This work demonstrates the omnidirectional anti-reflective nano-arrays can effectively increase the overall energy efficiency of PV modules, facilitating the reduction of environmental impacts.

title: Causality-enhanced interpretable assessment of renewable-driven hydrogen potential for regional multi-energy decarbonization
abstract: Hydrogen is emerging as a low-carbon energy carrier that links renewable electricity with end-use sectors, including industry, transport, and long-duration energy storage, and thus supports multi-energy decarbonization. Assessing regional hydrogen potential is important for infrastructure planning and policy design, but it is complicated by heterogeneous regional conditions and nonlinear interactions among renewable resources, demand characteristics, and infrastructure readiness. Although statistical and machine learning models have been used for regional assessment, most remain correlation driven and offer limited causal interpretation for planning-oriented decisions. This paper presents the Causality-Enhanced Hydrogen Potential Evaluation Framework (CE-HPEF), an interpretable hybrid approach that combines tree-based feature screening, domain-guided treatment selection, and leakage-aware variable exclusion with Causal Forest and Double Machine Learning to estimate heterogeneous treatment-effect patterns of key regional drivers, including renewable supply indicators, industrial demand, and transportation-related factors. The estimated causal effects are incorporated into an augmented feature representation and used for model-agnostic downstream hydrogen-potential classification. Experiments on two public hydrogen datasets show that CE-HPEF improves average classification performance across diverse downstream classifiers after causal-feature augmentation. The inferred effect patterns further provide region-specific diagnostic insights for hydrogen planning under renewable-based energy transitions.

title: Numerical investigation of the tapered-hole patterned porous transport layer in proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers based on multi-physics coupling model
abstract: Proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWE) are promising devices for converting renewable energy into green hydrogen, but the conversion efficiency is limited by gas-liquid transport in the porous transport layer (PTL). Therefore, this study proposes novel tapered-hole patterned PTL structures, including tapered through-hole PTL (TTH-PTL) and tapered blind-hole PTL (TBH-PTL). A comprehensive 3D coupled multi-physics model for PEMWE is established and experimentally validated. Based on the numerical model, the impacts of original PTL (O-PTL), TTH-PTL, and TBH-PTL on transport properties and electrochemical performance of the PEMWE are investigated. Results indicate that tapered-hole structure constructs a directional gas-liquid transport pathway, enhancing the water saturation of catalyst layer and facilitating product discharge, thereby improving the overall electrolytic performance. At a current density of 2.0 A/cm2, compared to O-PTL, the average water saturation of TTH-PTL and TBH-PTL electrolyzers increase by 2.98% and 2.78%, while the average reaction rate increase by 1.23% and 1.37%, respectively. Because the tapered blind-hole structure enhances gas-water transport efficiency while maintaining charge transport continuity, the overall performance of TBH-PTL is superior to that of TTH-PTL. Furthermore, parametric analysis indicates that increasing porosity and reducing contact angle of the PTL can improve capillary driving force.

title: Synergistic enhancement of methane yield and odor control in pig manure anaerobic digestion via micro-aeration pretreatment
abstract: The widespread adoption of anaerobic digestion for pig manure treatment is limited by malodorous gas emissions and low energy recovery efficiency. This study systematically examined the effects of micro-aeration pretreatment over a range of intensities (0-13.9 mL/g(TS)/d) on odor abatement and digestion performance. Micro-aeration reduced emissions of eight key malodorous gases, including sulfide (H2S), ammonia (NH3), methanethiol (CH4S), and ethanethiol (C2H6S), by 14.0-100%. Complete sulfide mineralization was achieved at intensities ≥9.3 mL/g(TS)/d. Mitigation of nitrogen- and sulfur-containing compounds was likely driven by selective enrichment of facultative aerobic consortia (e.g., unclassified_f__Bacillaceae and unclassified_c__Gammaproteobacteria) and the upregulation of sulfur oxidation and nitrogen transformation pathways. Methane production increased by 37.6-95.5%, owing to enhanced hydrolysis and acetogenesis resulting from upregulated fatty acid β-oxidation and acetyl-CoA synthesis. Moreover, syntrophic bacteria (Syntrophomonas) and key methanogens (Methanothrix and Methanosarcina) were selectively enriched. An aeration intensity of 4.6 mL/g(TS)/d was identified as optimal, as it balanced effective odor control and maximal methanogenic activity. These findings provide a theoretical foundation and a viable strategy for improving energy recovery and environmental sustainability in swine manure management.

title: Unlocking the potential of existing dams: A multi-mode comparison of pumped storage for hydro-wind-solar integration
abstract: Repurposing existing dams for pumped storage hydropower provides a cost-effective pathway to enhance flexibility in hydro-wind-solar integrated systems; however, the techno-economic suitability of different retrofit modes remains insufficiently quantified. This study develops a multi-timescale optimization framework that couples long-term capacity planning with short-term dispatch to capture the interactions among renewable curtailment, capacity configuration, and economic performance. Applied to a major clean energy base in Qinghai, China, three pumped storage hydropower retrofit modes—pure, augmented, and hybrid—are evaluated. Results show that the pure mode delivers the greatest technical benefits, increasing transmission utilization by 1.21 absolute percentage points per 300 MW under a 5% curtailment constraint. The augmented mode achieves the highest economic efficiency due to infrastructure reuse, with internal rates of return 0.2-0.4 percentage points higher than the pure mode. The hybrid mode performs best only at low renewable penetration (<12 GW). Economic inflection points occur at storage-to-renewable capacity ratios of 1:4.82, 1:4.80, and 1:3.52, corresponding to internal rates of return of 7.8%, 8.0%, and 8.5%. Relaxing curtailment constraints increases renewable integration but reduces profitability, revealing a trade-off between flexibility and economic efficiency. These results highlight the importance of market mechanisms that appropriately value flexibility services.

title: Study on the characteristics of hydrogen production from biomass gasification catalyzed by yellow phosphorus smelting slag
abstract: In this study, peanut shells were used as biomass raw materials in a circulating fluidized bed gasification system, and yellow phosphorus smelting slag (the main component CaO plays an important role in promoting biomass pyrolysis, tar cracking, and water-gas shift reactions, thereby increasing hydrogen production) was used as a catalyst for gasification hydrogen production. The purpose of this study is to prepare hydrogen-rich syngas by resource recycling and simultaneously reduce the amount of tar generated during gasification. The effects of gasification temperature, water-to-material ratio (S/B), mass ratio of phosphorus slag to biomass and oxygen excess coefficient (λ) on the yield of hydrogen-rich syngas, hydrogen concentration and tar production were systematically investigated. The results show that phosphorus slag has excellent catalytic performance for hydrogen production from biomass gasification. Under optimal conditions (900 °C, water-to-material ratio 0.8, phosphorus slag-to-biomass ratio 0.2, oxygen excess coefficient 0.18), the gasification system achieved a hydrogen yield of 36.50 g/kg. Compared with non-catalytic pure biomass gasification, the hydrogen production rate increased by 93.12%, while tar production dropped markedly from 4.92 to 2.79 g/Nm3. This study provides a theoretical basis for the resource utilization of industrial waste phosphorus slag and the efficient optimization of biomass gasification hydrogen production process.

title: Data-driven artificial intelligence for wind speed forecasting: A decade review and multi-site benchmark for operational wind energy applications
abstract: Accurate wind speed forecasting is essential for the reliable and cost-effective integration of wind energy into modern power systems. This paper provides a comprehensive state-of-the-art review on data-driven artificial intelligence methods for wind speed forecasting from 2014 to early 2026 and evaluates their practical performance through a multi-site benchmark. The bibliometric trend analysis is conducted to identify the methodological evolution. These methods are categorized into four groups, i.e., statistical, machine learning, deep learning, and hybrid, with particular attention to decomposition enhanced forecasting frameworks. Ten representative forecasting methods combined with three data decomposition techniques are evaluated using four datasets from China, Norway, and a public benchmark. The results show that hybrid models with wavelet based decomposition generally improve the accuracy and robustness of short-term wind speed forecasting. Decomposition enhanced Transformer and Gaussian process models achieve relatively stable performance across different datasets and forecasting horizons. It is suggested that model selection relies on multiple factors including data characteristics, forecasting horizon, and computational constraints. Based on the review and benchmarking results, this study provides practical guidance on model selection for wind energy applications and identifies key research directions, including long-term forecasting, data-physics fusion learning, forecasting under extreme conditions, adaptive learning and explainable AI for broader climatic and operational scenarios. The findings offer actionable insights for improving forecasting reliability in large scale wind energy deployment.

title: Enhancing flexibility and achieving negative emissions in gas turbine-power-to-gas systems through storage and bioenergy under risk assessment
abstract: The growing share of renewable energy has increased the need for flexible multi-energy systems able to manage variability, curtailment, and emissions. This paper proposes a combined gas turbine with power-to-gas, storage, and an extended bioenergy with carbon capture and storage (BECCS) pathway as a framework for sustainable and carbon-negative energy conversion. The system links electricity, heat, and gas flows while capturing, utilizing, and partly storing CO2 through synthetic methane production and biomass co-firing. A linear and convex model describes mass and energy balances and the feasible operating region connecting fuel input with energy outputs. Both deterministic and risk-based optimization are applied. Deterministic analysis shows the stepwise benefits of adding power-to-gas, storage, and BECCS, while the stochastic framework addresses operational risks from renewable and demand variability. Using second-order stochastic dominance, results confirm that the system reduces external gas dependence and CO2 emissions even under adverse conditions. Quantitatively, power-to-gas alone cuts both gas use and emissions by 39%, storage increases reductions to 48%, and the BECCS pathway lowers net emissions by 59%, achieving carbon-negative operation. These findings highlight a pathway toward efficient, resilient, and climate-neutral energy systems.

title: Experimental optimization of CO2 gasification using empty fruits bunch (EFB): Effects of reaction rates, temperature, oven type and CO2 flow rate on syngas quality
abstract: Employing palm oil empty fruit bunch (EFB) biomass waste for gasification process shows great potential to reduce the dependency on fossil fuels for power generation. The use of CO2 as gasification agent instead of air as the common agent eliminates N2 dilution in syngas which significantly improves the quality of syngas. The objectives of this work are to compare two heating mechanisms of microwave and thermal furnace on EFB gasification to determine the optimum gasification operating conditions in terms of temperature and CO2 flowrates. Full-factorial statistical optimization approach was utilized to evaluate the significance of these factors in respect of important gasification parameters such as the concentration of H2 and CO produced by the syngas ratio H2/CO and carbon conversion. The gasification reactions take place in the presence of CO2 at very high reaction rate because of the high operating temperature (700°C - 900°C). CO2 gasification of EFB achieved its best performance at 800°C with a 50 ml/min flow rate, underscoring temperature as the decisive factor in producing clean, energy-rich syngas from agricultural waste. Under these conditions, the process achieved an LHV of 11.4 MJ/m3, syngas composition of 76.8% CO and 13.3% H2, with a composite desirability of 0.78. Therefore, in overall, the research highlights the potential of CO2 gasification of EFB as a sustainable method to convert agricultural waste into clean fuel, particularly valuable in regions rich in oil palm biomass such as Malaysia.

title: Integrated acid washing–torrefaction–pyrolysis of agro-industrial waste biomass: Reaction mechanism, kinetics, thermodynamics, and product distribution
abstract: The effects of integrating an acid wash with torrefaction pre-treatment on pyrolytic properties of soybean hulls (SH), and subsequent reductions in nitrogen oxides emitted through thermal decomposition are investigated. Soybean hulls were subjected to acid treatment followed by torrefaction treatments over a range of temperature (180°C, 220°C, 260°C, and 290°C) for 30 min. Positive correlations were observed between torrefaction temperature and enhancement of SH calorific value, energy density, and fuel ratio. In particular, acid washed torrefied soybean hulls at 260°C treatment was found to be the most effective yielding the highest energy yields (70.31%) EMCEI (energy mass-cohesion efficiency index) (17.35%), and highest thermal resistance. Analysis of kinetic data demonstrated that torrefaction resulted in increasing average activation energy from 193 to 195 kJ/mol (raw SH) to 223-228 kJ/mol (acid washed torrefied soybean hulls at 290°C) indicating improved thermal resistance due to the pre-treatment process. Thermodynamic data indicated that the enthalpy values ranged from 186 to 215 kJ/mol (acid washed torrefied soybean hulls-180) to 195-320 kJ/mol (acid washed torrefied soybean hulls at 290°C) and the Gibbs free energy increased from 152.0 to 152.6 kJ/mol to 156.0-157.0 kJ/mol indicating increased thermodynamic barriers. Analytical data of functional groups indicate that the amount of C-H, C-C, and C=C bonds in SH increased with torrefaction temperatures, whereas, N-H, C-N, C=O, and C-O bond amounts decreased with torrefaction temperatures. Thermal gravimetric mass spectroscopy (TG-MS) data indicated an increase in H2 and CH4 production with a decrease in CO2 and H2O production. Specifically, pyrolysis of acid washed torrefied soybean hulls-260°C sample produced only a small amount of NO and NOx. This research provides beneficial information related to environmental SH utilization and clean biomass to energy conversion technology development.

title: Diagnosing subseasonal thermal memory and thermal interference from operational data in a dense urban GWHP network
abstract: Urban groundwater heat pump networks are expanding quickly, intensifying heat accumulation and raising concerns about long-term sustainability. We apply a data-driven diagnostic framework to 35 systems in Zaragoza’s alluvial aquifer (2016–2024), analysing 7.48 million measurements. By integrating polar-density plots, cross-correlations on deseasonalised residuals and seasonally integrated series, and residual coherence analyses, the framework quantifies injection-to-production response and thermal-plume redistribution timescales, evaluates how long injection- and production-temperature signals remain coupled, and classifies likely intra- and intersystem interference from routinely monitored data. Observed delays of 33–45 days in the production-temperature response to injection-temperature variations, together with 110–122-day timescales for redistribution of the thermal plume, indicate that the monitored network exhibits subseasonal thermal memory. Around 69% of systems show intra- or intersystem interference, while 31% display low-amplitude signals (<2 °C) consistent with urban heat-island background or distal attenuated plumes. Thermal impact at the production well increases at 0.12 °C yr -1 , three times the injection trend, evidencing cumulative warming and plume superposition under cooling-dominated network operation. Even with Darcy velocities of up to 3.24 m d -1 , rapid groundwater flow did not prevent subseasonal thermal effects from persisting at network scale. Coordinated operation, thermal-load balancing and recovery-oriented well design could reduce interference and cumulative warming. The methodology provides transferable diagnostics to characterise groundwater heat pump behaviour in urban aquifers and inform the planning and management of dense groundwater heat pump networks.

title: An efficient prediction strategy for biogas yields based on machine learning and private optimization technique
abstract: Optimizing operating conditions in anaerobic digestion (AD) systems is essential for maximizing biogas production; however, identifying optimal parameter settings remains challenging due to reactor-specific variations and the nonlinear nature of the process. This paper proposes a Private Optimization based Biogas Prediction (POBP) strategy, which combines a Naïve Bayes (NB) classifier with a modified Gray Wolf Optimizer (MGWO) to determine suitable operating conditions for a laboratory-scale biogas reactor. In the proposed framework, NB is used as a probabilistic predictor to estimate biogas yield classes, while MGWO performs parameter optimization through an enhanced prey localization mechanism. The approach is evaluated using a reactor-specific dataset constructed from experimental measurements and optimization-generated samples. Results demonstrate that the proposed method improves reactor performance, achieving up to 62.72% improvement for the best solution and an average improvement of ≈33% after 10 iterations. Rather than relying on direct regression, the proposed framework utilizes a Naïve Bayes-based value predictor that estimates biogas yield by classifying yield intervals and mapping the predicted interval to a representative numerical value, achieving a classification accuracy of 96.1% on the tested dataset. These findings indicate that the proposed POBP strategy demonstrated effectiveness for the investigated laboratory-scale reactor and provides preliminary evidence for the feasibility of reactor-specific optimization under limited-data conditions.

title: Oxidative pretreatment assisted hydrothermal carbonization of rice straw and sewage sludge for improved fuel properties: Mechanistic insights and understandings through machine learning
abstract: In the current study, sewage sludge and rice straw were co-hydrothermally carbonized to produce high quality hydrochar as potential fuel candidate alternatives to fossil-based coal. The HTC temperature of (160-240) 0C were applied with H2O2 concentration of (4, 6, 8, 10 and 12) % on w/w basis. The 8% concentration of H2O2 was concluded optimum to achieve higher heating value of 24.77 MJ/kg, 80.35% hydrochar yield and fuel ratio of 0.42. The oxidative treatment has significantly reduced the ash contents of the hydrochar from 17% to 3.75%. To evaluate the potential commercial scale competitiveness of the produce hydrochar, the O/C and H/C were estimated on atomic basis and van Krevelen diagram were studied. The hydrochar produced from 8% concentration of H2O2 had provided the lowest H/C and O/C values of 0.24 and 0.63 respectively which is very closer to that of peat. The thermal decay of lignin, cellulose, hemi-cellulose, carbohydrates and proteins were discovered detailed mechanism. Oxidative pretreatment had significantly altered the combustion behavior of the developed hydrochar and most of the energy was recovered before 4500C. The Pearson co-relation also concluded the role of oxidative cleavage treatment in enhancing energy contents, higher hydrochar yield and fuel ratio. Random forest and linear regression model have provided excellent fitness up to R2 of 0.96 and 0.80 respectively.

title: Carbon capture and oxy-combustion for glassmaking decarbonization through Power-to-Gas: technical and economic viability assessment
abstract: Decarbonization of the glass industry is addressed through indirect electrification achieved by the production and use of renewable synthetic methane under Power-to-Gas integration schemes. The CO 2 captured in the glass furnace reacts with e-hydrogen to produce renewable methane which substitutes the fossil natural gas currently burnt. Four novel low-carbon concepts are compared with a container conventional plant from techno-economic viewpoint. They mainly differ in the carbon capture technology: (1) calcium looping with replacement of raw material by CaO purge; (2) amine scrubbing, (3) oxy-glass melting with O 2 -CO 2 atmosphere, and (4) pure oxy-combustion in the melting furnace. Besides comparison of energy penalty and CO 2 emission reduction, the economic impact of implementing abatement technologies is analysed under three economic scenarios: full electricity purchase and self-production via photovoltaic or wind farm. In all cases, the natural gas consumption is reduced to 95%, but the maximum CO 2 reductions are achieved with pure oxy-combustion (96%). When combined with wind self-production, the amine case presents the best carbon abatement (60 €/t CO2 ) and specific implementation costs (13 €/t glass ) for a plant of 250 t glass /d. However, at bigger plant sizes (600 t glass /d) the pure oxy-combustion presents comparable results (51 €/t CO2 and 14 €/t glass ) to the amines case (57 €/t CO2 and 12 €/t glass ).

title: Experimental and numerical study of a shell-and-tube latent thermal energy storage for solar thermal applications
abstract: Shell-and-tube latent thermal energy storage plays a key role in buffering intermittent solar heat supply and ensuring reliable hot-water delivery in solar thermal systems. Previous studies have shown that shell-side flow maldistribution can cause short-circuiting and uneven heating between phase change material tubes, thereby degrading thermal performance. To address this issue, a perforated-plate-assisted latent thermal energy storage prototype was experimentally investigated, and a validated numerical model was used to clarify its internal thermodynamic behavior. The results show that the perforated plate markedly improves shell-side flow distribution and leads to excellent inter-tube uniformity during both charging and discharging. The liquid-fraction non-uniformity index between tubes is only 0.012 during charging and 0.0017 during discharging. However, the dominant non-uniformity appears as vertical stratification within individual tubes, with corresponding indices of 0.09 and 0.11. This vertical non-uniformity reduces effective heat utilization and degrades exergy performance. Higher flow rates enhance both charging and discharging rates. The maximum charging power and heat exchange capacity rate reach 3.1 kW and 343.61 W/K, respectively, while the maximum useful discharging power and heat exchange capacity rate reach 13.31 kW and 608.37 W/K. However, for practical domestic hot water applications, higher flow rates involve a trade-off: they increase hot water yield, but also lead to higher charging energy demand, lower average outlet temperature, and shorter useful supply duration. These findings show that the perforated plate effectively mitigates inter-tube non-uniformity, while future optimization should focus on suppressing intra-tube vertical stratification and adapting the flow-rate strategy to specific domestic hot water demands.

title: Performance analysis of solar desalination unit coupled with latent heat energy storage tank for stable freshwater production
abstract: Solar desalination systems commonly suffer from intermittent freshwater production due to the transient nature of solar radiation and the absence of effective thermal buffering during low- or off-sunshine periods. This study develops and optimizes a hybrid solar desalination system integrating flat-plate solar collectors, a packed-bed latent heat thermal energy storage (TES) tank filled with encapsulated RT65 phase-change material, and a four-effect solar still. A transient numerical framework is developed to describe the coupled thermal interaction among the collector loop, PCM storage tank, heat exchanger, and multi-effect still. The heat-transfer fluid flow is divided between direct heating of the solar still and TES charging, creating a trade-off between immediate freshwater production and delayed thermal supply. Response surface methodology is employed to optimize the total system flow rate Qsys and the TES flow fraction γ. The optimum operating conditions are obtained at Qsys = 0.87 m3/h and γ = 11%, yielding a distilled water production of 53.30 kg/day. Compared with the optimized conventional system under the same solar radiation profile, collector area, still geometry, and operating duration, the PCM-assisted configuration increases freshwater productivity by 21.97%. The solar-to-evaporation thermal efficiency increases from 50.68% to 62.20%, corresponding to a 22.73% relative improvement. The results demonstrate that optimized latent heat storage can stabilize thermal delivery, extend desalination operation, and improve freshwater productivity in solar-driven multi-effect desalination systems.

title: Energy, exergy, economic and environmental (4E) analysis of a hybrid power plant fed by sugarcane residues
abstract: One of the main challenges for the sugarcane sector is to develop efficient and low-cost solutions for energy recovery from residues generated during sugar and ethanol production. In this context, this work proposes a novel integrated energy system that simultaneously processes typical sugarcane residues (bagasse, straw, vinasse, and filter cake). While recent literature has predominantly explored thermochemical or biochemical routes, the proposed architecture introduces a Rankine and Brayton combined cycle in a conventional mill, without affecting the sugar and ethanol production. A numerical model on the Excel/VBA platform is developed to simulate steady state operation conditions and calculate energy, exergy, economic, and environmental (4E) indicators. The hybrid configuration provides predictable power generation during the sugarcane season, reaching an electricity production of 74.1 kWh e per tonne of sugarcane milled (TC), a value significantly higher than that reported for conventional sugarcane plants (34.1 kWh e /TC). An exergy efficiency of 28.9% and a carbon footprint of 44.97 kg CO2eq /MWh e are achieved, alongside a competitive levelized cost of energy of 26.31 USD/MWh e . The approach can be implemented in a short timeframe for both new and existing facilities. Consequently, hybrid sugarcane plants may emerge as a reliable alternative that strategically complements intermittent renewable energy sources.

title: GraPHsep-based construction of a low-grade thermal energy-driven ejector cycle for building cooling
abstract: The high electricity consumption of building cooling systems poses a significant challenge to carbon neutrality. Low-grade thermal energy-driven ejector refrigeration technology presents a promising alternative to mitigate this reliance on electricity. However, the efficiency of this technology is often limited, owing to conventional design methods that rely heavily on expert experience and thus tend to yield suboptimal solutions. To address these challenges, this study employs the intelligent GraPHsep method to construct a novel ejector cycle using low-grade thermal energy. This method integrates graph theory with heat exchanger network optimization, enabling the synergistic optimization of cycle structure and operating parameters. Through this approach, a novel zeotropic ejector refrigeration cycle incorporating a vapor-liquid separator (NSERC) was constructed. A progressive comparative framework spanning from the basic ejector refrigeration cycle (BERC) to the NSERC was developed for elucidating the thermodynamic advantages and pinpointing the sources of performance enhancement. Under baseline conditions, the NSERC using R290/600a (50/50 wt%) achieved a coefficient of performance (COP) 17.9% higher COP than BERC. Concentration optimization identifies a R290 mass fraction of 0.1 for peak cycle performance. Furthermore, parametric analysis at this concentration across a wide range of conditions (heat source: 70–95 °C; ambient sink: 20–40 °C; chilled water outlet: 5–15 °C) demonstrated a COP improvement of 11.9% to 30.4% for the NSERC.

title: P-Cu cooperatively modulated NiMoO4 micropillars enable energy-saving hydrogen production in alkaline seawater assisted by urea electrolysis
abstract: Hydrogen production via urea-assisted seawater electrolysis offers a promising route to advance the carbon-neutral economy. Therefore, a high-performance bifunctional electrocatalyst capable of catalyzing both urea oxidation reaction (UOR) and hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is of critical importance. In this study, an advanced binder-free electrocatalyst that P and Cu cooperatively modulated NiMoO4 micropillars grown on nickel foam (P&Cu-NiMoO4/NF) is developed via a simple heteroatom implantation strategy. Comprehensive experimental characterizations demonstrate that P and Cu dopants not only optimize the self-supported open architecture and accelerate charge transport, but also induce significant electronic structure modulation. This modulation is attributed to the formation of low-valence Cu site and phosphating treatment. Theoretical calculations further demonstrate that Cu and Ni sites serve as respective adsorption centers for water and urea molecules, thereby accelerating the subsequent activation and dissociation processes in HER and UOR. Additionally, the co-doped P and Cu improve the d-band center position in NiMoO4, improving the adsorption of key intermediates. Consequently, P&Cu-NiMoO4/NF electrode demonstrates exceptional performance toward both HER and UOR. Remarkably, an alkaline seawater-urea electrolyzer utilizing P&Cu-NiMoO4/NF as bifunctional electrodes requires merely 1.373 V to deliver 10 mA cm−2. This research renders a promising strategy for the purposeful design of highly efficient electrocatalysts aimed at producing green hydrogen from seawater-urea system.

title: Continuous catalytic ortho-para hydrogen conversion in hybrid plate-fin heat exchangers: A performance study
abstract: The continuous ortho-para hydrogen conversion plate-fin heat exchanger (C-PFHE) is a vital component in hydrogen liquefaction systems. However, limited research exists on quantitatively analyzing the effects of cold-side fin performance on flow, heat transfer, and ortho-para hydrogen conversion performance in the hot-side catalyst-filled channel. This study developed a one-dimensional mathematical model to simulate the characteristic of heat transfer, flow resistance, and ortho-para hydrogen conversion. We investigate three hybrid fin configurations: plain-plain, plain-perforated, and plain-serrated, utilizing principles of thermodynamics and field synergy to assess how variations in cold-side fin performance influence hot-side functionality. Results demonstrated that enhanced cold-side heat transfer improves overall heat transfer of hot-side and increases synergy between the heat transfer coefficients of across both sides. For engineering applications, employing a low Reynolds number with a plain-serrated hybrid fin C-PFHE is recommended for achieving optimal performance. Additionally, improving hot-side heat transfer boosts the para-hydrogen conversion rate. Two novel quantitative correlations are established: one between the hot-side j-factor and the cold-side j-factor, and the other between the hot-side j-factor and the para-hydrogen conversion ratio, with errors of ±1.5% and ±6%, respectively. These correlations offer theoretical guidance for designing new C-PFHE structures and enable rapid evaluation of impacts on hot-side performance.

title: Rational engineering defective g-C3N4 with tunable three coordinate nitrogen (N3C) vacancies for boosting photocatalytic H2 evolution
abstract: In this study, the defective graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) materials with three coordinate nitrogen (N3C) vacancies (Nv-DCN) had been directly synthesized via a simple ethylene glycol (EG)-assisted solvothermal strategy. The N3C defects density could be straightforwardly regulated by increasing the EG-etched time. By incorporating the N3C vacancies into the g-C3N4 skeleton, the as-obtained Nv-DCN photocatalysts can enlarge the specific surface area, extend the visible light absorption capability, and promote the charge migration and transfer efficiency. The resultant g-C3N4 treated with EG for 40 h (Nv-DCN-40) showed the highest photocatalytic H2 production activity (892.0 μmol g−1 h−1) because of it reaching the optimum N3C defects density range, which is approximately 4.0-folds than that of pristine g-C3N4 (PCN). This work provides a new insight into understanding of the role of N3C vacancies in the g-C3N4 materials for boosting renewable solar-to-H2 fuel conversion.

title: Contextual information based distributionally robust optimization for zero-carbon oil and gas field power systems
abstract: As a representative of industries with high carbon emissions and energy consumption, oil and gas field power systems (OGFS) must continuously advance green transformation to achieve carbon neutrality goals. This paper develops a distributionally robust approach for the flexible operation of zero-carbon OGFS. First, a comprehensive oil and gas field production model that incorporates detailed modeling of crude oil extraction, separation, storage, and transportation is proposed. Second, a demand response model considering the temporal shifting flexibility of crude oil production facilities is exploited to improve oil and gas production efficiency. Meanwhile, a carbon emission management strategy is also presented to achieve the zero-carbon goal of OGFS. Third, a novel distributionally robust joint chance-constrained (DRJCC) model is developed to account for renewable energy uncertainty that is capable of exploiting contextual information. Uncertain parameters are addressed by constructing an ambiguity set based on optimal transport and probability trimmings. Finally, a data-driven tractable reformulation is provided that can guard against the impact of limited knowledge regarding the dependence between renewable energy uncertainty and contextual information captured by samples of their joint distribution. Case studies on a real-world oil and gas field in North China verify the proposed model’s effectiveness.
keywords: Oil and gas field power systems (OGFS)

title: Topology optimization-driven structural engineering and hydrogenation enhancement for metal hydride reactor
abstract: The large-scale integration of renewable energy sources such as wind and solar introduces significant intermittency and fluctuations in power generation, creating an urgent need for efficient energy storage technologies. Hydrogen storage based on metal hydrides (MH) has attracted increasing attention due to its high volumetric hydrogen density and intrinsic safety. However, the performance of metal hydride reactors (MHRs) is often constrained by inefficient heat transfer within the hydride bed, while conventional reactor designs rely on simple geometries with limited design flexibility. In this study, a topology-optimization-driven spherical MHR with internal conductive fins (FSR@TO) is proposed to reconstruct internal heat-conduction pathways and enhance heat diffusion within the reactor. Furthermore, a coupled structural configuration integrating topology-optimized conductive fins with an external heat-exchange jacket (FSR@TO-J) is developed to establish a conduction–convection synergistic thermal management framework. Numerical simulations combined with response surface methodology are employed to systematically investigate the effects of structural and operating parameters on hydrogenation performance, and the volumetric hydrogen storage rate (Rv) is introduced as a comprehensive performance indicator to coordinate hydrogen storage capacity and hydrogenation kinetics.The proposed framework provides a systematic design strategy for improving thermal management and hydrogen storage performance in metal hydride reactors for renewable energy storage systems.

title: Application of RSM for modeling and optimizing green hydrogen generation from water splitting using Cu-MOF-Mg/CA based membrane under visible light
abstract: Solar-activated water splitting has emerged as a promising strategy for sustainable hydrogen (H2) production due to its eco-friendly nature and the potential for large-scale green energy generation. In this study, we synthesized cost-effective, photo active-membrane with tailored band gaps for efficient solar-driven photocatalytic water splitting. Transition metal copper (Cu) and magnesium (Mg) were incorporated with each other to optimize their band structure, while conjugation with high-surface-area membrane enhanced charge separation and light absorption. The photocatalytic membranes were evaluated for green H2 generation under visible light irradiation in a photo-reactor optimized via Response Surface Methodology (RSM). The photocatalytic performance was optimized, with the critical operational parameters for the bimetallic Cu-Mg-MOF/CA membrane identified as a catalyst dose of 0.5 g/L, a reaction time of 60 min, and a light source distance of 100 cm. Under these conditions, a maximal hydrogen generation rate of 439 mmolh−1g−1 was achieved. This exceptional performance, which surpasses that of the singular Mg-MOF/CA (152 mmolh−1g−1) and Cu-MOF/CA (236 mmolh−1g−1) membranes, is attributed to a synergistic effect within the bimetallic system that significantly enhances photocatalytic activity and improves charge carrier separation and transfer. This system exhibits competitive photocatalytic performance, achieving a high hydrogen generation rate along with excellent stability over seven consecutive cycles; its hydrogen generation lifetime symbolizes the maximum value described to date for metal-organic framework (MOF)-based membrane. The design successfully integrates defect engineering and demonstrates significant application prospective in the field of photocatalytic hydrogen production, thereby establishing a robust foundation for future research. So, this work presents a viable, economically feasible approach for green H2 generation, addressing key challenges in photocatalyst design for renewable energy applications.

title: Elucidating the influence of electrolyte compactness on electrochemical reaction processes in metal-supported solid oxide fuel cells
abstract: Plasma spraying (PS), characterized by sintering-free and rapid deposition of functional ceramic layers, offers a promising approach for fabricating metal-supported solid oxide fuel cells. However, insufficient electrolyte compactness in the PS cell can cause gas leakage and distort impedance-based electrochemical diagnosis. In this work, chemical infiltration was employed to heal the residual defects of the PS electrolyte, systematically investigating the influence of electrolyte compactness, with particular focus on the polarization characteristics of electrode reactions analyzed via the distribution of relaxation times. The sensitivity of individual electrochemical processes to operating parameters—including temperature, fuel flow, and current load—was further quantified using equivalent circuit modeling. The results reveal that the sprayed-electrolyte cell (ScSZ) shows a higher apparent initial power output than the infiltrated-electrolyte cell (ScSZ-Inf); however, this apparent enhancement arises from leakage-induced parallel pathways rather than intrinsic electrochemical improvement. Moreover, cross leakage in ScSZ disrupts local partial pressures and creates parasitic currents, which artificially lowers the measured surface oxygen exchange and gas conversion resistances, while amplifying low-frequency concentration polarization fluctuations, thus resulting in a polarization response distinct from that of ScSZ-Inf. This study elucidates the mechanistic role of electrolyte compactness in defining the electrochemical behavior of the as-sprayed cell and provides a diagnostic framework for identifying leakage-induced abnormal polarization responses in practical systems.

title: Circular flow field design and multi-physics characteristics study for high-pressure PEM electrolyzers
abstract: The flow field plays a crucial role in the distribution of proton exchange membrane electrolysis cell (PEMEC) reactants. High-pressure conditions bring in emerging phenomena in water-gas transport, introducing challenges to the multi-physics distribution. This study proposed a concept of “secondary distribution zone (SDZ)” and designed a forced-shunted flow field (FSFF). A three-dimensional, two-phase, full-scale PEMEC model was developed, integrating high-pressure and hydrogen permeation factors. Uniformity analysis substantiated the superior performance of FSFF. Analyzed the high-pressure characteristics of single-side high-pressure (SSHP) and differential pressure (DP) types, and the differences between parallel flow field (PFF) and FSFF under high-pressure conditions. The hydrogen permeation mechanism under high-pressure conditions was studied. The results indicates that FSFF mitigated “hot spot” and gas accumulation phenomena. Compared to PFF, FSFF improved flow uniformity by 35.2%, temperature distribution uniformity by 15.4%, and liquid saturation uniformity by 39.6%. High-pressure is proved to cause performance degradation, reduces temperature distribution uniformity, increases liquid saturation, and decreases inlet-outlet pressure difference. Additionally, the flow field exerts a substantial influence on the multi-physics uniformity of DP type anode side. The optimization rates for temperature and liquid saturation uniformity increased by more than 10% and 7%, respectively. Hydrogen permeation is primarily driven by the pressure difference between the anode and cathode, and electroosmotic at high current densities cannot be ignored.

title: Coupled envelope heat transfer pathways: Optimization of dynamic radiative cooling and wall thermal conduction
abstract: The actual performance of dynamic radiative cooling materials is constrained by non–radiative heat transfer properties of walls, particularly thermal conductivity and volume heat capacity. This study treats dynamic radiative cooling materials as an inseparable part of the thermal parameters of the building envelope to investigate its synergistic mechanisms with conductive heat transfer. To address this, the equivalent temperature was introduced to establish the relationship among ambient temperature, radiation, convection, heat conduction processes, and indoor temperature, and was used to identify the heat transfer direction as well as the positive and negative effects of thermal conductivity and volume heat capacity. Based on the equivalent temperature analysis, high thermal conductivity and high volume heat capacity are beneficial for reducing cooling energy consumption, whereas low thermal conductivity and high volume heat capacity are more favorable for reducing heating energy consumption. Under the reference building model and operating conditions adopted in this study, an optimization zoning criterion for thermal conductivity and volume heat capacity was established based on degree days. For this baseline configuration, low thermal conductivity and high volume heat capacity are recommended when degree days exceed 9120°C·d, while high thermal conductivity and high volume heat capacity are recommended when degree days are below 9120°C·d. Under this optimization strategy, the national total energy–saving potential ranges from 2.4% to 33.9%. In addition, dynamic switching of wall thermal conductivity is expected to reduce both cooling and heating energy consumption, thereby further lowering the total energy consumption by up to 7.3%. This study informs building energy–saving technologies and offers new insights for integrated optimization.

title: ECDA-M: Enhancing cross-domain adaptability with mechanism fusion for few samples: A case on PEMFC health status prediction
abstract: With growing environmental emphasis and rapid renewable hydrogen advances, proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFC) serve as a critical bridge between green hydrogen and clean power. Accurate degradation prediction ensures reliable operation and maintenance, yet current methods face significant limitations in data-scarce scenarios. Transfer learning provides a viable approach yet struggles with issues such as insufficient data, capturing nonlinear features, and selecting transferable representations. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes ECDA-M—a novel mechanism-data fusion framework for cross-domain health prediction under limited data. This method utilizes voltage data generated from first-principles models as source data, alleviating data acquisition difficulties. By integrating Pathformer and Adversarial Discriminative Domain Adaptation (ADDA), ECDA-M establishes a robust predictive model. It also incorporates a Fourier-based Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (FourierKAN) as the predictor and adopts a global-feature transfer strategy, which enhances nonlinear representation learning and improves prediction accuracy with scant data. Experimental results on the IEEE PHM 2014 dataset and real-world accelerated life test data demonstrate that ECDA-M surpasses several baseline models. Ablation studies further corroborate the contribution of each component, affirming the method's rationality and innovation within a mechanism-fused transfer learning framework.

title: Multi-objective optimization of operating parameters for solid oxide fuel cells with multiple gas flow configurations
abstract: Solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) are promising dispatchable conversion devices for renewable and low-carbon fuels, and their performance and durability strongly depend on operating conditions. However, existing studies rarely provide a unified framework that compares typical gas-flow configurations while simultaneously optimizing performance and accounting for durability constraints. In this study, a two-dimensional, non-isothermal SOFC model applicable to co-flow, counter-flow, and cross-flow configurations is developed and integrated with a multi-objective optimization framework based on the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II. The effects of key operating parameters, including current density, fuel composition, and air excess ratio, on the coupled electrical performance and thermal behavior are systematically investigated. For the investigated methane-fueled planar SOFC under identical geometry and boundary conditions, the counter-flow configuration yields higher power density and electrical efficiency, whereas the co-flow configuration provides improved thermal safety.
