Further optimization under both unconstrained and lifetime-constrained scenarios produces Pareto fronts that quantify the power-efficiency trade-off, where within the investigated operating/design space each 0.1 W/cm2 increase in power density corresponds to an approximate 8% efficiency loss. When lifetime constraints are introduced, the feasible performance boundaries shrink, and optimal conditions shift toward strategies prioritizing efficiency over power output. Across all configurations, maintaining high fuel utilization is crucial for meeting efficiency targets, though the optimal adjustment of operating parameters varies depending on flow configuration, performance objectives, and lifetime considerations. The proposed framework provides decision-oriented operating envelopes to support high-efficiency and durable SOFC operation for the utilization of renewable methane.

title: Ammonia-reformate-fueled PEMFC anode recirculation using cathode-degraded PEMFCs as electrochemical hydrogen pumps
abstract: As renewable energy use grows globally, managing waste from retired or degraded energy devices has become critical, particularly for polymer electrolyte membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs), which require sustainable and efficient recycling solutions. This study proposes a repurposing strategy that converts cathode-degraded PEMFCs directly into electrochemical hydrogen pumps (EHPs) without the need for disassembly, enabling efficient hydrogen recovery and reuse within PEMFC systems using ammonia-derived, post-purified reformate. To validate the feasibility of this approach, an PEMFC anode recirculation system was developed, in which the cathode-degraded PEMFC served as an EHP for off-gas hydrogen recovery. Accelerated stress tests were conducted to induce cathode catalyst degradation, and the performance of the cell was evaluated in both fuel cell (FC) and EHP modes using a segmented cell. In FC mode, the peak power density decreased by 10.6% and 18.2% relative to the initial performance after successive degradation cycles, accompanied by local current density deviations up to 22%. Incorporating a cathode-degraded PEMFC as an EHP increased the maximum system efficiency to 49% at an operating current of 20 A and a fuel utilization of 94%, which was 13 percentage points higher than that without hydrogen recovery, while maintaining a higher hydrogen mole fraction at the anode outlet, which may help mitigate fuel-starvation-related degradation. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of repurposing cathode-degraded PEMFCs as EHPs and provide insights into sustainable strategies for fuel cell reuse and resource circularity.

title: Activating tremella-like 2H-WS2 via electron rearrangement at industrial current density for dual-pH hydrogen production
abstract: To prepare non-precious metal-based electrocatalysts with high activity for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is of significant for electrochemical water splitting (EWS). Herein, we report a tremella-like nanosheet structure of Co and P co-doped WS2 (Co.P-WS2) that demonstrates efficient HER catalytic activity under dual-pH conditions. The synergistic effect of heteroatom doping combined with unique tremella-like nanosheet morphology, not only induces the electron rearrangement of Co and S, but also maximizes the exposure of active sites. The Co.P-WS2 catalyst exhibits exceptional dual-pH HER kinetics. In alkaline/acidic media, it requires ultra-low overpotentials of only 27/89 mV at 10 mA cm−2, and 197/332 mV at 500 mA cm−2, markedly outperforming single-doped Co-WS2 (101/125 mV at η10), P-WS2 (226/227 mV at η10), and pristine WS2 (262/237 mV at η10). Crucially, at an industrial current density of 500 mA cm−2, Co.P-WS2 outperforms the activity of commercial Pt/C in alkaline solution and maintains exceptional stability. The catalyst displays the Tafel value of 82.74 ± 0.12 and 83.87 ± 0.15 mV dec−1. The characterizations of kinetic isotope effect (KIE), and cyclic voltammetry (CV) indicate that Co.P-WS2 enhances the kinetics of the Volmer step. And the results of in-situ Raman spectra demonstrate that the catalyst regulates the interfacial water structure to create an optimal orientation for H-OH bond cleavage. This work provides a feasible strategy for designing high-performance transition metal dichalcogenide-based electrocatalysts, offering important guidance for advancing sustainable hydrogen production technologies.

title: Retraction notice to “The role of carbon taxes, clean fuels, and renewable energy in promoting sustainable development: How green is nuclear energy?” [RENE 193 (2022) 167–178]

Retraction notice to “Can integrating wastewater heat recovery with a passive geothermal borehole improve the cost-effectiveness? Optimal energy management through ANN and genetic algorithm” [RENE 242 (2025) 122337]
A data-driven decision framework for rural hybrid renewable energy system site selection based on GIS and preference disaggregation analysis: A case study of China
abstract: A challenge in hybrid renewable energy (RE) planning is to improve the objectivity of site decision while reducing the cognitive burden associated with preference elicitation. This study proposes a data-driven decision-making framework that integrates the geographic information system (GIS) with preference disaggregation analysis for rural hybrid RE potential assessment and site selection. GIS is used to screen candidate sites, while preference disaggregation analysis infers decision-model parameters that capture both criterion importance and interaction effects. Stochastic multicriteria acceptability analysis is further applied to enhance the robustness of the decision outcomes. Using the already constructed rural hybrid RE projects in China as decision samples, the inferred model by preference disaggregation analysis is applied to hybrid RE siting in Sichuan Province. Among fourteen screened candidate sites, Daocheng county is identified as the most suitable location owing to its strong resource potential and favorable geographical and economic conditions. Interaction analysis shows that, in wind- and solar-rich rural areas, higher disposable income significantly facilitates hybrid RE deployment, whereas sunshine duration and average temperature exhibit clear redundancy.

title: View factor modelling of photosynthetically active radiation and light sharing optimization in fixed agrivoltaic systems
abstract: Agrivoltaic systems combine solar photovoltaic electricity generation with agricultural production on the same land. Their overall performance depends on the sharing of solar radiation between the photovoltaic array and the underlying crops. A two-dimensional optical model, based on view factors derived from Hottel's crossed-string rule, is proposed to evaluate the spatio-temporal distribution of ground irradiance and agrivoltaic system performance for fixed-tilt configuration. The model is coupled with a previously developed bifacial PV electrical model and with a simplified transpiration-based crop model using Monteith–Beer–Lambert canopy light-interception model to compute the Light Productivity Factor and the Land Equivalent Ratio. It was validated against (i) the open-source bifacialVF model for two contrasted sites (Agadir, Morocco and Paris, France), with R2 = 0.99 and nRMSE < 3%, and (ii) field measurements at the INRA experimental field of Belfaâ (Agadir, Morocco), with an overall nRMSE of 4.34% and R2 = 0.99 on clear-sky days. A sensitivity analysis identified pitch, system elevation and module transparency as the dominant design parameters. For Agadir, a tilt angle of 30°, a pitch of 2.6 m and an elevation of 2.5 m let 70% of global horizontal irradiation reach the crops, giving a light productivity factor of 1.73. For raspberry cultivation, a pitch of 3.5 m and an elevation of 2.5 m provide 80% of the crop light requirement, with a light productivity factor of 1.58. Coupling with the canopy model yielded a land equivalent ratio of 1.39 for winter wheat under the studied configuration.

title: Energy performance analysis of ground-source heat pump systems in nursing homes based on winter-summer load differences: A case study in Xi'an, China
abstract: Against the backdrop of China's rapidly aging population, nursing homes face the dual challenge of ensuring thermal comfort for elderly adults while maintaining high energy efficiency. However, systematic investigations into how elderly-specific thermal preferences affect the load characteristics and long-term performance of ground-source heat pump systems remain limited. To address this gap, this study develops a framework that integrates dynamic building load modeling with transient ground-source heat pump system analysis, enabling a quantitative assessment of how elderly-oriented temperature settings influence the coupled behavior of building loads, system operation, and ground temperature evolution. A spatiotemporal zoning operation strategy tailored for nursing homes is also proposed. The results show that elderly adults generally prefer indoor temperatures approximately 2 °C higher than standard setpoints, which substantially increases winter heating demand, raising the annual heating load and total energy consumption by 55.4% and 30.6%, respectively. The spatiotemporal zoning operation strategy effectively reduces energy consumption by about 15% and enhances operational stability. Ten-year dynamic simulations further reveal that elderly-oriented parameters accelerate ground thermal depletion, whereas the proposed strategy significantly alleviates subsurface thermal imbalance. These findings provide important theoretical and technical guidance for the efficient design and long-term sustainable operation of ground-source heat pump systems in nursing homes.

title: Physics-informed solar modulation attention based dual-branch Transformer for ultra-short-term photovoltaic power forecasting with operational benefits analysis
abstract: Accurate ultra-short-term photovoltaic power forecasting is critical for real-time grid operation but remains challenging due to strong seasonal biases in input features, as well as physically inconsistent predictions during nighttime periods. To address these issues, this study proposes PhyMADformer, a physics-informed dual-branch Transformer that integrates physically meaningful solar priors into the attention-based representation learning process. The model explicitly decouples strongly seasonal trend components and weakly seasonal components via a dual-branch architecture, enabling more effective representation learning across heterogeneous temporal patterns. Unlike conventional physics-informed approaches that rely on external physical modeling, feature correction, or physics-informed probabilistic components, the proposed method embeds physical knowledge directly into the attention representation, improving interpretability and consistency. Extensive experiments on six utility-scale photovoltaic plants and multiple baselines show that PhyMADformer outperforms existing methods, achieving average reductions of 12.19% in root mean square error and 34.01% in mean absolute error. It also improves physical consistency, reducing nighttime absolute energy and nighttime mean absolute error by 74.26% and 74.51%, respectively. In addition, system-level evaluations demonstrate reductions in upward reserve requirement (48.02%), balancing cost (46.84%), and photovoltaic curtailment (40.21%), highlighting its practical value for real-world grid operation and improved dispatch efficiency.

title: Multiphase CFD study of biomass and coal co-gasification in a bubbling fluidized bed (BFB) reactor
abstract: Biomass-coal co-gasification in fluidized beds is recognized as a promising route for the clean utilization of energy resources, yet the coupling mechanism of fluidization-heat transfer-chemical reactions at the particle scale is still unclear, and the impact of particle density/size differences on thermochemical behavior requires further elucidation. This work performs a three-dimensional (3D) numerical investigation of biomass-coal co-gasification in a bubbling fluidized bed (BFB) reactor using a multiphase particle-in-cell (MP-PIC) approach, incorporating gas-solid interactions, heat transfer, and homogeneous and heterogeneous reactions. Comparison of the simulation results with experimental data for coal and biomass gasification in BFB reactors shows that the relative deviation in product gas composition is within 8%, confirming the reliability of the model. The model was then applied to study physical and thermochemical characteristics of solid particles in a BFB reactor. The temperature is relatively uniform with an overall range of 900-1050 K, while localized high-temperature zones near fuel inlets are 100 K higher than surrounding regions. Particle heat transfer coefficients (HTCs) are positively correlated with Reynolds numbers and vary significantly by particle type and spatial location. Increasing the inlet gas mass flow rate reduces particle temperatures by modifying gas-solid heat exchange, while a higher biomass blending ratio (up to 40%) increases H2O generation and reduces CO2 emissions. Distinct particle segregation is observed, with biomass particles accumulating in the upper dilute phase, coal particles in the mid-bed, and sand particles in the lower region. The segregation index of biomass particles (up to 0.20) is significantly higher than that of coal particles (around 0.13), and particle segregation influences fuel conversion, with ash content in solid fuels increasing with more complete conversion of moisture and volatiles.

title: A Bi-level allocation model for energy storage systems and soft open points considering time-of-use pricing differences of hybrid AC/DC distribution networks
abstract: Energy storage systems and soft open points are core flexible resources for mitigating the uncertainties induced by variable wind and solar generation. Their optimal allocation fundamentally dictates the hosting capacity of renewables and the overall operational efficiency of distribution networks. This paper proposes a spatiotemporally coordinated optimal allocation framework for energy storage systems and soft open points within AC/DC hybrid distribution networks, explicitly integrating a differentiated seasonal time-of-use electricity pricing mechanism. After extracting representative seasonal profiles to capture stochastic uncertainties, a bi-level “allocation-operation” optimization architecture is constructed. The upper level employs a particle swarm optimization algorithm to collaboratively determine the optimal siting and sizing of the energy storage systems and soft open points, aiming to minimize the total annualized comprehensive cost. Constrained by these allocation variables, the lower level establishes a second-order cone programming model to minimize daily operational costs, driven by the differentiated time-of-use price signals. The exact operational results, solved via the Gurobi optimizer, are iteratively fed back to the upper level to guide the global allocation process. Simulation results on a modified IEEE 69-bus AC/DC hybrid distribution network demonstrate that the proposed spatiotemporal coordination significantly enhances renewable energy absorption, mitigates network losses, and improves voltage profiles. Ultimately, this synergistic framework achieves a 3.14% reduction in the total annualized cost, fully validating its robustness and superior economic benefits. Subsequent testing on a larger-scale IEEE 141-bus system further confirms the scalability of the proposed framework.

title: Efficient photothermal-assisted photocatalytic hydrogen production over well-dispersed Cu@C nanoparticles/mesoporous TiO2 heterojunction photocatalyst
abstract: This study demonstrates a novel lattice-confined strategy was developed to prepare the well-dispersed carbon encapsulated Cu NPs (Cu@C) and then combined with Ti-MOF through a simple calcination treatment to obtain the heterojunction photocatalyst. The optimized Cu@C-8/TiO2 heterojunction photocatalyst achieved a notable H2 evolution rate of 4015.63 μmol g−1 h−1, making it 5.3 and 1.46 times superior to the rate of MOF-derived TiO2 (756.98 μmol g−1 h−1) and 1 wt% Pt/TiO2 (2743.05 μmol g−1 h−1), respectively. The Cu@C-8/TiO2 sample presented a high H2 production rate of 22470.72 μmol g−1 h−1 under the heating temperature of 110 °C. The results of experiments and DFT calculations indicate that the significant synergy between the Schottky junction and the photothermal effect is the reason for its outstanding performance. Besides, the H2 evolution activity of the heterojunction photocatalysts remains the same as the freshly prepared sample after 100-day-storage in the lab. This indicates that coating a layer of carbon on the Cu surface based on the lattice-confined strategy can effectively prevent its oxidation. This study provides a method to enhance the stability of Cu species during photothermal catalyst hydrogen production and effectively suppressing the drawback of rapid recombination of photogenerated charges in TiO2 semiconductor.

title: Effect of dynamic heat source variations on the performance of heat pipe thermoelectric generator: An experimental study
abstract: Heat flux density control at both the hot and cold ends of thermoelectric generators using heat pipes improves energy conversion efficiency. An experimental heat pipe thermoelectric generation system was constructed in this study to investigate the effects of dynamic heat source parameters on generator performance. Compared with steady-state operation, a dynamic heat source enables the heat pipe thermoelectric generator to achieve significantly higher peak output power, thereby increasing both the average power output and the average conversion efficiency. As the average heat source power increases, the enhancement in average output power and average energy conversion efficiency provided by the dynamic heat source gradually decreases. When the average heat source power is 40 W, the average output power increases by up to 44.05%. With the peak heat source power fixed at 200 W, increasing the duty cycle results in higher average output power and average energy conversion efficiency. At a duty cycle of 90%, the average output power reaches 4.26 W, while the average energy conversion efficiency reaches 5.33%. When the average heat source power is kept constant, a lower duty cycle leads to higher average output power and average energy conversion efficiency. Meanwhile, increasing the heat source period can further enhance the average output power. These experimental results provide guidance for the operational optimization of heat pipe thermoelectric generators.

title: Experimental and numerical investigation of cooling and energy-saving performance of a novel scalable radiative cooling coating in full-scale temporary houses
abstract: Radiative cooling (RC) technology is a promising method for building energy conservation, especially in temporary houses. Existing studies mainly focused on RC coatings applied on roofs, while their potential on façades remains largely unexplored. Therefore, this study fabricated a novel, scalable RC coating and investigated its performance on both roof and façades of full-scale temporary houses. Experimental measurements of surface/indoor temperatures, heat fluxes, and electricity consumption were conducted. In addition, a spectrally-selective RC model was developed and coupled with EnergyPlus to investigate the distinct performance of RC coating on roof versus façades. Experimentally, RC coatings reduced exterior peak temperature by 40.5 °C, indoor surface temperature by 9.8 °C, and indoor peak temperature by 4.9 °C under free-running conditions leading to improved thermal comfort. Under air-conditioning, RC coating increased sensible heat loss from nearly 0% to 31% of metabolic heat. Simulations revealed that while the roof maintains persistent cooling power, façade cooling performance is weakened by on-site ground radiative heating. The north façade even exhibits negative net radiative cooling power at noon. Finally, the energy savings of RC coating were evaluated: experiments showed a 21% reduction in cooling demand in September, while simulations showed a 14.8% reduction in midsummer. In summary, this work demonstrates the distinct cooling roles of roofs and façades, providing a basis for deploying RC coatings in energy-efficient temporary houses.

title: Understanding supported magnesium chloride sorbent materials for sorption-enhanced ammonia synthesis toward renewable hydrogen storage
abstract: As the world shifts to renewable energy, ammonia is emerging as a promising green alternative to hydrogen due to its high energy density and carbon neutrality. While conventional ammonia synthesis relies on energy-intensive condensation process to separate ammonia from unreacted gases following the catalytic reaction, metal halides offer a potential alternative for process intensification in renewable-driven ammonia production. However, moisture sensitivity hinders their applicability. Research on ammonia separation with metal halides often prioritizes absorption capacity, overlooking detailed sorbent characterization due to water contamination challenges. This study investigates MgCl 2 -impregnated porous supports, focusing on efficient characterization under inert conditions and ammonia sorption capacity. Porous supports improve material stability, reduce swelling, and enable long-term sorption by accommodating volume changes and enhancing kinetics. Results show that chemical absorption of ammonia by MgCl 2 is the predominant mechanism determining sorption capacity. Among tested materials, MgCl 2 /ZSM-5 achieves the highest sorption capacity (335 mg/g at 25 °C), while MgCl 2 /USY (500) excels in cyclic stability; however, capacity declines at higher temperatures. These findings emphasise the significance of considering support acidity and moisture effects in designing ammonia sorbents for renewable energy-integrated processes. Additionally, new mechanistic ammonia absorption/desorption kinetic model was developed, enabling future efficient CFD simulation for sorption-enhanced N 2 activation.

title: Optimization of sandstone geothermal reinjection: Integrating field tests, numerical simulations and machine learning
abstract: The decline in reinjection capacity reduces the resource efficiency and long-term sustainability of sandstone geothermal systems. To address this critical challenge while accounting for complex geological heterogeneity and multi-physics constraints, this study establishes an integrated decision-making framework that combines field tests, numerical simulation, and machine learning. Firstly, multi-stage stepped-pressure reinjection field tests and hydrochemical analysis quantitatively characterize the nonlinear response of near-wellbore fluid dynamic resistance and scaling risk. Furthermore, a vertical heterogeneous numerical model is constructed, revealing the control mechanisms of near-well head loss accumulation and dominant layer-driven flow distribution. Based on this, a stacking ensemble surrogate model driven by heterogeneous learners is constructed, and the SHAP method is used to conduct interpretability analysis. Finally, a preferred operating condition is selected from the Pareto front. The results show that while high-pressure reinjection boosts the driving force, the marginal reinjection gain decreases under persistent near-wellbore hydraulic resistance and increasing non-Darcy dissipation. Additionally, under the investigated hydrochemical conditions, lower-temperature reinjection reduces the calcite scaling potential. Therefore, a moderate-pressure and low-temperature reinjection strategy is identified from the Pareto analysis. Within the parameter space under study and based on the specified economic assumptions, the selected Pareto-optimal solution is predicted to increase thermal energy extraction capacity and hourly benefit by 35.66% and 28.91%, respectively, compared to the natural reinjection baseline case. This study elucidates the reinjection mechanism in porous reservoirs and provides technical support for the efficient and sustainable operation of geothermal systems.

title: Decarbonization of a sugarcane refinery in Mexico through bioethanol production and CHP generation with carbon capture and storage (BECCS)
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive strategy for the decarbonization of an existing sugarcane refinery through the integration of bioethanol production, combined heat and power (CHP) generation using bagasse, and Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS), collectively forming a Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage (BECCS) system. This study defines a base scenario (BS) with a typical Mexican sugarcane mill, Ingenio Motzorongo, producing sugar, molasses, anhydro ethanol as oxygenate agent of gasoline and including combined heat and power (CHP) from sugarcane bagasse combustion. Also, we propose an alternative scenario (AS) comprising the latter products and adding a carbon capture process. The research investigates the potential for achieving net-negative carbon emissions by capturing CO 2 from two sources: the highly pure stream from ethanol fermentation and the flue gas from the bagasse-fired CHP plant. The integrated model focuses on maximizing the use of CO 2 neutral bagasse and optimizing the energy balance. Techno-economic (TEA) and life cycle analysis (LCA) were conducted to assess system performance. The results indicate that the minimal total CCS cost is achieved using the internal steam generated from sugarcane bagasse. This scenario corresponds to a 22% CO 2 capture rate, with total and CCS costs of 86.8 and 73.9 US$/ton CO 2 , respectively. To achieve a higher CO 2 capture rate, external energy input (steam and/or power) is required. However, this necessity reduces the cost-competitiveness of the BECCS process, particularly if the external energy is sourced from conventional fossil fuels. Ultimately, the integration of the BECCS system significantly reduces the overall environmental impacts associated with the production of bioethanol, energy, and sugar; especially with key indicators such as Global Warming Potential (GWP100), human toxicit potential (HTP) y, and specific aquatic ecotoxicity potential (SAEP).

title: Dual-phase nanoconfinement effects: Vanadium-MOF derived nanoporous carbon-coated V2O3 nanorods as multifunctional additives for advanced Mg-based hydrogen storage
abstract: Due to their large specific surface area and high porosity, porous carbon materials have emerged as a prominent research focus in the field of hydrogen storage. In this study, nanoporous carbon-coated V2O3 nanorods (p-V2O3/C) were synthesized through high-temperature calcination under a gas mixture using a vanadium metal-organic framework (V-MOF) as a precursor, aimed at enhancing the hydrogen storage performance of MgH2. The incorporation of p-V2O3/C significantly reduced both the initial dehydrogenation temperature and the activation energy for dehydrogenation of MgH2 to 192 °C and 88.6 kJ∙mol−1, respectively. Notably, catalytic MgH2 can desorb 5.35 wt% hydrogen even at a low temperature of 225 °C over a duration of 75 min, with an impressive capacity retention rate of 98.5% after 30 cycles of hydrogen absorption/release. The proposed catalytic mechanism indicates that the presence of metals such as V, VO, V2O3, and MgO in the composite system formed by p-V2O3/C with ball-milled MgH2 serves to reduce the Mg-H bond strength, thereby facilitating easier dehydrogenation of MgH2. Additionally, incorporating MgO can stabilize the crystal interface of MgH2 while impeding particle growth and enhancing its dehydrogenation process. In this work, the multiphase composite system based on p-V2O3/C has improved the kinetic performance for hydrogen storage in MgH2.

title: A bi-level optimization framework for capacity configuration of high-penetration renewable energy systems enhanced by pumped storage
abstract: The large-scale integration of renewable energy, driven by the China’s carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals, has become an inevitable trend in modern power systems, yet its inherent stochasticity and volatility challenge system stability and economic operation. This study takes a prefecture-level city in East China (thermal 42.1%, wind 23.6%, photovoltaic 34.3%) as a case and develops a capacity configuration optimization model for a thermal–wind–photovoltaic–pumped storage integrated system (TWPIS). Using wind, photovoltaic, and load data from 2019, the Synchronous Backward Reduction (SBR) algorithm generates 27 typical scenarios to characterize source–load uncertainty. A bi-level optimization framework is then established: the outer level optimizes renewable capacity using the Multi-Objective Multi-Verse Optimizer (MOMVO), while the inner level solves a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) operational model via CPLEX combined with the ε-constraint method. The optimal configuration is selected from the Pareto frontier through an entropy-weighted TOPSIS approach. Results show that introducing pumped storage reduces the required wind and photovoltaic capacities from 3,978 MW and 2,274 MW to 2,700 MW and 1,110 MW, respectively. Through peak-shaving and valley-filling, wind and photovoltaic curtailment rates drop from over 20% and 50% to below 6%, while the total operating cost decreases by approximately 47% on average. Annual time-series simulation further confirms that the system operates efficiently and stably for more than 75% of the time. The findings demonstrate that pumped storage plays a critical role in enhancing flexibility, promoting renewable integration, and ensuring economic operation of high-renewable power systems.

title: Evaluation of the importance of urban morphological parameters in albedo-based three-dimensional solar potential estimation
abstract: Solar photovoltaic deployment is pivotal for achieving carbon neutrality by harnessing renewable energy in urban environments. Accurately assessing the role of urban morphology in shaping solar potential distribution is critical for policy design, particularly in metropolitan areas where vertical surfaces constitute a significant share of directly sun-exposed urban areas. However, conventional models relying on fixed albedo values oversimplify multi-reflective dynamics, underestimating indirect radiation contributions and introducing systemic errors in solar potential estimation. This simplification further obscures the interplay between urban morphology and solar redistribution, leading to an incomplete understanding of morphological impacts. In this work, we propose a machine learning-based framework that integrates material-specific albedo with 3D urban geometry to quantify morphological importance. Simulation results identify the mean façade albedo as the dominant annual-scale driver (22.7% relative importance), followed by building volume (21.6%) and façade area (7.5%). Seasonal and diurnal analyses reveal temporal dependencies: volumetric factors govern solar gains by affecting shadow effects during temporal transitions, while density and aggregated neighborhood reflectance synergistically enhance multi-reflections in these periods. These findings underscore the necessity of balancing urban morphology with material albedos to maximize solar harvesting in urban planning.

title: Exergy-aware design, deep learning PINN-deriven multi objective optimization of a next-generation solid oxide fuel cell–organic Rankine cycle–photovoltaic-thermal solar collectors hybrid power system
abstract: This study presents a next-generation hybrid power system that integrates a solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC), an organic Rankine cycle (ORC), photovoltaic–thermal (PVT) solar collectors, and an electrolyzer to simultaneously address the dual challenges of achieving high-efficiency energy conversion and enabling sustainable distributed power generation. While previous studies often relied on steady-state models or black-box optimizers, the proposed framework addresses this gap by combining rigorous first- and second-law thermodynamic modeling with a hybrid optimization strategy based on deep learning, Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) and the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II). Embedding physical constraints directly into the learning process enables accurate yet computationally efficient exploration of design and operating conditions. The novelty of this research lies in both system-level integration and methodological advancement. This study develops one of the fully coupled SOFC–ORC–PVT–Electrolyzer hybrid configurations with a comprehensive thermo-economic–environmental assessment. Moreover, the study establishes a physics-constrained optimization framework that avoids the pitfalls of black-box machine learning and purely heuristic optimization by using hybrid model. The results reveal that the SOFC provides high-temperature electrochemical power, the ORC recovers low-grade heat at 120 °C using R601 as working fluid, and the PVT collectors supply both electrical and thermal energy under realistic solar boundary conditions. Multi-objective optimization demonstrates operating points that maximize exergy efficiency (up to 63.2%) while minimizing the levelized cost of electricity to competitive values. The PINN surrogate achieves strong predictive accuracy (R2 = 0.87 for cost, R2 = 0.75 for exergy efficiency), demonstrating its ability to capture nonlinear thermo-economic interactions with physical fidelity.

title: Large language model-based swarm intelligence for parameter identification of photovoltaic cells
abstract: Accurate parameter extraction for photovoltaic models is critical for optimizing system efficiency and ensuring operational stability. However, conventional deterministic and metaheuristic methods often suffer from premature convergence due to the strong nonlinearity and multimodality of the objective function. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a framework capable of adaptive strategy selection, termed large language model-based swarm intelligence. By embedding Meta LLaMA-3.1-405B-Instruct as the high-level strategic reasoning core, the proposed method integrates a triple stagnation detection mechanism that dynamically switches between optimization algorithms to prevent local optima entrapment. Furthermore, a physics-informed validation module is incorporated to enforce boundary constraints and ensure the physical feasibility of the identified parameters. Comparative experiments demonstrate that large language model-based swarm intelligence yields superior accuracy over state-of-the-art metaheuristics, achieving root mean square error reductions of 84.6% for the single diode model, 84.3% for the double diode model, and 82.1% for the triple diode model.

title: Innovative non-precious metal ZnSe/NiCo2O4 S-scheme heterojunction photocatalyst with the abundant active sites and highly efficient carrier separation for the enhancement of photocatalytic H2 evolution
abstract: A novel nanoscale ZnSe/NiCo2O4 S-scheme heterostructure photocatalyst was successfully fabricated via a solvothermal method. Morphological characterizations demonstrate that ZnSe nanoparticles were tightly deposited on the NiCo2O4 nanorods, constructing S-scheme heterojunction. Ni and Co ions had multivalent states, which acted as abundant redox active sites. Benefiting from the synergy of the S-scheme heterojunction and multivalent redox centers, the separation efficiency of photogenerated charge carriers was remarkably improved. NiCo2O4 had the superior porous microstructure and higher specific surface area, which greatly promoted the adsorption of H2O molecules and the desorption of H2. Moreover, ZnSe/NiCo2O4 delivered a lower H2 evolution overpotential than pure ZnSe, indicating its faster H2 production kinetics. The optimized ZnSe/3NiCo2O4 could achieve a prominent photocatalytic H2 generation rate of 2120.26 μmol g−1 h−1, approximately 2.64-fold that of pure ZnSe. DFT calculations revealed that electrons transferred from ZnSe to NiCo2O4 occurred upon the formation of the S-scheme heterojunction, which further accelerated carrier separation. ΔG calculations confirmed that the introduction of NiCo2O4 endowed ZnSe/NiCo2O4 with superior H2O adsorption and H2 desorption capacities compared to pure ZnSe, consistent with the TEM and BET results. This study provided useful insights for reasonable design of S-scheme heterojunction photocatalysts by introducing bimetallic oxides. This non-precious metal photocatalytic system also shows great application potential for converting solar energy into renewable green H2.

title: Correlation of mechanical properties with biaxial and triaxial durability in polymer electrolyte membranes
abstract: Polymer electrolyte membranes (PEMs), primarily insulate gases and facilitate proton transfer. Mechanical degradation of membranes is a major cause of early fuel cell failure. However, existing research has yet to establish a clear relationship between mechanical properties and durability. This study aims to establish a structure-activity relationship linking uniaxial mechanical properties, biaxial and triaxial durability, enabling prediction of the mechanical lifetime of perfluorosulfonic-acid (PFSA) membranes from their mechanical properties. Additionally, a stress factor (SF), derived from uniaxial mechanical properties, is introduced as a key mechanical descriptor to quantitatively link mechanical properties with durability. Our findings revealed that mechanical properties and biaxial durability decreased with increasing temperature and humidity, with humidity-driven degradation primarily arising from weakened intermolecular interactions, particularly between water molecules, as demonstrated by molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. However, the temperature-dependent degradation was governed by both weakened intermolecular interactions and the increased kinetic energy of the polymer chains. More importantly, SF shows approximately exponential relationships with both biaxial and triaxial durability, while the two durability metrics are strongly linearly correlated. By integrating uniaxial mechanical properties, biaxial and triaxial durability, we clarified the mechanical degradation mechanism at micro- and macro-scales, providing an effective method and theoretical foundation for predicting mechanical durability.

title: Coordinated optimization scheduling of pumped storage and wind-solar power station considering CVaR risk in multiple electricity markets
abstract: With the increasing penetration of wind and photovoltaic generation, renewable-output and electricity-price uncertainties place growing demands on flexible resource scheduling. To support low-carbon operation and multi-energy coordination, this study develops a coordinated scheduling model for a wind–solar–pumped-storage hydropower (PSH) portfolio participating in multiple electricity markets. The model captures the physical and economic coupling among different market segments and reflects the competition for limited flexibility across multiple market products. Renewable generation and electricity price uncertainties are incorporated using a scenario-based approach, and Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) is introduced to quantify downside risk and support risk-aware scheduling decisions. A case study based on the Zhejiang power system shows that PSH dynamically switches among pumping, generation, and ancillary service provision in response to market signals. Through a comparison of four scheduling cases, the proposed model increases total profit by 15.5% over the spot-only benchmark and by 29.7% over the case without ancillary-service participation; under the combined extreme uncertainty scenario, it reduces the maximum drawdown by 43.7% compared with the risk-neutral model. Over the 7-day scheduling horizon, the portfolio achieves an expected revenue of 3.7989×10^7 RMB and a risk-adjusted revenue of 3.4190×10^7 RMB; renewable energy feed-in accounts for 40.2% of total revenue, while reserve and frequency-regulation services jointly contribute 22.9%. In addition, the synergy among wind, solar, and PSH improves system flexibility and renewable accommodation. Overall, the proposed scheduling approach balances economic performance and risk control, providing practical insights for multi-energy coordination and dispatch in power systems with high renewable penetration.

title: Assessing the impact of green bonds on renewable innovation and sustainable growth
abstract: Achieving global net-zero emission targets necessitates significant investment in clean energy transitions and the development of renewable energy technologies. Therefore, this study utilizes the panel data of 23 countries from 2014 to 2022 and apply (IV-GMM) technique to study the impact of green bonds on eco-innovation, low-carbon technology products, and renewable energy technology innovation. The findings indicated that a 1% increase in issuance volume of green bonds leads to 0.5122% of increase in eco-innovation, 0.8657% increase in low-carbon technology products, and 0.3026% increase in renewable energy technology innovation. Further analysis revealed that a 1% increase in green bond issuance reduce the carbon footprints of economic activity by 0.3205% while promoting investments in clean energy by 1.2188%. Furthermore, the mediation analysis reveals that a 1% rise in green bond issuance improves government environmental expenditure by 0.2863% and R&D investment by 0.4127%. Income-group heterogeneity reveals sturdier sustainability effects of green bonds in middle-income countries. Similar findings are obtained from robustness checks using Driscoll-Kraay fixed effect and alternative dependent variables. Policymakers are advised to enhance green bond frameworks and pair them with focused environmental spending and R&D assistance to boost low-carbon innovation and facilitate the shift to sustainable energy systems.

title: Numerical investigations of the thermal performance of a novel groundwater – filled ground heat exchanger design
abstract: Ground heat exchangers are key components of shallow geothermal systems, including ground-coupled heat pumps and underground thermal energy storage systems. Reducing their installation costs through innovative designs remains a major challenge. In this study, the thermal performance of a Novel groundwater-filled Ground Heat Exchanger (NGHE) designed to promote thermally induced natural convection is investigated. The system incorporates truncated conical heat exchange plates, which increase the effective heat transfer surface area per unit depth and enhance thermally induced convective flow. A numerical model is developed and validated using experimental data to assess the behavior of this new design at shallow subsurface installation depths (i.e. 3–9 m below basement level). Three installation configurations have been proposed and analyzed. A comprehensive set of simulations is carried out to quantify the influence of key design parameters, installation geometry, and subsurface hydrogeological conditions. The metropolitan area of Bari (Italy) is used as a climate and hydrogeological framework. Results indicate that the novel ground heat exchanger is more efficient than the Conventional Ground Heat Exchanger (CGHE) design under a wide range of installation configurations, hydrogeological conditions, and operating modes. These findings suggest that the proposed heat exchanger could enable more compact and cost-effective shallow geothermal systems.

title: Design of snowflake-inspired biomimetic flow fields in proton exchange membrane fuel cells guided by Murray's law
abstract: Proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) have attracted considerable interest owing to their high efficiency and clean operation, becoming a key focus in renewable energy technology research. The present study proposes a novel bionic snowflake flow field (BSFF) rooted in Murray's law traffic distribution mechanism, establishes a 3D steady-state numerical model, and validates its reliability through experimental data. Subsequently, the output performance of the BSFF is analyzed in terms of electrochemical performance and flow mass transfer characteristics, comparing it with conventional parallel flow fields and single serpentine flow fields. Finally, the influence of main channel number on BSFF performance is examined, and its mass-transfer characteristics are analyzed using the principle of field synergy. Results indicate that the pressure drop and center-plane velocity vector of the BSFF are significantly lower than those of conventional flow fields, thereby reducing pump power requirements. Concurrently, the output performance of the BSFF first increases and then decreases with the number of main channels, peaking at 8 main channels. This configuration achieves a maximum net power density of 5465.54 W/m2, representing improvements of 70.19% and 10.99% over the parallel flow-field and single serpentine flow-field, respectively. These performance improvements primarily stem from the bionic branching structure designed according to Murray's law, which enables rational traffic distribution and reduces energy consumption in the BSFF transport system. Additionally, increasing the number of main channels appropriately reduces mass-transfer losses, narrows the synergy angle between the velocity and concentration fields, and enhances water-management capabilities. The aforementioned study not only validated the applicability of Murray's law in fuel cell flow field design from a bionic perspective but also provided new design concepts and theoretical references for enhancing the overall performance of PEMFCs.

title: Identifying the ex-situ catalytic co-pyrolysis of lignin and waste tires to bio-oil over ZnCr2O4/HZSM-5 catalyst
abstract: Converting biomass and hydrogen-rich wastes (e.g., waste tires) into bio-oil represents a promising route to reduce dependence on fossil resources. However, poor bio-oil quality and catalyst deactivation remain significant challenges. In this study, a bifunctional composite catalyst composed of spinel oxides and molecular sieves was prepared for the ex-situ catalytic pyrolysis of lignin and waste tires to produce high-quality bio-oil. A combined strategy of characterization analysis and mathematical analysis methods (e.g., principal component analysis and two-dimensional correlation spectroscopy analysis) was employed to identify the catalytic pyrolysis mechanism. Results indicated that the combined effects of oxygen vacancies, the porous structure, and acid-base sites in the ZnCr2O4/HZSM-5 catalyst contribute to its high catalytic activity. The catalyst effectively promoted deoxygenation of oxygenates (especially phenols) and facilitated the conversion of aliphatics into aromatics via cyclization and aromatization. Under optimal conditions (600 °C catalysis temperature and 20% catalyst mass ratio), the aromatic content reached 83.89%. More importantly, the catalyst showed excellent stability and regenerability, maintaining high performance over five cycles. Principal component analysis identified catalytic temperature as the dominant factor governing bio-oil composition. Mechanism studies revealed that oxygen vacancies in ZnCr2O4 enhance the adsorption and activation of H2 and oxygenates. Subsequently, the acidic sites on HZSM-5 further catalyze C-O bond cleavage and aromatization reactions in these intermediates. The co-catalytic action of the two components significantly improves hydrodeoxygenation efficiency and aromatic content. This work not only demonstrates the promise of spinel-zeolite composite catalysts for high-quality bio-oil production but also provides a new catalyst design strategy and theoretical basis for the efficient conversion of biomass and hydrogen-rich wastes.

title: A novel all-non-metallic bipolar plate and the lightweight alkaline electrolyzer for system validation
abstract: Renewable-energy-based hydrogen production is an effective pathway for converting renewable electricity into storable hydrogen. However, heavy water-electrolysis equipment remains a key challenge, limiting deployment flexibility in some renewable-energy applications. Here, an all-non-metallic bipolar plate is proposed by decoupling the mechanical and electrochemical functions of the plate. A glass fiber-reinforced plastic frame is used for mechanical support, while a graphite component is used for current collection, heat transfer, and flow-field integration. A triple Chebyshev helix flow field is embedded to enhance electrolyte redistribution and bubble removal. The proposed non-metallic electrolyzer is compared with metallic and conventional flow-field configurations through numerical simulation and experimental validation. At 2.0 V and 0.4 m s−1, the optimized non-metallic configuration achieves a gas volume fraction of 0.09 and a current density of 0.094 A cm−2. Compared with the metallic parallel-serpentine and metallic triple-Chebyshev-helix configurations, the gas volume fraction decreases by 67.9% and 43.8%, while the current density increases by 68.5% and 51.1%, respectively. The specific energy consumption of the optimized non-metallic electrolyzer is 5.2 kWh Nm−3, only 1.96% higher than that of the metallic triple-Chebyshev-helix electrolyzer. The single-cell and five-cell non-metallic electrolyzers reduce stack mass by 66.4% and 69.1%, increasing the mass-index hydrogen production rate by 194.4% and 221%, respectively. A 100 h test further shows stable operation under the tested conditions. These results indicate that the proposed design can reduce hardware mass while maintaining comparable electrochemical performance, providing a lightweight electrolyzer strategy for renewable-energy-based hydrogen production systems.

title: Thermo-mechanical damage and stability of underground salt cavern energy storage under accelerated cyclic operations
abstract: Underground Energy Storage in deep salt caverns has emerged as a strategic imperative for buffering the volatility of renewable energy integration. However, the accelerated cyclic operations dictated by renewable grid demands introduce severe alternating thermo-mechanical fatigue, escalating the risks of structural failure and hydrogen migration. To overcome the limitations of classical steady-state rock mechanics models, this paper proposes a fully coupled thermo-mechanical Burgers model incorporating continuum damage mechanics. Validated through cyclic high-confining-pressure laboratory tests and acoustic emission monitoring, the model accurately captures the "S"-shaped nonlinear damage acceleration induced by thermal softening and effective stress amplification. Applying this model to the JK8-6 salt cavern, a comprehensive five-dimensional stability evaluation framework was established. Full-lifecycle numerical results demonstrate that while a conventional 1 cycle/year scenario limits the 30-year volume shrinkage to a safe 4.02%, accelerating to 3 cycles/year drives the shrinkage to 19.39% and breaches the 0.5 engineering damage threshold, triggering severe macroscopic seepage risks. This study provides critical geotechnical guidance for the safe, long-term management of Underground Energy Storage under accelerated cyclic renewable energy integration.

title: Investigation of the source-load characteristics of a PV-battery-refrigeration coupled system for long-distance transportation in vehicle-mounted refrigerated containers
abstract: Supplying refrigerated trucks with photovoltaic power has become an important strategy for improving energy efficiency and reducing emissions in the cold-chain transportation sector. In this study, a PV system was integrated into a standard refrigerated container. Considering various environmental influencing factors, heat transfer and power generation models of the PV-integrated refrigerated container were developed. The electric-cooling balance of the PV-integrated refrigerated container was then analyzed during cross-regional transport along the Tianjin-Tongliao route. Finally, the potential carbon emission reductions were evaluated. During a simulated cross-regional transport from Tianjin to Tongliao, the theoretical power generation of the photovoltaic system throughout the year is sufficient to meet the cooling needs of the refrigerated container, with a maximum theoretical power generation of over 25 kWh. The surplus power generation for each transportation in different months ranges from 7.55 kWh to 16.36 kWh in different months. Along the Tianjin-Tongliao transport route, the cumulative carbon savings over a ten-year service life are estimated to reach approximately 25.4 metric tons of CO2. By presenting clearly defined monthly and annual performance metrics, this study provides an intuitive understanding of the value of PV integration in refrigerated vehicles.

title: Hybrid algorithm for medium-term photovoltaic power prediction. Two-stage clustering-CNN-BiLSTM-Attention: Case study Lima (Peru)
abstract: The dimensioning of a solar plant requires historical information on seasonal meteorological variability where it will be installed. To ensure efficient photovoltaic (PV) energy production, accurate predictions that recognize variability are necessary. There are various hybrid prediction models without clear verification of the quality of clustering. Current PV prediction models have architectures with more accurate results but with a significant increase in computational time. A novel hybrid model is proposed that uses real historical data with a two-stage clustering process: physical-deterministic clustering for climatic seasons and clustering with the K-Medoids method to segment overcast and clear days, the results of which are incorporated into the CNN-BiLSTM-Attention prediction model trained on the residual over the cluster-mean baseline, allowing competitive results to be obtained over time horizons of 1, 2, 4, 7, 14, and 21 days. The clustering quality is supported by the joint optimization of three indices: Silhouette Score (SS) between 0.6698 and 0.8616, Calinski-Harabasz (CHI) up to 655.86, and Davies–Bouldin (DBI) as low as 0.4320, identifying 𝐾 ∗ = 2 as optimal across all four seasons. The proposed model attains 𝑅 2 between 0.8330 and 0.8453, RMSE between 0.1585 and 0.1627 kW, and MAE between 0.1156 and 0.1171 kW across the six horizons evaluated under stratified 7-daily split, 5-fold expanding-window cross-validation, 95% bootstrap confidence intervals, and Diebold–Mariano testing. During the 2023–2024 Coastal El Niño event, the model performs ＋2.6% better in 𝑅 2 than under normal conditions (0.8721 vs. 0.8498), demonstrating the robustness of two-stage clustering under anomalous climatic regimes.

title: A dimensionless state-space representation of wind turbines under sub-maximum power point operation and load-aware active power control
abstract: Wind turbines are increasingly required to operate below their maximum power point to provide active power control for grid support and wind farm optimisation. Such sub-MPP operation alters wind turbine behaviour, potentially increasing fatigue damage and compromising operational stability. However, the physical interactions among actuators and structural loads during active power control remain insufficiently understood. This paper introduces a dimensionless state-space representation of wind turbine operation formulated on the power and thrust coefficient (Cp-Ct) surfaces. This provides a geometric interpretation of wind turbine states, visualising how control actions affect structural loading. To verify this representation, a simple Thrust Coefficient Control strategy is developed to reduce fatigue damage induced by active power control, without compromising fast power response. OpenFAST simulations of the NREL 5 MW reference turbine show that the proposed strategy behaves as predicted by the dimensionless representation, while turbulent wind simulations indicate reductions in blade and tower fatigue damage of 73.1% and 23%, respectively, compared to the baseline implementation. Comparative simulations in similar environments further clarify the unique complementary role of the controller relative to existing ones. This shows that substantial fatigue mitigation can be achieved using a simple, physically informed control structure without resorting to complex multi-input multi-output optimisation.

title: Evaluation and mechanism study of high-entropy oxide catalysts for supercritical water gasification of biomass
abstract: Catalytic supercritical water gasification (SCWG) of biomass is a promising technology for sustainable hydrogen production, yet its development is constrained by the inherent complexity of SCWG reaction networks and catalyst deactivation under extreme operating conditions. Herein, a high-entropy oxide (HEO, NiMgCuZnCoO) catalyst was synthesized via a co-precipitation method, and its structure was confirmed through X-ray diffraction (XRD) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Experiments with a wide range of reaction parameters (temperature: 350-500 °C, glucose concentration: 2 wt%-10 wt%) were conducted, and the HEO catalyst achieved a carbon gasification efficiency of 71% and a hydrogen-containing gas yield of 14.55 mol·kg−1 at 500 °C with 2 wt% glucose, substantially outperforming common metallic oxide catalysts. Good reusability over four catalytic SCWG cycles, along with the preserved rock-salt structure and uniform elemental distribution (confirmed by XRD and TEM-EDX mapping), demonstrated its excellent hydrothermal stability. The contributions of individual elements in the HEO catalyst were uncovered through a multifaceted approach: benchmarking against element-deficient quaternary oxides, analyzing tri-phase products, and conducting in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy investigations of glucose steam gasification, including comparative studies with quaternary oxide catalysts. This NiMgCuZnCoO HEO catalyst exhibited good activity and versatility across SCWG of diverse real biomass feedstocks. A multi-site synergistic mechanism for the HEO catalyst was proposed to regulate the intricate SCWG reaction network of biomass, providing a new perspective for advancing SCWG technology.

title: Green diesel production via biodiesel upgrading over Ru/nitrogen-doped carbon catalysts derived from yeast cell wall waste
abstract: A sustainable strategy was developed to upgrade biodiesel (fatty acid methyl esters) from microbial lipids into green diesel (hydrocarbons) while valorizing waste byproducts. Waste yeast cell walls of Rhodosporidium toruloides were converted into nitrogen-doped activated carbon (NC) using their intrinsic nitrogen content, which served as a support for noble metal hydrodeoxygenation catalysts. Among four catalysts, Ru/NC delivered the best performance, achieving 100% conversion and 84.71% alkane yield in the hydrodeoxygenation of methyl stearate. Structural and theoretical analyses showed that electron transfer (1.03e–) from Ru to pyrrolic nitrogen sites. Additionally, Ru/NC exhibited stronger basicity and enhanced adsorption capacity for intermediate fatty acids. Applied to biodiesel from R. toruloides, Ru/NC reached 100% conversion and a C14–C18 alkane yield of 91.46%. This work presents a promising route for integrating waste utilization into biodiesel upgrading.

title: Renewable-homogeneity-based regions in European power system planning models
abstract: The increasing share of intermittent renewable generation in the European energy mix leads to a growing need for spatial detail in generation expansion planning models. High spatial resolution is desired to capture the spatial dependence of renewable technologies and identify important transmission bottlenecks, but it carries a substantial computational cost, especially with a detailed network representation. Models, therefore, rely on spatial aggregation, typically using administrative regions as the basis for aggregation. In this work, we ask whether that choice is in fact neutral. We define model regions by clustering locations based on renewable homogeneity, independent of national borders, and compare them with the conventional country-based approach across a range of network resolutions. We hold every other element of the model fixed so that the aggregation procedure is the only variable. We show that in the renewable-based method, model regions can be strong net importers or exporters of electricity, as opposed to the country-based model in which regions tend to be relatively self-sufficient. Most importantly, the total transmission volume in the new method is far more reflective of the high-resolution benchmark than in the traditional country-based approach. Because country-based aggregation underpins many policy-facing models, this finding is primarily diagnostic: it cautions that such models may systematically understate the transmission expansion required for the energy transition.

title: A novel six-in-one electrode design with a gas-permeable layer for enhanced mass transport in PEMWE
abstract: Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) is a critical technology for converting intermittent renewable energy into sustainable green hydrogen because of its rapid dynamic response and high efficiency. However, mass transport overpotential remains a major performance limitation at low catalyst loadings and high current densities, particularly under fluctuating power inputs. Here, we introduce a novel six-in-one integrated electrode with a gas-permeable layer (GPL) on the anode side of the proton exchange membrane. The GPL prevents catalyst embedding into the membrane and provides additional gas transport pathways, thereby improving electrolysis performance. By tuning the GPL thickness and ionomer content, we optimized its porosity and surface hydrophobicity, which further boosted performance. At an iridium loading of 0.3 mgIr/cm2, the optimized electrode achieved 4.22 A/cm2 at 2.0 V and reduced the total cell voltage by approximately 160 mV at 5.0 A/cm2. The electrode also exhibited degradation rates of 0.09 mV/h and 0.11 mV/h under steady-state and dynamic operation, respectively. This work provides an effective strategy for mitigating mass transport limitations in low-loading PEMWEs and supports their stable integration with fluctuating renewable energy sources.

title: Synergistic Photo–Biological coupling in photocatalytically assisted soil microbial fuel cells for renewable electricity generation and efficient cyfluthrin removal
abstract: Soil Microbial Fuel Cells (SMFCs) can simultaneously remove pollutants and generate bioelectricity, yet the low electrocatalytic activity of conventional carbon cathodes restricts their performance. This study develops a cost-effective “photocatalysis-SMFC coupling” system using CuO/MoS2 heterojunction photocathodes for the first time. The 2:1CuO/MoS2 photocatalyst exhibits strong absorption and efficient charge separation, significantly achieving a maximum open-circuit voltage of 734.9 mV and a peak power density of 16.85 mW m−2 when connected to a 2000 Ω resistor—nearly a threefold increase over the original system. In CY degradation applications, the degradation efficiency remained remarkably high at 82.7% after four cycles. Mechanistically, photoexcitation of CuO/MoS2 produces reactive species that initiate CY oxidation, while soil degraders (Pseudomonas, Bacillus, Sphingomonas) further convert intermediates. DFT calculations further reveal that the heterojunction reduces the ORR energy barrier from 0.62 eV to 0.44 eV, with the Cu d-band center upshifting from −4.837 eV to −4.594 eV, confirming that interfacial charge transfer and enhanced intermediate adsorption promote the four-electron ORR pathway. Enrichment of electroactive bacteria (Proteobacteria and Firmicutes) accelerates redox cycling and electron transfer at the anode, reinforcing mineralization and forming an efficient “photoelectric-microbial ternary coupling mechanism.” This work demonstrates a stable and high-performance photocatalytic-enhanced SMFC, providing a promising strategy for renewable energy utilization and self-powered in situ pollutant remediation.

title: Dynamic analysis of a hybrid methanol-fueled fuel cell and photovoltaic system powered solid oxide electrolysis cell system for co-electrolysis of hydrogen and carbon monoxide production
abstract: Solid oxide electrolysis cell (SOEC) technology enables efficient carbon dioxide conversion into value-added chemicals, providing a critical pathway toward carbon neutrality. This paper presents an integrated system that couples a methanol-fueled solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) with photovoltaics (PV) to power the SOEC, enabling highly efficient hydrogen and carbon monoxide production via co-electrolysis. The SOFC ensures continuous and stable system operation under all load conditions by supplying reliable backup power. The dynamic characteristics of the system were evaluated against benchmark PV operating conditions from Inner Mongolia, China, representative of the four seasons. A feedforward control strategy was employed to ensure stable and efficient system operation by regulating the SOEC's current density, water flow rate, and carbon dioxide flow rate. Throughout the annual cycle, the SOEC exhibits peak temperature variability in winter within 13K/d. The system demonstrated its optimal performance in autumn and poorest performance in winter. Specifically, an electrolysis efficiency of 83.24%, a specific hydrogen energy consumption (SHEC) of 3.70 kWh/Nm3, and a specific carbon monoxide energy consumption (SCEC) of 4.70 kWh/Nm3 were achieved in autumn. In contrast, the corresponding values for winter were 78.68%, 3.84 kWh/Nm3, and 5.24 kWh/Nm3, respectively. During spring, summer, and autumn, the system sequesters 0.33 t/d, 0.90 t/d, and 1.12 t/d of carbon dioxide from the environment, respectively. Conversely, it releases 1.7 t/d of carbon dioxide in winter due to shorter effective daylight hours and lower solar irradiation intensity.

title: Operational strategy assessment for seasonal hydrogen storage in homogeneous and heterogeneous deep saline anticline aquifers: Effects of cushion gas selection, well configuration, and cyclic injection
abstract: The growing mismatch between renewable energy supply and demand necessitates large-scale seasonal underground hydrogen storage in deep saline aquifers. This study presents a field-scale compositional numerical simulation assessment of operational strategies for underground hydrogen storage in homogeneous and heterogeneous anticline deep saline aquifers using CMG simulator on an optimized 91 x 44 x 10 corner-point grid model. Cushion gas type and fraction, well configuration, reservoir petrophysical properties, and cyclic injection-production schedules were systematically evaluated against cumulative hydrogen mass stored and recovery efficiency. Results show that nitrogen consistently outperformed CO2 and CH4 across all cushion gas fractions, yielding 268,706.5 kg at 20% fraction, attributable to its chemical inertness, low aqueous solubility, and favorable gravitational segregation from hydrogen. Reservoir heterogeneity enhanced stored hydrogen mass by approximately 12 to 15% relative to the homogeneous formation by enhancing plume distribution and improved volumetric sweep efficiency. Recovery efficiency remained insensitive to injector-to-producer spacing across 0 to 60 m, peaking at 91.48% at 15 m spacing. Mole fraction analysis identified nitrogen as providing the best operational producer placement, offering field operators a flexibility in well positioning without losing hydrogen purity. This study provides practical screening and operational design criteria for large-scale underground hydrogen storage in saline aquifer systems.

title: Machine-learning-assisted cathode GDL design for high-performance PEMFCs in renewable-hydrogen transportation systems
abstract: Renewable-hydrogen transportation requires proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) with high power density under demanding loads. However, oxygen-transport resistance and liquid-water accumulation in the cathode gas diffusion layer (GDL) remain major limitations. Here, we develop a machine-learning-assisted framework that coordinates three-dimensional cathode-GDL porosity design across four flow-field geometries. A three-dimensional two-phase model and four gradient boosting decision tree (GBDT) surrogates were used to screen X-, Y- and Z-dependent porosity profiles. At 0.50 V, optimization increased current density by 2.32%–2.84%. After cathode pumping correction, the optimized sinusoidal case achieved a slightly higher net power density than the sinusoidal-blocked case (0.830 versus 0.819 W cm−2). The serpentine design increased mean interfacial oxygen concentration by 31.24% and reduced liquid-water saturation by 25.84%, whereas the sinusoidal-blocked design reduced saturation by 33.83%. These results establish flow-field-dependent GDL optimization as a component-level strategy for high-load PEMFCs.

title: Multidisciplinary design optimization for wave-driven desalination systems
abstract: Wave-driven desalination systems are an innovative solution to the global freshwater crisis, leveraging the complementary characteristics of seawater reverse osmosis and wave energy converters. However, the high costs of this system pose a significant barrier to widespread adoption. Optimization can help these systems reach a more competitive levelized cost of water, but the highly coupled nature of the system necessitates a multidisciplinary design optimization approach. This paper presents a holistic, multidisciplinary design optimization framework for wave-driven desalination system design, integrating models for wave energy converter hydrodynamics, power take-off transmission, seawater reverse osmosis constraints, and economic analysis. This study demonstrates the impact of multidisciplinary design optimization for wave-driven desalination systems, resulting in a 69.5% reduction in levelized cost of water within this modeling framework compared to a nominal design. We demonstrate that multidisciplinary design optimization outperforms two different sequential design approaches, yielding lower levelized costs of water and substantially different optimal designs. The multidisciplinary design optimization results suggest major design changes compared to designs found in the literature. Notably, smaller wave energy converters and larger pistons, along with smaller accumulators and larger seawater reverse osmosis plant installations, are preferred within this modeling framework. These design trends are consistent across a range of sea states, suggesting potential generalizability beyond a single location. This study demonstrates the importance of holistic modeling and co-design for wave-driven desalination systems and establishes an effective optimization framework for future studies to build upon.

title: A phase-change flow distributor enhances thermal performance in thermocline thermal energy storage system
abstract: Single-tank thermocline thermal energy storage (TES) systems are gaining adoption over conventional two-tank systems, primarily due to their simpler structure and lower cost. However, the efficiency of thermocline systems is compromised by the mixing of hot and cold fluids, which disrupts critical thermal stratification. This study introduces two novel phase-change flow distributors (PFDs) with thicknesses of 20 mm and 40 mm. Compared to common flow distributors (CFDs) that only regulate the flow field, the PFD integrates latent heat storage with flow distribution, enabling simultaneous regulation of flow-guiding function and heat transfer. An experimental system was established to investigate the effects of distributor thickness on thermal-front evolution and thermal stratification under different inlet temperature. Evaluation metrics such as heat storage capacity and efficiency, were used to nondimensionalize and compare results. Results show the PFD effectively mitigates inlet thermal disturbances and stabilizes stratification. Moreover, PFD reduced the maximum radial temperature difference by 18.31%-25.62%, and reduced the average thermocline variation rate by 24.47%. By coupling flow field reconstruction with latent-heat thermal buffering, the novel PFD provides a promising approach for enhancing thermal stratification and improving the performance of thermocline TES systems.

title: Techno-economic and life cycle assessment of biomethane and biofertilizer production by solid- and liquid-state anaerobic digestion
abstract: Anaerobic digestion (AD) provides a sustainable pathway for managing organic waste and recovering renewable energy, contributing to environmental protection and energy security. This study integrates techno-economic analysis (TEA) and life cycle assessment (LCA) to evaluate the production of biomethane and biofertilizer from food waste, animal manure, and dry straw using solid-state (SS-AD) and liquid-state (LS-AD) configurations. Comparative results demonstrate that SS-AD consistently outperforms LS-AD across all feedstocks in energy conversion efficiency, economic performance, and environmental benefits. In the base-case scenario (10 ton/d), food waste-based SS-AD achieves a minimum biofertilizer selling price of $40.21/ton, below the market benchmark of $41.99/ton. LCA results show SS-AD of animal manure achieves the most significant reduction in global warming potential (0.12 kg CO2-eq/MJ), twice that of LS-AD. Sensitivity analysis identifies additive costs and governmental subsidies as the primary economic drivers, whereas methane yield variability exerts the most considerable influence on both energy and environmental outcomes. Under projected grid decarbonization, the GWP of food-waste SS-AD decreases from 49.3 to 1.2 g CO2-eq/MJ with a fully renewable electricity mix. This study highlights the environmental and economic viability of the SS-AD-based waste management system for renewable energy and bio-products production.

title: Thermodynamic evolution and semi-empirical correlations of underground compressed air energy storage caverns
abstract: Compressed air energy storage is a large-scale energy storage technology that bridges intermittent renewable energy and conventional power grids. The safety and operational efficiency of storage caverns are strongly governed by the coupled effects of geometric configuration, operating conditions, and material properties. In this study, a coupled Thermal-Hydro-Mechanical-Damage numerical framework is adopted and adapted to simulate turbulent flow, heat transfer, and gas behavior in the air domain, as well as heat conduction, mechanical deformation, and Darcy seepage in the surrounding rock. The multiphysical responses of the cavern system under a full charge-storage-discharge-storage cycle are systematically analyzed. Compared with linear caverns, full-circular caverns reduce the peak temperature and pressure by 13.85% and 6.46%, and exhibit a lower temperature change rate from 8.07 to 2.75 K/h, effectively alleviating thermal concentration. While the length diameter ratio decreases from 36.64 to 7.38, the peak wall temperature is reduced by about 7.12%, and the stress distribution becomes more uniform. Increasing the charging temperature significantly enhances thermal accumulation and enlarges the high-temperature zone, whereas increasing the convective heat transfer coefficient suppresses heat buildup. Improving the damage resistance of the surrounding rock reduces the extent of the damaged zone. Furthermore, temperature and pressure changing rates are introduced as dynamic indicators, and statistically evaluated semi-empirical correlations are established to describe the relative thermodynamic responses under varying geometric, operating, and material conditions. The proposed correlations are applicable within the investigated parameter ranges and can provide a rapid reference for preliminary cavern design screening and operating-condition assessment.

title: Inlet–outlet configuration effects on PEMFC cooling channels: A strategy for enhanced heat transfer and thermal management
abstract: During PEMFC operation, heat accumulation and temperature non-uniformity can adversely affect performance, durability, and system stability. Conventional single inlet–single outlet cooling channels often suffer from uneven coolant distribution, high pressure drop, and insufficient heat removal. Double inlet–double outlet configurations can improve flow distribution, reduce flow resistance, and enhance heat transfer, offering a promising strategy for thermal management in renewable hydrogen energy systems. This study systematically compares six double inlet–double outlet cooling-channel designs by evaluating pressure drop, membrane–electrode assembly temperature, heat-source characteristics, and polarization losses. The results show that the performance of double inlet–double outlet channels strongly depends on the specific inlet–outlet topology. Among the investigated configurations, the U–I channel exhibits the best overall performance, achieving an index of uniform temperature (IUT) of 1.67, an average MEM temperature of 354.61 K, and a cooling capacity (Qcool) of 26.13 W, representing a 76.5% increase over the N-type single inlet–single outlet benchmark under the prescribed inlet conditions. At 0.5 V, the U–I configuration reaches a current density of 1.251 A cm−2, which is 7.2% higher than that of the N-type benchmark, together with a peak power density of 0.758 W cm−2. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of double inlet–double outlet cooling channels for improving PEMFC thermal management and supporting efficient renewable hydrogen utilization.

title: Boundary mechanisms of externally induced chaos in wind turbine systems under fractional-order damping
abstract: Chaotic behavior in wind turbine systems is fundamentally governed by the interplay between external energy injection and intrinsic dissipation mechanisms, rather than by nonlinearity alone. From this perspective, this study examines how fractional-order damping influences the global dynamical behavior of a nonlinear wind turbine drivetrain while incorporating aerodynamic power capture, maximum power point tracking, and generator-side control. By incorporating the steady torque components into the equilibrium operating point and retaining unequal-amplitude dual-frequency perturbations, the relative torsional dynamics are reformulated via a time-scale transformation as a fractional-order Duffing-type system. Analysis of the unperturbed dynamics shows that under softening-stiffness conditions, the system exhibits a double-well potential with saddle and center equilibria, thereby creating homoclinic orbit structures associated with global chaotic instability. A generalized Melnikov function is derived by treating the two excitation amplitudes as independent parameters, enabling systematic characterization of the combined effects of excitation frequencies, amplitude allocation, nonlinear stiffness, fractional order, and damping intensity on the homoclinic chaos threshold.
