Numerical investigations based on two- and three-dimensional parameter spaces, bifurcation analysis, attractor geometry, time-domain responses, and spectral characteristics are further performed using the electromechanical model that incorporates maximum power point tracking and control dynamics. The results show that the two excitation components contribute differently to chaos onset, while fractional-order damping significantly shifts the instability threshold and modifies attractor expansion, oscillation intensity, and broadband frequency dispersion. These findings provide a mechanistic insight into drivetrain chaos and quantitative support for torsional instability assessment and parameter selection.

title: Beyond the IRENA baseline: Mapping end-of-life photovoltaic waste flows across EU-27 using Weibull lifetime distributions screened against Eurostat data and updated efficiency scenarios
abstract: As the European Union accelerates photovoltaic deployment to achieve the milestones outlined in the 2025 National Energy and Climate Plans, accurate waste forecasting emerges as a significant challenge for the circular economy. This study re-evaluates EU-27 PV waste projections through 2050, comparing theoretical models with available empirical Eurostat collection data. Findings indicate that the standard IRENA Regular Loss model systematically underestimates waste generation, resulting in collection rates that exceed 200%. A new scenario, RL NEW , is proposed, featuring a revised Weibull parameterization and an updated time-variable mass-to-capacity transformation function. This alternative baseline scenario, screened for consistency against Eurostat aggregate data, forecasts cumulative 2025 waste volumes that are 214% higher than previous estimates. For the first time, projections are disaggregated by application, revealing a rooftop-dominated market in which 60% of waste necessitates decentralized logistics. The analysis identifies a bifurcated challenge: established operators should expand capacity to manage 65% of the European Union’s waste, while rapidly growing markets encounter surges up to 12,000-fold. Additionally, the Collection Difficulty Index is introduced to quantify the logistical impact of waste stream fragmentation, identifying a "Logistical Pivot" around 2030 when utility-scale surges begin to alleviate the logistical burden of decentralized systems. This framework provides quantitative information that can be used for cross-border logistics and recycling capacity planning.

title: Closed-loop borehole heat exchanger systems: Insights from two Italian case studies
abstract: This paper presents a thermo-economic analysis of closed-loop borehole heat exchanger systems, investigating their feasibility for both direct thermal applications and heat and power cogeneration. A specific focus is placed on two Italian case studies: a residential district heating application in Gavorrano and an industrial/agricultural application in the Mt. Amiata area. A numerical model was developed to optimize the system components, including a novel cost correlation for Organic Rankine Cycle units operating under off-design conditions with well flow rates ranging between 50 and 300 kg/s. The results highlight the critical influence of geological characteristics and drilling costs on economic viability. Both applications proved to be generally in line with similar technologies in Europe from an economic point of view. In particular, the Mt. Amiata case study demonstrated significant economic potential, achieving a Levelized Cost of Heat of 0.1161 €/kWh for a 15-well configuration and 0.1462 €/kWh for a 20-well configuration. These findings suggest that borehole heat exchanger systems can be a cost-effective solution for decarbonizing industrial heat sectors in suitable geothermal settings.
keywords: Levelized cost of heat and energy

title: Study of the performance of SrCo0.50Fe0.45Ir0.05O3-δ cathodes for intermediate temperature solid oxide fuel cells (IT-SOFC) fueled by hydrogen and ammonia
abstract: This study presents the design, synthesis, and characterization of a novel perovskite-type cathode material, SrCo0.50Fe0.45Ir0.05O3-δ, for application in intermediate-temperature solid oxide fuel cells (IT-SOFCs). The reduction in cobalt content was achieved through partial substitution with Fe and Ir to stabilize the cubic phase near 400 °C. Structural characterization was performed using X-ray diffraction (XRD) and in situ neutron powder diffraction (NPD) in the range of 25–800 °C. A δ value of 0.306 was obtained at 800 °C, giving a final refined stoichiometry of SrCo0.50Fe0.45Ir0.05O2.694(1). The compound showed a weight loss of 1.585%. A thermal expansion coefficient (TEC) of 23.21 × 10−6 K−1 and an electrical conductivity of 39.44 S/cm at 800 °C were determined. Electrochemical performance was evaluated in single cells fueled with H2 and NH3, in which the electrodes were painted onto a 90 μm LSGM dense electrolyte, fabricated by tape casting. Power density was compared for Pd-infiltrated and non-infiltrated cathodes. At 800 °C under H2, the non-infiltrated cathode reached 314 mW/cm2, while the Pd-infiltrated cathode achieved 502 mW/cm2 after activation. Under NH3, the infiltrated cell reached 422 mW/cm2 at the same temperature. These results suggest that SrCo0.50Fe0.45Ir0.05O3-δ is a promising low-cobalt and structurally stable cathode material for IT-SOFC applications operating with hydrogen or ammonia fuels, while Pd infiltration provides an additional route to enhance electrochemical performance.

title: Comparative study of bottom- and top-incidence heating strategies in flowing surface and direct absorption solar collectors
abstract: The solar collector is a key component for solar photothermal conversion. Traditional surface absorption solar collectors (SASCs) rely on a high-absorptivity surface to absorb solar radiation and then transfer heat to the working fluid, which often leads to considerable surface heat losses. In contrast, direct absorption solar collectors (DASCs) (i.e., volumetric absorption collectors) employ optically absorbing nanofluids to directly convert solar energy into volumetric heat sources, thereby reducing thermal losses and improving efficiency. While a bottom-incidence strategy has recently been proposed to heat the fluid against gravity and promote buoyancy-induced mixing, existing studies are largely limited to static collectors. In this work, a two-dimensional coupled optical–thermal–fluid model is developed using the finite volume method (FVM) to investigate dynamic (flowing) collectors under different heating strategies. Four configurations are systematically compared, including SASC/DASC with top incidence and bottom incidence. The outlet temperature, photothermal efficiency, and temperature-field uniformity are evaluated. Parametric studies are further conducted for DASCs by varying inlet mass flow rate, fluid extinction coefficient, and collector geometry (length and height). The results show that bottom incidence increases efficiency by 10.71% for DASCs and 5.61% for SASCs, and that DASCs are approximately 8.84% more efficient than SASCs under the same incidence direction. Increasing inlet mass flow rate improves efficiency, and the DASC-bh achieves 83.22% efficiency at ṁ=0.05 kg/s. An optimal extinction coefficient of approximately 37.5 m−1 is identified. Moreover, the best trade-off between outlet temperature and efficiency is obtained at a collector length of 200 cm and a height of 7.5 cm.

title: A novel yawed wind farm parameterization for the mesoscale numerical weather prediction model
abstract: As the wind farm scale continues to expand, the impact of turbine wake effects has become increasingly significant. To mitigate these effects, yaw control in wind farms has garnered considerable attention. However, previous wind farm parameterization models have not accounted for operational controls, thereby limiting the ability to simulate wind farms under yaw control in mesoscale numerical weather prediction models. This study develops a novel yawed wind farm parameterization (Yawed-WFP) model and integrates it into a mesoscale numerical weather prediction framework. The proposed model introduces yaw control commands for the entire wind farm and calculates the wake-induced speed deficit of upstream turbines using both the yaw wake model and the wake superposition model. The updated speed deficit is then incorporated into the parameterization equations. After validation and verification, the yawed wind farm parameterization model is applied to simulations of two real wind farms over a certain period. The results demonstrate that, under yaw control, both wind speed and total power output are significantly enhanced, with total power increases of 1.24% and 2.55%, respectively. This proposed Yawed-WFP model facilitates the mesoscale simulation of long-term yaw control strategies in realistic atmospheric environments and can be used to assess the effectiveness of yaw control strategies in wind farm cluster operations.

title: Tunable all-day thermoelectric generator driven by solar heating and radiative cooling
abstract: The complementary utilization of solar heating and radiative cooling offers a promising approach for all-day thermoelectric energy harvesting. In this work, a tunable all-day thermoelectric generator (TAD-TEG) integrating a solar absorber, an optical filter, an IST-based phase-change radiative cooler, and a thermoelectric generator is proposed, and its optical, thermal, and power-generation performance is numerically investigated using a steady-state coupled thermal–electrical model. The optimized solar absorber achieves an AM1.5-weighted solar absorptance of 0.961, while the assembled cold-side system exhibits an emissivity of 0.980 in the 8–13 μm atmospheric window in the cooling-mode “on” state and 0.007 in the “off” state, enabling pronounced radiative modulation. Under representative baseline environmental conditions, the average power densities in the “on” state reach 12.80 W/m 2 during the daytime and 0.114 W/m 2 at night, markedly higher than the corresponding values of 7.45 and 0.011 W/m 2 in the “off” state. The corresponding 24-h electrical energy yields are 167.66 and 96.99 Wh/m 2 , respectively, indicating that radiative-state switching can effectively regulate the all-day thermoelectric output. Further analysis shows that the system exhibits tunable thermoelectric responses under different environmental conditions and TEG parameters, together with favorable power-generation performance across different seasons and geographical locations. These results indicate that the proposed TAD-TEG enables the synergistic utilization of solar heating and radiative cooling through cold-side radiative modulation, providing a promising tunable strategy for all-day thermoelectric energy harvesting under diverse climatic conditions.

title: Season-adaptive photovoltaic-adsorbent hybrid for module cooling and indoor air heating and humidification
abstract: Building-integrated photovoltaic systems commonly suffer from considerable module temperature rise in summer, leading to reduced electrical efficiency, while additional energy is required during the heating season for air heating and humidification. To address these challenges, a photovoltaic-adsorbent hybrid system is proposed by integrating a lithium chloride-loaded activated carbon fiber felt composite adsorbent encapsulated within polytetrafluoroethylene membrane onto the rear surface of a photovoltaic module. Unlike conventional adsorption-assisted photovoltaic cooling systems or photovoltaic/thermal air heating systems, the proposed system enables seasonal dual-mode operation, providing photovoltaic thermal management during non-heating season and air heat and moisture regulation during heating season. Experimental results show that, under 40°C and 60% relative humidity, the photovoltaic-lithium chloride-loaded activated carbon fiber felt hybrid system achieves an average temperature reduction of 9.8°C for the photovoltaic module. Under heating season operating conditions, a maximum air temperature lift of 8.1°C is obtained at 5°C and 50% relative humidity, while increase in humidity ratio of 4.7 g kg−1 is achieved at 7.5°C and 50% relative humidity. Further evaluation indicates that the daily electricity generation of the system can reach 1.05 kWh·m−2·day−1 in non-heating season, and the total daily equivalent energy benefit, including photovoltaic electricity generation, air heating, and humidification, can reach up to 4.85 kWh·m−2·day−1 during the heating season. The results demonstrate the feasibility of adsorbent-integrated photovoltaic systems for year-round dual-mode operation and highlight a promising pathway for extending building-integrated photovoltaic applications from standalone electricity generation to the synergistic integration of electricity generation, thermal management, and indoor air heat and moisture control.

title: Spacing matters: Experimental decoupling of transverse and longitudinal effects on wave farm performance
abstract: Systematic experimental studies on wave energy converter arrays remain scarce despite extensive numerical efforts, leaving a critical gap in understanding layout effects on farm performance. This study conducts physical model tests at a 1:26.67 scale of rocker-type WEC arrays to quantify the isolated effects of transverse (1×3 array) and longitudinal (2×3 array) spacing under regular and irregular waves. In the study of longitudinal spacing, a partially decoupled configuration with fixed transverse spacing was employed. Results reveal that transverse spacing governs destructive interference patterns: central WECs suffer significant suppression under resonance, weakening as spacing increases, boosting the q-factor (power-based) by 29% from 3R to 5R under regular waves at the wave period of 0.9s. Longitudinal spacing controls shielding and upstream-downstream coupling: WEC units on either side of the upstream (WEC1 and WEC5) in the 2×3 array harness constructive interference, achieving motion response enhancements of 51% at a 3R spacing and a wave period of 0.9s, though this gain decays with larger spacing. Array-induced resonance peaks emerge in high-frequency regions under irregular waves, offering bandwidth expansion opportunities. Moreover, resonance proves double-edged: it is beneficial for isolated devices but triggers destructive interference in arrays, causing the q-factor to drop to as low as 0.66 at critical spacings—a maximum reduction of 42% relative to the non-resonant condition. This study provides a systematic experimental and quantitative analysis of the spacing effect, providing insights at the physical level into the interference mechanisms in multi-device wave arrays.

title: Reaction behavior and kinetic analysis in the fast co-pyrolysis of bituminous coal with typical biomasses under CO2/N2 atmospheres: leveraging machine learning for char yield prediction
abstract: Co-pyrolysis of bamboo (BB), sawdust (SD), and wheat straw (WS), with Hongshaquan bituminous coal (HSQ), were conducted at 1000 K min−1 under CO2/N2 atmospheres. The maximum mass loss rates for the three biomass-coal blends were 0.94-3.29, 0.99-3.21, and 0.78-2.67%·K−1. Higher biomass proportion increased the maximum instantaneous reactivity, intrinsic reaction rate, and comprehensive pyrolysis index, with optimal performance for HSQ-BB at 30% CO2 and for HSQ-SD and HSQ-WS at 60% CO2. The contributions of CO2 on char yield for the three coal-biomass blends were 4.12-10.18%, 2-10.58%, and 3.8-9.88%, respectively. During the primary pyrolysis stage, the interaction effects depended on biomass properties and CO2 concentration. With increasing CO2 concentration, the effects shifted from inhibiting to promoting for BB, while opposite trends for SD and WS. A comprehensive interaction intensity index was established, with the values of 0.07-0.60, 0.04-0.52, and 0.12-0.63, suggesting HSQ-WS > HSQ-BB > HSQ-SD. The Avrami-Erofeev equation (n = 4) could best represent the co-pyrolysis process. As biomass proportion increased, the activation energy increased, while it decreased at higher CO2 concentration. The discrepancy between experimental and theoretical activation energy was correlated with the interaction intensity. A backpropagation neural network coupled with a genetic algorithm was employed to predict the char yield. The 13×8 node configuration yielded the best performance, with RMSE of 2.4090 and R2 of 0.9691. With larger datasets, the model's performance is expected to improve. This study provides a theoretical basis for coal-biomass co-combustion in industrial processes.

title: Comparative assessment of long-term methodologies for building-integrated photovoltaic façade energy yield estimation
abstract: ABSTRACT Modelling energy yield of building-integrated photovoltaics requires reliable long-term energy output predictions that match actual generation to encourage its adoption and guarantee cost-effectiveness. This paper evaluates the performance of a Typical Meteorological Year in building-integrated photovoltaic simulations across three façade orientations (east, south and west), and proposes two alternative strategies that improve energy output predictions: a Typical Energy Year based on simulations over 19 years and the Finkelstein-Schafer statistic, and a typical meteorological year specifically designed for building-integrated photovoltaic systems based on the plane-of-array irradiance—which better relates to the tilted positioning of photovoltaic modules on building envelopes—and custom weighting factors for the meteorological variables that are adjusted for each specific case study. Simulation results show good behaviour of both proposed strategies, which provide highly accurate annual energy yield estimations overall. The reliability of the existing Typical Meteorological Year varies with array orientation, boundary conditions and annual variability, suggesting that it requires case-specific analysis to assess suitability. The three methodologies are mutually complementary, and the paper provides guidance towards what strategy is preferable based on key decision aspects, marking a step forward towards better accuracy in building-integrated photovoltaic performance simulations and supporting its implementation in architectural projects.

title: Construction of the combustion mechanism for biodiesel-n-butanol dual-fuel systems and analysis of nitrogen oxides formation pathways
abstract: To investigate the mechanism of the impact of n-butanol on nitrogen oxides (NOx) emissions from biodiesel, a skeletal mechanism for biodiesel-n-butanol dual-fuel was constructed, which includes 878 reactions and 216 species. The mechanism accurately predicted ignition delay, laminar flame velocity, and concentrations of key intermediate species. Analysis of the effects of n-butanol blending ratios (0%–40%) on NOx formation revealed that blending 40% n-butanol reduced the peak areas of nitric oxide (NO) and nitrogen dioxide (NO2) by 19.46% and 13.87%, respectively. Analysis of formation rates showed that as the n-butanol blending ratio increased from 0% to 20%, the rate of the NO-forming reaction NO2 + H ⇌ NO + OH decreased by 7.04%, while the absolute NO-consumption rate through NO + O (+M) ⇌ NO2 (+M) decreased by 10.67%. Reaction pathway analysis indicated that the high latent heat of vaporization of n-butanol lowered the adiabatic flame temperature, thereby suppressing thermal NO formation. Oxygen-containing intermediates produced during n-butanol oxidation, such as CH3OH, HOCHO, and HOCH2O, compete with the biodiesel decomposition pathways for O, H, and OH radicals, reducing their peak mole fractions by 10.76%, 3.91%, and 4.74%, respectively, thereby increasing the contribution of the reaction converting N2O to N2. This study reveals the intrinsic mechanism by which n-butanol suppresses NOx formation based on the principles of chemical reaction kinetics, providing a theoretical foundation for the efficient utilization of biodiesel fuels blended with n-butanol.

title: Field testing of an axial-flow marine current turbine with passive adaptive blades
abstract: For axial-flow turbines, passive adaptive blades designed to passively feather in response to increasing thrust have the potential to decrease peak loads without the need for active pitch mechanisms, which come at the cost of additional failure modes and system complexity. In this study, we tested a 1-meter diameter axial-flow turbine in open water with two sets of composite blades: one blade set with a bend-twist coupling and a second, neutral blade set with no bend-twist coupling for comparison. Both blade sets were tested over a range of tip-speed ratios from 2 to 9, inflow speeds from 0.9 to 1.8 m/s, and yaw angles of 0, 15, and 25 degrees. The neutral blades were also tested over a range of preset blade pitch angles from −3 to 20 degrees. Testing over this wide range of operating conditions allowed us to assess the benefits of passive adaptive blades under low-frequency flow fluctuations in above-rated flow speeds (like those experienced during a tidal cycle) as well as cyclic, once-per-revolution loading. The bend-twist coupled blades were observed to achieve the same peak power coefficient as the neutral blades with a 7% reduction in thrust when operating at peak efficiency, and up to a 15% reduction in thrust at high tip-speed ratios. Interpolating across the experimental data, we simulated multiple off-design control strategies which estimate even greater load reduction potential. Further comparisons under yawed inflow are also discussed.

title: Multi-physics coupling simulation of biomass chemical looping gasification (CLG) for H2 production and CO2 mitigation
abstract: Biomass chemical looping gasification (CLG) offers a promising route for sustainable hydrogen production and carbon mitigation, yet its coupled hydrodynamic and thermochemical mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. A coarse-grained CFD-DEM framework is developed for three-dimensional biomass CLG simulations, incorporating momentum, heat, mass, and species transfer together with drying, pyrolysis, gasification, homogeneous reactions, and CaO carbonation/calcination. The framework is validated against experiments for conventional biomass gasification and CLG with different sand/CaO compositions, supplemented by statistical-time, grid, and coarse-graining sensitivity analyses. At the selected coarse-grained ratio of 8, the mean deviation of the major product gas mole fractions in the pure-CaO validation case is 9.25%, while 30 s of physical operation is simulated in 9.2 h using 32 CPU cores. Increasing CaO content enhances CO2 capture, shifts the water–gas shift reaction toward H2 formation, and promotes biomass conversion through localized carbonation heat release. H2 content and yield peak at 650 °C, while the CO2 emission at this temperature is only approximately 2% higher than the minimum at 700 °C, identifying 650 °C as the optimal overall temperature. Finally, varying the sand-to-CaO ratio demonstrates that both excessive and insufficient sand inventories cause pronounced fluctuations in gas production and flow hydrodynamics, whereas an intermediate ratio of around 2 fosters stable operation and efficient hydrogen generation and carbon reduction. These findings demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed framework and provide quantitative guidance for biomass CLG optimization.

title: Improving solar irradiance estimates for PV production in Ireland using Bayesian spatio-temporal modelling with open-source data
abstract: Accurate solar irradiance estimation is essential for reliable modelling of solar photovoltaic(PV) power production. In Ireland’s mid-to-high latitude maritime climate, solar estimation is shaped by seasonal variation, low winter sun angles, frequent cloud variability, sparse ground-based measurements and discrepancies among satellite products, making solar irradiance dataset selection challenging. We develop a Bayesian spatio-temporal framework for country-specific solar irradiance estimates across Ireland using openly available data. The model produces hourly and sub-hourly estimates with full uncertainty quantification, and is designed to support site evaluation and near-real-time applications. Cross-validation demonstrates statistically robust performance across temporal resolutions with hourly showing highest precision whereas sub-hourly encounters higher errors but improved uncertainty quantification. We compare with reanalysis data(ERA5), nearest-station interpolation and satellite-based products(CAMS). Our model outperforms ERA5 for hourly resolutions, reducing RMSE from 82 W/m² to 36 W/m² highlighting the limitations of coarse-resolution global reanalysis products in Ireland’s persistently cloudy climate. We also present the first evaluation of CAMS in an Irish context. For hourly irradiance, CAMS outperforms ERA5; however, our model further reduces RMSE(40 W/m² vs 35 W/m²). For PV power estimation, our framework remains competitive with CAMS while providing uncertainty unavailable for CAMS or ERA5. Our framework's practical value is demonstrated through comparisons with PV power output from residential, industrial and utility sites in Ireland, showing strong agreement with observed generation and providing an open-source irradiance dataset with full uncertainty quantification for high resolution solar resource assessment and improved estimation of PV system losses(e.g.clipping).

title: Study on operational characteristics and performance prediction of a water-cooled photovoltaic and thermal system
abstract: Water-cooled photovoltaic-thermal systems have garnered significant attention for their combined power and heat generation capabilities. However, existing studies suffer from insufficient operating conditions, low prediction accuracy, and incomplete regional applicability analyses. To remedy these deficiencies, an experimental platform was established to investigate the heating and power generation performance of a water-cooled photovoltaic-thermal system under various seasonal operating conditions. Subsequently, an innovative performance prediction model was developed based on a back-propagation neural network and further optimized using a hybrid optimization framework integrating the ant colony algorithm, the beetle antennae search algorithm, and the variable neighborhood local search algorithm. The coefficient of determination of the optimized model increased by 15.2 %, and the mean absolute error decreased by 75.51 %. It was applied to analyze Beijing, Guangzhou, and Lijiang, revealing average annual heating powers of 136 W, 178 W, and 126 W, and power generation of 38 W, 29 W, and 46 W, respectively. Finally, annual performance predictions were conducted for 15 representative cities in typical climate zones, and the performance curves of a single water-cooled photovoltaic-thermal module under variable operating conditions were analyzed. The results demonstrated that increasing ambient temperature from −10 °C to 40 °C raised peak heating power from 476 W to 769 W, while reducing electrical power from 230 W to 189 W. Furthermore, elevating solar irradiance from 0 to 1000 W/m2 increased heating output to 769 W and electrical output to 230 W.

title: Atmospheric regime clustering based on aerosol optical depth and cloud fraction for the improvement of 1-minute direct and diffuse solar irradiance separation
abstract: Limited observations of direct normal irradiance and diffuse horizontal irradiance, particularly the latter, have driven the development of irradiation separation models. This study proposes a novel minute-level irradiation separation model based on atmospheric condition clustering, utilizing aerosol optical depth and cloud fraction from global stations across five radiation observation networks. Four clustering methods were compared, and it was determined that K-means performed better. It was used to classify atmospheric conditions at all stations, successfully classifying them into three categories: Cluster 0 (high-AOD and high-CF); Cluster 1 (low-AOD and high-CF, high-AOD and low-CF); Cluster 2 (low-AOD and low-CF). Validation against ground observations demonstrates that DNI achieved an R2 of 0.93, RMSE of 91.6 W/m2 and an rRMSE of 14.4%, while DHI achieved an R2 of 0.78, RMSE of 53.2 W/m2 and an rRMSE of 34.0%. Furthermore, a comprehensive comparison with nine state-of-the-art separation methods reveals that our proposed model consistently achieves the highest average rank across all observation sites and various time scales. Additionally, we observed that interannual variations in atmospheric clusters lead to a slight decrease in the rRMSE of the DNI (14.7% vs. 11.2%), but substantially increase the rRMSE of the DHI (33.3% vs. 46.1%). All in all, the minute-level solar irradiation separation method proposed in this study can improve the estimation accuracy of solar irradiation components under different atmospheric conditions.

title: Biomethane-driven SOFC vehicles: Dual role in emission reduction and renewable energy production
abstract: : Fossil fuel combustion in road transport significantly contributes to greenhouse gas emissions and air pollution, necessitating sustainable alternatives. Solid Oxide Fuel Cells (SOFCs) fueled by biomethane offer a viable decarbonization pathway, leveraging existing biofuel infrastructure and enabling internal fuel reforming. This study employs an Integrated Assessment Model to assess the environmental benefits of introducing a biomethane-powered SOFC fleet. Additionally, this study explores the potential of SOFC vehicles to operate as prosumers, generating surplus energy to the grid during idle periods, thereby enhancing renewable energy integration. The impact assessment is analyzed in terms of CO 2-eq emission reduction and air quality benefits. The scenario focuses on the emissions variation affected by the substitution of traditional light-duty vehicles with SOFC vehicles, the replacement of energy produced by non-renewable sources with the energy produced by the fleet, and the influence of the biomethane production process (including biomethane production sites and feedstock waste management). The case study is the Lombardy region in Northern Italy, characterized by elevated pollution levels. Results indicate that replacing conventional vehicles with SOFCs can reduce GHG, NOx, and NH 3 emissions substantially, leading to measurable air quality improvements and decreased fossil fuel dependence in transport and energy sectors.

title: How do solar energy landscapes transform geography? Synergistic multi-objective optimization for robust PV and CSP planning in island regions
abstract: Despite its influence on PV and CSP techno-economic and socio-environmental performance, placement optimization is largely absent from current CSP siting practices. The author's systematic review of 10,121 publications identifies only three PV optimization studies, demonstrating exclusive reliance on techno-economic metrics. To address these methodological gaps, this work introduces an original multi-objective optimization framework designed to support robust PV and CSP deployment. The approach entails: (i) constructing a geospatial multi-criteria decision assessment framework to delineate priority areas and exclude unsuitable land; (ii) defining optimization objectives and performance metrics; (iii) developing automated stand-alone Python scripts within a Geographic Information System to extract site-specific characteristics; (iv) establishing a novel mathematical formulation, implemented as a MATLAB function with defined constraints and decision variables; and (v) operationalizing the optimization through an enhanced Python-based Skyline algorithm to identify Pareto-optimal siting solutions. The methodological framework is demonstrated and validated through an application to the North and South Aegean Regions of Greece. The study identifies 23 PV and 3 CSP sites as Pareto-optimal across the island regions, supported by multiple optimization scenarios capturing divergent stakeholder priorities. The findings underscore the framework's versatility across renewable energy technologies and spatial-planning contexts, offering robust guidance for decarbonizing energy-intensive island sectors.

title: Assessment of waste-energy-hydrogen technologies as a pathway to sustainable transportation in Gaza Strip, Palestine
abstract: Many developing regions face significant challenges in reducing transportation-related emissions, particularly in densely populated areas such as the Gaza Strip. This study evaluates waste-to-hydrogen (WtH) technologies as an integrated solution to address resource limitations and energy insecurity. Moreover, four conversion technologies including landfill gas capture, incineration, gasification, and anaerobic digestion are assessed by applying a multidisciplinary assessment covering their potential for generating electricity and producing green hydrogen to be used as fuel for hydrogen fuel cell automobiles. The results indicate that incineration provides the highest hydrogen yield, producing 10.47 tons/day. This superior performance is attributed to the high energy recovery rate of incineration within waste-to-energy processes, which in this study reached 565.55 MWh/day. The hydrogen produced via waste-to-energy pathways—incineration, gasification, anaerobic digestion, and landfill gas recovery can be stored at 276.38, 180.8, 157.09, and 132.29 m3/day, respectively. This paper assesses the environmental performance and economic impacts of WtH production to provide information on clean and sustainable energy solutions to curb pollution from conventional energy resources and solid waste. The high costs of investment still pose a challenge, but the long-term economic benefits, lower fuel costs and potential revenue from the by-products make the deployment of WtH technology viable. The results show this technology is a promising and effective way to improve energy security and reduce greenhouse gases emissions. This can then encourage sustainable development in resource-limited areas such as the Gaza Strip.

title: Design of a Francis turbine for wider range of head and power via runner inlet and outlet optimization
abstract: Francis turbine plays a vital important role in the supply side of the power grid. To increase the flexibility of power supply, Francis turbine is demanded to increase its comprehensive hydraulic efficiency in a wider range of head and power. In this case, the high-weight region is defined as the operating region that simultaneously meet the commend of head ranging from 61 m to 69 m and power ranging from 75% to 95% rated output power. And the total design weights in the high-weight region reaches nearly 80%. The design conception bowed, twisted and swept are introduced in the parametric design of runner inlet and outlet. Thereafter, based on Design of Experiments, Hydraulic characteristic collection, Meta model generation, Multi-objective optimization and Trade-off in Pareto front, the average hydraulic efficiency of four control points in the high-weight region are increased by 2.11%. The optimized runner shows more 3D design characteristic in spanwise direction compared with the original runner. In design parameters analysis, it is found that the contribution of design parameters at runner outlet is much large than that at runner inlet and the demand for bowed, twisted and swept in runner outlet is higher. In blade loading analysis, compared to the original runner, the local Euler head at runner out is closer to 0 m and shows clear M type loading trend in middle and shroud in the optimized runner. Finally, hydraulic loss analysis is conducted based on local hydraulic loss rate method. The hydraulic loss strength is effectively decrease in the shroud of runner outlet. Moreover, the chaotic flows (backflow, dean vortex, helical vortex structure) in draft tube are also well-controlled in the optimized runner. We believe that the methods proposed in present paper could contribute to the design of other hydraulic machinery for wider operation range and more flexibility.

title: Who gets the jobs? Embedding regional employment equity in energy system planning
abstract: The energy transition can create substantial employment, yet its spatial distribution can reinforce territorial inequalities. Most energy planning studies compute employment ex post from predefined pathways, so distributive objectives cannot influence investment or operation and the marginal cost of redistribution remains unobservable. This study proposes a novel methodology to evaluate territorial employment distributive policies within energy system optimization by making regional direct employment endogenous and subject to distributive constraints. We extend the multizonal H2RES model by linking region- and technology-specific employment factors to annual capacity decisions and requiring each region to reach a minimum share of national net direct employment. Employment thus becomes a policy constraint that shapes investment siting, technology choice, and system operation, while revealing marginal redistribution costs through shadow prices. Applied to Chile’s National Electric System through 2050 across seven equity levels, the framework reshapes decarbonization pathways, altering renewable siting, technology mix, and flexibility use. Stronger equity raises system costs up to 3.95%, driven by higher wind investment and solar relocation toward lower-yield regions, while net direct employment rises up to 27% under maximum equity. Marginal costs show that Norte Chico and Centro are most costly, Sur binds only at high equity, and Norte Grande never binds.

title: Experimental investigation of coupled heat and mass transfer in a solar humidification–dehumidification desalination system
abstract: This work presents a comprehensive experimental investigation of the coupled heat and mass transfer mechanisms in a solar desalination system operating on the humidification–dehumidification (HDH) principle under the climatic conditions of Bizerte, Tunisia. The system consists of a humidifier integrated into a solar collector (solar evaporator) and a tubular condenser (dehumidifier). The convective, radiative, latent and total heat transfer coefficients, their corresponding Nusselt numbers, the mass transfer coefficients, and the corresponding Sherwood numbers were determined from the experimental data. Results show that heat and mass transfer in both the solar evaporator and the condenser increase with solar irradiation. In the evaporator, these transfers also increase with air velocity, whereas in the condenser, they reach an optimal air velocity of 3.34 m s−1, beyond which they decrease. The existence of optimum air velocity was confirmed through an air residence-time analysis. Based on the experimental investigation, correlations relating the latent, convective, radiative, and total Nusselt numbers to the Reynolds and Prandtl numbers, and the Sherwood numbers to the Reynolds and Schmidt numbers, were developed for both the solar evaporator and the condenser. The experimental results show good agreement with both literature data and numerical simulations, validating the proposed correlations.

title: Multiscale assessment of market concentration and inequality in the global wood pellet trade: Implications for the bioenergy transition
abstract: Densified biomass fuels, particularly wood pellets have emerged as strategic assets in the global low-carbon energy transition. This study conducts a multiscale assessment of spatial concentration and inequality in wood pellet production and consumption from 2012 to 2022 using FAO data and five structural indicators: Concentration Ratios (CR k ), Herfindahl–Hirschman Index (HHI), Theil Entropy Index (E), Gini Coefficient (G), and Hall–Tideman Index (HTI). Results reveal significant market expansion, especially in Europe and East Asia, alongside declining production concentration. While CR k and HHI suggest growing diversification, G and HTI indicate persistent inequalities, particularly in national-level consumption. Brazil stands out with the highest growth rate among major producers. These findings offer robust evidence to guide renewable energy policies, promote fair international trade, and foster a more inclusive global bioeconomy.

title: An automated forced-draft air-injection control system for low PM2.5 emissions from a cordwood heating stove under variable operating conditions
abstract: A temperature-feedback-based forced-draft airflow control strategy for a retrofitted legacy cordwood heating stove was extended and systematically tuned to reduce PM2.5 emissions across a wide range of operating conditions. The system employed a floor-mounted, multi-zone primary air delivery configuration with temperature-based control, enabling sequential progression of combustion along the fuel bed. The automated stove successfully adapted to variations in fuel loading (2.9–5.3 kg dry-fuel mass), firepower (∼10–20 kW), and fuel moisture content (∼13–36% dry mass basis) for Douglas-fir and maple cordwood fuels. The stove achieved PM2.5 emission rates below 2.5 g/h in two to three replicate tests under all test conditions, similar to NSPS-certified stoves. A customized test protocol was followed for each replicate test including hot-start ignition, flaming, burn-out, and charcoal burn phases. The stove maintained PM2.5 emission factors below 1 g/kg, lower than the 2 g/kg limit for Nordic Swan Ecolabel stoves. Dry-fuel burn rate remained 2 to 4 kg/h, such that PM2.5 emissions decreased with increasing burn rates without reaching an inflection point. During wet-wood combustion, simultaneous air-injection along an extended fuel bed, implemented through control-logic modification alone (i.e., without any additional hardware changes), demonstrated PM2.5 emissions below 2.5 g/h and 1 g/kg. At high loading densities, increasing secondary airflow by approximately 40% compared to low load operation maintained PM2.5 emission rates below the target limit. PM2.5 emission factors from wet-wood burning tests remained within −29% to +25% of those measured under the corresponding dry-wood conditions, indicating limited sensitivity of the stove to fuel moisture content.

title: Hydrodynamic coupling mechanisms and shape optimization of a Vitosinski-derived duct for passive yaw tidal turbines
abstract: To support in-situ and high-efficiency energy supply for long-term wireless ocean platforms such as instrumented buoys, this study investigates a ducted horizontal-axis tidal turbine (HATT) that realizes passive yaw (i.e., the ability to change its orientation horizontally with respect to the flow direction) and velocity augmentation. A novel convex duct profile derived from the Vitosinski curve is proposed. Based on computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations that couple the fluid field with rigid-body motion, the mechanisms by which duct geometry affects the velocity augmentation and passive yaw performance are clarified for different profiles. Optimization of hydrodynamic performance is further carried out by adjusting the duct profile, for which a bi-objective optimization model is established adopting the curve parameters and the rotor and yaw-axis locations as variables. This model is solved using simulated annealing (SA) method. Water-channel experiments and matched-condition CFD further support the predicted performance-improvement trend.

title: Sequential Ultrasound–Laccase pretreatment of Bambusa bambos for enhanced bioethanol production
abstract: Lignocellulosic biomass represents a sustainable, non-food-competing feedstock for second-generation bioethanol, yet its recalcitrance remains a critical bottleneck for efficient conversion. The present study addresses this challenge by developing a synergistic sequential ultrasound–enzyme (laccase) treatment (SUET) to enhance lignin depolymerisation and biomass accessibility in Bambusa bambos, a holocellulose-rich bamboo species. Ultrasound-induced structural disruption followed by enzymatic delignification significantly improved substrate digestibility and pretreatment conditions were optimized using central composite design-based response surface methodology (CCD-RSM). Structural analyses confirmed progressive delignification, increased surface porosity and enhanced cellulose crystallinity following SUET pretreatment. Following saccharification of biomass derived from the optimized SUET process, a yield of 388.76 mg/g of reducing sugar was achieved, exceeding the yields of individual ultrasonic or enzymatic pretreatments. Subsequent simultaneous saccharification and co-fermentation (SSCF) achieved a maximum ethanol concentration of 44.72 g/L, corresponding to a yield of 0.248 g/g biomass, which exceeded those of PSSF and SSF processes. The results indicate an effective and environmentally friendly pretreatment approach with significant potential for scalable bioethanol production, hence contributing to renewable energy systems and the advancement of a circular bioeconomy.

title: CeF3-modified Ni8P3 nanoarchitecture with built-in electric field for high-performance bifunctional water splitting electrocatalysis
abstract: Developing efficient, stable, and earth-abundant bifunctional electrocatalysts is critical for advancing large-scale alkaline water electrolysis. Herein, we report a hierarchical Ni8P3-CeF3/NF nanoflower catalyst grown in situ on nickel foam via a pH-controlled hydrothermal–phosphidation process. Electrochemical tests revealed excellent bifunctional performance, featuring low overpotentials of η100 = 310 mV (for oxygen evolution reaction, OER) and η10 = 89 mV (for hydrogen evolution reaction, HER), small Tafel slopes (51/87 mV dec−1), as well as the highest electrochemical surface area (ECSA, 415 m2 g−1) among all tested samples. Impedance and Bode phase analyses reveal reduced charge transfer resistance and enhanced interfacial kinetics, resulting from the formation of a built-in electric field (BEF) and electronic redistribution from CeF3 to Ni8P3. In situ Raman spectroscopy and Fourier-transform infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy studies confirm the accelerated formation of NiOOH and the accumulation of *OOH intermediates. When assembled into a symmetric electrolyzer, Ni8P3-CeF3/NF delivers industrially relevant current densities of 100 mA cm−2 at a cell voltage of 1.85 V and maintains 99.2% activity after 260 h of continuous operation at 100 mA cm−2. These results position Ni8P3-CeF3/NF as a highly promising candidate for cost-effective, scalable alkaline water splitting.

title: A hybrid approach for the techno-economic analysis of wind power plants
abstract: This study presents an integrated framework combining design of experiments, the System Advisor Model, and machine learning to improve energy production and economic forecasting for wind power plants. A multi-level full factorial design of experiments generated 2688 scenarios by varying four critical parameters—turbine spacing (3–8 rotor diameters), hub height (80–140 m), rotor diameter (75–110 m), and wind speed (5.66–10.18 m/s)—across eight U.S. regions. These scenarios were simulated in the System Advisor Model to compute five techno-economic outputs: annual energy production, net present value after tax, levelized cost of energy, net capital cost per watt, and total balance-of-system cost. Five machine learning algorithms—neural networks, support vector machines, partial least squares, k-nearest neighbors, and stochastic gradient descent—were then trained on the system advisor model dataset. Among the eight sites, Wyoming yielded the highest energy production (659,434 MWh/year) and the lowest levelized cost of energy (1.59 ¢/kWh), while Florida recorded the lowest production (317,876 MWh/year). Neural networks and support vector machines demonstrated superior predictive performance, with neural networks achieving R2 values of 0.964 for the levelized cost of energy and 0.944 for the annual energy production. The sensitivity analysis using a box plot confirmed the robustness and reliability of the developed models. These results demonstrate that integrating the design of experiments, the system advisor model, and machine learning provides accurate, scalable, and robust forecasting tools for the wind power plants’ planning and investment decisions.

title: Co-production of hydrogen and ethanol from enzymatic hydrolysate of KOH-urea treated mixture of crops’ straws with a co-culture of Klebsiella aerogenes and Saccharomyces cerevisiae
abstract: Hydrogen bio-production from lignocellulose using a single microbial strain is constrained by poor tolerance to high substrate loads, low yields of valuable byproducts like ethanol, and single-source feedstock limitations. To tackle these bottlenecks, this study constructed an efficient hydrogen–ethanol co-production system via co-cultivation of Klebsiella aerogenes ATCC13048 and Saccharomyces cerevisiae Y2034 for fermenting 85.85 g/L sugar hydrolysate derived from KOH–urea-pretreated corn stover (CS) and wheat straw (WS) blends. Substituting KOH with urea from 0.5% to 1%, the lignin removal of CS decreased from 82.61% to 54.16%, while that of WS increased from 62.07% to 69.83%. Additionally, greater structural and chemical modifications happened in WS than in CS. Notably, the performance of KOH–urea pretreatment of lignocellulosic mixture is highly governed by the biomass mixing ratio and the KOH/urea proportion. A full enzymatic hydrolysis efficiency (100%) was attained for the 1:1 (mass) CS–WS blend pretreated by 1% KOH + 1% urea. Compared with fermentation by K. aerogenes alone, the co-culture with S. cerevisiae drastically boosted hydrogen production from 115.65 mM to 430.51 mM and ethanol titer from 31.31 mM to 641.67 mM, and improved glucose utilization from 44.20% to 100% and xylose consumption from 1.50% to 26.63%. In a scenario where waste pretreatment liquor is recycled as fertilizer and on-site cellulase accounts for over 50% of commercial enzyme use, a profitable biorefinery process for co-producing hydrogen and ethanol from the CS–WS mixture would be achieved. This study establishes a sustainable biorefinery paradigm to efficiently co-produce hydrogen and ethanol from lignocellulosic mixture.

title: Sobol-based global sensitivity analysis of D-shaped bluff body piezoelectric energy harvesters using SVM surrogate model
abstract: To address the unclear parameter regulation mechanism of D-shaped bluff body piezoelectric micro wind energy harvesters caused by strong geometric-system parameter coupling and pronounced nonlinearity, this study develops a synergistic parameter analysis framework combining Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Sobol global sensitivity analysis to investigate the effects and synergistic mechanisms of wind speed, aspect ratio, mass damping ratio and system stiffness on amplitude ratio.540 sets of full-condition vibration response data were obtained via three-factor three-level orthogonal tests and continuous wind speed scanning. An SVM surrogate model with radial basis function kernel was established, achieving a test set coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.9655, meeting high-precision analysis requirements. Global sensitivity analysis shows that wind speed dominates amplitude ratio across all conditions with a total effect index of 59.00%, followed by aspect ratio (19.05%), stiffness (10.33%) and mass damping ratio (8.92%). Mass damping ratio exhibits strong interaction effects, while aspect ratio acts almost independently. Dominant parameters evolve significantly with wind speed: mass damping ratio dominates at low speeds, stiffness at medium speeds, and both aspect ratio and stiffness at high speeds. This study reveals the multi-parameter mechanism under coupled vortex-induced vibration (VIV) and galloping in D-shaped bluff bodies, providing an efficient analytical tool and theoretical support for parameter matching and optimal design of micro wind energy devices.

title: A novel mothballed pipeline-based CAES system with low-melting-point molten salt TES: Dynamic characteristics and flexible operation
abstract: In response to grid instability caused by the large-scale integration of renewable energy and the limited site options for compressed air energy storage systems, as well as the resource underutilization and asset depreciation risks of decommissioned pipelines during the ongoing energy transition, this study proposes a novel compressed air energy storage system based on mothballed pipelines. The system can utilize the existing pipeline valves to construct distributed air storage spaces, enabling capacity adjustments according to the fluctuation of renewable output and load demand for flexible operation. The results indicate that the proposed system achieves a round-trip efficiency of 68.23%, which is comparable to that of salt cavern storage, along with a 59.31% decrease in storage equipment cost under the design conditions. However, an axial pressure gradient exists in the air within the pipeline during the charging and discharging processes. Segmented operation can improve the renewable energy accommodation rate by 23.59%. These results demonstrate the potential of utilizing mothballed pipeline infrastructure for compressed air energy storage system applications and provide insights into the thermodynamic feasibility and operational characteristics of pipeline-based energy storage.

title: Experimental investigation on the impact of nanoparticles as passive performance enhancement in a single-effect LiBr/H2O absorption chiller using MWCNT, Fe3O4, and CuO nanofluids
abstract: This study presents an experimental evaluation of a single-effect LiBr/H2O absorption chiller system (ACS) enhanced with MWCNT, Fe3O4, and CuO nanoparticles at 0-1 wt% concentrations and generator temperatures of 75-100°C. Results indicate that the LiBr salt concentration increases with the generator temperature (Tgen) due to intensified water vapor generation, reaching crystallization at 100°C for the basefluid and at 94-95°C for the nanofluid working pairs at 1 wt%. The addition of nanofluid reduced the circulation ratio as Tgen increased, with MWCNT showing the most significant decrease. Cooling capacity, heat recovery, and COP improved across all nanoparticle types, with MWCNT achieving the highest gains. Exergy efficiency declined with Tgen but was mitigated at higher nanoparticle concentrations, most effectively with MWCNT. These findings demonstrate that nanoparticle-enhanced LiBr/H2O solutions can greatly enhance ACS performance and facilitate better use of low-grade heat sources, though crystallization limits still pose challenges for operational optimization.

title: Optimization of different filling strategies of copper foam in fin-copper foam composite solar phase change heat storage
abstract: Phase change heat storage technology plays an important role in alleviating the mismatch between supply and demand timing of solar energy. Nevertheless, the practical implementation of this technology is often stymied by the poor thermal conductivity exhibited by phase change materials. Incorporating fins and porous media can effectively enhance its thermal conductivity. This study investigates a solar phase change heat storage device that integrates a fin-copper foam composite, aiming to further improve thermal performance by optimizing the copper foam filling strategy. First, experiments were conducted to compare the melting characteristics of pure fin structure, pure copper foam structure, and composite structure. Based on this, numerical simulations examined the effects of different filling strategies (filling position and height) using complete melting time, temperature uniformity index, heat storage capacity, and heat storage rate as evaluation metrics. Results indicate that the composite structure synergistically combines the directional low-resistance heat paths of fins with the highly conductive copper foam skeleton, enabling efficient heat transport and accelerated melting. Among configurations, bottom filling generally outperforms top filling, and the 85% bottom-filled copper foam configuration delivers the optimal overall performance. Compared with the full foam copper filling structure, its total melting duration is shortened by 13.22%, the time-average index of temperature uniformity is shortened by 45.01%, heat storage capacity increases by 7.11%, heat storage rate rises by 18.17%. Therefore, the fin-copper foam composite structure with 85% bottom filling can be considered a superior configuration, providing theoretical guidance for the development of high-performance solar latent heat storage systems.

title: Participation assessment of diverse multi-energy microgrids in integrated power–water distribution systems considering outages
abstract: The increasing deployment of multi-energy microgrids (MEMGs) as aggregators is transforming the operation of modern distribution systems, particularly during outage events. However, the growing diversity of MEMG architectures and their interdependency on power and water distribution systems introduce significant coordination and privacy challenges, particularly with the increasing adoption of green hydrogen. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a privacy-preserving distributed coordination framework for multiple independent operators and aggregators. MEMGs are categorized based on geographical resource availability into coast-based and hydrogen-based configurations. Unlike existing studies that confine MEMG interactions to the power distribution system, this work extends their role to coupled power–water operations, where coast-based MEMGs support the water distribution system through desalination, while hydrogen-based MEMGs can utilize water for hydrogen production to support the power distribution system during outage events. A consensus-based alternating direction method of multipliers (C-ADMM) optimization model is developed to coordinate multiple aggregators and operators while preserving their autonomy and privacy. The proposed framework is validated on an IEEE 33-bus power distribution system interconnected with a 15-node water distribution system. Extensive outage case studies shows its effectiveness in enhancing resilience and mitigating cascading failures, with diverse MEMGs providing average support of 39% and 22.4% to the power and water distribution systems.

title: Impact of circumsolar irradiance and aerosol optical depth on CAMS surface solar irradiance estimates
abstract: The global horizontal irradiance is a main variable in the integration of solar energy systems in electricity grids, and in climate and weather studies. The physical model McClear is the clear-sky module for the all-sky irradiance retrievals from the CAMS Radiation Service. Validations of McClear against high-quality in situ measurements reveal very accurate global horizontal irradiance estimates with negligible bias. Albeit still good, the beam and diffuse irradiance components exhibit biases generally opposing each other. These biases are mainly attributed to the aerosol optical depth used as input to McClear, and the forward scattered circumsolar irradiance surrounding the solar disc which is not modelled by McClear but intercepted within the solid angle aperture of radiometers measuring beam irradiance (and blocked by those measuring diffuse irradiance). This study performs a global scale validation of a desert-based circumsolar correction, and evaluates the influence of this circumsolar correction and the aerosol optical depth on the beam and diffuse irradiance estimates from McClear. Circumsolar corrected retrievals are enhanced globally, especially for the diffuse component of McClear, with the standard deviation of deviations improving from 26.3 to 24.4%, the bias from 19.0 to 13.1%, and the correlation remaining constant at 0.837. Comparing ground measured and CAMS modelled aerosol optical depth, improvements are expected with further developments to the CAMS aerosol model.

title: Response of photovoltaic power generation to rising temperatures in Central Asia
abstract: Under climate warming, clarifying how photovoltaic power generation in Central Asia responds to temperature changes is essential for assessing the climate adaptability of photovoltaic systems. Using hourly ERA5 meteorological data and the PVLIB model, this study simulated PV specific yield across Central Asia during 2001–2020. The direct thermal effect of air-temperature variation was isolated by comparing a historical-temperature simulation (S1) with a reference-temperature simulation based on 2001–2005 [S2(2001–2005)], while keeping solar radiation and wind speed identical. During the study period, air temperature, solar radiation, and wind speed all showed increasing trends in Central Asia. The mean annual PV specific yield was 1886.9 kWh/kWp/yr, generally increased from north to south, and showed a regional upward trend of 1.23 kWh/kWp/yr. Despite this overall increase, the regional mean difference between S1 and S2(2001–2005) was −3.22 kWh/kWp/yr, and the predominance of negative differences and trends showed that the rise in historical air temperature relative to the early-period reference reduced PV specific yield and that this thermal loss generally intensified over time. Within the fitted range, relative to the reference-temperature scenario, a 1°C increase in mean air temperature was associated with an approximate 0.654 kWh/kWp reduction in monthly PV specific yield. The direct thermal effect was predominantly negative in spring and summer but showed both positive and negative values in autumn and winter; April had the largest monthly reduction, November showed a positive difference, and December was close to zero. Compared with S2(2001–2005), S1 showed a stronger negative association between air temperature and PV specific yield, a locally weaker positive association with solar radiation, and broadly similar weak associations with wind speed. These results show that recent air-temperature rise has imposed a measurable direct thermal loss on PV generation in Central Asia, partly offsetting the increase associated with concurrent changes in other meteorological conditions.

title: Editorial Board
Co-combustion of eucalyptus bark and coal: Thermal decomposition behavior, heavy metals migration and environmental risk assessment
abstract: Co-combustion of biomass and coal can alleviate energy pressure and reduce carbon dioxide emissions. This work investigated the combustion behavior, heavy metals migration, and environmental risk of eucalyptus bark (EB) blended with four coal types (MC, IC, TC, SC) compared to pure coal. Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) showed that EB-coal co-combustion exhibited superior combustion characteristic indices (S) relative to pure coal. However, elemental analysis revealed that higher levels of K2O, CaO, and P2O5 during co-combustion increased heavy metal retention in ash. Morphological analysis further indicated that co-combusting TC and SC with EB produced more compact, less porous ash, potentially exacerbating heavy metal retention. As a result, inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) measurements showed that co-combustion led to higher residual rates of Cu, Ni, and Zn in all ashes than pure coal combustion. Moreover, the Nemerow pollution index (PN) and potential combined risk index (RI) of the ash were elevated due to co-combustion, with only the RI of MBE (95 wt% MC + 5 wt% EB) decreasing. Among these, the ecological risk was primarily attributed to Hg. This work emphasized the importance of selecting the appropriate combination of coal and biomass, and provided a scientific basis for balancing the efficiency and environmental risks of coal-fired power plants.

title: Augmented solar energy harvesting in an integrated system of heterojunction solar cells and pressure retarded osmosis heat engine
abstract: Photovoltaic devices convert only part of the absorbed solar energy into electricity, while the remaining low-grade heat is usually dissipated and limits overall energy utilization. To recover this residual heat, this study proposes an integrated power-generation system coupling a lead sulfide colloidal quantum dot thin-film heterojunction solar cell with a thermolytic pressure-retarded osmosis heat engine. In this configuration, the solar cell generates electricity from incident radiation, and the osmotic heat engine uses the photovoltaic waste heat to regenerate an ammonium bicarbonate concentration gradient for additional power production. A coupled theoretical framework combining semiconductor device physics, heat balance, and osmotic heat-engine thermodynamics is established to evaluate power density, energy efficiency, and exergy efficiency. The results show that the hybrid system achieves a maximum power density of 142.78 W m−2, representing an 8.76% improvement in power density over the standalone thin-film heterojunction solar cell. The corresponding peak energy and exergy efficiencies are 15.03% and 15.31%, respectively. Parametric analyses indicate that absorber thickness, solution concentration difference, operating temperature, and interface defect density strongly affect the coupled performance. These findings demonstrate the potential of photovoltaic–osmotic integration for low-grade heat recovery and efficient solar energy harvesting.

title: Thermosiphon-enhanced heat extraction and power generation using supercritical CO2 in a 3D U-shaped closed-loop well
abstract: This study develops a coupled wellbore–formation–power model for a three-dimensional U-shaped closed-loop geothermal system that circulates supercritical CO2 and drives an organic Rankine cycle. One-dimensional non-isothermal wellbore flow is coupled with three-dimensional transient heat conduction in the formation, and a CoolProp-based dynamic organic Rankine cycle model using R134a converts the transient wellhead state into electricity at each time step. The well comprises a 2 km vertical section and a bottom loop of two 1 km horizontal segments joined by a 180° arc 1 km in diameter. Over 20 years, supercritical CO2 balances cumulative heat extraction against heat-source grade better than water, 20% NaCl brine, or R134a on the geothermal side, yielding 6.4 × 1014 J of heat, an outlet temperature of 90.0 °C, and 4.9 × 103 MWh of electricity in the base case. Power output is governed jointly by heat extraction and heat-source grade rather than by heat extraction alone. Raising the injection rate to 20 kg/s increases heat extraction but depresses the outlet temperature below the organic Rankine cycle threshold after the fourth year, whereas reducing the rate stepwise from 20 to 5 kg/s restores operation and lifts the 20-year generation from 337 to 3339 MWh. A higher injection temperature raises the outlet temperature only marginally while reducing heat extraction, and an outlet pressure of 15–20 MPa offers the best compromise, reaching 5.0 × 103 MWh at 20 MPa. Optimization should therefore coordinate heat extraction, heat-source grade, and organic Rankine cycle conversion rather than maximize heat extraction alone.

title: Methodology to compare levelized cost drivers for repurposing global offshore infrastructure for clean energy - Offshore California vs. Gulf of Mexico case study
abstract: Offshore platforms producing oil and gas are typically decommissioned when production ceases. The ROICE (Repurposing Offshore Infrastructure for Continued Energy) program has been investigating an alternate pathway – continued use of these structures to support clean energy projects such as offshore wind power and wind to hydrogen. In previous work, the authors have developed levelized cost (LC) models and maps for ROICE projects in the Gulf of Mexico (GOM), considering critical factors such as wind speed, water depth, and operational costs. Here, the authors discuss how this methodology can be adapted to any global offshore region in the world, such as the North Sea, offshore Brazil, etc. Results from a case study of Offshore California structures are presented and compared to the GOM. The LC range is wider in California. While several assets in the GOM are situated in low LC regions, very few of the California assets are situated favorably. Combined with the relative sparsity of offshore assets, California is thus better suited for new build clean energy projects versus repurposing. The underlying technical reasons for these differences in the two geographical areas, such as a vastly different overlay of wind patterns and bathymetry, are discussed here.

title: Systematic modeling and performance comparison of control strategies in vapor compression refrigeration systems for cold storage application across representative operating envelopes
abstract: This study investigates dynamic coupling and control of a vapor-compression refrigeration system for cold storage across three ambient temperature ranges (15–19°C, 20–25°C, and 26–30°C). A dynamic model was developed in Dymola and validated against a 2 kW R410A experimental rig with a physical cold-storage chamber (0–5°C); relative errors of key performance indicators and most state parameters are within 5.83%. The model captures the full dynamic response chain —compressor speed, refrigerant mass flow rate, pressure, temperature, and heat exchange rate—and predicts a maximum cooling capacity of 2.86 kW and a coefficient of performance (COP) of 2.85 under baseline conditions; coordinated speed-valve control raises these to 3.89 kW and 3.39. Compressor speed primarily governs the condensing side, whereas valve opening dominates the evaporating side. Compared with single-speed control, the coordinated strategy improves cooling capacity by up to 31.94% and COP by up to 36.82% (at 26-30°C); compared with single-opening control, by up to 13.89% and 25.99%. It saves 849.0 kWh/year and 0.45 t CO2 per unit, supporting digital-twin development and validating its effectiveness in improving energy efficiency and operational stability.

title: Investigation on the optimal combination of backplane fin design and spray design for cooling PV panels
abstract: High operating temperature of photovoltaic panels reduces their conversion efficiency and service life. This study aims to investigate the optimal combination of backplane fin design and spray design for cooling photovoltaic panels by simulation. The effects of fin height, fin space, spray flowrate and nozzle number on the photovoltaic panel performance are studied. Results show that under the conditions of solar radiation 800 W/m2 and ambient temperature 35 °C, the optimal backplane fin design is 0.4 D space (i.e., 27.2 mm) and 1.2 H height (i.e., 120 mm), reducing the surface-average temperature of the photovoltaic panel from 55.42 °C to 53.79 °C when compared with the basic fin design (i.e., 1.0 D space as 68 mm and 1.0 H height as 100 mm). For the selected fin design, the corresponding photovoltaic conversion efficiency is 17.19%. Moreover, eight combinations of backplane fin design and nozzle spray design are compared, named as Combinations 1-8. Under the conditions of solar radiation 800 W/m2 and ambient temperature of 35 °C, the Combination 7 (i.e., fin space of 27.2 mm and fin height of 120 mm with spray flowrate of 0.055 kg/s by two nozzles) achieves the best performance improvement. The Combination 7 reduces the average temperature of photovoltaic panels from 60.97 °C to 45.38 °C, increases the photovoltaic conversion efficiency from 16.62% to 18.03% and provides 5.72 Wh increment of net power generation when compared with the Combination 1 (i.e., no fin and no spray). This study proves that the combination of backplane fins and nozzle spray is an effective way to improve the performance of photovoltaic panels.

title: Performance and robustness evaluation of retrofit and standard LiDAR-assisted control in wind turbines
abstract: LiDAR-assisted control has emerged as a promising approach to proactively mitigate turbine loads by exploiting upstream wind measurements. Standard LAC designs, however, typically require modifications to the existing controller architecture, such as injecting a feed-forward pitch signal to the actuator or embedding feed-forward pitch rates in the feedback loop. This work proposes a novel retrofit LiDAR-assisted control solution that can be implemented without prior knowledge or modification of the existing feedback controller. The retrofit strategy achieves feed-forward pitch action by perturbing the rotor speed measurement. A theoretical analysis establishes the equivalence between the proposed retrofit and standard methods in terms of closed-loop performance. This study presents a systematic performance and robustness analysis of standard and retrofit methods using sparse and dense LiDAR beam configurations. The sensitivity to LiDAR pre-filtering parameters, including buffer time and filter frequency, as well as retrofit-specific tuning parameters, is investigated. Simulation results show that, with appropriate tuning, standard and retrofit methods achieve comparable performance in reducing key turbine loads. Furthermore, robustness analysis demonstrates that retrofit design maintains satisfactory performance under tuning uncertainties. These findings provide practical guidelines for deploying retrofit solutions in operational turbines and highlight their potential to extend turbine lifetimes cost-effectively.

title: Energy potential and environmental benefits of hybrid floating photovoltaic systems on dams in Thailand
abstract: Floating photovoltaic systems installed on hydropower reservoirs can expand renewable capacity without occupying land, yet country-specific, operationally calibrated assessments for Southeast Asia remain scarce. This study provides the first province-resolved techno-economic and environmental assessment of hybrid floating photovoltaic deployment on Thailand's hydropower dams, using a performance model calibrated against the operating Sirindhorn plant (measured specific yield 1289 kWh/kWp). Potential generation, levelized cost, net present value, evaporation savings and carbon abatement were quantified across 1%, 5% and 10% reservoir-coverage scenarios for the country's dam provinces, and a 10,000-run Monte Carlo simulation with Sobol variance decomposition was used to quantify uncertainty. At 10% coverage the dams could host about 83.8 GWp and generate roughly 103 TWh per year, equivalent to a large share of national demand, while reducing reservoir evaporation and avoiding carbon emissions. The national levelized cost of electricity is about 60 USD/MWh (10th to 90th percentile range 55 to 79), below Thailand's average retail tariff and competitive with regional utility-scale solar; the investment remains net-present-value-positive across the entire 10th to 90th percentile uncertainty range and improves further under carbon pricing. Cost is governed chiefly by capital expenditure and financing, and value by the electricity price. These results offer a locally grounded, uncertainty-quantified evidence base for integrating floating solar with existing hydropower in Thailand and comparable Southeast Asian settings.

title: Renewable energy production forecasting based on fractional order polynomial sinusoidal driving grey prediction model
abstract: Energy production data, such as wind power generation, exhibit nonlinear growth trends and quarterly periodic fluctuations, posing significant challenges for conventional forecasting methods. To address this issue, this paper proposes a fractional order polynomial sinusoidal driving grey prediction model, denoted as FPSGM(1,1,N). First, the constant grey action quantity is extended to a fractional order polynomial and a sinusoidal driving term. A systematic framework is then established for parameter estimation, time response function, and restoration of predicted values. Second, theoretical analysis shows that the proposed model generalizes several classical grey models, demonstrating the flexibility and inclusiveness of its theoretical framework. Third, the particle swarm optimization algorithm and a hierarchical optimization strategy are employed to collaboratively optimize the model parameters. Finally, the proposed model is first validated on a transitional energy case to examine its robustness, and then applied to wind power generation as a renewable energy case to demonstrate its applicability in the renewable energy domain. Experimental results show the FPSGM model outperforms the comparison models in prediction accuracy, verifying its effectiveness and superiority in handling non-stationary periodic series of energy data.

title: Shallow geothermal energy in the Canary Islands: Resource and technical potential for energy planning
abstract: This study presents an archipelago-wide assessment of shallow geothermal potential in the Canary Islands, integrating subsurface thermal properties, groundwater influence, and spatially explicit heating and cooling demand within an enhanced GIS-based application of the G.POT methodology. Ground thermal conductivity was estimated by accounting for lithology and groundwater depth, enabling differentiation between saturated and unsaturated conditions. A municipality-level comparison between aggregated thermal demand and shallow geothermal potential was performed to evaluate the extent to which local resources could offset climatization needs. Results indicate that cooling potential consistently exceeds heating potential across all islands, reaching up to 14 MWh per borehole per year, reflecting the cooling-dominated energy profile of this subtropical region. Thermal demand is highly concentrated in Tenerife and Gran Canaria, which together account for 67.7% of total climatization requirements. While municipal-scale results suggest a substantial technical resource, realistic deployment is strongly constrained by land availability. Urban case studies in Tenerife show that compact metropolitan areas can meet only 1.7% of cooling demand under realistic installation conditions, whereas more dispersed municipalities with greater surface availability can reach up to 17%. The study provides a spatial framework to support renewable cooling planning in volcanic and warm-climate island contexts.

title: Influences of copper foam geometrical parameters on the quenching behavior of premixed green H2-air venting flames
abstract: The flames from green hydrogen (H2) explosions, which have high burning rates, pose a serious threat to nearby equipment and personnel, underscoring the importance of research on flame quenching. However, the relationship between copper foam geometric parameters and flame suppression performance remains insufficiently understood. To investigate the influence of copper foam geometric parameters on explosion venting and flame suppression behaviors of H2–air mixtures, experiments were conducted on a gas explosion venting and quenching platform. Explosion pressure and temperature fields were examined under different copper foam parameters, including Pores Per Inch (PPI: 20–80), porosity (ε: 80–96%), thickness (20–40 mm), and static activation pressure (Pstat: 0.105–0.175 MPa).
