Results showed that successful quenching occurred when the pressure drop of copper foam (v = 1.829 m/s) exceeded 176 Pa. When ensuring structural strength, increasing PPI and porosity enhanced quenching efficacy by increasing C1 and C2. This study establishes a quantitative relationship between copper foam geometric parameters and quenching performance. The simulated annealing algorithm (SA) optimized the extended Ergun formula, enabling direct prediction of geometric parameters according to required pressure drop and providing guidance for safety design of hydrogen storage, transportation equipment, and explosion venting systems.

title: Robust planning for multi-path retrofits of coal-fired power plants considering biomass gasification co-firing
abstract: Under the carbon neutrality vision, early retirement of coal-fired power plants (CFPPs) reduces system flexibility and increases supply-demand imbalance risks. Effective low-carbon retrofit technologies can retain existing capacity and support secure operation of the power system. Biomass gasification co-firing (BGCF) is recognized as a key retrofit pathway, yet practical planning models remain scarce. Additionally, multi-timescale energy storage can enhance energy adequacy and system flexibility, supporting the safe transition of CFPPs. To this end, this study proposes a robust planning method for multi-path CFPP retrofits considering BGCF. First, a BGCF planning model is proposed based on energy flow balances among gasification, co-firing, and power generation. Then, a robust planning framework is introduced to coordinate multi-path retrofits, multi-timescale storage deployment, and variable renewable energy expansion under supply-demand uncertainty. To ensure tractable solution of the large-scale robust planning model, an improved column-and-constraint generation algorithm is adopted. Case studies on the HRP-38 system show that BGCF contributes over 25% of retrofitted output, with daily carbon reductions exceeding 1.4 × 105 tons. Compared to single-path retrofits, the proposed model reduces total cost by up to 79.36%.
keywords: Multi-path retrofits of coal-fired power plants

title: Real-time I–V curve scaling and MPP estimation through polynomial regression model for photovoltaic modules based on Gompertz functions
abstract: This paper proposes a simplified and computationally efficient method for scaling the current–voltage and estimating maximum power point characteristics of photovoltaic modules, specifically designed for real-time monitoring. The proposed approach firstly estimates the symmetrized and shifted Gompertz model under standard conditions. By considering other irradiance and temperature conditions, both short-circuit current and open-circuit voltage values are used to scale the current–voltage curve and, subsequently, the maximum power point value is then estimated by using a polynomial regression model, avoiding iterative and complex processes. A large-scale statistical analysis is performed using 130 monocrystalline silicon photovoltaic modules from 44 manufacturers, producing 4550 scaled current–voltage curves. The results showed that 99.51% of the polynomial regression maximum power point values differed by less than 1% from those calculated by the Gompertz model, and 100% remained within a 1.5% error margin. A case study using 1725 real operating points from a commercial photovoltaic plant further validated the model, providing an average energy deviation of less than 5.6% compared to real collected photovoltaic generation for 11 days. The computational time was significantly reduced from 14–212 s per current–voltage curve by using the iterative Gompertz method to lower than one second with the proposed approach under different current hardware platforms. These results confirm the feasibility of the method for low-resource, real-time applications, including embedded systems and micro-inverters. Future work will focus on integrating thermal dynamic behavior and extending the model for accurate energy forecasting under variable environmental conditions.

title: Carbon-responsibility-aware peer-to-peer trading mechanism for microgrids with heterogeneous energy
abstract: Peer-to-peer (P2P) trading enables microgrids, acting as prosumers, to exchange surplus electricity locally. The traded power often originates from heterogeneous sources such as photovoltaics, gas turbines, and energy storage systems, each with distinct carbon intensities. However, most existing P2P profit distribution mechanisms treat electricity as a homogeneous commodity and overlook the carbon heterogeneity among energy sources, thus failing to capture the environmental implications of trading behaviors. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a carbon-responsibility-aware P2P trading mechanism that embeds carbon responsibility into the cooperative benefit allocation process, thereby extending traditional P2P trading from economic optimization to environmentally accountable decision-making. Specifically, a carbon responsibility attribution model is developed based on a carbon-weighted graph neural network, which embeds the carbon intensities of heterogeneous energy sources into the adjacency matrix to capture the propagation of carbon emissions along trading paths and accurately learn the mapping between electricity flows and transaction-level carbon responsibility. Furthermore, an asymmetric bargaining mechanism is designed, where heterogeneous carbon responsibilities are converted into environmental values to determine bargaining factors, and an asymmetric exponential weighting function is introduced to adjust allocation coefficients. Compared to the standard graph convolutional network, the proposed model improves the coefficient of determination for carbon attribution by 16.60%. Furthermore, the trading framework reduces aggregate carbon emissions by 12.14% while incurring a marginal 0.90% operational cost increase for the heterogeneous energy cluster, providing an economical and efficient approach to transitioning the system toward low-carbon operation.

title: Seasonal resilient operation of a solar-based off-grid integrated energy system for plateau mining areas: A risk-averse IGDT approach
abstract: Off-grid integrated energy systems (OIES) in plateau mining areas face the challenge of balancing economy and resilience under significant seasonal variations and source-load uncertainty. This paper develops an optimal dispatch model that accounts for high-altitude characteristics and incorporates a risk-averse approach based on information gap decision theory (IGDT), together with a demand response (DR) mechanism, to investigate the operational characteristics and resilience of the system across different seasons. Based on typical heating and non-heating season scenarios, the system's operating mode, cost structure, and resilience level are comparatively analyzed. The results show that the system relies more heavily on the coordinated operation of concentrated solar power (CSP) and energy storage during the heating season, with a total operating cost of 88,776.14 CNY, significantly higher than the 61,375.30 CNY in the non-heating season. As the cost deviation coefficient increases, the system's tolerable uncertainty level also increases. The introduction of DR further enhances the system's operational efficiency and resilience. The maximum uncertainty tolerance reaches 25.67% during the non-heating season and 10.39% during the heating season. Furthermore, under the deterministic model, the total operating cost during the heating season decreases by 3.96%, while reliance on diesel generators decreases and the share of renewable energy in the supply increases slightly. The results demonstrate that the proposed method can provide decision support for the safe, economic, and low-carbon operation of OIES in plateau mining areas.

title: Assessment of photovoltaic energy potential over Italy from an ensemble of convection permitting climate models
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) energy production is crucial to achieve climate neutrality by 2050 and is tightly linked to climate variability and change. In particular, variations in the availability of surface solar radiation impact PV energy potential, while temperature and wind affect PV cell efficiency. Here, for the first time, we evaluate the ability of a 16-member km-scale convection-permitting climate model (CPMs) ensemble to reproduce PV energy potential over Italy. The assessment is conducted at station and national level using ERA5-land reanalysis dataset as reference. Driving climate variables are further evaluated against available high-resolution observations. The quality assessment of CPMs and ERA5-land data reveal an overestimation of downward shortwave radiation at the surface by CPMs (+6% in summer) and underestimation by similar amounts in ERA5-land compared to the high-resolution observational dataset. The 2m temperatures and 10 m wind speeds are slightly overestimated in CPMs as well by 1.24C and 0.54 m/s respectively. Based on this good agreement, the energy potential model previously validated with ERA5-land is applied to CPMs. The CPM ensemble shows realistic diurnal and seasonal cycles, but tends to overestimate PV potential relative to ERA5-land by up to +10 % at individual stations and +13 % at bidding zones, in particular due to the bias in radiation. Ensemble spread is 20% in summer, but significantly lower within model families. These findings support the use of CPM ensembles for climate change impact studies on solar resources, providing high resolution information to support adaptation strategies in power system planning at local scale.

title: Modified multidiode solar cell equivalent circuits with explicit Lambert W-based analytical current – voltage formulation
abstract: Accurate modeling of photovoltaic cells is essential for simulation, optimization, parameter identification, and real-time control of solar energy systems. Although multi-diode equivalent circuits generally provide higher accuracy than the conventional single-diode model, their current–voltage characteristics are typically described by implicit nonlinear equations requiring iterative numerical solutions, which reduces their suitability for real-time applications and analytical investigations. This paper introduces four novel modified multi-diode equivalent circuits (MMSCC1–MMSCC4) based on the progressive addition of diode–resistor branches, providing greater flexibility in representing nonlinear carrier transport, recombination phenomena, parasitic losses, and internal energy dissipation mechanisms within photovoltaic cells. The main contribution is the preservation of an explicit analytical current–voltage formulation despite the progressive increase in circuit complexity. The analytical expressions are derived using the Lambert W function, enabling direct current calculation without iterative root-finding procedures. The model parameters are identified using the Whale Optimization Algorithm, and the proposed circuits are validated using the RTC France solar cell, the PHOTOWATT PWP photovoltaic module, and experimentally measured data from the Kyocera KC200GT photovoltaic module under different irradiance and temperature conditions. The results show a progressive improvement in modeling accuracy as additional nonlinear branches are introduced. In particular, the most comprehensive proposed model, MMSCC4, reduces the RMSE relative to the conventional single-diode model by 25.41% for the RTC France cell and by 56.17% for the PHOTOWATT PWP module, while consistently outperforming the single-diode model for the experimentally tested KC200GT module under varying irradiance and temperature conditions. Despite the increased circuit complexity, MMSCC4 requires only approximately 0.09–0.10 ms to compute a complete I–V characteristic, confirming the low computational burden of the explicit Lambert W-based formulation. Therefore, the proposed circuits provide a favorable compromise between modeling accuracy, physical flexibility, analytical tractability, and computational efficiency, making them suitable for photovoltaic simulation, parameter identification, and applications requiring rapid current evaluation.

title: Corrigendum to “A flexible and secure model predictive control strategy for frequency regulation of wind turbines considering fatigue load mitigation” [Renew. Energy 273 (2026) 126129]
Data-driven prognostic algorithm based on Bi-LSTM transformer model for proton exchange membrane fuel cell
abstract: The complex interaction of internal physical phenomena makes predicting the degradation of Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (PEMFCs) under dynamic operating conditions a critical but persistent challenge. To address this, the present work develops a hybrid model based on Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) layers with a multi-head self-attention mechanism to capture degradation dependencies across both short and long time-frames. When benchmarked against state-of-the-art architectures, including attention-based LSTM variants and the Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT), the model achieves a reduction of up to 52.7% in Root Mean Square Error (RMSE). The model’s accuracy is confirmed across single-step, multi-step, and long-term forecasting scenarios, where it consistently maintains high predictive accuracy ( R 2 ≥ 0.998 ) for prediction horizons of up to 175 steps ahead. Furthermore, this high performance is achieved with notable data efficiency, requiring a training dataset of 300 h. These combined strengths in accuracy, long-term reliability, and data efficiency make the proposed Bi-LSTM Transformer an effective tool for predictive health management under dynamic load cycles.

title: Coordinated dispatch of hydro-wind-photovoltaic systems based on a differentiated peak-shaving method for cascaded hydropower stations
abstract: The rapid expansion of wind and photovoltaic generation increases the need for peak-shaving in large scale hydro-wind-photovoltaic hybrid systems. Existing cascade hydropower dispatch methods generally performs unified computational processing for all hydropower stations, which neglects differences in peak-shaving capability and may produce computational burden or operationally impractical schedules. To address this issue, this paper proposes a hydro-wind-photovoltaic coordinated optimization dispatch method considering differentiated peak-shaving participation of cascaded hydropower stations. The cascaded stations are classified into flexible peak-shaving hydropower stations and stable power output hydropower stations according to installed capacity and reservoir regulation capability. The former are dispatched with one period as dispatch interval to undertake the main peak-shaving task, whereas the latter follow segmented stable output trajectories to reduce unnecessary adjustments. Case studies are conducted for the Guangxi power grid with 37 hydropower stations. In the typical system load scenario, compared with the conventional peak-shaving method, differentiated peak-shaving method substantially reduces the model scale, with the numbers of constraints, continuous variables and integer variables reduced by approximately 70.0%, 67.0% and 71.9% respectively. Although its maximum residual load is 2.35% higher, differentiated peak-shaving method reduces cumulative station output variation by 64.8% and the number of output adjustment over 100 MW in 15min by 70.3%. Supplementary high system load and high renewable penetration scenarios further show that differentiated peak-shaving method can maintain effective peak-shaving capability while consistently reducing unnecessary regulation. These results demonstrate that differentiated peak-shaving method improves computational tractability and dispatch implementability under the premise of full wind and photovoltaic accommodation.

title: Interpretable machine learning analysis of anode operating parameters on the performance of a high-power PEMFC system
abstract: In the global transition to carbon neutrality, hydrogen serves as a vital carrier for storing intermittent renewable energy such as wind and solar power. Proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFC) are essential devices for reconverting hydrogen into electricity. However, the complex multiphysics coupling of gas, water, electricity, and heat makes output behavior difficult to predict through mechanistic models. Consequently, optimizing stack performance by adjusting auxiliary system parameters remains a significant control challenge at current stage. Based on system experiments, machine learning models, and the Shapley Additive Explanation (SHAP) methodology derived from game theory, this paper systematically explores the effects of operating parameters of the hydrogen supply subsystem on the output performance of high-power fuel cell systems. First, controlled-variable experiments were designed to investigate the voltage response under diverse operating conditions. Subsequently, the experimental data were preprocessed and subjected to feature selection to construct a neural network-based prediction model. Finally, interpretability analysis based on SHAP values was conducted globally at different current densities. The results show that at low current density, operating temperature has a significant negative effect on the output voltage, while ambient water vapor pressure ratio exhibits a strong positive effect. At high current density, anode hydrogen concentration, anode molar flow rate, and anode water vapor concentration become the three parameters with the highest contribution. This study quantifies the effects of anode operating parameters on high-power fuel cell system performance, providing optimization solutions for hydrogen supply subsystem and guidance for formulating control strategies to enhance hydrogen utilization efficiency.

title: Optimization research on multi-mode collaborative air cycle refrigeration system
abstract: In response to environmental protection requirements for refrigerants, air cycle refrigeration technology is valued for its safety and zero pollution but is limited by low energy efficiency. To overcome this bottleneck, this paper proposes a novel integrated optimization and control framework for air cycle refrigeration systems. The framework introduces a dual degree-of-freedom architecture that combines two-compressor dynamic coordination with adaptive high/low-pressure cycle switching, and develops a particle swarm optimization (PSO)-based control strategy to simultaneously optimize pressure ratio and mass flow rate, explicitly accounting for their coupling and enabling near-global optimal operation. Simulation studies were conducted using a computational fluid dynamics model validated by experiments and the effectiveness-number of transfer units method. Taking a residential building in Beijing as an example, the results show that the air cycle refrigeration system controlled by PSO algorithm performs 30% and 26% better in annual performance compared to traditional optimal pressure ratio control and optimal mass flow rate control methods. The two-compressor dynamic switching significantly enhances system performance, with annual performance improvements of 7% (using two compressors) and 8% (using two compressors and high/low pressure cycles) compared to the single-compressor system. The payback period of the single compressor system controlled by PSO is only 0.54 years. The results demonstrate that this optimization scheme broadens the high-efficiency operating envelope and provides a scalable pathway to overcome the energy efficiency bottleneck of air cycle refrigeration systems, offering a practical solution for analogous gas cycle.

title: Corrigendum to “The role of glacier retreat for Swiss hydropower production” [Renew. Energy 132, (2019), 615-627]
A Deep learning-based market mechanism providing reasonable incentives for low-carbon power system
abstract: Current electricity market mechanism based on marginal pricing theory lacks incentives that ensure competitive equilibrium and fairness with the increasing proportion of renewable energy and generalized energy storage in the low carbon power system. This paper first introduces a social welfare contribution degree (SWCD) mechanism, allocating welfare based on marginal contributions without generating opportunity costs or surpluses, thereby preventing the competitive disequilibrium often arising from such factors. Also, it aligns incentives with contributions, adhering to Adams’ equity theory. To improve SWCD’s computational efficiency, we developed a deep learning method combining multi-head self-attention and residual network, named MHSA-ResNet, creating the final automatically calculated SWCD (AC-SWCD) mechanism. Simulations show that MHSA-ResNet performs better than some other classic neural networks. The proposed mechanism is compared with the locational marginal price and Vickrey-Clarke-Groves mechanisms through case studies. Results show that it can provide incentive signals with high computational efficiency ensuring competitive equilibrium and incentive fairness.

title: Unveiling the sectoral impact of renewable energy on growth in Europe: A threshold and machine learning approach
abstract: Our paper uncovers a hidden structure in the renewable energy-growth nexus of the European countries by showing that “why renewable energy is consumed” matters as much as “how much”. Using a dynamic panel threshold model and complementary machine learning techniques for 27 European countries from 2004 to 2024, we demonstrate that renewable energy is associated with economic growth in fundamentally different ways across sectors. Four distinct turning points emerge: transportation (9.611%), electricity generation (13.615%), overall renewable energy consumption (14.152%), and heating and cooling (27.601%). Above these thresholds, transportation, renewable electricity, heating and cooling, and total renewable use generate increasing returns to GDP, with heating and cooling exerting the strongest effect, each 1% rise in renewable penetration corresponds to a 0.044% increase in GDP. In sharp contrast, transportation displays diminishing returns: below its threshold, a 1% increase is associated with a 0.032% increase in GDP, but the effect weakens once the threshold is exceeded. Machine learning results (SHAP and PDP) corroborate these non-linear patterns, revealing heterogeneous and purpose-specific marginal effects across the renewable energy landscape. Taken together, the findings show that Europe's energy transition is not a uniform growth engine but a constellation of sectoral regimes, each with its own economic leverage point.

title: Electron transfer kinetics of Shewanella on algae-derived biochar anodes in microbial fuel cells
abstract: This study evaluated three macroalgae-derived biochars, UPB (Ulva prolifera), SHB (Sargassum horneri) and LJB (Laminaria japonica) as cost-effective anode modifiers in Shewanella oneidensis MR-1 MFCs. The maximum power densities achieved with UPB, SHB, and LJB were 362.9 mW m−2, 278.9 mW m−2, and 262.4 mW m−2, respectively, representing improvements of 342%, 240%, and 220% over the CC-based MFC (82 mW m−2). Biochar modification also induced a shift of Shewanella extracellular electron transfer mode from a direct, surface-controlled pathway to an indirect, diffusion-mediated process. Furthermore, UPB-MFC also exhibited the highest chloramphenicol degradation ratios (62% within 12h), with a kinetic constant of 0.079 h−1, substantially exceeding the CC control (29%, 0.028 h−1). These corresponded to relative increases of 113%, 69%, and 48%, respectively. These findings highlight algal biochar as a sustainable anode material for simultaneous energy recovery and antibiotic remediation.

title: Design and evaluation of a compressed air energy storage system coupling geothermal and solar energy
abstract: In response to the intermittent nature of renewable energy sources and the performance limitations of traditional compressed air energy storage technology, this paper proposes and evaluates an integrated solar–geothermal hybrid compressed air energy storage configuration. The proposed configuration coordinates geothermal power generation, parabolic trough solar collection, compressed air energy storage, organic Rankine cycle-based waste-heat recovery, and hot-water production to achieve cascade energy utilisation. Thermodynamic models of the principal subsystems are established and individually validated against data reported in the literature.Through comprehensive thermodynamic and economic analyses, a quantitative sensitivity assessment of key operating parameters is conducted to reveal their impact on system performance. The results indicate that the round-trip efficiency, electrical energy storage efficiency, and exergy efficiency reach 68.95%, 77.03%, and 67.11%, respectively. Exergy analysis reveals that the compressor is the component with the highest exergy destruction, accounting for 20.68%. Sensitivity analysis results indicate that system performance is significantly influenced by key component parameters. Specifically, increases in ambient temperature and the system charging/discharging pressure difference have a negative impact on overall performance, while an increase in storage pressure exhibits a positive effect.Finally, under the assumed economic conditions, the system shows potentially favourable economic performance, with a total investment of approximately USD 8.73 million and a dynamic payback period of 3.61 years.

title: Performance evaluation of rotational thermal storage tank in energy harvesting and releasing cycle: design of gradient fin structure
abstract: To address the issue of low thermal conductivity of phase change materials (PCMs) in energy system applications, this study develops a numerical model to investigate the effects of gradient-height fin configurations on the melting and solidification performance of a rotating TES unit, and compares three types of fin arrangements (uniform, positive-gradient, and negative-gradient). The results indicate that the optimized negative-gradient fin structure significantly accelerates the melting process, reducing the complete melting time by 20.42%. Moreover, it enhances heat transfer in the lower PCM region, improving temperature uniformity by 29.66%. The combination of negative-gradient fins and rotation significantly improves melting efficiency, especially in the upper and middle sections, where velocity field uniformity is improved by 19.98%. In contrast, the positive-gradient configuration exhibits better performance during solidification, as heat dissipation in the upper region is enhanced. This study provides valuable guidance for the design of efficient TES systems.

title: Optical properties of Ni/Ce1-xZrxO2 and the effect of light enhancement on CO2 dissociation
abstract: Photothermal catalytic technology ensures efficient catalysis while achieving the objectives of energy conservation and carbon reduction. It facilitates the reduction of reaction temperatures, the mitigation or even elimination of carbon deposition, and the extension of catalyst lifespan. Five catalyst models of Ce1-xZrxO2 (x = 0, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, 1) are constructed based on density functional theory using the first-principles plane-wave ultrasoft pseudopotential method to compute their electronic structures and optical properties. The results demonstrate that the Ce1-xZrxO2 doping system markedly improves light utilization and induces greater charge transfer, with Ce1/4Zr3/4O2 exhibiting the most optimal optical properties. The loading of Ni improves the conductivity of the catalytic system. By simulating the dissociation process of CO2 on the surface of Ni/Ce1-xZrxO2 catalysts under illuminated and dark conditions, it is found that Ce-Zr doping significantly reduces the dissociation energy barrier of CO2, light substantially promotes the adsorption and dissociation of CO2. The aforementioned research provides theoretical guidance for the preparation of high-performance photothermal synergistic reforming catalysts.

title: Analytical modeling of multiple borehole heat exchangers in layered soil with pile-soil thermal contact resistance
abstract: Heat transfer in multiple borehole heat exchangers within layered ground is influenced by imperfect pile-soil contact, which induces thermal contact resistance and substantially reduces system efficiency. Conventional models, however, neglect pile-soil thermal contact resistance entirely, leading to biased predictions. To address this limitation, this study develops an analytical model that explicitly accounts for both groundwater seepage and pile-soil thermal contact resistance, enabling simultaneous resolution of heat transfer within boreholes and thermal diffusion in the surrounding soil. The model is validated against numerical results and published experimental data. The results show that a fivefold increase in seepage velocity reduces the upstream outlet temperature of the borehole by 2.3% while elevating the downstream soil temperature by 23.6%, thereby intensifying the thermal asymmetry within the temperature field. In cooling mode, thermal contact resistance raises the outlet temperature and lowers the adjacent soil temperature by 5.8%, thus delaying thermal interaction among boreholes; the opposite occurs under heating conditions. These results indicate that both pile-soil thermal contact resistance and groundwater seepage have a non-negligible effect on heat transfer in borehole heat exchangers. These findings provide a theoretical basis for the optimal design of borehole heat exchanger under complex geological conditions.

title: Estimating daily run-of-river hydropower generation from open hydrometeorological data: Limits of hydrology-based modelling
abstract: Hydropower is important for energy system modelling, where run-of-river hydropower is commonly represented as prescribed non-dispatchable generation. This study uses open hydrometeorological datasets to estimate the aggregated daily run-of-river generation and to assess the explanatory limits of hydrology-based modelling. ERA5, GEOGLOWS V2, and GloFAS v4.0 reanalyses are evaluated against reported generation for six European countries as a case study: France, Austria, Germany, Finland, Portugal, and Romania. Different input sets are compared within a consistent modelling framework, and the best-performing baseline model is used to diagnose remaining estimation errors. The results show that GloFAS river discharge provides the most suitable input for reproducing reported run-of-river generation, as it captures the dominant seasonal hydrological variability more robustly than the models with ERA5 and GEOGLOWS. The remaining error is the uncaptured short-term variation in reported generation. Additional tests indicate that accounting for reservoir generation provides limited improvements in model performance at the aggregated daily country level, while part of the residual is associated with electricity-price deviations, potentially reflecting short-term operation enabled by unclassified pondage within reported run-of-river generation. Accordingly, representing reported run-of-river generation as fully non-dispatchable in large-scale energy system models may overlook the potential short-term flexibility contained in the reported profiles The hydrology-based run-of-river estimates should therefore be interpreted as weather-dependent availability profiles, and the reproducible workflow in this study can produce such profiles for large-scale energy system studies across historical weather years beyond the period covered by reported data.

title: Balancing profit and exergy efficiency: Optimal dispatch strategies for integrated energy systems with high renewable penetration
abstract: The synergistic optimization of economic viability and thermodynamicefficiency in Integrated Energy Systems (IES) with multiple stakeholders presents a significant challenge. This paper proposes a novel exergy-economic bi-objective optimization framework for a regional IES featuring shared hybrid energy storage, structured as a bi-level Stackelberg game. The framework captures the hierarchical interactions among a microgrid operator (MGO) as the leader, and a user aggregator (UA) and a shared storage operator (SSO) as followers. The MGO aims to maximize economic profit, while the system's overall exergy efficiency is simultaneously maximized to enhance energy quality. The Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II), combined with a Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) process, is employed to solve the model and identify the best compromise solution. Case studies demonstrate an inherent trade-off between the maximum profit strategy (operator profit: $118.6, exergy efficiency: 61.24%) and the maximum exergy efficiency strategy. The best compromise solution achieves a superior balance, capturing significant arbitrage profits while preserving the core efficiency of cogeneration. The analysis reveals that while hard constraints define a robust operational corridor, the bi-objective optimization acts as a fine-tuning force, enabling a sophisticated balance between market-driven arbitrage and thermodynamics-aware cogeneration.

title: How low-level jets impact the power curve of floating offshore wind turbines: Comprehensive analysis and prediction model
abstract: The wind turbine power curve, essential for wind turbine monitoring, is typically modeled assuming uniform or shear inflow. However, the low-level jet disrupts this conventional single-point wind speed to power relationship due to its unique wind profile, causing significant actual power output deviations. To enhance power curve prediction under low-level jet conditions, this study introduces a low-level jet model from measurements. The research methodology progresses by first quantifying the sensitivity of power output to low-level jet characteristics, followed by an analysis of how low-level jets impact the power curve, ultimately leading to a new minute-level model. The findings identify three low-level jet characteristics (jet height, jet intensity, and friction velocity) that significantly impact the power curve, causing deviations up to 32.91% from the reference. Moreover, friction velocity significantly affects power fluctuations, impairing the accuracy of real-time minute-level power prediction and control. By acquiring these characteristics through wind field perception technology and integrating the proposed model, which considers only the jet height and jet intensity, minute-level power prediction errors can be effectively reduced. Furthermore, based on the actual power curve, the control strategy's switching criterion can be adjusted to the actual rated wind speed. This reduces energy losses from existing strategies.

title: Assessment of the technical feasibility of pruning waste gasification in a pilot-scale downdraft plant
abstract: Pruning activities for the maintenance of electrical distribution lines in the city of Bogotá and peripheral municipalities produce tons of residues to be treated. This study aims to evaluate the technical feasibility of the valorisation route through gasification, evaluating the different particle size distributions, and the effect of operational conditions in a downdraft gasification process. A systematic homogenization and classification of biomass is conducted to define three size fractions, followed by the selection of the best mixture based on the angle of repose (AOR), using an adapted method with the Abrams cone. Statistical analyses (ANOVA and Tukey HSD’s test) revealed that a 70–30 wt.% mixture of intermediate and fine particles offers the most favourable flow characteristics. This mixture is used in a pilot-scale 20 kW downdraft gasifier to evaluate the effect of different equivalence ratios (ER) on the gasification performance. A low-cost and easy-to-implement analysis of the reactor temperature stability through Gaussian Mixture Modelling (GMM) is proposed, showing that the 70–30 wt.% mixture and an ER of 0.22 facilitate continuous feeding without blockages. The findings demonstrate that combining flowability analysis with thermal performance evaluation is a powerful tool to evaluate the performance of biomass gasification using heterogeneous feedstocks like pruning waste in real operative conditions, ultimately contributing to local bioenergy initiatives and sustainable waste valorisation strategies.

title: Optimizing China's offshore wind-solar power systems for supply–demand matching: exploring wind-solar and wind-solar-storage integration models
abstract: Hybrid offshore wind–solar development can exploit resource complementarity to reduce generation variability. However, systematic optimization of offshore wind–solar configurations for electricity supply–demand matching in China remains limited. This study develops offshore wind–solar and wind–solar–storage optimization models for mainland China's exclusive economic zones to determine province-specific wind–solar capacity allocation and storage configuration for electricity supply–demand matching, and subsequently evaluates their electricity supply capability and the levelized cost of electricity. After optimization, the average installed wind and solar capacities of a single generation unit (500 km2) are 2587 and 19,803 MW, respectively, with a wind capacity share of 0.117 and average annual generation of 37,250 GWh. The wind–solar system achieves a supply guarantee rate above 90% while maintaining curtailment below 15.2%. At the same electricity supply ratio, incorporating storage substantially reduces both the required wind–solar capacity and curtailment, with an average storage capacity of 3937 MW, equivalent to 18.2% of total wind–solar capacity, and increases the wind capacity share by 0.001. Among the 11 coastal provinces, Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, and Guangxi exhibit the greatest development potential, combining high generation with an average LCOE below €66/MWh. These findings provide a quantitative basis for optimizing offshore wind–solar capacity allocation and storage deployment to improve electricity supply–demand matching across China's coastal provinces.

title: Experimental validation of a dynamic double-layer photovoltaic installation for enhanced energy production per unit of occupied land area
abstract: Large-scale photovoltaic deployment requires solutions that increase electricity production per unit of occupied land area. This study presents and validates through on-field tests a dynamic double-layer photovoltaic installation, consisting of two vertically stacked bifacial layers occupying the same land area of a conventional single-layer installation. The two stacked layers are capable of independent solar tracking. A custom-built scaled prototype with twelve rotating bifacial modules and independent current sensing was operated on field under three different operation modes and compared with a conventional single-layer installation occupying the same ground area. The most efficient operation mode, which has the top layer dynamically tracking the sun and the bottom layer fixed, achieved a gain of about +42% relative to a monofacial single-layer installation and +27% relative to a bifacial one, while a more simple open-loop tracking strategy based on a five-parameter sigmoid yielded gains close to +39% and +25% with negligible loss compared with closed-loop optimal control. The proposed installation is in principle agnostic with respect to the cell technology adopted and scalable from compact dynamic modules to utility-scale and agrivoltaic applications.

title: An innovative multiple substrates proportioning method for anaerobic co-digestion: from mechanism analysis to practical verification
abstract: To address the absence of substrates proportioning rule in the anaerobic co-digestion (AcoD) field, an innovative method based on the regulation of organic components proportion was preliminarily proposed. Through co-digestion tests of model compounds, the synergistic effect and synergistic interval of organic components were determined. Accordingly, a maximal synergistic effect of 1.23 was achieved at the proportion of 6:3:1 (carbohydrate:protein:lipid), corresponding to the optimal ratio. Based on the similar substrate degradation efficiency and the increasing ratio of CH4 to CO2, it could be inferred that the increase in methane yield from the synergistic effects was more likely attributable to the optimization of metabolic pathways rather than to the increase in substrate degradation. Moreover, the presence of a similar microbial community structure within the synergy interval of organic components further confirmed this inference. The co-digestion tests with different kinds of actual materials further optimized the accounting method of carbohydrate (VS-protein-lipid-lignin) and verified the universality of the synergistic effect at the optimized components proportion. Organic loading rate was increased to 8.0 g VS/(L·d) by 100% through organic composition optimization in the continuous test. Thus, this study provides a more scientific and reliable multi-substrate proportioning method for AcoD, contributing to promoting the energy production and environmental benefit of anaerobic digestion.

title: Techno-economic optimization of a grid-connected community microgrid with net metering using metaheuristic algorithms
abstract: Reliable and affordable electricity remains a challenge for community loads in Bangladesh because of frequent grid load shedding and rising tariffs. This study presents a techno-economic optimization of a hybrid microgrid with net metering for a community load in Nazipur, Naogaon. The system comprises solar photovoltaic, an optional wind turbine, lithium iron phosphate battery storage, a bidirectional converter, and a utility-grid connection. An hourly 8760-h simulation of renewable resources, demand, and energy management was integrated with three metaheuristic optimization methods to minimize the cost of energy subject to reliability and regulatory constraints. Because grid outages are stochastic, reliability was evaluated using expected loss of power supply probability over outage realizations. For an annual demand of 2003 MW-hours and a 420-kW peak load, all three methods identified the nominal least-cost configuration: 780 kW of solar photovoltaic capacity, zero wind capacity, 312 kW-hours of battery storage, and a 600-kW converter. Stochastic assessment yielded an expected loss of power supply probability of 1.16%, exceeding the 1% target; therefore, battery capacity was increased to 550 kW-hours while retaining other capacities. The final configuration achieves a cost of energy of 0.0959 dollars per kilowatt-hour, 8.8% below the reliability-matched grid benchmark, with a net present cost of 2.03 million dollars, renewable fraction of 49.8%, internal rate of return of 11.3%, and payback period of 8.2 years. Across 40 outage realizations, the mean loss of power supply probability was 0.96%, while the final design avoids approximately 644 tonnes of carbon dioxide per year on an operational basis.

title: Engineering hierarchical microporous carbon with oxygen functionalization from enzymatic hydrolysis lignin for high-performance supercapacitors via Hydrothermal-KOH activation
abstract: The growing demand for sustainable energy storage technologies highlights the urgent need for renewable, biomass-derived materials with superior electrochemical performance. In this work, hierarchical porous carbons (HPCs) were synthesized from enzymatic hydrolysis lignin (EHL) via a sulfuric acid-assisted hydrothermal treatment followed by KOH activation. The hydrothermal pretreatment effectively depolymerized lignin, enabling the creation of a highly interconnected microporous network with enriched oxygen-containing functionalities. By tuning the KOH-to-carbon ratio, the optimized sample (HPC-2) achieved an ultrahigh microporosity of 91.8% and a specific surface area of 1610.2 m2/g. These structural advantages endowed HPC-2 with a superior specific capacitance of 202.8 F/g at 0.5 A/g and excellent rate capability, retaining 80.0% capacitance at 20 A/g. Furthermore, a symmetric supercapacitor device assembled with HPC-2 delivered a high energy density of 14.1 Wh/kg at 250 W/kg. This study offers a sustainable and efficient strategy for engineering biomass-derived carbons with tailored pore structures and surface chemistry, paving the way for high-performance energy storage applications.

title: Land-resource endowment and photovoltaic deployment in China
abstract: China's rapid expansion of utility-scale photovoltaic power has raised growing concerns about whether deployment is aligned with land-resource endowment. We develop an S-weighted photovoltaic land-resource endowment framework, in which the area of each land parcel is weighted by a composite suitability index (S) integrating solar resource, terrain, and land-cover characteristics, so that more suitable land contributes more to estimated photovoltaic potential. We apply this framework to 43,190 utility-scale photovoltaic power plants totaling 670 GW across China from 2019 to 2025. Photovoltaic land endowment exhibits a pronounced west–east gradient, while deployment is disproportionately concentrated on cropland and rangeland and underrepresented on bare ground. Resource utilization efficiency remains below 2% nationally, and substantial spatial divergence persists between potential and realized deployment. Although provincial deployment is positively associated with land potential (R2 = 0.44, p < 0.001), considerable mismatch remains. Redirecting future expansion toward suitable bare-ground resources, particularly in northwestern China, could improve land-use efficiency while reducing pressure on agriculturally sensitive land.

title: Transfer learning and convolutional neural networks for solar photovoltaic systems detection in distributed power grids
abstract: Accurate mapping and characterization of distributed solar photovoltaic (PV) systems are essential for energy planning, net demand forecasting, and policy-making. Traditional methods for collecting data on distributed electricity generation are often labor-intensive, costly, or impractical. This study leverages recent advances in machine learning, introducing state-of-the-art image segmentation architectures for automated PV panel detection from remotely sensed data. To address constraints in training time and dataset size, transfer learning is applied using pre-trained large-scale deep neural networks as feature extractors. Additionally, a novel hard example mining scheme is proposed to enhance detection accuracy. Through a comprehensive framework, factors influencing prediction accuracy, such as PV recognition thresholds, segmentation model architecture, sampling strategies, and encoder parameter freezing, are systematically examined. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms other models, achieving an F1 score above 0.91 and an IoU exceeding 0.83. This research advances automated infrastructure mapping, providing scalable solutions for monitoring distributed PV systems and offering transferable methodologies for broader applications.

title: Bimetallic Ni-Ca/MgO and HZSM-5 catalysts for two-step synergistic catalytic co-pyrolysis of lignin and low-density polyethylene into jet fuel range products
abstract: To enable the production of jet-fuel-range hydrocarbons from lignin and low-density polyethylene (LDPE), it is crucial to enhance the activity of catalysts towards the deoxygenation reaction. Herein, a two-step catalytic strategy was developed to achieve this target over bimetallic Ni-Ca/MgO and HZSM-5 catalysts. The synergistic effect of Ni and Ca increased the liquid yield and enhanced the hydrocarbon quality. The deoxygenation of phenols and the aromatization of chain hydrocarbons were promoted by the Ni-Ca/MgO and HZSM-5, respectively. DFT calculations confirm that the Ni-Ca/MgO was catalytically unique compared with MgO, Ni/MgO and Ca/MgO, and the dissociation energy of Caromatic-OH bond in phenol was significantly reduced upon adsorption on Ni-Ca/MgO, resulting in its distinct selectivity to aromatics. 84.3 area% jet-fuel-range products was obtained at the temperature of 550 °C with catalyst to feedstock ratio of 1:1. This work provided a promising approach for the catalytic valorization of lignin and LDPE into jet-fuel-range hydrocarbons.

title: Performance assessment of dual phase change material integration in building-integrated photovoltaics: A coupled Thermal–Electrical, economic, and environmental assessment
abstract: Building-integrated photovoltaics can reduce building electricity demand and emissions, but elevated photovoltaic operating temperatures reduce conversion efficiency. This study develops a seasonally adaptive dual-phase-change-material photovoltaic system using RT21HC and RT35HC with different melting temperatures and layer thicknesses to provide complementary thermal regulation under varying conditions. A coupled one-dimensional thermal–electrical model is developed using an enthalpy-based formulation to describe phase change and thermal interactions within the multilayer photovoltaic structure. The model is evaluated using 8760 hourly meteorological data points for Tehran and directly validated against published experimental data for a dual-phase-change-material photovoltaic configuration. The validation shows good agreement, with mean absolute percentage errors of 2.13% for photovoltaic temperature and 2.31% for electrical power, and root mean square error values of 0.91 °C and 0.072 W, respectively. Annual simulations indicate that the proposed system generates 499.23 MWh of electricity and can theoretically supply 67.12% of the annual electricity demand of the building. The base-case levelized cost of electricity is 0.050 $ kWh−1, while varying photovoltaic and phase-change-material costs from 70% to 130% changes the levelized cost of electricity to 0.045–0.055 and 0.040–0.059 $ kWh−1, respectively. Delaying phase-change-material replacement from 10 to 25 years reduces the levelized cost of electricity from 0.052 to 0.046 $ kWh−1. The operational carbon dioxide assessment indicates 616.6 kg of carbon dioxide avoided per panel annually, 5% above conventional building-integrated photovoltaics, without representing a full life-cycle assessment.

title: Retraction notice to “Transforming Costa Rica's environmental quality: The role of renewable energy, rule of law, corruption control, and foreign direct investment in building a sustainable future” [RENE 239 (2025) 121993]
Clinkering characteristics of corn straw biochar with biomass blends
abstract: Biochar is a renewable, low-carbon fuel with high calorific value and clean combustion characteristics. This study investigates the clinkering behavior of corn straw (CS), Pinus tabulaeformis (PT), and their blends with corn straw biochar (CSB) using ICP-OES, XRD, XRF, SEM-EDS, clinkering rate determination, and ash fusibility analysis. CSB produced at 500°C undergoes deep deoxygenation and carbon enrichment, yielding higher thermal stability and calorific value than PT. Adding CSB significantly reduces CS clinkering. The CS5CSB5 blend exhibits clinkering rates of 13.57%, 26.65%, and 33.58% at 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3 m/s, shifting from strong to slight clinkering. Notably, the clinkering rate drops sharply (from 58.31% to 26.65% at 0.2 m/s) while ash fusion temperatures remain stable, indicating that the coal-derived AFT index is inadequate for biochar-blended biomass. XRD reveals that CSB promotes high-melting phases (potassium feldspar, plagioclase), suppressing the KCl-driven pathway. SEM-EDS confirms that CSB fixes potassium into aluminosilicate networks, transforming dense clinker into porous ash. For PT, which inherently has a low clinkering tendency, adding CSB caused only a minor increase in clinkering rate from 19.03% to 27.04% at 0.2 m/s due to localized particle bridging, without forming KCl. This study demonstrates that biochar blending is a viable strategy for controlling alkali-induced clinkering in high-alkali biomass. The findings can guide the development of biochar-based additives for clean combustion in industrial boilers and power systems.

title: Colloidal stability governs the photothermal performance of direct absorption solar collectors
abstract: Direct absorption solar collectors convert sunlight to heat volumetrically within a nanoparticle-laden working fluid, which avoids the surface temperature losses of conventional collectors. The performance of such collectors is commonly predicted under the assumption of a spatially uniform and time-invariant suspension. Real dispersions, however, undergo migration, aggregation, and sedimentation that continuously reshape the optical field during operation. This work develops and applies an experimentally grounded, stability-informed framework that translates measured colloidal evolution into depth-dependent optical fields and collector-scale photothermal performance. Time and height-resolved multiple light scattering data are fused with paired spectral transmittance and reflectance measurements to construct depth-dependent optical fields, which are then propagated through a Beer–Lambert radiative transfer model and a finite-volume collector energy solver. The framework is applied to a carbon nanofluid and a carbon-Fe2O3 hybrid nanofluid, each at a total particle volume fraction of 10−5 in deionized water, over the operating range from 30°C to 60°C. Accounting for the measured dispersion state reveals performance penalties that the uniform assumption cannot capture. For the unstabilized hybrid nanofluid, the solar-weighted absorbed fraction decreases by more than half, and the thermal efficiency decreases from 68% to 38%, whereas targeted surfactant stabilization restores both metrics to within 1% of the uniform baseline. The carbon nanofluid is more robust yet still degrades markedly at higher temperatures without a stabilizer. These findings identify colloidal stability as a primary determinant of practical photothermal performance and establish stability optimization as an explicit design variable for multicomponent solar nanofluids.

title: Wind-induced optical degradation in heliostats: A site-specific probabilistic assessment with joint wind–tracking sampling
abstract: Wind-induced structural deformation poses a critical threat to the optical performance and operational reliability of heliostats in tower-type Concentrating Solar Power (CSP) plants. Conventional assessments based on worst-case uniform hazard assumptions tend to overestimate operational risk and yield overly conservative designs. This study presents a probabilistic aero-structural-optical reliability and fragility framework for a representative heliostat at the Golmud CSP site. A physics-guided Kriging surrogate model is constructed using wind-tunnel-validated multi-physics simulation data. By integrating site-specific meteorological statistics with solar-tracking kinematics, this model establishes a joint spatiotemporal sampling strategy to enable efficient Monte Carlo analysis. Sensitivity analysis reveals that wind direction governs structural loading, whereas optical degradation is primarily controlled by the sun-heliostat-receiver geometric configuration rather than peak aerodynamic conditions. For a 15% concentrating efficiency loss threshold, the probability of exceeding this limit is approximately 2% under site-specific wind–tracking sampling, compared to about 7% when all wind–tracking conditions are assumed to be equally probable. Fragility analysis indicates that when the average mirror deformation reaches 15.20 mm, the probability of exceeding this threshold reaches 50%. Furthermore, concentrating efficiency losses above 15% occur predominantly when solar-noon tracking states (13:00–15:00) coincide with frontal to near-frontal winds (βw ≤ 40°); these wind–tracking conditions account for only 1.75% of annual conditions but contribute 84% of all cases exceeding the 15% loss threshold. These findings support the design of wind-adaptive stow strategies and risk-informed operational control for CSP heliostats.

title: Thermoeconomic optimization of an integrated biomass CHP system with waste heat-driven drying
abstract: Biomass-based energy systems offer significant potential for sustainable energy production and waste valorization; however, high biomass moisture content reduces conversion efficiency and limits system performance. This study proposes an integrated biomass-based combined heat and power (CHP) system consisting of a rotary dryer, downdraft gasifier, gas turbine, and organic Rankine cycle (ORC), in which waste heat from the ORC condenser is recovered for biomass drying. Four representative biomass feedstocks, namely spent mushroom substrate, Miscanthus, coffee grounds, and herbal medicine waste, were evaluated through thermodynamic, economic, and optimization analyses. The effects of dryer outlet moisture content, pressure ratio, excess air coefficient, and ORC condensation temperature were systematically investigated. Results indicate that moisture content is the dominant factor affecting syngas quality, turbine inlet temperature, power output, and economic performance. Miscanthus achieved the lowest levelized cost of electricity, LCOE, (0.0949 $/kWh), whereas coffee grounds produced the highest power output but required higher capital investment. Multi-objective optimization revealed a clear trade-off between LCOE and net present value (NPV), achieving up to 22.09% reduction in LCOE. The results demonstrate the importance of system-level integration for enhancing the thermodynamic and economic performance of high-moisture biomass utilization.

title: Sustainable tunnel cooling driven by fluctuating geothermal inflow heat: Dynamic assessment of a pressure regulated absorption refrigeration system
abstract: Hot groundwater entering deep tunnels creates a construction heat load but also supplies an intermittently available source of low temperature heat. This work examines the transient operation of a pressure regulated absorption refrigeration cycle under the variable boundaries associated with tunnel construction. The generator is maintained at an intermediate pressure and a water vapour compressor raises refrigerant to the condensation pressure, allowing the thermal and mechanical driving forces to be adjusted separately. A component based MATLAB Simulink model was formulated with fluid inventories, thermal capacitances, solution concentration states, pressure dependent flow and transient heat exchange. Step disturbances were imposed on the heat source, chilled water and cooling water circuits, followed by variation of compressor pressure ratio to determine feasible operating combinations. Pressure lift preserved refrigerant generation when thermal input weakened, but increasing compressor work and discharge temperature bounded the useful regulation range. On the experimental platform, increasing hot water inlet temperature from 45 to 65 °C lowered chilled water outlet temperature from about 18.5 to 14.5 °C and raised cooling capacity by approximately 10 kW. After the initial thermal adjustment, predicted and measured outlet temperatures generally differed by less than 10%. The results identify how the compressor pressure ratio can be adjusted in response to changes in tunnel inflow-water temperature while maintaining cooling output and limiting compressor discharge temperature.

title: Numerical modeling of aquifer-well interactions and energy performance in standing column well geothermal systems
abstract: Shallow geothermal energy represents a renewable, low-carbon resource for sustainable urban heating and cooling. Standing column wells exploit the hydraulic and thermal connection between a borehole and the surrounding formation to provide compact, high-capacity heat exchange from a single well. However, their performance is strongly controlled by subsurface hydraulic conditions and operating strategy. This study develops a coupled thermal-hydraulic numerical model of a standing column well system to investigate the subsurface effects. The model is validated against field thermal response test data and is then applied to a field case representative of the study area. A parametric analysis examines the effects of aquifer permeability, bleed ratio, well radius, reinjection temperature, and depth on thermal and hydraulic performance. The results reveal a permeability-dependent transition from conduction-supported to aquifer-supported operation. At low permeability, heat transfer is conductive unless bleed induces groundwater inflow. At high permeability, groundwater exchange increases thermal capacity and reverses the effects of well geometry. Larger wells favor conductive heat exchange, whereas smaller wells enhance aquifer inflow and thermal output. Greater depth provides modest benefits under conduction-supported conditions but substantially increases capacity under active aquifer exchange conditions. Bleed improves performance in both regimes, although the associated drawdown constrains operation. These trends persist over 120 days, with performance declines quantified. Thermal short-circuiting during upward flow through the riser reduces the temperature gain acquired in the annulus by approximately 9-13%. Therefore, standing column well design should consider aquifer-well connectivity, bleed operation, and well geometry.

title: Design and performance study of triple reflection solar concentrated photocatalytic nitrate reduction reactor
abstract: Photocatalytic technology holds great promise for nitrate reduction but is constrained by low optical efficiency and uneven light intensity distribution. This study proposes a solar-concentrated photocatalytic system with a triple-reflection structure and establishes a corresponding photothermal catalytic performance model. Optical simulations indicate that under 0°–3° incidence conditions, the relative optical efficiency is 84.05–86.04%. Outdoor optical measurements yielded a representative experimental concentration ratio of 9.04 and a normalized spatial irradiance coefficient of variation of 6.55%, confirming solar concentration and internal optical-field redistribution. Experimental results show that effective illumination, assisted by thermal input, enhances ammonia production: the reactor achieves 688.48 μg (67.50 μmol g−1 h−1) and 640.21 μg (62.77 μmol g−1 h−1) within 6 h under 0° and 3° incidence conditions, respectively. In a 10-consecutive-day stability test, the average ammonia production reached 670.01 ± 18.16 μg (65.56 ± 1.78 μmol g−1 h−1), indicating good repeatability under outdoor conditions. In addition, the photothermal catalytic model couples reaction temperature and irradiance to describe reactor performance under dynamic solar conditions. Overall, the results establish a relationship among multi-stage optical-energy transfer, spatial irradiance redistribution, and photocatalytic performance.

title: Plantwide dynamic optimization of a hybrid solar thermal power plant modeled using deep neural networks
abstract: We present a plantwide dynamic optimization framework for optimal economic operation of a multi-concentrator hybrid solar thermal power plant (HSTPP) integrating parabolic trough collectors (PTC) and a linear Fresnel reflector (LFR). The existing first-principles HSTPP model involves more than 120,000 coupled ordinary differential equations obtained after spatial discretization of distributed parameter concentrator models. While it provides detailed dynamic representation of interactions across multiple concentrators, heat-exchangers, and the power block, it remains computationally prohibitive for use in plantwide optimization. To enable tractable plantwide dynamic optimization, neural network (NN) based digital-twin framework is developed by replacing the concentrator models with data-driven surrogates. A feedforward NN predicts PTC outlet oil temperature, while a nonlinear finite impulse response long short-term memory model with moving window average captures steam drum pressure of the LFR-Steam drum (SD) subsystem. Both surrogates are trained using dynamic data from a validated first-principles simulator and achieve high predictive accuracy in infinite-step-ahead simulation, with the PTC-FFNN model giving R2:0.9964, RMSE 2.58 °C, and fit 93.96%, and the LFR-SD NFIR-LSTM model giving R2:0.9922, RMSE 1.12 bar, and fit 91.19%. The resulting gray-box HSTPP-Surrogate model reduces the standalone plantwide simulation time from 42.7 min to 1.33 min, corresponding to a 32.1 times speed-up. The surrogate-based multi-concentrator digital twin is integrated with a first-principles model of balance-of-plant components of the HSTPP to solve a market-driven revenue maximization problem using a genetic algorithm. The resulting optimal operation increases daily revenue from Rs. 26,424 to Rs. 37,199, corresponding to a 40.78% improvement over the nominal fixed-flow base operation.

title: Energy and economic performance evaluation of photovoltaic/thermal modules with serpentine and parallel flow channels: a comprehensive analysis
abstract: This study presents a comparative energy–economic assessment of water-based photovoltaic/thermal modules employing serpentine and parallel flow channels. Utilizing a bond graph methodology, a numerical model was developed to account for the thermal–hydraulic characteristics of the modules. Results demonstrate that the serpentine configuration significantly outperforms the parallel design. Under still-air conditions, the serpentine layout improves electrical, thermal, and net overall efficiencies by 2.2%, 13.7%, and 11.1%, respectively, with thermal improvements reaching 37.6% at higher wind speeds. Both configurations achieve optimal net efficiency at a water mass flux of 1000 kgs-1m-2, representing a critical balance between energy generation and pumping consumption. Economically, while photovoltaic/thermal modules generally incur higher payback periods than standalone photovoltaic module, the serpentine configuration achieves superior cost-competitiveness. At optimal flow and optimal channel row count, the serpentine system yields a levelized cost of energy up to 10% lower than a standalone photovoltaic module, whereas the parallel configuration incurs economic penalties due to elevated pumping requirements. Furthermore, implementing an intermediate pumping cut-off threshold effectively improves the economic performance in high mass flux scenarios. Overall, the proposed modeling framework offers a highly transferable approach for assessing and optimizing the energy and techno-economic performance of photovoltaic/thermal modules across varying climates.

title: Adaptive control of hybrid electrolyzer systems for coordinated frequency regulation and hydrogen production in low-inertia power networks
abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy sources has introduced considerable frequency instability in low-inertia power networks, highlighting the need for flexible and fast-acting frequency regulation solutions. This paper proposes a hybrid electrolyzer (HE) system featuring dual-mode operation for both frequency regulation (FR) and hydrogen production (HP). The system integrates a fast-response proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolyzer with a cost-effective alkaline (AL) electrolyzer, coordinated through an adaptive control strategy coupled with an electricity price-responsive mechanism. The proposed approach enhances both frequency quality and hydrogen yield while accounting for the dynamic characteristics and operational constraints of the electrolyzers. The study further examines the interaction between frequency regulation and hydrogen production, revealing that power sharing ratios and setpoint flexibility critically influence system economics, frequency reserves, and HP capacity. In addition, a hybrid optimization technique is employed to tune the proportional–integral (PI) controller gains of the DC–DC converter, ensuring stable active power control of the HE system. Simulations are conducted across three test systems to validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. Results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves frequency stability and hydrogen generation while achieving notable economic advantages over conventional single-electrolyzer-based systems.

title: From waste to wealth: Optimizing biogas plants for the energy transition
abstract: This work presents an approach for distributing support payments in volatile electricity markets. It focuses on a key regulatory issue: how incentive time windows can be designed to track market signals while limiting public costs and maintaining transparency and fairness. A generic Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) framework is proposed to determine the optimal bonus allocation timing across different support schemes, including annual, quarterly, monthly, and semi-flexible schemes. The model is based on start–stop logic, duration constraints, and rules linked to electricity market prices and incentive payments. The framework is applied to a full-year case study of the 2024 Czech electricity market, using hourly market prices data. By combining the lowest support payment (12.3 million CZK) with total annual revenues of 21.6 million CZK (evaluated ex-post), the Monthly Flexible Scheme achieves the lowest total green bonus expenditure while maintaining competitive revenues. The Quarterly Scheme yields the highest revenues (21.9 million CZK), but at the expense of higher incentive costs (12.5 million CZK). The Yearly Scheme results in the highest incentive cost (12.7 million CZK) due to its limited responsiveness to market dynamics. The results highlight the importance of temporal flexibility in the design of renewable support mechanisms in practice.

title: Inertial effects on the mechanical efficiency of a semi-passive oscillating hydrofoil energy harvester
abstract: Oscillating-foil-based energy harvesters have demonstrated strong potential for low-speed hydrokinetic energy extraction; however, the actuator-level mechanical energy balance associated with prescribed pitching motion remains poorly understood. The present work experimentally characterizes how foil mass ratio, pitching-axis location, and reduced frequency jointly govern the hydrodynamic and mechanical efficiencies of a semi-passive oscillating hydrofoil. Results show that rotational inertia redistributes actuator demand through phase-dependent torque exchange, while heave-pitch coupling can partially cancel this demand when favorably phased. Pitching-axis location modifies the phase and direction of the fluid torque through changes in the effective hydrodynamic moment arm. Reduced frequency governs the balance between enhanced unsteady loading and inertia-amplified actuator demand. Optimal performance is achieved within reduced frequency region of 0.125-0.16 using quarter-chord to one-third-chord pitching axes and relatively low foil mass ratios from about 0.5 to 2.0, yielding a peak mechanical efficiency of 33.96% -- which can diverge from the hydrodynamic efficiency by approximately 38.16% depending on configuration. Torque-loop analysis and PIV measurements show that this synchronization is a key mechanism governing the observed efficiency trends.

title: Efficient biomass pyrolysis under sub-design solar input through SiC foam integration and process parameter optimization
abstract: Solar thermochemical reactors often operate below their design power because solar irradiance varies. This study evaluates whether silicon carbide (SiC) foam can extend the effective operating window of a solar-driven packed-bed biomass pyrolysis reactor under sub-design input. A Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) framework coupled a one-dimensional shrinking-core particle model with a semi-detailed kinetic model (SDKM). The model was applied to a 5 kW prototype by varying the peak incident radiative flux densities ( I ) from 1.24 to 2.49 MW∙m −2 (40–80% of the design power), SiC foam porosity ( ϕ SiC ), and nominal residence time ( NRT ). At ϕ SiC = 0.9 and NRT = 15 s, essentially complete biomass pyrolysis was achieved at I = 1.55 MW∙m −2 , corresponding to only 50% of the design power, and the oil fraction reached 45%. Above this threshold, additional input mainly intensified PLPS decomposition and oil cracking rather than biomass conversion. Direct comparison with a bed without foam showed that SiC foam increased the conversion rate from 29% to as high as 79%. At ϕ SiC = 0.94, the axial temperature difference decreased from 1018 to 347 K, and the effective conversion rate reached 73%. Increasing NRT from 15 to 120 s increased oil-to-gas conversion by 150% with little change in bed temperature. These results quantify the extension of the reactor operating window enabled by SiC foam and clarify the distinct effects of radiative input and NRT on product distribution.

title: Integrating Gaussian splatting and machine learning for solar analysis in sustainable buildings
abstract: This study presents a geometry-aware framework for residential solar energy estimation that integrates unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based photogrammetry, three-dimensional Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), physics-based energy modeling, and multimodal machine learning (ML) for active and passive solar prediction. Building geometries are reconstructed from low-cost UAV video using segment anything model 3 (SAM 3) segmentation, structure-from-motion, and dense reconstruction, with 3DGS generating scene representations that preserve roof and facade features relevant to solar analysis, converted into watertight level of detail 3 (LOD3) building envelopes with integrated fenestration and transformed into EnergyPlus-compatible energy models at five performance levels. Validation across 33 residential buildings confirms good agreement between reconstructed and ground-truth dimensions and realistic thermal energy demand trends. Solar simulations evaluate annual photovoltaic (PV) potential, sunlit area, and internal solar gains, and a multimodal graph neural network (GNN) jointly processing geometry-aware and scalar building features for rapid, simulation-free estimation, achieving testing R 2 values of 0.890, 0.753, and 0.815 for annual internal solar gain, PV generation, and total sunlit area, respectively. The results demonstrate the potential of geometry-aware scene representations and machine learning as a scalable approach for rapid solar-performance assessment.

title: Simple radial translation of sub dishes for enhanced concentration ratio and flux uniformity in multi-dish solar concentrators
abstract: Multi-dish solar concentrators (MDSCs) provide modularity, scalability, and fault tolerance, yet scaling sub-dish numbers often demands excessive adjustment degrees of freedom, hindering deployment. This study develops a low-degree-of-freedom optimization approach that combines axially fixed sub-dishes with radial translation to enhance MDSC optical performance, achieving high concentration ratios while preserving focal spot uniformity and minimizing adjustment complexity for practical applications. A 1200 mm effective aperture prototype comprising twelve 250 mm sub-dishes was designed and optimized using the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II), evaluating over 500,000 configurations with integrated optical error models for alignment and surface imperfections. Four coupled metrics—concentration ratio, spot uniformity, shape factor, and RMS radius—were simultaneously refined, yielding coordinated gains: uniformity of 0.53, RMS radius of 38 mm, and robustness to ±10 mm receiver shifts. Outdoor testing under 620 W/m2 irradiance and 35 °C yielded an infrared-camera-estimated peak receiver-surface temperature of 1042 °C within 4 s, a measured concentration ratio of 692. The observed focal-spot distribution was qualitatively consistent with the ray-tracing prediction and supports the short-duration focusing feasibility of the prototype. The results indicate that the proposed ring-level radial layout can improve focal-spot compactness and uniformity while maintaining a simplified adjustment strategy for modular multi-dish concentrator systems.

title: A dimensionless framework for predicting thermal recovery efficiency in HT-ATES under coupled buoyancy and ambient groundwater flow
abstract: High-temperature aquifer thermal energy storage is a promising technology for large-scale seasonal heat storage. Under realistic hydrogeological conditions, thermal recovery efficiency can be reduced by irreversible heat losses caused by buoyancy-driven vertical uplift, groundwater-induced lateral drift, and injection-induced forced convection. Existing evaluation frameworks are often developed for axisymmetric systems without ambient groundwater flow, and therefore do not fully capture the competition among buoyancy, groundwater flow, and cyclic injection and extraction. To address this gap, this study extends the conventional Rayleigh- and Peclet-number-based interpretation by introducing a two-index dimensionless competition framework, expressed by Π1 and Π2. Π1 describes buoyancy-driven vertical uplift relative to groundwater-induced lateral drift, whereas Π2 describes groundwater-induced lateral drift relative to injection-induced forced convection. A three-dimensional thermo-hydraulic model coupling buoyancy effects and groundwater flow was developed to simulate cyclic hot-water injection and extraction. The results show that ambient groundwater flow produces asymmetric plume morphology and directionally biased heat transport. Four transport regimes are identified in the Π1-Π2 space: injection-dominated, drift-dominated, buoyancy-dominated, and mixed transition regimes. Groundwater-induced lateral drift is the primary control on irreversible heat loss, whereas buoyancy-driven vertical uplift mainly reduces thermal recovery efficiency through vertical plume segregation and thermal stratification. Aspect ratio, cycle number, and confining-layer thermal diffusivity further modulate recovery behavior, while conductive heat loss plays a secondary role. Finally, Latin Hypercube Sampling and Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator regression are combined to develop a mechanism-informed surrogate model for rapid prediction of thermal recovery efficiency, supporting site screening, operation optimization, and risk management.

title: Reversible actuation of artificial muscle proppants for self-regulating fracture flow and long-term geothermal sustainability
abstract: Thermal short-circuiting represents a critical bottleneck in Enhanced Geothermal Systems, severely limiting energy extraction efficiency and economic feasibility by causing premature thermal breakthrough. To overcome this systemic inefficiency, this study proposes a smart temperature-responsive hydraulic conductivity controller proppant designed for autonomous, macroscopic fracture flow regulation.
