This composite encapsulates a prestretched Nylon artificial muscle within a chemically cross-linked fluoroelastomer matrix, engineered to exploit a reversible two-way shape-memory effect: contracting at 200 °C to maximize heat extraction and expanding at 20 °C to restrict flow in thermally depleted zones. Hydrothermal aging tests confirmed superior hydrothermal stability, exhibiting no structural or chemical degradation after twelve weeks of immersion in 200 °C water. Standardized API hydraulic conductivity tests on a 25 wt% polymer-sand composite demonstrated a 116.4% permeability enhancement as temperature rose from 20 °C to 150 °C, culminating in a peak of 362.45 D. Furthermore, the composite exhibits rapid expansion kinetics upon cooling, enabling immediate flow restriction to prevent thermal energy loss. A fully coupled 3D thermal–hydraulic–wellbore simulation, parameterized using the experimentally measured temperature-dependent permeability response and validated against analytical and field-scale temperature data, predicted that the TR-HCC proppants sustained production-fluid temperatures up to 26 K higher than conventional proppants and increased cumulative heat extraction by 40.58% over 50 years under the modeled conditions. These results provide a laboratory-supported basis for passive, temperature-responsive fracture-flow regulation and demonstrate its potential to mitigate thermal short-circuiting and improve long-term heat recovery in enhanced geothermal systems.

title: Ultra-short-term solar irradiance forecasting for missing data: A multi-modal fusion-based incomplete multi-view clustering method
abstract: Ultra-short-term solar irradiance forecasting is crucial for photovoltaic integration, yet missing multimodal observations from sensor or communication failures severely disrupt prediction reliability. To address this problem, this paper proposes an adaptive weighted incomplete multi-view clustering-guided forecasting framework. Treating meteorological time series and sky images as complementary views, a selective encoding strategy is designed to extract reliable features from available data. Missing features are reconstructed by integrating cross-view predictions and long short-term memory based autoregressive estimates. Furthermore, a ScoreNet module assigns sample-aware confidence weights to enhance imputation robustness under diverse missing patterns. Using these completed representations, multi-level contrastive learning and clustering refinement align cross-view semantics to extract discriminative weather-regime features. Eventually, weather-cluster-specific multimodal sub-models execute targeted forecasting. Extensive experiments on public and real-world datasets from Shandong, China, illustrate that our method consistently outperforms traditional imputation and state-of-the-art clustering baselines under 10%–30% missing rates, exhibiting exceptional robustness against severe data incompleteness.

title: Optimal design and multi-objective optimization of a biomass gasifier–PV–battery hybrid microgrid for rural electrification
abstract: Reliable and affordable electricity remains a major challenge for rural communities in developing countries despite abundant renewable energy resources. This study develops a physics-based thermodynamic-equilibrium hybrid photovoltaic (PV)–battery–biomass gasifier–engine microgrid for sustainable rural electrification in Makurdi, Nigeria, using locally available agricultural residues. The framework integrates biomass gasification modelling, dynamic energy management, exergy analysis, techno-economic assessment, Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis, and NSGA-II-based multi-objective optimization. Six competing objectives were optimized: net present cost, cost of energy, fossil carbon dioxide emissions, renewable fraction, diesel substitution ratio, and exergy efficiency. Groundnut husk was identified as the most suitable biomass feedstock. The selected configuration comprised a 15 kW PV array, a 20 kWh battery bank, a 15 kW biomass gasifier–dual-fuel engine, and a 10 kW diesel backup generator. The optimized system achieved a net present cost of USD 102,303, a cost of energy of USD 0.1347 kWh−1, a renewable fraction of 97.18%, a bounded diesel substitution ratio of 95.0%, and fossil CO2 emissions of 1715.2 kg yr−1 while maintaining 100% electricity supply availability. The gasification model predicted an equivalence ratio of 0.29, a cold gas efficiency of 76.4%, and a producer gas lower heating value of 5.82 MJ Nm−3. Because tar formation, incomplete carbon conversion, and reactor transport losses are not explicitly represented, these equilibrium-model predictions are interpreted as theoretical upper-bound design targets requiring pilot-scale verification. Monte Carlo analysis confirmed robust performance under resource, fuel-price, and battery-lifetime uncertainty. The proposed framework provides a transferable methodology for designing resilient, low-carbon hybrid microgrids for developing regions.

title: Dynamic wind turbine wake estimation based on non-intrusive reduced order modeling
abstract: Accurate modeling of dynamic wind turbine wakes is essential for wind turbine structural analysis and wind farm power optimization. To predict dynamic wakes under different inflow conditions and wind turbine layouts, this paper proposes a dynamic wake estimation framework based on non-intrusive reduced order modeling that integrates a two-step proper orthogonal decomposition, a modified feedforward neural network, and a Transformer network. Specifically, the two-step proper orthogonal decomposition is applied to separately compress the temporal and parametric subspaces of a single wind turbine wake, extracting low-dimensional modes and corresponding projection coefficients. By incorporating attention mechanisms and residual blocks, a modified feedforward neural network is proposed to predict the projection coefficients for reconstructing the high-fidelity single wind turbine wake. In addition, to enable multiple wind turbine wake estimation, the Transformer network establishes a mapping from the projection coefficients of a single wind turbine wake to those of multiple wind turbine wakes, effectively and accurately modeling wake superposition. The proposed framework is evaluated for cases of the single wind turbine and multiple wind turbines under different wind speeds, yaw angles, and aligned layouts. Results show that the proposed method reduces the root mean square error by approximately 3% relative to the compared methods. For the reported 3×3 case, The LES farm-averaged power ranges from 2554.7 to 2650.7 kW, while the DWTWE range from 2367.0 to 2818.0 kW. Hence, the proposed method provides dynamic wake estimation for the single wind turbine and multiple wind turbines. The computational efficiency of the framework may support future studies on dynamic wake control after further validation.

title: Anode pressure regulation for proton exchange membrane fuel cell based on improved active disturbance rejection control
abstract: Proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) are crucial for harnessing green hydrogen, a cornerstone of renewable energy storage, but their reliability is compromised by anode pressure fluctuations during discontinuous purge operations. To address this issue, this article develops an improved active disturbance rejection control (IADRC) strategy for anode pressure regulation. A control-oriented lumped model (CLM) and an extended state observer (ESO) are developed to simplify the hydrogen supply dynamics and estimate the total disturbance. The IADRC then combines a boundary layer function with a fuzzy adaptor to compensate for purge-induced observation errors, while Lyapunov analysis establishes exponential convergence of the tracking error to a bounded neighborhood of the origin. Hardware-in-the-loop (HiL) and test bench experiments, as well as simulations validate the effectiveness and real-time capability of our approach. The results demonstrate that the proposed IADRC reduced the peak-to-peak transmembrane pressure difference by 67.9% and 88.5% and shortened the recovery time by 22.2% and 46.1% relative to regular ADRC and FFPI, respectively. The improved pressure stability supports more reliable and efficient PEMFC operation in renewable energy systems using green hydrogen.

title: Mechanisms of pressure pulsation and axial force in high-head pumped-storage units under extreme pumping conditions
abstract: Extreme pumping conditions in high-head pumped-storage units can intensify hydraulic instability and affect energy-conversion stability. A validated full-passage unsteady numerical model was established for a prototype high-head pump-turbine under low-, intermediate-, and high-head pumping conditions, including the main flow passage and crown and band clearance cavities. Pressure pulsation, vortex evolution, axial hydraulic thrust, and shaft-power fluctuation were investigated. Increasing pumping head strengthens leakage jets, rotating-wall shear, and unsteady interactions between the main passage and clearance cavities. The vaneless space is identified as a major region of pressure-pulsation amplification. Correlation with normalized input power shows that local pressure pulsation varies non-monotonically with energy input. As the normalized input power increases from 0.91 to 1.00 and then to 1.06, the Cp,RMS values at all runner monitoring points first increase and then decrease, with RN4 reaching a maximum of 2.8035% at the intermediate-head condition. The axial hydraulic thrust is mainly governed by the pressure difference acting on the large annular load-bearing surfaces. Although the strongest local pressure pulsation occurs at the intermediate-head condition, the shaft-power fluctuation coefficient increases from 0.096% under Pcase1 to 0.992% under Pcase3 , demonstrating that local pressure pulsation and overall power fluctuation are not completely synchronous. The maximum-head condition therefore represents the most unfavorable case for energy-conversion stability.

title: A spectral-shifting radiative cooling film for improving photosynthesis, water use efficiency, and energy savings in greenhouses
abstract: Greenhouse cultivation is essential for addressing global food security by enabling year-round, climate-controlled agriculture. However, sustainable production in greenhouses is often challenged by the need to maintain optimal growing conditions in hot climates, which require simultaneous spectral optimization for photosynthesis, passive cooling, and water conservation. In this study, we introduce a spectral-shifting radiative cooling film for effective microclimate regulation in greenhouses. The film features a multi-layer structure: the top layer dissipating heat via broadband mid-infrared (2.5–20 μm) emission, while the middle and bottom layers reduce solar heat gain by reflecting near-infrared (0.7–2.5 μm) radiation and selectively converting low-efficiency green light (0.5–0.6 μm) into highly photosynthetically active red light (0.6–0.7 μm). Under peak solar irradiation (885 W m−2), the film reduces greenhouse temperature by 9 °C and water evaporation by 13%. Remarkably, experimental results demonstrate that lettuce (Lactuca sativa L. cv. 'Tiberius') production increases by 41%–150% across three independent replicates, attributed to the optimized light spectra, temperature regulation, and improved water retention. An energy-saving model indicates a 23% reduction in cooling energy demand compared to conventional glass. This integrated microclimate-regulating strategy offers a sustainable, energy-efficient approach to augmenting greenhouse productivity.

title: Experimental and numerical investigations on heat transfer characteristics of thermal energy storage systems with discontinuous fins: Effect of inclination angle
abstract: To address the slow thermal response and uneven temperature distribution caused by the low thermal conductivity of phase change materials, this study experimentally compares the heat storage and release performance of novel discontinuous fins versus conventional straight fins under inclined conditions. Furthermore, it systematically investigates the influence of four inclination angles (45°, 60°, 75°, and 90°) on the melting and solidification processes of the discontinuous-fin configuration. The results show that at an inclination angle of 60°, the discontinuous fins, which enhance natural convection through their contraction-expansion regions, reduce the temperature uniformity coefficient (σ) by 38.5% during melting and by 40.45% during solidification, compared to straight fins. The inclination angle exerts distinct regulatory effects on melting and solidification. For the melting process, dominated by natural convection, the inclination angle plays a significant role: the vertical (90°) case yields the shortest melting time, which is 36.6% shorter than that at 45°; the 60° case achieves the highest temperature response coefficient, while the 45° case offers the best temperature uniformity. For the solidification process, governed primarily by heat conduction, the effect of inclination angle is weaker: the 45° case gives the shortest solidification time, 15% shorter than that at 90°, while the improvement in temperature uniformity is only 3.1%. These findings elucidate the coupled heat transfer mechanism between discontinuous fins and inclination angle, providing a theoretical basis for the design of latent heat thermal energy storage systems under variable operating conditions.

title: Metal-free catalytic hydropyrolysis of cellulose-rich waste to jet-fuel aromatics via zeolite-enabled hydrogen activation and deep deoxygenation
abstract: Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) requires aromatic hydrocarbons for maintaining jet fuel compatibility and performance; however, current aromatics are primarily fossil-derived, necessitating renewable routes from biomass. Herein, we demonstrate an integrated, metal-free catalytic hydropyrolysis approach to convert cellulose-derived waste directly into SAF-relevant aromatic hydrocarbons using ZSM-5 zeolites. Under a pressurized hydrogen atmosphere (0.4 MPa), cellulose predominantly yields stable ketone-rich oxygenates. Introducing ZSM-5 dramatically transforms these intermediates, with aromatic hydrocarbons accounting for approximately 98% of the total GC-MS peak area of the detected volatile organic products. The major aromatic products were further quantified using compound-specific external calibration with authentic standards. Comprehensive studies reveal that ZSM-5 with a low SiO2/Al2O3 ratio (27) exhibits superior catalytic performance, completely deoxygenating oxygenates through Brønsted-acid-mediated hydrogen activation without metal assistance. Increasing the catalyst-to-feedstock ratio significantly enhances aromatic yields, facilitating polycyclic aromatic formation via intensified secondary condensation reactions. Furthermore, extending the optimized conditions to diverse real-world feedstocks—including pinewood and textile wastes—validates the process robustness, consistently achieving high aromatic selectivity (>90%). This work provides new perspectives on metal-free hydrogen activation by zeolite acidity, paving a promising pathway for converting cellulose-rich wastes into SAF-precursor aromatic hydrocarbons.

title: Synergistic depth-insulation optimization for solar buried pipeline in permafrost via thermal-hydraulic coupled modeling
abstract: The Qinghai-Xizang Plateau contains extensive permafrost faced dual challenges from infrastructure instability caused by permafrost degradation and the increasing demand for renewable energy. A critical issue was the thermal disturbance of permafrost caused by heat dissipation from buried pipeline in solar district heating system. To fill the research gap in coordinated optimization of pipeline depth and insulation, this study developed a thermal-hydraulic coupled model for unsaturated permafrost around a buried pipeline. The model elucidated the thaw evolution mechanisms under pipeline-induced thermal disturbance and, through parametric scanning, quantified the interactive effects of buried depth and insulation thickness on thaw depth, heat loss, and outer wall temperature. Results indicated that the pipe crown suggested placing 0.3∼1.3 m below the upper limit of permafrost. Coordinated optimization reduced the thaw depth by approximately 0.62∼0.64 m and heat loss by 9.12∼9.19 W/m. Economic analysis recommended an optimal buried depth of 2.7∼3.3 m with corresponding insulation thicknesses of 120∼150 mm, achieving a balance between thermal performance and economic costs. A multi-constraint feasible region for depth-insulation combinations was proposed, providing a thermo-economic design framework for buried pipeline in permafrost regions.

title: Thermal energy utilization grade improvement and performance optimization of isobaric adiabatic compressed air energy storage systems
abstract: Traditional adiabatic compressed air energy storage systems face performance limitations due to the passive heat control modes and single-system topology. This paper proposes and designs an integrated isobaric adiabatic compressed air energy storage system coupled with a high-temperature pumped thermal electricity storage system, aiming to establish an active thermal control framework in terms of the multifunctional utilization of CO2 as an auxiliary fluid. Based on an integrated power generation mode that combines variable-speed turbine work with the organic Rankine cycle system, the proposed system achieves a significant improvement in the integrated system efficiency. By combining factor analysis with a comprehensive evaluation method within a multi-objective optimization framework, it also showcases the synergistic optimization. The results show that round-trip efficiency exhibits a nonlinear relationship with compression ratio of CO2 compressor, air discharge mass flow rate and storage pressure, reaching the optimal values at 3.0, 22 kg/s and 6000 kPa, respectively. Through the integrated decision-making method, the round-trip efficiency, levelized cost of electricity and annual CO2 emission reduction are 74.27%, 115.21 $/MWh and 11,754.2 t, respectively. Compared to the conventional isochoric adiabatic compressed air energy storage system, the round-trip efficiency and energy density have been enhanced by 17.11% and 312.6%, respectively. This work establishes an integrated conceptual design of thermal energy active regulation and working fluid multifunctional utilization.

title: Study on a novel parabolic trough solar receiver-reactor of a mixed filling catalyst bed for solar-driven hydrogen production
abstract: For improving hydrogen production comprehensive performance, a novel parabolic trough solar receiver-reactor of a mixed filling bed combining the particle packed catalyst bed zone and the metal foam coated catalyst bed zone is proposed. The influence mechanism of metal foam parameters, mixed filling structures and mixed filling ratios were revealed by a three-dimensional comprehensive numerical model. Results show that the novel system of optimized number of pores per inch of 40 and the porosity of 0.9132 with an outer partially high velocity channel can be recommended to effectively improve synergistic effects of multiphysical fields. The recommended optimal pressure drop, maximum temperature and carbon monoxide selectivity are respectively improved by 74.09%, 16.42 K and 16.72% averagely, while the methanol conversion rate keeps almost the same level with that of corresponding original systems. The recommended optimal methanol conversion rate and carbon monoxide selectivity are respectively improved by 1.56% and 16.43% averagely, while the pressure drop and the maximum temperature are desired nearest to that of parabolic trough solar receiver-reactors of metal foam coated catalyst beds. An optimal mixed filling ratio can be balanced between total chemical reaction performances and fluid flow characteristics. It provides a new idea for optimizing similar solar-driven reactors.

title: Synergistic energy and carbon integration in sector-coupled energy systems using carbon quota exchange and renewable-driven P2G under dominance analysis
abstract: Sector-Coupled Energy Systems (SCESs) enable the integrated operation of electricity, heating, gas, and mobility infrastructures, offering a promising pathway for enhancing renewable energy utilization, and achieving deep decarbonization across urban and regional energy networks. Interlinking these systems enables regional energy and environmental exchanges, promoting cooperative resource utilization and contributing to global decarbonization and pollution mitigation goals. This paper presents a transactive SCES architecture designed to facilitate both economic coordination and environmental collaboration across interconnected systems. Each SCES incorporates a diverse mix of technologies, including renewable energy sources, electric mobility infrastructure, demand response programs, and conventional generation assets. Beyond conventional energy exchanges, the proposed framework enables carbon quota trading, which is synergistically integrated with renewable power through power-to-methanation units, converting surplus electricity and captured carbon into synthetic gas. This mechanism enhances cross-vector coordination, strengthens system sustainability, and supports the transition toward carbon-neutral energy networks. To address the operational uncertainties of renewable generation, demand fluctuations, and market volatility, the model employs a second-order stochastic dominance optimization approach. This method enables risk-averse decision-making while maintaining economic efficiency. Simulation results reveal that the coordinated operation leads to 100% net CO2 reduction and enhances robustness with only a 19.3% increase in operational cost.

title: Climate change impacts on the hydropower potential of a small hydropower plant in Southwest China: A modeling and scenario analysis
abstract: Climate change is altering hydrological regimes and affecting hydropower generation. As a major renewable energy source, hydropower contributes substantially to global climate change mitigation and plays an important role in China's energy structure. Understanding the effects of climate change on hydropower generation is therefore essential for sustainable hydropower development and the achievement of carbon neutrality targets. However, assessing climate change impacts on hydropower, particularly for small hydropower plants, remains challenging because hydrological observations are often limited and robust models suitable for data-scarce conditions are lacking. This study proposes a parsimonious model to simulate runoff and power generation, and quantitatively assesses climate change impacts on reservoir inflow and hydropower generation using the Mabozi small hydropower plant in Southwest China as a case study. The proposed model performs well, with a Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency of 0.73 and a relative error of 2.0% for monthly discharge and a deviation of −4.8% for annual power yield estimation indicating reliable simulation performance. Under the Shared Socioeconomic Pathway (SSP 2-4.5) scenario, the ensemble median temperature and precipitation derived from 19 GCMs are projected to increase consistently over the upcoming decades. Relative to the 1961-2020 baseline, warming increases from +1.79°C in the near term (2031-2060) to +2.29°C in the far term (2061-2090), while precipitation changes from +4.4% to +5.7%. Reservoir inflow is projected to change by 1.6% [-14.3%, 17.8%] and 3.8% [-12.9%, 24.5%] in the near and far terms, respectively. Correspondingly, hydropower generation is projected to change by 1.2% [-12.4%, 15.6%] and 2.9% [-10.3%, 18.7%], respectively. These projected rises in runoff and hydropower output in Southwest China can support China's Dual Carbon strategy. To mitigate growing extreme climate risks under global warming, future research will adopt high-resolution climate-hydrology coupling and multi-objective optimization integrating flood control, ecological flow constraints and power generation to refine adaptive management for mountainous hydropower basins.

title: An equipment-specific carbon emission-based Shapley value method for cost allocation in multi-integrated energy systems
abstract: Despite the potential of enhancing renewable energy utilization via technologies, such as Power-to-Gas (P2G), Combined Cooling, Heating, and Power (CCHP), and energy storage systems, their integration have different preferences in economic viability and carbon reduction. In order to explore their synergistic benefits, this work build integrated energy systems (IESs) which share a similar structural framework consisting of distinct components that include reversible solid oxide cells (RSOCs), CCHP, and energy storage systems. It is revealed that RSOCs have the strongest cost-saving effects (153.5 € reductions) while energy storage systems have the weakest carbon reduction effects (53.67 kg CO2 absorption). The dispatched capacity of the energy storage system and the renewable energy station is discussed. RSOCs operating in SOEC mode consume more than 16% of total electricity, enhancing the use of renewable energy significantly. It has been demonstrated that cooperative configurations improve the integration of renewable energy while reducing storage requirements substantially. Moreover, we developed an improved Shapley value method that incorporates carbon emissions in order to address the challenges of cost allocation. In the range of C∈[0.02, 0.16], the optimal solution of IES1, IES2, and IES3 are selected to find the Nash equilibrium as the final allocation ratio, which is [33.2%, 30.3%, 36.5%]. This study provides a quantitative framework for allocating costs and providing concessions to low carbon energy storage systems.

title: A thermal-electric hybrid profiling float with ultra-long endurance enabled by multi-parameter optimization
abstract: Profiling float serves as an essential platform for ocean observation, yet their operational endurance is fundamentally restricted by limited battery capacity. This study develops a thermal-electric hybrid profiling float, and presents a multi-parameter optimization method to achieve ultra-long endurance. Firstly, a transient model is established to enable high-fidelity prediction of the full-profile dynamic states of thermal-electric hybrid profiling float. Secondly, a hierarchical multi-parameter optimization framework is proposed to facilitate comparative analysis and optimization of design parameters based on optimal operating parameter baselines. Thirdly, the proposed model and optimization strategy are validated via a hardware-in-the-loop experimental platform, achieving energy reductions of 41.6% and 37.3% through the optimization of operating and design parameters, respectively. Finally, a prototype is developed and results demonstrate that single-profile energy consumption decreased from 30.25 kJ to 6.35 kJ, with theoretical endurance exceeding 839 profiling cycles, substantially surpassing the operational endurance of existing electric profiling floats. This study contributes to sustainable ocean observation by offering a renewable thermal energy replenishment pathway. The modeling and optimization methodology offers a scalable design paradigm for underwater vehicles to enhance the efficiency of ocean observation.

title: Recovery-aware PEMFC prognostics for reliable electricity generation in renewable hydrogen systems: a multi-scale hybrid framework
abstract: Renewable hydrogen systems convert variable wind and solar electricity into stored hydrogen and later reconvert that hydrogen into dispatchable electricity through proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs). The reliability of this electricity-generation stage is limited by irreversible aging and reversible voltage recovery during frequent start-stop and dynamic-load operation, which can bias health assessment and maintenance decisions. This paper therefore proposes a multi-scale hybrid prognostic framework that integrates physical degradation mechanisms with data-driven optimization. An Aging-Recovery Voltage Model (ARVM) combines a physics-based aging model with a multivariate grey recovery model to capture start-stop-induced voltage surges. The ARVM is fused with a Gaussian-transformed Multivariate Grey Model (MGM) through Recursive Least Squares (RLS), enabling online optimization of model parameters and fusion weights. Validation on 50 W single-cell and 300 W stack datasets yields MSE values of 0.0002 and 0.0003 V2, MAE values of 0.0008 and 0.0002 V, and R2 values of 0.9999 and 0.9999, respectively. Because current is measured at each operating point, the voltage forecast maps directly to generated electrical power through P=IV. The framework thus supplies recovery-aware health information for reliable operation and maintenance of the PEMFC electricity-generation stage in renewable hydrogen systems.

title: Signature of water evaporation in gas diffusion layer with varied perforation diameter and hydrophobicity in polymer electrolyte membrane fuel cells: a lattice Boltzmann study
abstract: This study utilizes the lattice Boltzmann method to analyze gas-water drainage patterns and evaporation processes in gas diffusion layer (GDLs) with different perforation diameters (dp) and wetting properties. Results demonstrate that drainage efficiency significantly improves with higher hydrophobicity and larger perforations, as hydrophobic fibers effectively direct water toward larger pores, forming efficient drainage pathways. In contrast, GDLs with smaller dp or no perforations exhibit more uniform but less effective drainage. Evaporation initiates preferentially at perforations or larger pores. Strong through-plane mass transfer is induced when dp ≥ 54.4 μm, whereas smaller dp promotes smoother in-plane evaporation fronts. Increased perforation size and hydrophobicity enhance water discharge and evaporation rates, supported by elevated effective diffusivity and reduced tortuosity. Capillary flows from non-perforated to perforated regions further intensify evaporation. During purging, three evaporation stages are identified: saturation evaporation regime (SER), constant rate period (CRP), and falling rate period (FRP). Water saturation decreases as the process transitions from SER to CRP and finally FRP, where evaporation rates drop sharply due to water fragmentation into isolated droplets. Larger perforations delay FRP onset by maintaining capillary flow—crucial for effective water removal after shutdown. These insights inform the design of high-performance GDLs to enhance fuel cell performance.

title: A methodology for selecting phase transition models in solid/liquid phase change materials
abstract: Phase change materials play a critical role in latent heat thermal energy storage and thermal management systems due to their ability to absorb and release large amounts of heat during quasi-isothermal phase transitions. Accurate modelling of their thermophysical properties is essential for the optimal design and performance assessment of such systems. This study presents a systematic methodology for identifying the most reliable mathematical model to describe phase transition in a given material. First, a comprehensive review of modelling approaches was conducted. In addition, a classification of the existing models is proposed based on their underlying mathematical characteristics. Then, a benchmarking process is presented, which comprises three steps, a visual comparison of the experimental data and model outputs, numerical performance evaluation through the normalised root-mean-square error, and statistical assessment via the Taylor diagram. The performance of these models was evaluated by comparing their numerical estimations of enthalpy and apparent heat capacity against experimental data obtained for sodium nitrate. The selection of this particular PCM was associated with the ongoing research of the authors on high-temperature PCM-based TES systems. Experimental data were acquired using a differential scanning calorimeter within the temperature range of 285-330 °C, with a heating rate of 1 K/min, and employing isothermal periods of 10 minutes. The results revealed significant differences in model accuracy, offering valuable insights for selecting appropriate models for specific material. Utilising the concept of normalised root mean squared error, the Gumbel model demonstrated superior adjustment for apparent heat capacity, whereas the triangular model exhibited a more accurate fit for the enthalpy function of sodium nitrate, with errors of 26% and 17%, respectively. Based on the Taylor diagram, the Gumbel model was selected to represent the phase transition of sodium nitrate due to its high accuracy, evidenced by an error margin of less than 25%, and its strong correlation coefficient exceeding 0.95. This study not only enhances the understanding of modelling thermal properties in phase transition but also guides future research and development in this field. The proposed selection procedure can be effectively replicated to model the phase transition of various phase change materials commonly utilised in industrial applications, because its fundamentals are based on the mathematical principles of phase transition. Consequently, it can be applied to other materials, regardless of their melting temperature.

title: Parameter matching and operational optimization of solar-assisted ground-source heat pump systems in hot-summer/cold-winter regions
abstract: This study develops an integrated optimization framework for a solar-assisted ground-source heat pump system in hot-summer and cold-winter regions to increase renewable energy utilization while maintaining long-term ground thermal balance. The framework combines a coupled dynamic model, multi-objective optimization, and decision-making to assess annual system performance, cost, and carbon emissions. Relative to the initial design, optimization increased the annual system seasonal performance factor by 23.6%, while reducing annual cost by 17.7% and carbon emissions by 34.5%. The selected configuration comprised a solar collector area of 2970.74 square meters, a thermal storage tank volume of 148.61 cubic meters, 280 boreholes with a depth of 94 m, and rated cooling and heating capacities of 0.750 and 0.363 MW, respectively. Optimization also produced a more uniform source-side soil temperature distribution, increased the frequency of soil temperatures between 12 and 18 degrees Celsius, and reduced extreme values. These changes indicate improved seasonal ground thermal regeneration and a closer approach to long-term ground thermal balance. By integrating dynamic modeling, parameter matching, operational optimization, and decision-making, the proposed framework provides engineering guidance for designing solar-assisted ground-source heat pump systems under strongly seasonal heating and cooling demands.

title: Effects of oxidative torrefaction on the fuel properties, grindability, and pelletization of rice straw
abstract: Torrefaction of rice straw produces a high-energy-density, uniform-quality solid fuel for combustion and co-firing. This research investigates rice straw torrefaction in an oxidative medium at temperatures of 220, 250, 270, and 300 °C for 30-35 min in a continuous moving bed reactor. The grindability and pelletability of torrefied rice straw are carefully examined. At 220 °C, mass yield and energy yield are 81% and 92.5%, respectively; at 300 °C, they are 53% and 73%. From 220 to 300 °C, Index of torrefaction (Itorr), total carbon content, and fixed carbon rose by 38%, 8%, and 49%, respectively. Higher heating value (HHV) of torrefied rice straw rises from 16.73 to 20.32 MJ/kg, and loose bulk density increases from 0.093 to 0.148 g/cm3 at 220-300 °C. The Hardgrove Grindability Index (HGI) of torrefied biomass increases with temperature as power consumption decreases. The energy requirement for grinding followed the temperature trend: raw > 220 > 250 > 270 > 300 °C, and the reverse of this trend is followed for pelletization. The pellet's durability, bulk density, and hydrophobicity increased with torrefaction temperature, reaching up to 95%, 561.53 kg/m3, and 93.93%, respectively, at 300 °C. The results indicate that torrefied rice straw at 300 °C is a viable solid biofuel.

title: Fluid flow, temperature, and cell voltage non-uniformity in high-power PEMFC stacks induced by scaling-up: Development of a high-precision model and a case study
abstract: The integration of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) with renewable energy systems has emerged as a core solution to address the challenges of energy supply intermittency in the transition to low-carbon energy. As PEMFCs are evolving toward higher current density and power output, the non-uniformity induced by stack scaling-up has emerged as a critical factor impeding the further advancement of PEMFCs. In this study, a comprehensive model integrating the flow network, voltage, and thermal network models is developed for high-power PEMFC stacks. The model is validated against the experimental data from a commercial stack consisting of 260 single cells, with stack voltage and temperature errors of 4.0% and 1.96%, respectively. Moreover, the simulated cell voltage distribution shows a high degree of consistency with the experimental results, confirming the model's high precision. A case study based on this model is performed on a high-power PEMFC stack to investigate the impacts of current density and cell number on the fluid flow characteristics, temperature consistency, and cell voltage uniformity. The results are conducive to further improving the current density and stack power of commercial PEMFC stacks, and also facilitate the rapid determination of the maximum cell number in a stack.

title: Optimal co-design of Electricity-Water remote microgrid: A MILP framework to integrate sizing, energy management and seasonal dynamics
abstract: The growing interdependence between Electricity and Water needs necessitates integrated resource management, especially for remote microgrids in isolated areas. Conventional optimization studies frequently rely on models with daily-cycle storage, failing to rigorously account for the inter-seasonal dynamics. This deficiency renders unsubstantiated the common claim of 100% electric and water demand satisfaction. The main objective of this study is to propose a Mixed-Integer Linear Programming optimization framework to co-design both sizing and operational scheduling of a remote Photovoltaic-Pumped Storage Hydropower microgrid, employing a single reversible Pump-as-Turbine unit instead of separate pump and turbine machines. A key methodological contribution lies in the explicit enforcement of a 100% simultaneous satisfaction constraint for both water and electricity demands over the system lifecycle. A techno-economic objective function is formulated to minimize the Net Present Cost of the microgrid. The results reveal that inter-seasonal autonomy requires long-duration PSH storage capacity, significantly exceeding sizing based on daily-cycle assumptions. The optimization yields a range of Levelized Cost of Energy from 0.11 €/kWh to 0.83 €/kWh and a Levelized Cost of Water ranging from 0.03 €/m3 to 0.23 €/m3 directly sensitive to the reservoir construction cost (ranging from 10 €/m3 to 300 €/m3) while eliminating 33 tons of CO2 equivalent emissions. Notably, the optimal system configuration remains structurally locked across this thirty-fold cost increase, this zero-elasticity indicates that the design space is entirely governed by the Electricity-Water demands rather than marginal economic optimization. This study provides an innovative optimal co-design framework for policy makers and planners to investments risks in fully autonomous, renewable microgrids.

title: The bifacial gain gap: Nominal and regulatory vs. effective performance across five utility-scale PV sites
abstract: This study evaluates effective bifaciality and bifacial power gain in utility-scale bifacial photovoltaic systems. The analysis uses two years of 15-min data from a 50 MWp single-axis-tracker plant in Spain and results are validated against four additional plants covering three mounting configurations, two countries, and contrasting climates. For the reference plant in Spain, the time-weighted bifacial power gain, compared to the temperature and irradiance corrected front-side nominal power, is 0.495, with a 90th percentile of 0.804. Effective bifaciality averages 0.610 when time-weighted and 0.599 when irradiance-weighted, 13–15% below the nominal value of 0.70, with the largest deviations under irradiance conditions dominating energy production. Across the five plants, irradiance-weighted effective bifaciality ranges from 0.464 to 0.722, equivalent to 66–103% of 0.70 nominal value depending on site specific conditions, while median bifacial power gain ranges from 0.229 to 0.535. Rear-side irradiance increases direct-current string current by up to 110%, reduces string voltage by 8–9% and raises module temperature by up to 3.5°C. A seasonal anti-correlation between bifacial power gain and effective bifaciality is also identified. The 1.15 factor established by Spanish Royal Decree 997/2025, is evaluated as an administrative capacity conversion factor rather than an expected operational performance gain. The common irradiance-dependent effective-bifaciality and bifacial power gain response observed across all sites supports their use as transferable performance indicators, while the measured electrical and thermal effects demonstrate the relevance of field-derived bifacial metrics for yield modelling, direct-current design, and performance assessment.

title: Enhanced photothermal CO2 reforming with ethanol over oxygen vacancy-rich Cu/ZnO@CeO2 nanorod catalyst
abstract: CO2 reforming with ethanol represents a promising strategy for greenhouse gas elimination and value-added syngas production. In this work, Cu/ZnO nanorod decorated with CeO2 (Cu/ZnO@CeO2) was synthesized via a hydrothermal method for photothermal ethanol dry reforming. Systematical characterization results revealed that CeO2 promoter could strengthen metal-support interaction in Cu/ZnO@CeO2 catalyst. Furthermore, CeO2 decoration enhanced the generation of oxygen vacancies, thereby fostering CO2 adsorption/activation and enlarged light utilization efficiency, as well as facilitating the separation of photoinduced charge carriers. Consequently, the oxygen vacancy-rich Cu/ZnO@CeO2 catalyst presented excellent photothermal performance with 90.3% ethanol conversion and stable operation over 45 h at 450 °C. DFT calculations depicted strong adsorption energies of C2H5OH on Cu/ZnO@CeO2 (−1.69 eV) compared to Cu/ZnO (−0.84 eV) and the similar trend for CO2 adsorption. Under light irradiation, ethanol conversion remarkably increased from 71% to 90.3%, while by-product formation was significantly suppressed, as photogenerated electron-hole pairs also participated in the redox cycle. This study certifies CeO2 as an attractive promoter in photothermal dry reforming and offers insights in developing high-efficient catalysts for CO2 conversion.

title: Dual mesoporous Janus nano-snowmen for spatially resolved interfacial biocatalysis: Breaking the stability-activity trade-off in biodiesel production
abstract: Enzymatic biodiesel production represents a sustainable approach for renewable energy generation, yet its industrial implementation is often hampered by the inherent trade-off between enzyme inactivation at the oil-water interface and severe mass transfer limitations in conventional immobilized systems. To tackle these issues, we report a robust, magnetically recyclable Pickering interfacial biocatalytic (PIB) system based on Janus interfacial engineering. Snowman-shaped Janus nanoparticles (Janus MSN&mPDA) were designed with distinct twin mesoporous compartments (6.7 nm and 10.5 nm) for stable lipase immobilization and an embedded Fe3O4 core for magnetic responsiveness. The intrinsic Janus character endows the particles with controllable amphiphilicity, driving the particles to autonomously position and stabilize at the oil-water interface as Pickering emulsifiers. By regulating surface wettability, a unique parallel configuration was achieved, which greatly enlarges the interfacial area and improves mass transfer efficiency, thus alleviating the activity-stability trade-off. Without additional external solvents transesterification, the resulting magnetic biocatalytic system achieves a nearly complete conversion of 96.9% within 6 h, exhibiting a high catalytic efficiency (9.1 mmol h−1 g−1) that is 1.7 times higher than that of free enzymes. Moreover, the system demonstrates excellent durability, retaining over 90% activity after 10 cycles, facilitated by rapid magnetic separation. Molecular docking further revealed that the multiple synergistic interactions between the lipase active centers and substrate molecules. This work enables the efficient valorization of high-acid-value rice bran oil and provides a promising strategy for constructing high-performance interfacial biocatalytic platforms toward sustainable manufacturing.

title: From yaw to 3D wake steering: A cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning approach for wind farm power–aerodynamic-load-proxy trade-offs
abstract: Dense wind farm layouts intensify wake interactions, resulting in significant power losses and increased aerodynamic loading on downstream turbines. Conventional yaw-only wake steering controls horizontal deflection but neglects vertical wake dynamics. This work proposes a three-dimensional wake steering strategy coordinating both yaw and tilt angles to redirect wakes laterally and vertically. A customized Multi-Agent Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient framework learns cooperative yaw-tilt policies under dynamic inflow, using a reward function that balances farm power output with aerodynamic-load-proxy reduction. Using an engineering wake-model simulation across six wind scenarios, from idealized fixed conditions to variable wind speeds and directions, we compare the joint strategy with matched yaw-only and tilt-only controls. Under strongly fluctuating high-wind conditions, the representative joint-control policy yields a power gain of 3.296% and an aerodynamic-load-proxy reduction of 13.416%, compared with 2.7% and 5.0% for yaw-only control and 1.1% and 13.0% for tilt-only control. These results demonstrate the added value of cooperative horizontal–vertical wake steering over single-degree-of-freedom control under strongly fluctuating high-wind conditions, highlighting tilt-enabled wake steering as a promising direction for future power–load-aware wind-farm operation.

title: Comparison of mounting systems in utility-scale photovoltaic installations: Analysis of land occupation
abstract: Utility-scale photovoltaic installations require substantial land areas. This study investigates the land area required for utility-scale photovoltaic installations as a function of the photovoltaic module mounting system employed. The study focuses on the photovoltaic field; therefore, roads, substations, service buildings and other related infrastructure are excluded. To examine the influence of geographic location on utility-scale photovoltaic systems design and performance, 18 sites across both hemispheres were analysed. Four representative mounting configurations were evaluated: 2 V × 15 and 3 V × 10 (fixed tilt angle systems), and 1 V × 60 and 2 V × 30 (horizontal single-axis trackers). The analysis process was predicated upon four assessment indicators, namely land use intensity, power density, energy density, and ground coverage ratio. A detailed analysis leads to several conclusions. Fixed-tilt systems show strong latitude dependence due to variations in optimal tilt angle, whereas horizontal single-axis trackers are largely insensitive to latitude except at high latitudes. The 2 V × 30 configuration provides the best performance across both hemispheres based on four indicators. For fixed-tilt systems, the 3 V × 10 configuration is the best. As a general tendency, configurations with more vertically stacked modules per row tend to achieve superior performance.

title: Numerical investigation of heat extraction performance of a multi-casing coaxial well with multilateral branches for enhanced geothermal systems
abstract: A novel enhanced geothermal system is proposed using a multi-casing coaxial well with multilateral branches, where a single main wellbore with three concentric pipes separates the injection zone from two production zones. This configuration creates two independent production zones, significantly expanding the heat exchange volume and improving overall heat extraction efficiency. A three-dimensional fully coupled thermo-hydro-mechanical numerical model was established to systematically simulate the heat extraction performance of the newly proposed system and compare it with a conventional Enhanced Geothermal System using a single-casing coaxial well with multilateral branches. The results show that the cumulative power of the newly proposed system increases by approximately 14%-52% compared to the conventional one under different fracture densities over a 60-year operation period. The pressure difference between the injection well and production well decreases by 81%-94%. Parametric analysis reveals that heat extraction efficiency is further improved by controlling the fracture dimensions, selecting an appropriate number of branches, maximizing the length of the branches, and adjusting the injection rate. Furthermore, economic analysis shows that the newly proposed system can significantly reduce the levelized cost of energy compared with conventional systems. This research proposes an alternative enhanced geothermal design that significantly improves heat extraction performance.

title: A comparative study of different rotor designs for enhancing the coupled performance of semi-submersible floating vertical-axis wind turbines
abstract: Floating vertical-axis wind turbines have attracted increasing interest for deep-water offshore wind applications, but a key challenge remains before they can be deployed at utility scale – the lack of a unified design. Given the diversity of blade geometries, the selection of rotor configuration is challenging, especially because systematic full-scale models accounting for coupled aerodynamic, hydrodynamic, and mooring effects under realistic sea conditions remain scarce. To address this gap, full-scale models of two representative configurations (H-type and Φ-type) are developed with identical swept areas and key geometric parameters. A coupled aero-hydro-mooring analysis framework is established using computational fluid dynamics by integrating dynamic fluid-body interaction with a volume-of-fluid model, and is applied to compare their dynamic responses under combined wind-wave loading. Results show that the Φ-type configuration benefits from its closed blade-end connection and root-concentrated supports in the low tip-speed region, which reduce the blockage and negative torque associated with the large-span supports of the H-type configuration, increasing the power coefficient by 11.04%. Unlike the coherent blade-tip vortices of the H-type configuration, the blade-end vortices of Φ-type configuration mainly develop as circumferential shear layers along the closed boundary, promoting momentum exchange and turbulent mixing during downstream propagation. Its smaller upwind projected area also reduces platform surge drift and mooring tension under aerodynamic thrust, indicating better global dynamic stability. Frequency-domain analysis further reveals that wave excitation and drift forces dominate periodic platform motions and affect rotor aerodynamics, while blade-rotation-induced unsteady loads introduce high-frequency fluctuations in platform rotational degrees of freedom.

title: Two-stage degradation threshold-time estimation for crystalline-silicon PV modules using long-term operating data and short-term measurements
abstract: Long-term photovoltaic module degradation affects energy yield, asset value, and reliability management. System-level records provide long-term evidence of climate-dependent performance loss rates, while short-term module measurements resolve technology-specific performance and electrical-state variation. A scale-resolved hierarchical framework integrated public operating and accelerated-aging data with regional observations and paired current–voltage and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy measurements from Hainan, Hailar, and Turpan. Expected-power normalization and regional calibration established long-term distributions of performance loss rates. Accelerated aging constrained technology- and stage-dependent responses, and grouped machine learning estimated current and next-stage maximum-power retention. A continuous two-stage model separated early-stage loss from stable degradation and propagated uncertainty to threshold-crossing times through Monte Carlo simulation. Quality screening retained 33 of 51 public photovoltaic systems. Climate transfer and regional calibration yielded annual performance loss rates of 0.739% yr−1 in Hainan, 0.624% yr−1 in Hailar, and 0.655% yr−1 in Turpan. Passivated emitter and rear cell technology showed the largest early-stage loss, while regional variation in stable rates exceeded technology adjustments. Measured current–voltageretention reduced median current-state root mean square error from 0.6 to below 0.2 percentage points, with impedance spectroscopy providing modest sample-specific residual refinement. Estimated times to 90%, 85%, and 80% maximum-power retention were 12.4/19.9/27.8, 14.3/22.9/32.1, and 14.1/22.4/31.2 years, respectively. These conditional estimates support technology and region-specific risk screening. Independent long-term module validation remains necessary for service-life qualification.

title: Editorial Board
Hydrodynamics of double-impeller fermenter for bioethanol production
abstract: This study investigated the hydrodynamic performance of fermenters equipped with two different impeller designs, namely a 4-pitch blade impeller and a 6-Rushton turbine. The effects of rotational speed, impeller type, glucose-to-water ratio, and mixing duration were evaluated experimentally and through Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations. Transient CFD simulations were performed using a homogeneous Euler–Euler multiphase approach, the Volume of Fluid (VOF) method, and the Realizable k–ε turbulence model. The Multiple Reference Frame (MRF) approach was applied to represent impeller motion. Agitation speeds of 20, 40, 60, 80, and 100 rpm were tested to assess their influence on fluid flow and mass transfer within the fermenter. In addition, glucose–water mixtures with ratios of 1:4 and 2:3 were examined. Key hydrodynamic parameters, including flow velocity and concentration distribution, were analyzed in detail using CFD. The results demonstrated that the optimal mixing performance was achieved at 100 rpm with a glucose–water ratio of 1:4 using the 4-pitch blade impeller. Under these conditions, the system exhibited the most efficient power consumption, improved flow distribution, and the shortest homogenization time for the glucose–water mixture. Furthermore, the predicted mixing times showed good agreement with the transient CFD simulation results under the investigated operating conditions. The 4-pitch blade turbine impeller decreased the power number by 55% compared to a 6-Rushton turbine impeller. The optimal mixing duration for achieving maximum homogeneity occurred with a 4-pitched blade turbine impeller at 100 rpm and a glucose-water ratio of 1:4 for 340 s.

title: A physics-guided dual-channel convolutional neural network wake model for a wind turbine over a hill
abstract: Wind turbine wakes over hilly terrain are influenced by the combined effects of the turbine and the underlying terrain. Terrain-induced flow acceleration, separation, and other complex flow phenomena pose major challenges to analytical wake models. To accurately predict wake flow fields over hilly terrain, this study proposes a physics-guided dual-channel convolutional neural network wake model. The model first decomposes the target flow field into a turbine-induced velocity deficit field and a terrain-induced background flow field, then combines low-fidelity physical representation, data-driven enhancement, and fusion-based reconstruction to predict the high-fidelity wake field. A high-fidelity dataset covering different hill slopes and turbine operating conditions is constructed using a limited number of large-eddy simulations. Physics-based methods then transform the turbine operating conditions and terrain information into low-fidelity velocity deficit and background flow fields, which serve as physics-guided inputs to the network. Both fields contain representation errors arising from simplified physical assumptions, and their direct superposition cannot adequately represent the nonlinear coupling between the turbine wake and terrain-induced flow. The dual-channel convolutional neural network therefore encodes and enhances the two low-fidelity fields separately to reduce the errors associated with their respective physical approximations. The resulting features are then fused to learn the nonlinear coupling and reconstruct the high-fidelity wake field. Generalization tests show that the proposed model achieves a mean absolute percentage error of 4.98% relative to large-eddy simulation results. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining flow-field decomposition, low-fidelity physics guidance, and data-driven fusion for wind turbine wake prediction over a two-dimensional hill.

title: Thermoresponsive building envelope with optical modulation and latent heat storage: Energy savings and thermal comfort evaluation under diverse climatic conditions
abstract: Thermal comfort is essential for occupant well-being, yet maintaining it consumes a substantial portion of building energy. To address this, this study proposes and fabricates an innovative thermoresponsive building envelope integrating a thermoresponsive hydrogel (TH) layer with a phase change material (PCM) layer. The TH enables optical modulation, adjusting solar absorption and reflection with temperature to reduce solar radiation during hot seasons while capturing solar heat during cold seasons. Simultaneously, the PCM provides latent heat storage, reducing daily temperature fluctuations and maintaining nighttime indoor temperatures during cold seasons, thereby lowering heating demand and improving thermal comfort. Sensitivity analysis indicated that the optimal transition temperature of the TH layer is higher in the colder regions due to greater heating demand and lower ambient temperatures, whereas the optimal phase change temperature of the PCM layer lies below the heating setpoint to compensate for the heating reduction. Based on typical meteorological year weather data, simulations across 34 provincial-level capital cities of China demonstrated that the proposed envelope can reduce annual energy consumption by 4.0-18.2% (7.8-17.1 MJ m -2 ) and increase comfort hours by 0.2-9.7% compared to a bare envelope in residential buildings with heating and cooling setpoints of 20 °C and 26 °C, respectively, depending on the region and the optimal transition temperatures of both the TH and PCM layers. These results highlight the feasibility of passive building envelope designs as an effective energy-saving and thermal comfort strategy across different climates.

title: Combined disposal of water treatment and sewage sludge within the water municipal system
abstract: This study investigated the mesophilic anaerobic co-digestion of sewage sludge (SS) and water treatment sludge (WTS) as an integrated strategy for sludge management and renewable energy recovery in municipal water and wastewater systems. Batch respirometric tests were conducted at 35 ± 1 °C using SS–WTS mixtures prepared on the basis of volatile solids (VS), with WTS doses ranging from 0.1 to 1.0 g VS per 1.0 g VS of SS. The effect of WTS addition was evaluated through unit biogas production, specific methanogenic activity (SMA), and physicochemical characterization of both sludge types. The results showed that WTS influenced anaerobic digestion in a strongly dose-dependent manner. The highest process efficiency was obtained at 0.3 g VS WTS per 1.0 g VS SS, where biogas production increased by up to 50% and methanogenic activity by up to 35% compared with SS digestion alone. Higher WTS doses reduced fermentation efficiency, most likely due to the increasing contribution of mineral components, including aluminium- and iron-rich phases. The findings indicate that WTS should not be considered a conventional energy-rich co-substrate, but rather a mineral conditioning component that can improve anaerobic digestion only within an optimized dosage range. The proposed SS–WTS co-digestion approach may support sustainable sludge valorization, enhanced biogas recovery, and circular management of residues generated in municipal water systems.

title: A new hybrid approach for waste heat recovery in high-temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells using sweeping gas membrane distillation: Performance evaluation and optimization strategies
abstract: The integration techniques, performance characteristics, and optimization strategies of coupling high-temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells (HT-PEMFCs) with sweeping gas membrane distillation (SGMD) remain underdeveloped, hindering further advancement. Herein, based on electrochemical and thermodynamic principles, a steady-state mathematical model is developed that quantitatively accounts for the dominant irreversible losses within the system. Simulation results demonstrate that, relative to a standalone HT-PEMFC operating at 453 K, the integrated configuration delivers a 43.22% enhancement in peak power density, along with energy and exergy efficiency gains of 20.69% and 20.66%, respectively. Comprehensive parametric studies reveal the influence of critical design and operating variables—including leakage current density, doping level of phosphoric acid, operating temperature, relative humidity, and membrane thickness—offering valuable insights for performance enhancement. In addition, local sensitivity analysis highlights phosphoric acid doping as the dominant factor affecting output, whereas leakage current density shows the weakest effect. Overall, this study provides critical insights into the design, optimization, and operation strategies of HT-PEMFC/SGMD hybrid systems, significantly advancing their potential practical applications in sustainable energy conversion and freshwater generation.
keywords: High-temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cell

title: An integrated thermo-electric performance evaluation and design decision-making framework for closed-air-cavity sandwich-type wall-integrated photovoltaics
abstract: Closed-air-cavity sandwich-type wall-integrated photovoltaics (SWIPV) provide power-generation and building-envelope functions, but their complex electrical and thermal behavior challenges the simultaneous calculation and evaluation of thermo-electric performance and engineering design. By analyzing the different operating mechanisms during daytime and nighttime, this study proposes cumulative electricity generation (ESWIPV) and the period-averaged operational apparent equivalent heat-transfer coefficient (KSWIPV) to characterize thermo-electric performance, respectively, and develops a coupled calculation model. Furthermore, by incorporating the comprehensive performance index (CI) and performance balance index (BI), an integrated evaluation and design decision-making framework is established. Experiments were conducted to verify the accuracy of the model. The response regularity of thermo-electric performance and the corresponding design decisions were analyzed by constructing combined conditions involving nine representative sites in 5 Chinese climate zones, 3 facade orientations, and various air layer thicknesses. Results show that the maximum model error is below 6.0%; differences in ESWIPV among climate zones are mainly determined by facade irradiation, whereas KSWIPV is jointly affected by facade irradiation, air temperature, and seasonal distribution; nighttime Scenario 2 contributes 31.8% and 22.0% to KSWIPV in Guangzhou and Nanchang, respectively; ESWIPV and KSWIPV tend to stabilize when air layer thickness exceeds 300 mm; climate and air layer thickness are the dominant factors affecting ESWIPV and KSWIPV, respectively; under the thickness-constrained scenario, the South-200 mm scheme is recommended for 8 sites except Guiyang under all 5 weighting coefficients. The framework can be transferred to other regions by inputting candidate conditions, local meteorological data, and design preferences.

title: Coordinated operation and multi-criteria evaluation methodology for heterogeneous pumped storage clusters
abstract: Large-scale renewable-energy integration increases the need for bulk flexibility, frequency support, and long-duration storage. Pumped-storage development is therefore evolving from isolated plants toward heterogeneous cluster-oriented hydro-storage resources. However, mixed plant topologies, shared reservoirs, cascade interactions, hydro-electrical coupling, and the different support capabilities of fixed-speed and variable-speed units make simple plant-level aggregation insufficient for coordinated operation and system-level value evaluation. This paper proposes a coordinated operation model and a multi-criteria value evaluation framework for heterogeneous pumped-storage clusters in renewable-dominated power systems. A generalized reservoir-balance model with multi-source inflows is developed to represent closed-loop, open-loop, hybrid, and cascade-coupled pumped-storage plants under shared-reservoir conditions. The regulation, reserve, inertia, and primary-frequency-response capabilities of different unit types are incorporated into a frequency-security-constrained scheduling model considering source-load uncertainty. A value evaluation framework covering energy, flexibility, environmental, and economic effects is then established to quantify the system-level contribution of cluster integration. In the projected 2030 Qinghai case, the additional PS cluster increases renewable-energy accommodation from 98.16% to 100.00% and reduces operational carbon emissions from 67.88 kt to 36.16 kt while satisfying the frequency-security constraints. The system-level return on investment (ROI), defined here as the ratio of quantified benefits to equivalent cluster cost, reaches 1.1323 under the adopted economic assumptions. A constructed Southwest China test system further illustrates the adaptation of the framework to different hydropower resources and renewable generation profiles.

title: Net-Zero carbon pathway for integrated energy systems: co-optimizing biomass-coupled carbon capture and trans-seasonal thermal storage dispatch
abstract: To facilitate the low-carbon transition of energy systems and enhance renewable energy accommodation, this paper proposes a near-zero carbon scheduling framework for electricity-gas-heat integrated energy systems, which integrates full-cycle synergistic optimization of carbon source-capture-mineralization processes and trans-seasonal energy storage, addressing the dual challenges of high carbon emissions from coal-fired units and renewable energy curtailment caused by seasonal supply-demand imbalances. First, considering the zero-carbon attributes of biomass and carbon capture-mineralization technology, a coal-biomass co-firing system integrated with carbon capture-mineralization processes is established to analyze its electric-carbon coupling dynamics and emission reduction mechanisms. Second, a mine water-based trans-seasonal thermal storage system is introduced to reduce renewable energy curtailment and achieve deep decarbonization through spatiotemporal heat transfer. Finally, a co-optimization dispatch model is developed, incorporating synergistic reserves from biomass-coupled carbon capture plants and hydrogen storage systems. At the same time, energy characteristics under typical days in different seasons are analyzed. Simulation results show that the proposed model reduces system operating cost by 32.41%, decreases carbon capture energy consumption by 51.73%, and increases the unit net output by 7.78%, demonstrating its effectiveness in supporting near-zero-carbon IES operation.

title: Polyimide-based anion exchange membranes with synergistic bifunctional block phase separation for alkaline water electrolysis
abstract: Anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE) is a key technology for converting renewable electricity into green hydrogen, but its large-scale deployment remains constrained by the performance of anion exchange membranes (AEMs). Traditional AEMs suffer from an inherent trade-off between high conductivity and excessive swelling. Polyimides, which combine excellent mechanical properties, dimensional stability, and structural designability, are promising alternative AEM substrates; however, their application is limited by the susceptibility of imide rings to alkaline degradation. This study proposes a synergistic bifunctional block phase separation strategy, in which a chemically phase-separated structure comprising a trifluoromethyl-based hydrophobic block and a benzimidazole-based hydrophilic block is constructed, and the microphase-separated morphology is optimized by tuning the block ratio. This strategy suppresses imide ring hydrolysis through bifunctional synergy, while bicontinuous microphase separation creates continuous, low-resistance OH− transport channels, thereby decoupling the conductivity-swelling trade-off. The optimal QAPI-70 membrane exhibited a conductivity of 130.2 mS cm−1 and a swelling ratio of only 22.1% at 80 °C, and retained 88.7% of its initial conductivity after 1000 h in 1 M NaOH at 80 °C. MD simulations provided supporting evidence for the superior microphase-separated morphology and OH− transport properties of QAPI-70. An AEMWE single cell based on this membrane delivered 1050 mA cm−2 at 1.8 V and 60 °C with stable operation over 100 h. This work provides a new strategy for developing high-performance AEMs, advancing AEMWE toward cost-competitive renewable green hydrogen production.

title: A unified geometric design and optical evaluation of a V-shaped secondary reflector for parabolic trough collectors
abstract: Parabolic trough collectors are the most mature concentrating solar power technology, yet their optical performance is constrained by two coupled limitations: a limited geometric concentration ratio and a strongly non-uniform flux on the absorber tube. This study proposes a V-shaped secondary reflector that, by introducing a reflector-inclination angle absent in the conventional flat secondary reflector, provides an additional geometric degree of freedom for exploring the trade-off between concentration enhancement and flux homogenization. A unified geometric-design framework combining the split-source method with the boundary-ray principle is established; it classifies the absorber–reflector coupling into four geometric cases and yields closed-form solutions for the size and position of both the secondary reflector and the absorber. Two key findings emerge from the analysis. First, the effective geometric concentration ratio closely tracks the ray-traced average local concentration ratio in the examined sweeps, supporting its use for rapid pre-screening before targeted ray tracing. Second, the V-shaped configuration provides two complementary advantages over its flat counterpart: an equal or higher concentration ratio for rim angles up to 90°, with gains of up to 36% near the feasibility boundary, and continued geometric feasibility at rim angles beyond 90°, where the flat secondary-reflector configuration considered here is no longer feasible. A sensitivity analysis shows only limited degradation for equivalent per-surface slope errors up to about 2 mrad and for a secondary-reflector reflectivity as low as 0.90.

title: A WRF-LES/CFD coupled method for simulating ice accretion on a three-dimensional rotating wind turbine rotor incorporating atmospheric stability in high-altitude cold regions
abstract: High-altitude cold regions offer abundant wind energy, yet low-temperature and humid environments frequently trigger ice accretion on wind turbine blades. Meanwhile, significant diurnal temperature variations lead to drastic atmospheric stability transitions in these regions. However, existing blade ice accretion simulation studies predominantly rely on two-dimensional airfoil models with uniform inflow assumptions, neglecting the three-dimensional rotational effects of operating rotors and the non-uniform atmospheric boundary layer profiles that arise under different stability conditions. To elucidate the ice accretion characteristics of a three-dimensional rotating wind turbine rotor in high-altitude cold regions, this study proposed a cross-scale multiphysics “meteorology-flow-ice accretion” coupling framework. High-resolution atmospheric boundary layer simulations for high-altitude cold regions were conducted using the Weather Research and Forecasting Model, with atmospheric stability conditions classified based on the Monin-Obukhov length. A three-dimensional high-fidelity numerical ice accretion simulation method for the rotating wind turbine rotor was established, wherein a volumetric body-force source term was imposed to account for the rotational inertial forces acting on impacting droplets and runback water films on the rotor surface, and thermal flux correction was applied based on convective heat transfer flux under an adiabatic wall condition. Mesoscale meteorological parameters were interpolated onto the microscale computational boundaries using the inverse distance weighting method, enabling dynamic downscaling of the flow field. The proposed method was applied to compare rotor ice accretion under stable, neutral, and unstable atmospheric conditions using realistic atmospheric profiles and uniform inflow assumptions. Validation against a rotating-blade ice accretion experiment indicates that the proposed 3D RWTR CFD ice accretion simulation method achieves high prediction accuracy, with a maximum relative error of 4.85% among the evaluated ice-shape parameters. Ice accretion on the three-dimensional rotating rotor primarily occurred at the hub and along the blade leading edge. Spanwise from tip to root, both ice thickness and sectional ice shape area follow a pattern of an initial increase followed by a decrease. The stable atmospheric condition yielded the maximum ice thickness and overall sectional ice shape area, whereas the unstable condition resulted in the maximum icing limits and tip sectional ice shape area. The uniform inflow assumptions caused deviations in ice thickness, ice shape area, and relative icing limits, particularly under unstable atmospheric conditions. Further analysis indicates that the vertical temperature profile has the dominant influence on ice thickness and icing limits.

title: A soft-linking approach to couple urban microclimate analysis and renewable integration in energy district planning
abstract: ABSTRACT Rapid urbanisation and climate change are intensifying urban overheating, energy demand, and greenhouse gas emissions, highlighting the need for strategies that jointly address microclimate mitigation and energy system decarbonisation. However, passive urban design measures and active energy solutions are often assessed independently, limiting the understanding of their combined effects at the district scale. This study develops and applies a multi-scale sequential soft-linking to assess how outdoor microclimatic conditions affect building thermal demand and, subsequently, district energy system performance in urban regeneration contexts.. The approach connects ENVI-met, EnergyPlus, and EnergyPLAN, enabling the transfer of microclimatic boundary conditions into dynamic building simulations and the resulting demand profiles to district-level energy modelling. The framework supports the coordinated assessment of nature-based solutions, envelope retrofitting, and renewable-based energy systems. The methodology is applied to a Mediterranean residential district through four scenarios (reference, passive-only, active-only, and integrated) evaluated using environmental, energy, and economic indicators. Results show that passive measures reduce thermal loads and improve outdoor comfort, while active solutions enhance renewable penetration and system flexibility. The combined passive–active scenario achivesprimary energy reductions of about 60% and CO 2 emission cuts up to 75-80%, while mitigating peak summer thermal stress and supporting climate-responsive, low-carbon urban district planning.

title: A novel adaptive control strategy for hydro-turbine governing systems based on physics-informed neural networks
abstract: Hydropower units are critical regulating resources that mitigate power fluctuations induced by renewable energy grid integration and provide rapid frequency support for power systems. With limited labeled trajectories and continuously changing loads, however, fixed-parameter proportional-integral-derivative controllers struggle with the nonlinearities and coupled constraints of operation over a wide operating range. Frequent intraday load transitions can consequently degrade regulation performance or cause instability. This study integrates physics-informed state-transition prediction with composite adaptive regulation to address state evolution under exogenous loads and regulation across operating conditions. Simulations of a 100 MW Francis turbine unit show improvements in both prediction credibility and regulation performance. Compared with a same-architecture data-only network, the physics-informed neural network reduces physical residuals by 39.3%-43.1% and 300-step free-running prediction errors by 66.3%-80.5%. Compared with fixed-parameter control, the composite adaptive controller reduces maximum overshoot and the integral of absolute error by 58.4% and 86.4%, respectively. Continuous-load and disturbance tests further show adaptability to substantial operating-point changes, identifying rapid load ramp-down and high-load operation as the principal performance-sensitive stages. The framework provides a systematic approach to intelligent state awareness and adaptive control of hydropower units with limited operating data.

title: Effect of PVC-derived acid on two-stage seaweed hydrothermal liquefaction: Experiment and SHAP-enhanced modeling
abstract: Due to the high ash and protein contents, the direct hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) of seaweed has problems such as low bio-oil yield and high nitrogen content.
