In order to solve the above problems, the aqueous product from PVC dechlorination (PVC-AQ) was used in the acid-hydrothermal pretreatment (AHP) of seaweeds to reduce its ash, nitrogen, and oxygen contents. Compared with the conventional hydrothermal pretreatment, the removal efficiencies of ash, nitrogen, and oxygen increased significantly and reached 73.80 %, 32.76 % and 49.85 %, respectively, indicating that the acidic environment helps to break the cell structure of seaweeds, thereby promoting the dissolution of ash and the hydrolysis of proteins and amino acids. In the subsequent HTL, the bio-oil yield also increased by 34.71 % but the N-heterocycles content decreased by 12.58 %. This is because the AHP reduced the precursor content of Maillard reaction, which inhibits the formation of N-containing compounds in bio-oil. In addition, the machine learning and SHAP analysis also reveal that the AHP conditions play important roles in improving bio-oil yield and reducing its N/O content. These findings provide a credible basis for producing high-quality bio-oil via PVC-derived acid enhanced two-stage HTL.

title: Dark fermentation of chicken manure and citrus wastewater for renewable biohydrogen production: The role of microbial functional balance
abstract: ABSTRACT Dark fermentation of chicken manure waste and citrus wastewater was evaluated as a strategy to enhance biohydrogen production from agro-industrial residues. Eight batch assays using autochthonous and allochthonous inocula were conducted to assess hydrogen production, metabolite profiles, and microbial community dynamics under different substrate and inoculum configurations. The highest cumulative H 2 production reached 2774 mL H 2 L -1 , corresponding to 0.186 L H 2 g -1 VS added, with faster kinetics and reduced lag phases in the best-performing assays. The observed hydrogen performance was consistent with the established importance of metabolic pathway selection and electron partitioning in mixed culture dark fermentation. High performing systems were characterized by acetate–butyrate fermentation, whereas propionate and C1-related pathways were associated with reduced or delayed hydrogen production. Metagenomic analysis revealed enrichment of hydrogenogenic KEGG Orthologs associated with pyruvate oxidation and [FeFe]-hydrogenases in high-performing reactors. Enhanced hydrogen production was linked to functionally complementary microbial consortia involving hydrolytic and fermentative genera, particularly Bacteroides, Clostridium , and Caldicoprobacter . Overall, the results are consistent with previous evidence highlighting the importance of microbial functional organization and metabolic pathway distribution in determining hydrogen production from mixed agro-industrial substrates, providing mechanistic insights for the optimization of dark fermentation systems.

title: Gradient thermal expansion structured cell improves thermal cycle life and mechanical stability of solid oxide fuel cell stack
abstract: Solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) provide high-efficiency energy conversion for renewable energy applications but suffer thermal-cycling instability caused by thermal expansion mismatch, leading to delamination and fracture. In this study, three novel thermal expansion coefficient (TEC)-gradient single cells and corresponding stacks are developed by incorporating LSC0.7GDC0.3 transition layers and LSC0.9GDC0.1 composite cathodes, with composite cathodes fabricated by physically mixing La0.6Sr0.4CoO3-δ and Gd0.1Ce0.9O1.95. The gradient design smooths TEC transitions among the electrolyte, barrier, transition, and cathode layers, reducing the maximum TEC difference by 57.94%. The three-layer gradient stack (Cell-D) exhibits only 11% voltage decay after 30 cycles at 35 A, achieving an electrochemical lifetime at least ten times that of the original stack unit. After five cycles, the original cell loses 61.2% of tensile strength and fails by cathode delamination, whereas Cell-D retains 110.68 ± 9.01 MPa, 1.77 times higher. Multiphysics simulations show that cathode stress in Cell-D decreases by 60.81%, mitigating strain and structural damage. The results establish a stack-level design rule that balances cathodic activity, TEC, and high-temperature mechanical compatibility. This material-efficient and engineering-feasible strategy improves the durability and reliability of SOFC stacks for renewable-energy applications.

title: From interfacial modulation to Bi2WO6 activation: MOF-808-regulated S-scheme photocatalysis for solar hydrogen evolution
abstract: Photocatalytic H2 evolution provides a sustainable route for addressing energy shortages, but its efficiency is still limited by rapid carrier recombination and poor charge separation. In this work, a Bi2WO6/MOF-808 composite was fabricated through an in situ growth strategy to construct an S-scheme heterojunction for enhanced photocatalytic H2 evolution. Under visible light irradiation, BM-15% achieved the optimal H2 release rate of 846.27 μmol g−1·h−1, which was approximately 33.7 times that of the original Bi2WO6. The superior performance stems from the introduction of MOF-808, which increases the specific surface area, exposes more accessible active sites and simultaneously regulates the interfacial electronic structure of Bi2WO6. Experimental characterization combined with DFT calculations revealed pronounced interfacial electronic reconstruction and a built-in electric field, while EPR and fs-TA analyses further supported an S-scheme charge-transfer pathway. This interfacial regulation improves the utilization of photoexcited carriers and promotes the conversion of incident light energy into chemical energy stored in H2. The present work therefore provides an interface-engineering strategy for solar-driven renewable hydrogen production and highlights the potential of photocatalytic H2 evolution for renewable-energy conversion and storage.

title: Thermal-assisted low-energy hydrogen production through a thermoregenerative ammonia-decoupled water electrolysis system
abstract: Conventional water electrolysis faces challenges due to the tight link between the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER), including gas mixing risks and high energy use. This study introduces a new decoupled system using a thermoregenerative ammonia electrolyte. It enables separate hydrogen and oxygen production while significantly reducing energy consumption. The key approach is to replace the high-energy HER with electrochemical reduction of Cu2+, while storing protons (H+) through the OER. A major innovation is adding ammonia gas, which reacts spontaneously with the deposited copper to reduce the stored H+ and produce hydrogen. This allows "on-demand" hydrogen generation without external power. The system operates at a cell voltage about 50% lower than that of conventional water electrolysis, as low as 1.31 V. Reaction agents are recycled through low-temperature thermal breakdown of the copper-ammonia complex, achieving a specific energy consumption for hydrogen production as low as 5.02 kWh·m−3 H2, matching top-tier performance. By separating energy input from hydrogen output in time and space, this research offers a new direction for flexible and efficient hydrogen production.

title: A fast estimation method for small-signal stability region of wind farms under variable wind speed conditions
abstract: As the critical factor influencing the power output of wind farms, the wind speed is increasingly emerging as a new variable that can change the operating status of grid-connected systems. During extreme weather conditions, due to the wide-ranging variation in wind speed, the operating point of the system fluctuates frequently, which poses challenges for the effective assessment of the small-signal stability of the wind farms. To address this challenge, from a novel perspective, a fast estimation method for the small-signal stability region of wind farms considering the influence of wind speed is proposed in this paper. First, the impedance identification model of wind farms based on graph convolutional networks is established, which enables accurate impedance identification under unknown control and parameter states. Subsequently, the small-signal stability classification method based on deep operator networks is proposed, which allows fast stability judgment under massive variable wind speed conditions. Finally, the stable region of wind farms considering wind speed and short-circuit ratio variations is established, thereby supporting the fast stability assessment both online and offline under variable operating conditions. Case studies validate the accuracy and rapidity of the proposed estimation method for the small-signal stability region.

title: Medium-term wind power forecasting based on the strategy of “independent encoding - joint decoding” considering multi-source data
abstract: The precision and dependability of wind power forecasting are significant for the safe and stable operation of the power system. Longer prediction horizons and higher forecasting accuracy are required with wind power development. However, current research primarily focuses on intra-day (generally 4-6h) and day-ahead (generally 1-3 days) forecasting, with limited attention to medium-term (generally 1-10 days) forecasting. Furthermore, research on medium-term wind power forecasting is mainly based on operation data of the wind farm and weather prediction data, neglecting the mesoscale meteorological data around the stations that can provide information on weather changes under large-scale, as well as the differential contributions of various data to the forecasting results. Aiming at the above problems, a medium-term wind power forecasting method based on the strategy of “independent encoding - joint decoding” considering multi-source data is proposed in this paper. Firstly, a multi-variable selection module is constructed based on the gating mechanism to select the most important features at each time point as input for subsequent modules. Then, a multi-encoding module is built based on independent parameters, employing a sequence-to-sequence approach to handle the different features of multi-source data, and transform them into unified temporal features. Finally, a joint decoding module based on multi-head attention mechanism is constructed, which can dynamically integrate the information obtained from each independent encoder to improve the forecasting accuracy. To validate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method, different types of data are used as inputs, and four commonly used models, including CNN, LSTM, GRU, and Transformer, are employed as basic models for comparison. Two wind farms in North China are taken as examples, the results show that the forecasting error can be reduced by 0.53% to 30.97% when RMSE is used as the evaluation index, 0.55% to 34.34% when MAE is used as the evaluation index.

title: Coupled effects of insulation and operating modes on heat extraction performance and thermal response of energy tunnels in cold regions
abstract: With the expansion of tunnel construction in cold regions, balancing structural frost protection with low−carbon energy utilization has become a critical challenge in underground engineering. Energy tunnel technology integrated with ground-source heat pump systems offers a promising solution, yet the combined effects of insulation and operating mode on long-term thermal performance remain poorly understood. This paper examines how insulation layers and operating modes affect heat extraction performance and lining thermal response in cold-region energy tunnels. A field test system was established at the Lianhua Tunnel in Linxia, Gansu, China, to monitor inlet and outlet water temperatures and the lining's thermal response during intermittent operation. The field data were then used to validate a numerical model developed in COMSOL Multiphysics®. Based on the validated model, the effects of internal insulation and different operating modes were examined. The results show a distinct crossover in heat-extraction performance associated with the insulation layer. This occurs because insulation reduces early heat loss but blocks long-term thermal replenishment from tunnel air, unlike the uninsulated case where tunnel air acts as an auxiliary heat source. Furthermore, the Extraction−Heating mode significantly reduces the decline in lining temperature and provides better thermal stability than the Extraction-Intermittent mode. While insulation reduce the thermal influence zone of low−level thermal disturbance in surrounding rock and soil, it markedly expands the zone of intense thermal disturbance near the lining. Based on these findings, a hybrid insulation strategy is proposed to balance energy recovery and thermal stability of the surrounding ground.

title: Comparison of N-S axis bifacial agrivoltaic systems in vertical and gabled-roof configuration for different latitudes and their applicability to agricultural pumping
abstract: This work compares two bifacial photovoltaic configurations for irrigation across different latitudes: Vertical panels and a gabled-roof arrangement, both aligned along a north–south axis, with their front sides facing east and west, considering both water volume-to-energy productivity (m 3 /kWh) and annual specific pumped volume (m 3 /kWp per year). Photovoltaic generation was simulated in the software tool PVsyst tapping Typical Meteorological Year data for Low (27.89 °N), Mid (39.50 °N), and High (52.55 °N) latitudes. Pumped flow was estimated as a function of power using a polynomial model with a single pump to two pumps in parallel switching rule. In terms of annual specific energy yield, the vertical configuration outperformed the gabled counterpart by 5.4%, 14.7%, and 13.7%, while in terms of annual specific pumped volume the vertical outperformance was of 4.0%, 7.5%, and 9.0%, for the Low, Mid, and High latitude, respectively. Although the gabled-roof configuration achieved slightly higher water volume-to-energy productivity, the vertical configuration delivered more total annual pumped volume due to its higher integrated energy yield. A ±20% sensitivity analysis on the pump-switching power threshold confirmed the robustness of these results. As a takeaway, vertical bifacial PV is more effective for maximizing annual irrigation water delivery across the latitudes considered.

title: Electric bus scheduling and charging optimization: A comprehensive review of energy consumption estimation, operational technologies, and future prospects
abstract: Electric buses (EBs) represent a crucial solution for mitigating carbon emissions and are being increasingly adopted worldwide. However, challenges such as limited driving range, prolonged charging times, and high costs associated with disordered charging hinder efficient scheduling and increase operating costs. In response to these issues, numerous interdisciplinary studies on EB scheduling and charging optimization have surged, with the aim of enhancing operational efficiency and management effectiveness. This paper presents a comprehensive review of EB operations and charging scheduling. Specifically, we investigate the key factors influencing deployment and scheduling decisions, with particular emphasis on energy consumption estimation methods, especially those employing machine learning techniques. Subsequently, we examine various charging technologies and their interactions with fleet operations, focusing on the rapidly evolving domain of fast charging technology. Then, the scheduling problem of EBs is analyzed from the level of bus planning tactics, including an analysis of optimization models, critical factors influencing charging schedules, solution methodologies, and considerations regarding the integration of EBs with power grids and renewable energy sources. Finally, we discuss current challenges in this domain while providing recommendations and prospecting potential future developments related to EBs and their associated charging scheduling issues.

title: Coupled selection method for the runner and converter of doubly-fed variable-speed pumped storage units
abstract: Currently, the selection of runners and converters for doubly-fed variable-speed pumped storage units is typically conducted independently by professionals from different fields. This disjointed approach fails to account for their coupling relationship, often resulting in oversized converter capacities. To address this, this paper proposes a coupled optimal selection method considering the interaction between runner parameters and converter capacity requirements. First, a steady-state mathematical model of the doubly-fed induction generator is established to derive calculation methods for rotor-side active, reactive, and apparent power, clarifying the basis for capacity selection. Second, using a domestic pumped storage station as a case, the synchronous speed and speed variation range are determined via traditional methods to analyze the influence of runner diameter on converter capacity. Finally, the runner diameter is optimized to achieve coupled selection of the runner and converter. Results show that, without changing the unit operating range, the optimized runner diameter decreases by 0.53%. The reduction in runner diameter modifies the variable-speed characteristics of the unit and reduces the difference in maximum rotor-side apparent power between supersynchronous and subsynchronous conditions, thereby reducing the converter capacity from 26 MW to 15 MW (42.31%). Meanwhile, the optimized runner diameter brings the unit's operating conditions closer to the optimal characteristic curve, thus increasing the hydraulic efficiency in turbine mode by 0.35%. These improvements enhance the turbine size utilization coefficient, reduce manufacturing difficulty by 1.06%, and improve equipment utilization, providing potential economic benefits for the power station.

title: Thermal taming of supercooled SAT-STP binary eutectic phase change materials for long-term energy storage
abstract: Seasonal thermal energy storage can improve energy utilization efficiency by reconciling the temporal and spatial imbalance between solar-energy availability and demand. Spontaneous crystallization remains a key drawback of phase change materials, as it shortens the period over which latent heat can be retained. In this study, sodium acetate trihydrate and sodium thiosulfate pentahydrate were combined to form a binary eutectic system. At the eutectic composition, the system undergoes congruent melting, which fundamentally mitigates the phase separation caused by the incongruent melting of conventional hydrated salts. Rheological characterization and Arrhenius model analysis confirmed that the three-dimensional network established by sodium carboxymethyl cellulose significantly elevated the viscous flow activation energy of the system (from 40.35 to 46.54 kJ mol−1).The optimized composite remained in a metastable liquid state for over 120 days at room temperature and, in a separate low-temperature test, remained visibly liquid without spontaneous crystallization after 5 h in an external bath maintained at −15.75 °C. The material achieved a photothermal conversion efficiency of 85.12% and enabled on-demand latent-heat release through 3 V electrical triggering. Prototype-scale experiments further demonstrated solar thermal charging, controllable latent-heat release, and continuous water heating. These results support the potential of the proposed system for cross-seasonal thermal management. The synergistic strategy combining eutectic design with kinetic regulation provides a promising pathway toward efficient and controllable seasonal solar thermal energy storage.

title: Power and control performance of a TMD based wave energy converter built in a floating offshore wind turbine
abstract: The floating offshore wind turbine effectively utilizes abundant offshore wind resources but remains incapable of harnessing wave energy from seawater. To mitigate the impact of wave action on FOWT and reduce energy costs, this paper proposes a hybrid wind-wave energy utilization system incorporating the built-in wave energy converter, which combines the principles of both point absorber and tuned mass damper. It utilizes a spring-mass unit to absorb kinetic energy from the hybrid system's motions. The motion of the mass unit drives a permanent magnet synchronous motor through a transmission system to generate electricity, which is then stored in the battery pack. Taking a semi-submersible floating offshore wind turbine as the subject of study, three wave energy converters are installed in the three side columns of the semi-submersible platform, and a coupled model of the hybrid system is established using the Euler-Lagrange equations. The parameters of the wave energy converter are determined based on the dynamic characteristics of the floating offshore wind turbine and power output. The control effect and power performance of the wave energy converter under combined wind and wave conditions are analyzed. Results indicate that the wave energy converter not only reduces the response but also provides additional power output. Furthermore, the wave energy converter maintains favorable performance under varying wave incidence angles.

title: Multi-stage thermochromic smart windows: Response design optimization for building energy efficiency and climate adaptability
abstract: Thermochromic smart windows are widely used for passively regulating solar radiation. Current research mainly focuses on material performance improvement, but multi-stage composites lack rational design criteria. Their phase transition temperatures often mismatch with real climates, limiting large-scale application and energy savings. This study constructs single-stage, two-stage and three-stage thermochromic material systems targeting minimum building energy consumption, and simulates their performance in five typical cities to determine suitable ranges and optimal phase transition temperatures. Results show that the energy-saving performance of composite systems can be enhanced by up to 5.7 times under optimal parameters, with a peak total energy-saving rate of 24.26%. At the optimal phase transition temperature (Tc), the three-stage system is most suitable for Harbin. Single-stage or three-stage systems can be deployed in Beijing, Shanghai and Guangzhou as required to balance daylighting and heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) loads. For mild Kunming, single-stage hydrogel yields the lowest HVAC energy consumption, whereas the two-stage system minimizes overall energy demand. This study reveals the matching mechanism among the optimal Tc, phase transition stage and climatic characteristics, providing theoretical support for climate-adaptive design and practical application of multi-stage thermochromic smart windows.

title: Corrigendum to “Thermal depletion patterns of CO2 and water in closed-loop coaxial geothermal systems with vertical and L-shaped wells” [Renew. Energy, 274, (2026), 126159]
A novel heat-recovery system with seasonal energy storage for data centers
abstract: Data centers generate substantial and huge amounts of heat annually. Current heat-recovery strategies for data centers predominantly focus on the heating season and underutilize the heat during the non-heating season. Hence, this study proposes a novel heat-recovery system with ground heat exchangers for seasonal thermal storage (HR&STS) for data centers, which can achieve annual heat recovery. The system stores data center waste heat underground via ground heat exchangers during the cooling season and extracts it for building heating in the heating season, enabling continuous thermal utilization. The energy and economic performance of the HR&STS system are evaluated, including the heat-recovery rate, energy savings, and payback period. To improve the performance of the HR&STS, both time-based and temperature-based operation strategies are proposed and tested. Results indicate that the HR&STS can significantly improve the annual heat recovery by 20.51% compared with conventional heat recovery systems. The economic performance is very attractive with a payback period of 1.6 and 3.5 years. The “2 + 2” time-based control strategy is recommended with a higher heat recovery rate and shorter payback period. This study provides an effective and systematically evaluated pathway for enhancing data center waste heat recovery and supporting community-scale carbon reduction.

title: Carbon option valuation and management: An uncertain fractional-order mean-reverting dynamics
abstract: This study develops an uncertain fractional-order mean-reverting framework for valuing European carbon emission options, motivated by the dual features of epistemic uncertainty and long-memory effects in carbon price dynamics. The model is formulated as a Caputo-type uncertain fractional differential equation (UFDE), and analytical α-path solutions are obtained for both call and put contracts. A residual-based moment estimation method is employed to calibrate model parameters from historical price data, with the fractional order adaptively determined through a search algorithm. The framework is applied to daily carbon allowance prices from five Chinese pilot markets (Shanghai, Guangzhou, Chongqing, Shenzhen, and Tianjin) across diverse option types. Model adequacy is confirmed through uncertain hypothesis testing, while forecasting experiments demonstrate that the UFDE captures both relatively stable and highly volatile market behaviors, with credible uncertainty bands generated from the α-path construction under the Liu process. Sensitivity analysis further illustrates distinct patterns in the dependence of option values on strike and maturity across regions, revealing heterogeneous risk-return trade-offs. Beyond pricing accuracy, the UFDE framework also offers managerial insights for carbon risk control. By simulating credible future price trajectories, firms can treat allowances as assets and use call options to cap compliance costs, thereby supporting precise carbon budget planning. From the perspective of real options, carbon management further enables enterprises to retain flexibility under uncertainty, seize growth opportunities from technological upgrades or market expansion, and balance short-term compliance with long-term sustainable development. Such strategies help enterprises balance economic performance with regulatory requirements and strengthen their competitiveness in emerging carbon markets.

title: Investigation of leakage current paths in PV module under different climatic conditions
abstract: Potential induced degradation is a major cause of power loss in photovoltaic modules operating in outdoor field conditions in power plants. Due to high string voltages, leakage current flows through the module and can determine degradation severity. Leakage currents are affected by climatic conditions such as temperature and relative humidity and can flow through different paths within the module depending on environmental conditions and material properties of the module components. The path of leakage current can play a critical role in the severity of potential induced degradation in a module and therefore needs to be investigated in detail. While current literature provides insights into degradation mechanisms and mitigation, detailed investigations focusing on leakage current paths under varying climatic conditions remain limited. Identifying these leakage paths is essential, as they can be connected to the degradation mechanisms and mitigation strategies. This work investigates leakage current paths in framed, glass fronted, encapsulated photovoltaic modules under varying climatic conditions, focusing on the influence of temperature and relative humidity. Activation energies of the module at different humidities were calculated and analysed to identify the probable dominant leakage current paths. Results reveal that leakage current increases exponentially with both temperature and humidity. At higher humidities, the results indicate an increased contribution from moisture assisted glass surface conduction. These findings highlight glass surface conductivity as an important consideration for potential induced degradation mitigation strategies. Overall, this work highlights the importance of optimizing material selection and module design to mitigate potential induced degradation and improve module reliability.

title: Coupled effects of atmospheric stability and terrain slope on wind turbine wake evolution and downstream power performance over hilly terrain
abstract: The rapid deployment of onshore wind farms in complex terrain is an important pathway for expanding wind energy deployment. However, the coupled effects of atmospheric stability and terrain slope on wind turbine wake evolution and downstream power performance remain insufficiently understood, hindering accurate energy-yield assessment and effective wind-farm layout optimization. In this study, high-fidelity large-eddy simulations are conducted to investigate turbine wakes over flat terrain, a gentle hill, and a steep hill under convective, neutral, and stable atmospheric conditions. The results demonstrate that wake evolution and downstream power performance are jointly controlled by atmospheric stability, terrain slope, and upstream turbine wakes. Coriolis-induced wind veer and terrain-induced flow distortion lead to three-dimensional wake deflection, which becomes more pronounced with increasing atmospheric stability and terrain slope. Under stable conditions over the steep hill, the downstream distributions of power loss and power variability exhibit pronounced asymmetry, together with faster power recovery. Momentum-flux analysis shows that this accelerated recovery is primarily driven by downward mean advective transport from the low-level jet rather than by enhanced turbulent mixing. Terrain-induced power loss and variability increase with terrain slope because of intensified flow separation on the leeward side. In contrast, the power loss and variability caused by upstream turbine wakes decrease over steeper terrain because the increased elevation difference reduces direct wake impingement on the downstream rotor. These findings clarify the coupled terrain–stability mechanisms governing wind turbine wakes and provide guidance for energy-yield assessment and turbine layout optimization in complex terrain.

title: Large eddy simulations on the wake characteristics of a wind turbine in sand-laden environment
abstract: Wind turbine wakes in desert and Gobi regions evolve in the presence of airborne particles, but the effects of these particles remain poorly understood. Large-eddy simulations coupled with an actuator-line model are employed to investigate sand-laden wakes at different Stokes numbers. The effect of particles on wake recovery varies with both Stokes number and downstream distance. Near-wake recovery enhancement increases with Stokes number and is strongest at a Stokes number of 1.5. Farther downstream, recovery is greatest at a Stokes number of 1, whereas the enhancement at 1.5 progressively diminishes. Proper orthogonal decomposition and spectral analyses show that, at a Stokes number of 0.01, the blade-rotation-frequency signature is strengthened, while the low-frequency energy is broadly distributed without an isolated dominant meandering peak. The corresponding spatial modes exhibit fragmented vortex-pair patterns. At a Stokes number of 1, large-scale vortex-pair patterns remain identifiable, and the dominant low-frequency peak coincides with that of the sand-free case. At a Stokes number of 1.5, these patterns are retained, but the dominant low-frequency peak shifts to a higher frequency. Overall, increasing Stokes number enhances the low-frequency energy in the temporal coefficients while attenuating the blade-rotation-frequency contribution. Sand-laden wakes require fewer modes for reconstruction than the sand-free wake, particularly at a Stokes number of 0.01. These results clarify how airborne particles modify wake recovery and meandering in a sand-laden environment.

title: Development and classification of an all-sky radiation distribution model based on the CIE standard luminance model
abstract: Accurately characterizing the distribution of sky radiation is crucial for the design and evaluation of solar energy systems and building energy efficiency, but existing sky radiation distribution models suffer from issues such as overlapping sky type characteristics and statistical instability. This paper first proposes a full-sky radiation distribution model based on the International Commission on Illumination standard. When applying 15 sky types to this model, the correlation coefficient (R) ranges from 0.53 to 0.92, with a root mean square error (RMSE) reaching up to 50%; Second, by comprehensively considering influencing factors such as intra-class homogeneity, physical continuity, and interpretability, this paper proposes four new classification schemes (12, 9, 6, and 3) suitable for the radiation distribution model; Subsequently, a comprehensive evaluation of the five classification schemes for the all-sky radiation distribution model was conducted. The results indicate that, when factors such as classification resolution and statistical robustness are taken into account, the 9-class sky type scheme achieves the optimal balance; compared to the original 15-class sky-type classification, the minimum R value increased from 0.54 to 0.82, establishing a sky classification system suitable for this model. This indicates that more classifications are not necessarily better; rather, a reasonable division should be based on the characteristics of the spatiotemporal distribution of sky radiation. This study provides a new theoretical basis for research on efficient solar energy utilization and building energy conservation.

title: Design and multi-objective optimization of a novel axially-magnetized rotary-linear permanent magnet generator using grey relational analysis for integrated wind-wave energy conversion systems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel axially magnetized rotary-linear permanent magnet generator for integrated wind-wave energy conversion systems. A single annular mover, assembled from alternating axially magnetized ring magnets and salient-pole cores, serves independent inner rotary and outer linear stators. This arrangement uses axially magnetized ring magnets and spatially differentiates the dominant rotary and linear flux paths, with the intention of simplifying magnet arrangement and assembly. A hierarchical optimization framework is established in which shared-mover parameters are optimized before independent refinement of the two stators, while weights obtained by the analytic hierarchy process and entropy weight method are fused through the principal eigenvector of their Gram matrix for multi-objective decision-making. Three-dimensional finite-element results show that the optimal design increases the output powers of both generation units and reduces linear detent force. A prescribed translation with a 100 mm peak-to-peak stroke and a 5 s period is used only to examine low-frequency electromagnetic response. Separately, a one-degree-of-freedom buoy–generator heave model is established using hydrodynamic coefficients in a time-domain model. Simulations with regular waves and a joint North Sea wave project spectrum quantify wave-induced motion, force, and absorbed power.

title: Reducing hoary bat mortality using curtailment: Potential impacts to wind energy generation and value in the contiguous United States
abstract: : Mitigating wildlife impacts of wind energy involves power generation and conservation trade-offs. For bats, curtailing wind turbines reduces collision risk. Although curtailment is generally implemented during a narrow set of conditions (e.g., at night in late summer when wind speeds are relatively low), the impact on power production and revenue can be substantial at some wind energy facilities. Several studies have documented significant reductions in bat fatalities when wind turbines are curtailed, but few assess the energetic and economic costs. We modeled 12 curtailment scenarios using 3 cut-in speeds (5.0, 6.0, and 6.9 meters/second) and 4 seasons to assess the reduction in energy generation and energy value. Three of the curtailment periods were based on time periods curtailment has historically been tested or implemented. The fourth, based on when most hoary bat fatalities occur, was included to examine whether regionally specific data could reduce impacts to the wind industry. The median reduction in annual energy production was between 0.18% and 2.9%, with most scenarios involving a reduction of less than 1%. The median reduction in annual energy value was below 2% in most scenarios but was nearly 4.8% in the scenario with highest level of curtailment. Cut-in speed had a greater effect than seasonal duration, for both energy production and value, but the duration of the season moderated some of the impact of higher cut-in speeds. Given the conservation value increases with higher cut-in speeds, implementing curtailment based on regional, or even local, data could benefit bats, wind energy generation, and grid reliability.

title: Sustainable energy recovery from the aluminum industry: Thermoelectric power generation under strong magnetic field environments
abstract: Aluminum production suffers from severe energy waste, with approximately 50% of input electrical energy dissipated as waste heat. Thermoelectric conversion technology can directly convert waste heat into electrical energy, but its application in the aluminum industry has not been sufficiently studied. This study combines numerical simulation, experimental testing, and industrial experimental results to systematically analyze the heat dissipation characteristics, optimal thermoelectric generator (TEG) parameters, and the influence of strong magnetic fields in aluminum electrolytic cells, providing theoretical and technical support for the application of thermoelectric conversion technology in the aluminum industry. Symmetrically installing two TEGs at the steel shell grooves of aluminum electrolytic cells can balance the thermal equilibrium of electrolysis cells with power generation performance. The steady-state output power of the TEG reaches 31.79 W at a cooling airflow velocity of 5 m/s, with an error of less than 5% compared to the numerical calculation result. Industrial experiments revealed that strong magnetic fields around aluminum electrolytic cells constitute the core constraint on TEG performance, while TEGs can recover to 97.86% of initial performance 130 h after removal from magnetic fields (with 2.14% permanent loss). Magnetic field effects can be mitigated by using magnetic shielding materials with high saturation magnetic flux density (e.g., Fe-Co-V alloy), thereby reducing the magnetic-field impact on TEGs.

title: Source–load matching and battery sizing for a PV/T-driven dual-source heat pump in rural heating
abstract: Coupling of photovoltaic/thermal systems with heat pumps offers a promising route to clean heating for cold-region rural buildings, but local utilization of the generated electricity is constrained by the timing mismatch among solar generation, heating load, household electricity, and storage. While electrical or thermal storage has been introduced to mitigate this mismatch, the manner in which electrical energy storage reshapes on-site solar electricity utilization under a complete user-side electrical boundary and aids battery capacity selection remains unquantified. This study proposes and validates a photovoltaic/thermal direct-driven air/water dual-source heat pump system with battery storage for space heating. Based on a full-scale demonstration on a rural house in Lanzhou, China, a TRNSYS heating-season model was validated against measured data. Four electrical-side boundary cases (with/without battery storage and household electricity) were analyzed using power-mismatch identification and battery-sizing methods based on marginal solar-electricity utilization gains per unit capacity and investment. The system supplied 20.10 MWh of heat with a seasonal performance factor of 1.94. Without battery storage or household electricity, only 25.5% of the generated electricity was locally consumed; this value increased to 86.3% with battery storage and reached 98.5% when household electricity was incorporated. Mismatch analysis showed that battery storage shifts daytime surplus electricity to non-generating periods, while household electricity shortens the surplus duration. Combining marginal utilization gain with the battery price curve identified 10.24 kWh as the engineering-rational capacity, beyond which utilization gains per investment dropped sharply. The proposed boundary–mismatch–capacity methodological chain provides an engineering basis for sizing similar systems.

title: Efficient thermal management of lithium-ion battery modules by using U-shaped heat pipes in static immersion cooling systems
abstract: Static flow immersion cooling (SFIC) systems provide crucial advantages for battery energy storage, including zero pumping power and silent operation, but suffer from degraded cooling capacity in compact modules, where the narrow battery spacing restricts natural convection and the coolant thermally stratifies, leaving the low-temperature coolant at the bottom of the tank unutilized. To exploit this stratification rather than suffer from it, U-shaped heat pipes are arranged across the thermocline: the evaporation section of each pipe is horizontally embedded within the interlayer of the battery module, whereas the condensation section is horizontally positioned in the low-temperature coolant near the bottom of the oil tank, which enlarges the driving temperature difference between the two sections and establishes additional thermal pathways from the cells to the coolant. Experimental results demonstrate that, with twelve U-shaped heat pipes in the optimized 3-6-3 arrangement, the maximum module temperature decreases from 54.5 °C to 49.3 °C (a reduction of 5.2 °C) and the maximum module temperature difference decreases from 5.1 °C to 1.8 °C (a reduction of 3.3 °C) after five consecutive 5C-rate cycles, compared with the heat-pipe-free module. The effects of the heat-pipe geometry, quantity, and spatial distribution are further analyzed, providing optimization guidelines for SFIC systems applied to high-density battery modules.

title: Precisely controllable fabrication of gradient porous photothermal sponges for solar-driven interfacial evaporation
abstract: Against the global background of carbon neutrality and large-scale renewable energy integration, photothermal porous materials have been extensively employed in solar-driven interfacial evaporation (SDIE). However, on-demand control of pore size and distribution in photothermal porous materials remains a critical challenge. Herein, a salt template method was proposed to fabricate polydimethylsiloxane-carbon nanoparticle (PDMS-CNPs) sponges with precisely tunable pore size (50–150 μm) and distribution. Results reveal that vertical water transport time was reduced from 190 s to 130 s as the average pore size decreased from 150 μm to 50 μm. A vertical gradient porous structure was further designed to shortening the vertical water penetration time to 37 s. The gradient-pore evaporator achieved an evaporation rate of 1.54 kg m−2 h−1 under 1-sun illumination, which could be boosted to 3.74 kg m−2 h−1 under 3-sun illumination. It also retained 74.1% of its initial evaporation rate after 3 h of operation in 25 wt% NaCl solution. This work provides reliable quantitative datasets and design principles for the intelligent optimization of SDIE systems, and exhibits great application potential in low-carbon multi-energy coupling and smart renewable energy utilization scenarios.

title: Research on multi-objective optimization of wave-trapezoidal flow channels in proton exchange membrane fuel cell considering the impact of mechanical properties on gas diffusion layer deformation
abstract: The flow channel structure of bipolar plates plays a crucial role in improving the performance of proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC). In this study, a novel wave-trapezoidal flow channel (WTFC) was proposed, which adopts the constant cross-sectional area design concept, enabling effectively enhanced mass transfer performance while maintaining a relatively low pressure drop. Furthermore, the effect of mechanical properties on gas diffusion layer deformation was considered. To improve the overall performance of the PEMFC, the optimization objectives were defined as net power density (Pnet), maximum liquid water saturation (MLWS) at the interface between the cathode gas diffusion layer and the cathode catalyst layer, and effective mass transfer coefficient (EMTC) at the same interface, while the optimization variables included flow channel geometric parameters and cell operating conditions. The BO-CNN-LSSVM model establishes the mapping between optimization variables and optimization objectives. The optimal wave-trapezoidal flow channel (OWTFC) is obtained through multi-objective optimization. Results show high agreement between BO-CNN-LSSVM regression predictions and numerical simulations, with all R2 values higher than 0.98 for the three objectives. Compared with the genetic algorithm-back propagation neural network, it reduces fitting time by 45.12% while improving accuracy. OWTFC outperforms trapezoidal flow channel and single straight flow channel: Pnet increases by 5.13% and 20.58%, MLWS decreases by 11.05% and 38.33%, and EMTC rises by 8.43% and 29.65% respectively under the same conditions.

title: Accelerating transport decarbonization through second-generation biofuels in Australia: A DSIT-informed statistical forecasting and scenario modelling framework
abstract: The purpose of this study is to advance a data-driven transition framework that helps to convert Australia's existing bioenergy sector into a sustainable second-generation (cellulosic) biofuels industry. This study quantifies how the energy sector transition reduces long-term CO2 emissions, strengthens national energy security, and promotes circular-economy goals by using agricultural residues. This study employed a SARIMAX (1,1,1) forecasting model and used annual national time-series data (2010–2024). This study uses Business-as-Usual (BAU) to forecast CO2 emissions from 2025 to 2050 and to highlight the key drivers of CO2 emissions. This study used a Monte Carlo simulation of 1000 bioenergy adoption paths and sensitivity/elasticity analysis. This study explains how regional clustering and social policy affect biofuel adoption pathways by using A Dynamic Social Impact Theory. The SARIMAX model achieves high predictive accuracy (MAPE ≈ 1.5%) and indicates that BAU emissions will increase to 131 Mt CO2 by 2050. Stochastic adoption simulations indicate a mean decrease of ∼92 Mt (≈30% below BAU), with faster-adoption scenarios achieving up to ∼46% mitigation. Policy-driven adoption of bioenergy, at 40% to 60% by 2050, will lower emissions to 79 Mt and 55 Mt, respectively, showing strong reduction potential aligned with zero-carbon emissions. This study applied an integrated SARIMAX–Monte Carlo modeling framework for the first time to Australia's transport sector within a biofuel-transition setting.

title: Graph processing driven decoding of microstructure in solid oxide cell fuel electrodes with self-assembled voids
abstract: The electrode microstructure governs mass transport and charge transfer kinetics, restricts the performance of solid oxide cell (SOC) and its widespread use for renewable energy, necessitating precise quantification for targeted optimization. Herein, a fractal theory-integrated graphic processing to quantify the microstructure of SOC fuel electrode (FE) are developed, to acquire intrinsic characteristics thereby exploring structure-performance correlation of proposed FE utilizing self-assembled voids. Achieved results indicated that FE fabricated with fine/coarse particles (1.048 μm/3.316 μm) demonstrated optimal performance, achieving peak power densities of ∼0.467 W/cm2 and ∼0.486 W/cm2, with area specific resistance (ASR) around 0.498 Ω cm2 and 0.488 Ω cm2. Quantitative analysis revealed voidage of ∼44.4%, triple phase boundary (TPB) area of ∼2.92 × 105 m−1, connectivity of ∼0.06, ∼0.10, and ∼0.19 for electron conductive phase (ECP), oxygen ion conductive phase (OCP), and voids, with effective H2/H2O diffusion coefficients around ∼2.88 × 10−4 m2/s and ∼2.48 × 10−4 m2/s, respectively. A competitive relationship was identified between the ECP and OCP connectivity. Meanwhile, ECP connectivity and TPB area demonstrate positive correlation with ECP particle size, yet negative correlation with effective diffusion coefficient. Crucially, excessive mass transfer capacity would widen the disparity between H2 and H2O diffusion, inducing an imbalance in reactant adsorption and product desorption.

title: Scenario-based multi-objective optimization for hydro–wind–solar–storage integrated systems
abstract: Hydro–wind–solar–storage (HWSS) systems provide an effective pathway for integrating renewable resources into low-carbon power systems. However, the stochastic and fluctuating outputs of wind and photovoltaic generation increase the difficulty of HWSS planning and operation. To address this issue, this study develops a scenario-driven multi-objective capacity planning framework for an HWSS system. A Markov chain and a C-vine Copula are jointly employed to characterize the spatiotemporal dependence of hydro, wind, and solar outputs. On this basis, Monte Carlo simulation is combined with K-medoids clustering to construct representative joint output scenarios. A multi-objective capacity optimization model is then formulated by considering energy generation, fluctuation complementarity, and ramping complementarity. An NSGA-III–TOPSIS decision framework is used to derive Pareto-optimal solutions and determine the final compromise configuration. A case study in the Panxi region of Sichuan Province shows that the proposed method effectively preserves spatiotemporal dependence. The final configuration achieves balanced performance, with a fluctuation complementarity index of 0.8062, a ramping complementarity index of 0.7665, and a TOPSIS closeness coefficient of 0.6815. The results indicate that the proposed framework can provide effective support for HWSS capacity planning under renewable output uncertainty.

title: A concept of dam-free hydropower storage coupled with industrial waste heat and LNG cold energy using “CO2+water” dual fluid mediums
abstract: Pumped hydro energy storage comprises most of global storage power capacity, however its development is limited by geographical constraints, environmental concerns, and significant infrastructure costs. In this paper, we present a conceptually design of dam-free hydropower storage using “CO2+water” dual fluid mediums, combined with the thermal cycle of CO2 utilizing the cold energy provided by liquefied natural gas and the low-grade waste heat from industrial circulating water for gasification of liquid CO2, respectively. Experiments were conducted to investigate the thermodynamic state change of CO2 in a prototype power tank (1.94 m height and 0.7 m3 volume). Results show that the output power of the power tank increased with increasing the initial CO2 pressure, reducing the initial water level, and increasing the final water level during the water drainage process. Under a typical experimental condition (an initial water level of 1.16 m, an initial CO2 pressure of 5.45 MPa, an initial CO2 temperature of 26.0 °C, and a final CO2 pressure of 1.30 MPa), an output power of 43.6 kW was achieved for the power tank, with a CO2 exergy efficiency of 43.3%. Additionally, a simplified model including the gaseous CO2 re-liquefaction process was constructed and simulated, and an overall exergy efficiency of 40.8% was obtained for the entire system. This concept demonstrates the application potential in energy storage, low-grade waste heat recovery, and liquefied natural gas cold energy utilization, providing a preliminary design and foundation for future optimization and experimental investigation of the entire system.

title: Interlayer-engineered Ti2C MXene enables activation-free and kinetically enhanced hydrogen storage in Mg-rich Mg-Ni-Ce alloy
abstract: Magnesium-based alloys possess high hydrogen storage capacity; however, their practical application is critically impeded by mandatory activation procedures and sluggish reaction kinetics. Herein, we present an interlayer engineering approach utilizing Ti2C MXene functionalized with NH3·H2O, which enables activation-free and kinetically enhanced hydrogen storage in a Mg-rich Mg10Ni5Ce alloy. This material achieves 4.58 wt% H2 uptake within 3 min at 250 °C and 3 MPa without pre-activation, substantially outperforming the pristine alloy (1.72 wt%). More hydrogen can be released by Mg10Ni5Ce-Ti2C(NH3·H2O) (3.90 wt%) than by Mg10Ni5Ce (1.42 wt%) within 5 min at 350 °C. Moreover, the peak desorption temperature (Tpeak) is lowered by 25 °C, and the apparent desorption activation energy is reduced by ∼28 kJ/mol, evidencing a dramatically lowered kinetic barrier. Systematic mechanistic studies reveal that intercalated NH3·H2O species expand the Ti2C interlayer spacing, creating abundant catalytic interfaces and promoting electron transfer from multivalent Ti ions. Owing to this synergistic effect, H2 dissociation and recombination are facilitated while the energy-intensive initial activation step is avoided. This work validates an efficient MXene catalyst and proposes interlayer engineering as a versatile strategy to eliminate activation, accelerate kinetics, and realize practical high-capacity hydrogen storage.

title: Capacity sizing and isolated operation strategy for a Solar-sCO2 hybrid microgrid in remote islands: Balancing cost and renewable energy penetration
abstract: Islands that depend on diesel face high fuel costs and environmental damage. This study proposes a solar tower and diesel hybrid microgrid built on the supercritical carbon dioxide (sCO2) power cycle, dispatched by a hierarchical strategy in which seawater desalination acts as a flexible load. A two-step dimensionality reduction scheme combines 72-h extreme weather pre-extraction with improved K-means clustering. It preserves the safety boundary for multi-day low-irradiance sequences at acceptable computational cost. An adaptive NSGA-II co-optimizes the levelized cost of energy (LCOE) and the renewable fraction (RF). In the South China Sea case study, the LCOE falls from 0.58 USD/kWh under the pure-diesel benchmark to 0.33 USD/kWh, a reduction of 43.1%, at an RF of 68.4%. The recommended configuration curtails 14.8% of its annual solar input, against 28.6% for the maximum-penetration configuration. The difference is a curtailment penalty from oversizing the solar field and thermal storage beyond the accommodation limit, not a change in dispatch flexibility. During the 72-h extreme sequence the desalination load performs deep peak shaving of the net load seen by the diesel generator and lowers the required backup capacity. Solar field sizing carries an asymmetric penalty. Undersizing by 20% raises the LCOE by 28%, whereas oversizing by the same margin raises it by 12%.

title: Temperature interval based heat extraction and flow regulation for thermal matching in solar driven TTES-ORC systems
abstract: Solar driven ORC systems integrated with thermocline thermal energy storage (TTES) offer a promising approach for dispatchable renewable power generation by coupling medium and low temperature solar heat utilization with thermal energy buffering. However, the heat source temperature fluctuations can weaken thermal matching between heat supply and power generation demand, reduce annual electricity generation, and increase control frequency. To address these limitations, a temperature interval based heat extraction and flow regulation strategy is proposed for a solar driven TTES-ORC system. The strategy extracts heat according to predefined TTES temperature intervals and regulates the ORC flow rate based on the operating conditions matched to each interval, thereby improving the coordination between thermal energy release and ORC operating demand while reducing the frequency of control actions. Results indicate that flow regulation increases annual electricity generation by 32.9%, to 29.1 MWh. When a temperature interval of 5 °C is applied, the control frequency decreases by 77.8%, whereas the annual electricity output decreases by only 6.3, indicating a favorable balance. These results demonstrate that the proposed strategy can effectively improve thermal matching, operational stability, and annual energy performance, offering a practical framework for the coordinated operation of solar driven TTES-ORC systems under fluctuating heat source conditions.

title: Sonochemical engineering of Ag-Ni loaded ZnIn2S4 nanocomposites for enhanced solar-driven hydrogen evolution
abstract: The development of efficient photocatalytic routes for hydrogen production is of growing interest for sustainable energy conversion and the storage of renewable energy in the form of a chemical energy carrier. In this work, ZnIn 2 S 4 -based photocatalysts were engineered through the loading of commercial Ni nanoparticles (NPs) and the in-situ formation of Ag NPs via a sonochemical process, leading to enhanced photocatalytic performance. Among the synthesized photocatalysts, ZIS/AgNi-10 (10 min of sonication) exhibited the highest hydrogen evolution activity, reaching a value of 1.65 ± 0.04 mmol g -1 h -1 and apparent quantum efficiency (AQE) of 9.4 % at 420 nm. This improvement is attributed to the synergistic effect of Ni and Ag loading, where Ni provides active catalytic sites, while Ag NPs promote plasmon resonance and facilitate charge separation. These effects result in improved charge carrier dynamics and enhanced light absorption, as supported by optical and electrochemical analyses. Although a reduction in specific surface area is observed after sonication, this limitation is offset by the improved electronic and optical properties. Structural and compositional characterization further confirmed the effective integration of both components, inducing modulation of the electronic structure, including bandgap tuning and a shift in the valence band position. Overall, this work presents a simple, green and scalable strategy to optimize ZIS-based photocatalysts toward sustainable hydrogen generation and photon-to-chemical conversion, with relevance to renewable hydrogen technologies.

title: How increasing green hydrogen blending affects techno-economic and environmental performance of renewable energy communities across Italian climates
abstract: Renewable Energy Communities (RECs) can support the decarbonization of local energy systems by promoting renewable generation and sector coupling. This study evaluates the effect of increasing the hydrogen blending ratio from 10% to 20% by volume within an already hydrogen-integrated REC framework. Twelve scenarios are analysed across three Italian climatic zones-Reggio Calabria, Rome, and Turin-considering Combined Heat and Power (CHP) and Gas Absorption Heat Pump (GAHP) configurations coupled with photovoltaic generation, hydrogen production and storage, and hydrogen-natural gas blending. Results show that the response to higher hydrogen blending strongly depends on climate, thermal demand, and system architecture. Moving from 10% to 20% H 2 generally improves renewable-energy utilization and economic and environmental performance within the hydrogen-integrated configurations. The lowest Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE), 148.5 €/MWh, is obtained for the GAHP configuration in Reggio Calabria at 20% H 2 , with a Carbon Avoidance Cost (CAC) of 892.8 €/tCO 2 . CHP systems benefit more from high and sustained thermal demand, resulting in stronger thermal-electric coupling in colder climates. A trade-off also emerges: increasing the H 2 blending ratio can reduce the Self-Consumption Ratio (SCR) and Self-Sufficiency Ratio (SSR), because the additional PV generation required to support electrolysis also increases grid exports, while LCOE, CAC, and renewable-energy utilization improve. Comparisons with the conventional reference case are used to assess the overall PV-hydrogen-CHP/GAHP architecture and are not attributed to hydrogen blending alone. Sensitivity analysis shows that electricity and natural-gas prices and district-heating infrastructure costs dominate economic performance, whereas ±50% variations in hydrogen-component CAPEX have comparatively limited effects.

title: Nanostructured colored radiative cooling for energy-efficient buildings and thermal management applications
abstract: Passive radiative cooling (PRC) reduces cooling energy demand by reflecting solar radiation and dissipating heat through the atmospheric transparency window. Although high-performance PRC has traditionally favored highly reflective or light-colored surfaces, growing demands for aesthetics and architectural integration have promoted the development of colored radiative cooling (CRC). However, coloration often increases solar absorption and introduces additional constraints on spectral design and practical deployment. This review provides an application-oriented overview of nanostructured CRC from the perspectives of photon management and sustainable thermal regulation. The fundamental coloration mechanisms and spectral requirements of CRC are discussed, with emphasis on visible color generation, near-infrared solar heat rejection, and thermal emission within the atmospheric window. Four representative architectures, planar multilayers, periodic photonic structures, hybrid nanostructures, and hierarchical porous structures, are critically compared in terms of optical mechanisms, color-cooling trade-offs, fabrication feasibility, and application suitability. Applications in buildings, transportation, personal thermal management, and cold-chain systems are further examined. Finally, challenges involving durability, scalable manufacturing, standardized evaluation, climate adaptability, techno-economic feasibility, and year-round thermal regulation are discussed. This review establishes a structure, mechanism, performance, application framework for advancing practical CRC technologies.

title: Experimental evaluation of planar heat pipes with active cooling integration for photovoltaic thermal hot-spot mitigation
abstract: Photovoltaic module efficiency declines at high operating temperature, while localized hot spots accelerate degradation, and may reduce module lifetime. This study develops and experimentally evaluates planar heat pipes intended for rear surface heat spreading and for feeding a compact active water-cooled sink. Five full-scale prototypes with different internal configurations were fabricated from stainless steel and tested in a fully automated test rig under non-uniform heating conditions. Experiments were conducted at heating-pad setpoints between 50 and 100 °C, inclination angles of 30° to 45°, and under both natural-convection and localized active water-cooling conditions. Under natural convection, the transferred heat was comparable to that of the reference case without planar heat pipes, indicating limited benefit in bulk heat removal. When coupled to the water-cooled sink, heat removal increased by approximately 15-25 percent relative to the non-cooled baseline. The principal benefit of the planar heat pipes was temperature homogenization, which reduced peak surface temperatures by approximately 8 to 32 °C, depending on the prototype configuration and operating conditions, while markedly suppressing thermal hot spots. To illustrate the potential impact on photovoltaic performance, the experimentally observed temperature reductions were evaluated using a simplified temperature-dependent PV model and representative meteorological data for Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The assessment indicated potential improvements in annual electricity production under the investigated assumptions. The results demonstrate that planar heat pipes are effective thermal spreaders for photovoltaic applications, particularly for reducing temperature gradients and mitigating hot-spot formation.

title: Thermodynamic characteristics and off-design performance of a direct heated supercritical CO2 Brayton cycle driven by solar-biomass complementarity
abstract: The solar-biomass driven S-CO2 cycle system not only effectively copes with the inherent intermittent problems of solar energy, but also fully consumes straw and other biomass resources, realizing the efficient conversion and recycling of energy. This paper is a simulation study that innovatively constructs a multi-energy flow collaborative utilization architecture of "solar - heat storage - biomass" and establishes a thermodynamic model of the solar heat storage power generation system using Ebsilon software. Based on thermodynamic analysis, it reveals the in-depth analysis mechanism of key components of the integrated system's thermal performance and quantitatively analyzes the dynamic characteristics under four typical daily operating conditions. The results show that under the design conditions, the newly proposed S-CO2 cycle efficiency reaches 42.79 %, an increase of 0.79 % compared to previous studies. Under the summer solstice conditions, the molten salt heat storage system can independently support basic power supply for 7 h. The dynamic operation strategy and the in-depth study of off-design working conditions proposed in this study provide important theoretical references for the optimal dispatch of high-percentage renewable energy power systems.

title: Measuring renewable energy droughts – A standardized framework for quantifying the “Dunkelflaute”
abstract: Securing the electricity supply during renewable energy droughts (German: Dunkelflauten) constitutes a major challenge to the process renewable energy transition. However, the lack of a consistent approach to measuring renewable energy droughts, or Dunkelflauten has limited our ability to understand the magnitude of the problem and develop specific policy recommendations. This study proposes a standardized approach to quantify renewable energy (RE) droughts in direct reference to the installed capacity and the overbuilding of renewable energies using the German renewable electricity market as a case in point. The analysis identifies annual, prolonged RE droughts lasting up to 11 days, mainly during winter months, with generation deficits of up to 50 GW. Smaller scale RE droughts are relatively frequent, posing charging challenges for potential storage systems. Our results point to the need for increased renewables capacity, more favorable conditions for the integration of additional (renewable) gas-fired backup power plants, and other long-term storage solutions. Together with a push for grid expansion and Demand Side Management (DSM) measures major system upgrades are needed to ensure security of supply particularly during winter months.

title: Aromatic acid-driven deep eutectic solvents unlock sugarcane bagasse recalcitrance for high-yield cellulosic ethanol
abstract: Fossil fuel depletion has driven interest in second-generation bioethanol, with sugarcane bagasse (SCB) being a promising lignocellulosic feedstock for its production. However, the recalcitrance of SCB limits its efficient conversion, thus necessitating effective pretreatment strategies. Herein, four ternary deep eutectic solvents (DESs) composed of triethyl benzyl ammonium chloride (TEBAC), ethylene glycol (EG), and benzoic acid derivatives were synthesized and applied to SCB pretreatment. Compositional and structural analyses, coupled with quantum chemical calculations, were used to evaluate pretreatment performance and elucidate the underlying mechanism. Among the tested solvents, TEBAC/EG/salicylic acid (SA) achieved 82.45 ± 2.54% lignin and 84.96 ± 0.52% xylan removal, enhancing cellulose digestibility to 92.79 ± 3.01% under optimal conditions (160°C, 30 min). The pre-hydrolysis combined with simultaneous saccharification and fermentation (PSSF) process yielded 29.40 ± 0.09 g/L ethanol. Furthermore, quantum calculations revealed that the ortho-hydroxyl and carboxyl groups of SA synergistically strengthen lignin-DES interactions via hydrogen bonding and π-π stacking, offering a mechanistic basis for designing efficient DESs for lignocellulose valorization.

title: Renewable energy and storage systems for net/nearly zero energy buildings integrating electric vehicles with correlated stochastic charging: Uncertainty-aware multi-objective optimization and dynamic analysis
abstract: Integrating electric vehicles (EVs) with net/nearly zero energy buildings (NZEBs) is crucial for advancing sustainable, resilient, and low-carbon energy infrastructures. However, this integration introduces additional complexity and uncertainty due to the unpredictable nature of EV charging behaviors, which further complicates system design. This study proposes a multi-objective optimization approach for designing renewable energy systems (RESs) in NZEBs, accounting for stochastic EV charging behaviors and uncertainty correlations. By employing a multivariate copula model, this study effectively captured the dependence structures in EV charging events, preserving the inherent complexity and correlations of EV behaviors. The simulation results demonstrated that the designed RESs performed reliably under uncertain conditions, with average metrics for net interaction level, self-sufficiency ratio, and carbon dioxide emission reduction of 113.4%, 66.8%, and 45,280.0 kg, respectively. These results validated the effectiveness and feasibility of the designed RESs. The study advances the integration of EVs with NZEBs to enhance the resilience and sustainability of building energy systems, and provides practical insights for developing energy-efficient, low-carbon NZEBs in real-world applications.

title: Enhanced parameter estimation accuracy in Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells through analytical modelling, experimental validation, and real-time simulation
abstract: Accurate modelling of Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (PEMFCs) is essential for evaluating their real-time behavior and performance. This study introduces a new analytical framework that formulates a reduced-order PEMFC model and identifies its key parameters using four experimental test systems: Ballard Mark V, 250 W stack, H-12 stack, and a 1 V testbed. To minimize computational burden, the proposed method extracts only four parameters (EN, C4, RC and b) from polarization data, instead of seven conventional parameters (C1, C2, C3, C4, RC, λ and b). A comparative assessment with recent optimization algorithms, namely MRFO, ICEFO, and MFFO, demonstrates that the analytical method achieves superior performance based on the sum of squared errors (SSE) under identical conditions. Furthermore, the reduced-order PEMFC model is implemented on a real-time simulator (OPAL-RT 4510) for parameter estimation, which yields parameter values closely matching those obtained by the analytical approach. A sensitivity analysis is also conducted to assess the variations in EN, C4, RC and b parameters with SSE and efficiency. Accurate PEMFC model and its efficient integration with DC/AC microgrids can greatly improve the stability, reliability and efficiency of renewable power generation.

title: Design and multi-objective optimization of complementary pulsating flow control for H-shaped manifold microchannel photovoltaic coolers
abstract: Under high heat load conditions, effective thermal management is crucial for stable operation of photovoltaic cells. However, for H-shaped manifold microchannel photovoltaic coolers using complementary pulsating flow, the coupled effects of multiple pulsation parameters and the trade-off between heat transfer enhancement and hydraulic loss still lack systematic quantification and optimization. This paper establishes a three-dimensional transient numerical model and combines central composite design with response surface methodology to study the effects of pulsation period F, pulsation amplitude J, and recovery time ratio P on heat transfer enhancement and pressure drop, and further conducts multi-objective optimization and experimental evaluation of optimized conditions. Results show that pulsation amplitude has the most significant effect on heat transfer performance and pressure drop, generally positive on the former and negative on the latter. The optimal parameter combination is pulsation period 10 s, amplitude 0.15, and recovery time ratio 0.75. Compared with steady flow, under optimized conditions the Nusselt number increases by 1.800% and pressure drop decreases by 2.348%; compared with the intermediate pulsating condition F = 35 s, J = 0.10, P = 0.50, the Nusselt number increases by 0.593% and pressure drop decreases by 3.254%. Experimental results further show that under optimized pulsating conditions, the maximum heating plate temperature decreases from 328.8 K under steady flow to 323.9 K. These results indicate that reasonably coordinating complementary pulsation parameters can enhance heat transfer while reducing hydraulic loss, providing a quantitative basis for thermal-hydraulic design and operating parameter selection of H-shaped manifold microchannel photovoltaic cooling systems.

title: Diaphragm stress analysis and cavity profile optimization for hydrogen high- and ultra-high-pressure diaphragm compressors
abstract: Diaphragm compressors are critical for efficient hydrogen storage and transport, where accurate prediction of diaphragm stress is required for operational stability, service life, and cavity profile design. Existing studies primarily focus on diaphragm bending and tensile stresses induced by oil-gas pressure difference, while neglecting the influence of absolute oil-gas pressure loads under high-pressure working conditions. To address this gap, a three-dimensional (3D) stress analysis is performed by incorporating oil-gas absolute pressure loads. The effects of absolute pressure and diaphragm geometric parameters on the diaphragm triaxial stress state are systematically investigated, followed by cavity profile optimization based on an improved stress model. Results indicate that absolute pressure loads significantly affect the stress distribution in all directions. As the pressure increases from 5 MPa to 270 MPa, radial and circumferential stresses in certain regions transition from tensile to compressive, with a maximum reduction of 73.66%. The through-thickness stress remains compressive, with a decrease comparable to the pressure increase. This behavior is attributed to the squeezing effect of oil-gas pressure, which induces greater compressive strain in the thickness direction. The proposed optimization approach improves cavity flow capacity or reduces material cost while ensuring structural reliability. At 270 MPa, the cavity volume increases by up to 66.19% at fixed radius, while the radius decreases by up to 13% at constant volume. These findings establish absolute pressure as a pivotal design parameter, offering critical insights for enhancing the gas deliverability and operational reliability of compression systems integral to the renewable hydrogen infrastructure.

title: Renewable energy droughts as seen by the grid: An observed-generation climatology across three continents
abstract: Periods of persistently low wind and solar output, often called renewable energy droughts or Dunkelflauten, shape storage and adequacy needs of power systems, yet nearly everything known about them comes from reanalysis-driven simulations of hypothetical fleets. Here we characterise these events directly in metered fleet output: 59 regional fleets (balancing areas, bidding zones, and the Australian market aggregate) across the United States, Europe, and Australia between 2019 and 2026, validated in the United States against independent plant-level reporting with a median energy ratio of 0.996, and screened by a five-rule quality-control protocol that separates meteorological droughts from reporting and availability artefacts. Audited against this benchmark, a widely used first-order simulation chain reproduces day-to-day variability well (daily correlations 0.88–0.93) but misestimates drought frequency by −29% to ＋256%; conventional mean-level calibration leaves errors of ＋81–90% in onshore-wind-dominated fleets, and even full quantile mapping cannot repair event timing: drought-day sets agree at a Jaccard overlap of at most 0.71, and in California only half of observed drought days are recovered. Observed droughts synchronise across up to 86% of European zones on single days and decorrelate over roughly 700 km. In ERCOT, where wind and solar grew together, observed drought burden fell from 32 to 7 days yr−1, while solar-only expansion left California’s unchanged—a contrast that recurs across the Tier-1 panel. We release the full event catalogue.

title: Coupled dynamics and energy capture of oscillating water column and point absorber arrays on a shared floating platform
abstract: Array deployment is a promising route for the large-scale utilization of wave energy, and hybrid systems combining oscillating water columns with point absorber buoys may enable energy capture over a wider frequency range. However, their capture characteristics when integrated on a shared floating platform remain insufficiently understood. This study investigates the coupled dynamics and capture characteristics of such a configuration using a time-domain model based on linear potential flow theory. Specifically, platform motion modifies the capture spectra of both converters. For the configuration considered here, platform heave plays the dominant role. The resulting spectra exhibit a short-period capture peak associated with the characteristic response of the converters, a long-period capture peak associated with platform heave resonance, and an intermediate trough caused by nearly in-phase motion between the converters and the platform. Near the platform heave resonance, the responses of the two converter types partially overlap, and the coupled system exhibits negative coupling, with its total captured power below the sum of the two standalone systems. Outside this region, their distinct frequency responses provide spectral complementarity, mitigating the capture trough and broadening the effective capture range. Additional irregular-wave simulations show that the resonance-related negative coupling and frequency complementarity identified under regular waves remain evident under broadband excitation. These results demonstrate how shared-platform dynamics govern both negative coupling and spectral complementarity between different wave energy converters.

title: Role of solar spectral variability in the performance assessment of photovoltaic technologies
