abstract: One of the most fundamental parameters pushing the theoretical efficiency limits of solar cells is spectral mismatch. Although the photon flux from the sun covers a wide range of 300-2500 nm, solar cells are effective in a specific area of the solar spectrum due to the energy gap restriction. The performance of solar cells is obtained using standard test conditions. However, these conditions are rarely encountered in operating conditions. In this study, clear-sky representative-day solar spectra were calculated for Ankara, Aras de los Olmos, Beijing, and Thessaloniki using SPCTRL2 for spectral comparison only, not for estimating real-world monthly PV energy yield. Atmospheric parameters such as aerosol optical depth, precipitable water vapor content, and ozone data were obtained from the NASA AERONET database. By selecting regions with different atmospheric characteristics despite being in the near latitude zone, the effect of spectral differences on photovoltaic performance was analyzed according to different seasons and time of day. Spectral factor, average photon energy, and ultimate efficiency parameters were calculated for c-Si, a-Si, CdTe, and CIGS solar cell technologies. The results showed that atmospheric conditions significantly influence solar spectral characteristics and photovoltaic performance, even at near latitudes. High-bandgap cells (a-Si, CdTe) were less affected by spectral variations in summer, whereas low-bandgap cells showed greater sensitivity.

title: Corrigendum to “Synthesis of carbon nitride in-situ coupled tungsten oxide heterojunction with efficient photocatalytic redox properties” [Renew. Energy 245, (2025), 122806]
Renewable district heating systems in rural areas considering seasonal storage and decreasing use of biomass
abstract: In rural areas, renewable heating networks can immediately achieve carbon-neutral heat supply. Such networks with a high proportion of biomass are already well established. However, these systems are not a universal solution due to future biomass competition and sustainability constraints. While previous studies mainly focus on retrofitting existing networks, this study addresses the techno-economic optimization of newly planned rural heating networks with progressively reduced biomass use. Six system combinations are modeled in TRNSYS and optimized using SciPy for heat demands of 2, 4 and 8 GWh/a and heat densities of 250, 500 and 750 kWh/m a, considering both subsidized and non-subsidized cases. The results show that biomass can be avoided in summer using solar thermal energy or PV-driven heat pumps at 10%–20% higher LCoH. Fully biomass-free systems increase costs by around 50% for low-demand cases, while seasonal pit thermal energy storage enables > 80% solar heat shares for high-demand networks at > 20% higher costs than biomass-based systems. German subsidies reduce LCoH by approximately 18% while having only a marginal influence on system sizing. Furthermore, heat density has a stronger influence on costs than demand scaling.

title: Wave power extraction by a circular-sector oscillating water column attached to a coastal corner
abstract: Integrating oscillating water columns with coastal infrastructure can reduce construction requirements and improve the deployability of wave energy converters. This study investigates the hydrodynamic performance, wave power extraction and wave loading of a circular-sector oscillating water column attached to a coastal corner. An analytical model is developed based on linear potential flow theory. The fluid domain is divided into an inner region, a ring region and an outer region, and the velocity potentials are solved using the eigenfunction matching method. Reciprocity relations are further employed to derive the wave excitation volume flux and radiation damping. The model is validated against existing theoretical solutions and is then used to examine the effects of the water wedge angle, incident wave direction, chamber radius, air chamber volume and chamber wall thickness under regular and irregular waves. The results show that the wave excitation volume flux, hydrodynamic coefficients and capture factor are independent of incident wave direction, whereas the free surface elevation and wave loads remain direction-dependent. The wave excitation volume flux is unaffected by the water wedge angle, while the radiation damping and added mass vary linearly with this angle. At resonance, the theoretical maximum capture factor is 2/ν, where νπ denotes the water wedge angle. The circular-sector oscillating water column provides better mid-frequency power extraction than a conventional full circular oscillating water column embedded at a coastal corner. For convex corner configurations, sharp peaks in the maximum wave load are caused by sloshing modes inside the chamber. Under irregular waves, spectral averaging smooths the resonant response and reduces the peak capture factor, while broadening the effective operating frequency range. These findings provide theoretical guidance for the hydrodynamic design of corner-integrated oscillating water column devices.

title: A systematic methodology for PTO sizing and hydrodynamic optimization of OWC systems in high-energy Atlantic environments
abstract: This study presents a systematic methodology for the hydrodynamic optimization and power take-off sizing of an L-shaped oscillating water column wave energy converter for high-energy Atlantic environments. While standard oscillating water column designs, such as the Mutriku wave power plant (18.5 kW per unit), serve as a global benchmark, this research demonstrates that such configurations lead to significant energy underutilization in more energetic sea states. The proposed methodology combines multi-criteria site assessment, hydrodynamic resonance tuning, and time-domain numerical simulations. It is validated through a case study on Tenerife (Canary Islands, Spain), where an optimal chamber geometry was identified, matching the dominant wave period (T p = 12.5 s). A key contribution of this work is the optimization of the power take-off capacity. Sensitivity analysis revealed that increasing the rated power to 60 kW effectively mitigates clipping losses, increasing the annual energy production by 105.66% to 138.48 MWh/year compared with the 18.5 kW reference. Furthermore, the capture width ratio improved from 12.16% to 22.51%, highlighting the importance of hydrodynamic–pneumatic impedance matching. Comparative results show that the Tenerife site is 60.61% more energetic than the Mutriku wave power plant, achieving 2308 full-load hours and a capacity factor of 26.45%. These findings provide a transferable engineering methodology for designing resource-optimized oscillating water column systems in high-energy coastal environments. • Systematic four-stage framework for OWC design and PTO optimization. • Hydrodynamic resonance maximized through chamber geometry tuning. • PTO sizing mitigates clipping losses in energetic wave environments. • Optimized PTO increases annual energy production. • Framework transferable to high-energy breakwater-integrated OWC systems.

title: Dynamic stall behaviors of the IEA 15 MW blade controlled by the passive vortex generators
abstract: Unsteady aerodynamic loads and fluctuating power output of ultra-large wind turbines remain exceptionally challenging to predict and control under complex yawed environments. This study presents a numerical investigation into the dynamic stall behaviors of the 15-MW reference blade equipped with passive vortex generators. Utilizing fully-resolved unsteady Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes simulations coupled with the transition model and sliding mesh technique, the intricate spatiotemporal interactions among yaw-induced cross-flows, ultra-high Reynolds number boundary layers, and generated streamwise vortices are comprehensively elucidated. Results demonstrate that vortex generators successfully mitigate massive root separation, yielding a remarkable 4.6% power recovery even under a severe 60° yaw misalignment. A fundamental scale-dependent mechanism is revealed: unlike rotation-dominated stall in small-scale rotors, the thick inboard sections of the massive 15-MW blade exhibit quasi-two-dimensional bluff-body aerodynamic responses, characterized by separation-dominated clockwise hysteresis loops. Vortex generators effectively inject momentum to delay leading-edge vortex detachment during the upstroke and accelerate flow reattachment during the downstroke. This decisively fragments the massive separation bubble, prevents explosive vortex bursting, and transforms dead wake zones into highly active lift-generating regions. These unprecedented physical insights confirm that vortex generators remain an indispensable, robust flow control technology for mitigating extreme unsteady loads on next-generation giant offshore rotors.

title: A lumped-parameters dynamic model for metal hydride hydrogen storage in renewable energy systems
abstract: This study presents a zero-dimensional dynamic model for simulating a metal hydride hydrogen storage system integrated into renewable energy applications. The model is developed in MATLAB and subsequently integrated into TRNSYS to perform one-year dynamic simulations. The aim of this work is to provide an efficient and reliable simulation tool for hydrogen-based energy systems. The considered hydrogen storage system includes a cylindrical metal hydride tank filled with LaNi 5 alloy. The tank is integrated with an alkaline electrolyzer that produces the hydrogen to be stored and a high-temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cell that uses the hydrogen released from storage. The model simulates hydrogen absorption and desorption under different operating conditions. It is based on a set of ordinary differential equations representing the mass and energy balances, obtained by simplifying partial differential equations to reduce computational effort. The main novelty lies in integrating the metal hydride hydrogen storage with the high-temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cell, using its heat for hydrogen desorption. The model also includes a suitable heat transfer model based on the logarithmic mean temperature difference. Validation against experimental and numerical data shows excellent agreement, with percentage errors below 5%. The investigated system achieves a primary energy saving of 58% and a payback period of approximately 8 years.

title: Multi-energy co-optimization method for net-zero energy and transportation system considering durability and hydrogen safety
abstract: The transition towards a net-zero energy and transportation system (NZETS) that integrates renewable energy sources, an electric-hydrogen hybrid energy storage system (HESS), and zero-emission vehicles (ZEVs) can be a crucial step in building a low-carbon future society. Given the importance of dynamic energy efficiency, durability, and hydrogen safety in the collaborative scheduling of the integrated operation of ZEVs and energy systems, this paper proposes a multi-energy co-optimization method for NZETS that considers a three-dimensional optimization indicator. A refined energy system model has been established to consider dynamic energy efficiency, degradation mechanisms, and temperature rise risk, as well as a flexible load model aggregated from the charging/hydrogenation behavior of ZEVs. Based on this model, a cost-minimization optimization model for operation, degradation, and hydrogen safety has been designed to achieve coordinated scheduling between the energy system and ZEVs. The results show that the proposed method effectively constrains the temperature rise phenomenon. Moreover, this paper analyzes the impact of ZEV flexibility on the energy system, achieving a maximum temperature rise reduction of 2.6K.

title: A novel enhanced open-loop geothermal system with a single horizontal well: Heat extraction performance improved by liquid nitrogen stimulation
abstract: To improve the heat extraction performance of the new proposed single-well open-loop geothermal systems with a horizontal well, a liquid nitrogen (LN2)-assisted stimulation strategy is proposed to reduce flow resistance and enhance fracture connectivity. This study develops a coupled experimental–numerical framework by integrating experimentally measured permeability evolution from real-time high-temperature triaxial LN2 seepage tests into a three-dimensional discrete fracture network model. The model is used to simulate fluid flow and heat transfer in fractured reservoirs under different connectivity conditions. The results show that: (1) the fracture connectivity has a strong control effect on the system performance. (2) LN2 stimulation significantly enhanced the permeability of fractured reservoirs. Compared with the unstimulated, the total power of 100-500 fractures after stimulation increased by 89.23%, 82.75%, 52.06%, 11.50%, 3.41% and 4.29%, respectively. (3) when the fracture connectivity is high (>250 fractures), the enhancement effect becomes limited. (4) cyclic stimulation can also improve the heat extraction efficiency of the system, which is increased by 10.31%, 30.37%, 52.06% and 80.15% respectively after 1,5,10 and 20 times. This study highlights the realistic impact of LN2 stimulation on fractured reservoirs and provides theoretical and technical guidance for hot dry rock geothermal development.

title: Triple-bottom-line impacts of bioenergy production in China: Intra-and inter-sectoral heterogeneity
abstract: Bioenergy production spans diverse conversion pathways, each with triple-bottom-line (TBL) impacts on the economy, employment, and environment. However, conventional input-output analyses aggregate bioenergy activities, obscuring pathway-specific heterogeneity in industrial linkages and associated impacts. This study develops a sector-disaggregated hybrid IO model by integrating process-level data from nine representative bioenergy conversion pathways into China’s 2023 national IO table. Building on the analysis of industrial scale and intersectoral linkages, we assess TBL impacts and decompose their indirect effects across production layers and sectors. Results indicate that China’s bioenergy production generated approximately CNY 60 billion in value added in 2023, with bioelectricity remaining the dominant contributor. Despite differences in upstream and downstream linkages, most pathways exhibit two-way intersectoral connections. Each CNY of final demand induces CNY 1.71–2.46 in total economic effects. Biogas power generation shows the highest employment intensity, supporting 17.5 jobs per CNY million. Total emission intensities range from 64.7 to 188.1 ton/CNY million. Substituting liquid biofuels and BNG for their fossil counterparts offers potential reductions of 294.7–451.5 ton/CNY million when fuel combustion is considered. Over 90% of indirect TBL impacts are captured within the first seven layers, although their sectoral distributions vary substantially across pathways. Relative to socio-economic effects, indirect emissions extend further into upstream supply chains and are heavily concentrated in thermal power generation and cogeneration. Pathway-specific development strategies and cleaner energy supply are proposed to enhance socio-economic benefits while reducing upstream emissions across the bioenergy industry.

title: Pore-metal dual engineering: Nb-modified hierarchical zeolites enable green aromatics from waste biomass pyrolysis
abstract: Bifunctional metal–hierarchical zeolite catalysts enable efficient biomass waste valorization. Herein, a hierarchical Nb/m-HZSM-5 catalyst was developed for the catalytic fast pyrolysis (CFP) of macadamia nutshells (MNS). The catalyst synergistically combines a hierarchical pore structure with highly dispersed NbOx species, which collectively optimize the acid site distribution and enhance textural properties. These structural and compositional advantages resulted in markedly enhanced catalytic performance in CFP of MNS, driving MAHs selectivity from 46.9% to 77.8%, while concurrently boosting bio-oil yield. Integrated analysis of catalytic products and characterization data revealed the pivotal roles of NbOx species and acid sites in promoting deoxygenation and aromatization, while simultaneously preventing excessive aromatization and condensation reactions. In parallel, hierarchical porosity alleviated the intrinsic diffusion constraints of conventional HZSM-5, thereby further enhancing catalytic selectivity toward desirable monocyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (MAHs). In summary, this study provides an effective strategy for sustainable bio-oil production from waste biomass, with suppressed polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and coke formation ensuring premium bio-oil quality.

title: Unlocking bioenergy from municipal organic waste via anaerobic digestion in off-grid coastal communities of low-resource regions
abstract: Increasing municipal solid waste generation, projected to exceed 3.8 billion tons annually by 2050, calls for biomass valorization beyond conventional disposal. This study evaluates anaerobic digestion (AD) of the organic fraction of municipal solid waste (OFMSW) as a decentralized waste-to-energy solution for isolated coastal communities in developing countries. Compositional and physicochemical characterization of locally generated OFMSW revealed high biodegradable organic content and favorable parameters for AD. Biomethane potential (BMP) was assessed at inoculum-to-substrate ratios (ISR) of 1.0–2.5 under mesophilic conditions (35 °C) without mechanical mixing. ISR 2.5 achieved the highest yield (455 mL CH 4 g -1 VS), with production stabilizing within 17 days. These conditions informed subsequent semi-continuous operation using solid swine manure (SM) as inoculum at an organic loading rate (OLR) of 1.08 g VS L -1 day -1 . The reactors maintained stable performance without mechanical mixing or external alkalinity addition, producing 0.53 NL biogas g -1 VS at steady state, with pH of 6.4–6.8 and VFA-to-alkalinity ratios below 0.3. Community-scale energy balance and sensitivity analyses indicated that projected biogas production could replace 17.67–69.51% of local liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) demand, yielding estimated fuel-cost savings of USD 552–2,171; the departmental reference scenario yielded 29.54% substitution and USD 923 in savings. By integrating local feedstock characteristics, experimental digestion performance, and scenario-based energy substitution, this study provides evidence for decentralized bioenergy assessment and potential deployment in resource-constrained coastal communities, consistent with recovery priorities within the waste hierarchy.

title: Effects of fracture-geometry uncertainty and dynamic-aperture feedback on heat extraction and net electric-power potential in a hot dry rock reservoir
abstract: We quantify how fracture geometry and aperture evolution affect heat extraction and electricity potential in a Gonghe Basin hot dry rock reservoir. A three-dimensional thermal–hydraulic–mechanical model represents post-stimulation flow and heat transfer through four embedded fracture surfaces. Fifty geometries are simulated with fixed and evolving apertures under common pressure controls and constitutive parameters. At year 40, dynamic opening lowers mean production temperature from 436.04 to 424.99 K. Mean production flow increases from 5.69 to 99.02 kg/s and heat extraction from 2.39 to 36.81 MW. All 50 pairs show lower production temperature and greater flow and heat output. The flow gain outweighs the reduced production–injection temperature difference. With a Carnot-relative conversion factor of 0.45 and reservoir-port pumping, mean year-40 net electric-power potential is 5.52 MW. The 5th–95th percentile interval across geometries is 4.19–6.80 MW; ideal continuous operation yields 1.77 TWh over 40 years. Tree-ensemble importance ranks fracture-area variability first and fracture-4 dip second for heat rate, with the order reversed for net electric-power potential. Proper orthogonal decomposition and geometry regression predict complete response curves from temporal coefficients. Twenty geometries augment training and validation; another 20 provide independent testing. Expanding training and validation from 50 to 70 geometries reduces independent-test curve errors for eight of nine responses. Net electric-power curve root-mean-square error decreases by 7.82%, with power calculated jointly from predicted temperature, heat rate and pumping power. The method supports pre-development comparison of hot dry rock reservoirs through joint thermal–hydraulic and electricity-potential assessment.

title: Sustainability analysis of power supply chain with risk aversion under the uncertainty of renewable power generation
abstract: Against the backdrop of the ongoing energy transition and sustainable development, this paper investigates the uncertainty of renewable power generation and constructs a power supply chain, which is divided into noncooperative and cooperative models based on members’ independent competitive and collaborative decision-making. The mean–variance utility function is adopted to reflect models’ economic efficiency, and risk aversion is adopted to reflect members’ attitudes towards the uncertainty. Based on different levels of members’ risk aversion, three scenarios are discussed. First, their optimal decisions are developed. Then, the advantages and disadvantages of noncooperative and cooperative models under the three scenarios in terms of sustainability are compared. Next, a two-part tariff contract is proposed with the aim of preserving both the adaptability of the noncooperative model and the sustainability of the cooperative model, thereby effectively achieving the global coordination of the power supply chain with risk aversion. Finally, the impacts of members’ risk aversion are revealed, and the management implications are provided for promoting the transition, ensuring the power supply stability, and enhancing the system’s economic efficiency.

title: Mechanistic insights into N2O abatement over SFCMO-based direct ammonia solid oxide fuel cell: polarization behavior and environmental application
abstract: Solid-oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) are investigated for N 2 O abatement, targeting the decomposition of this potent greenhouse gas while generating electricity as by-product. Although O 2 is typically the oxidant in SOFCs, N 2 O can also serve this role, as N 2 O decomposes into N 2 and O 2 under operating conditions. This work analyzes a double-perovskite Sr 2 Fe 1.45 Co 0.05 Mo 0.5 O 6− δ (SFCMO) as a cathode for N 2 O reduction. Dilatometry indicated an average thermal expansion coefficient of 10.7 x 10 -6 °C -1 , compatible with common SOFC electrolytes. The SFCMO|GDC|YSZ|Ni-YSZ cell was tested with O 2 or N 2 O, while the anode was fueled with NH 3 . Electrochemical characterization of the cell was performed via electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) and distribution function of relaxation times (DFRT) between 600 – 750 °C. Analysis indicated that surface exchange was the rate-limiting step of the oxygen reduction reaction. N 2 O as a source of oxygen atoms, which effectively lowers the oxygen partial pressure ( ) at the cathode, may increase the concentration of oxygen vacancies and enhance surface redox activity. Accordingly, the cell supplied with N 2 O exhibited more than a 30 % increase in power density compared to operation with O 2 , with an average N 2 O conversion of ∼41.7 %. These findings demonstrate SFCMO electrode as an efficient electrocatalyst for N 2 O abatement for intermediate-temperature SOFCs fueled by ammonia.

title: Advanced amorphous high entropy phosphide toward high-performance seawater electrolysis
abstract: Designing electrocatalysts with outstanding corrosion resistance and activity for seawater electrolysis is essential for practical application. However, achieving this goal faces significant challenges on account of the sluggish kinetics of oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and competitive chlorine evolution reaction (CER). In this study, a series of chromium (Cr)-enhanced amorphous high-entropy phosphides (FeCoNiMoCrPx-n) were prepared on nickel foam (NF) through a hydrothermal method followed by phosphorization, and applied to seawater electrolysis. Remarkably, the inclusion of Cr notably optimized the proportion of high-valence metal active species and strengthened the synergistic effects inherent to the high-entropy materials, which in turn facilitated the generation of active metal oxy(hydroxide) species, thereby improving electrocatalytic OER performance. The as-fabricated FeCoNiMoCrPx-0.75/NF electrode exhibited superior OER activity in both simulated and alkaline natural seawater (overpotentials as low as 230 and 237 mV at 10 mA cm−2, respectively). More importantly, this electrocatalyst demonstrated remarkable stability as well as corrosion resistance during continuous testing for over 500 h under the alkaline natural seawater condition at a commercially relevant current density of 500 mA cm−2. Furthermore, as a bifunctional electrocatalyst enabling overall water/seawater splitting, the cell fabricated by using FeCoNiMoCrPx-0.75/NF electrode required merely 1.50 V in simulated seawater and 1.54 V in alkaline natural seawater to deliver 10 mA cm−2, highlighting its great potential for prolonged electrochemical seawater splitting.

title: Optimizing of multi-layer porous media inserted combustion for the energy conversion improvement of zero-carbon fueled thermophotovoltaic generator
abstract: To improve the combustion stability and thermal performance of micro power systems, experiments on premixed NH3/H2/Air combustion with various porous media (PM) inserted are conducted. A numerical model investigates the combustion and heat transfer with the maximum relative deviation of 5.83% against measured outer-wall temperatures. The effects of equivalence ratio and PM parameters of porosity ε, PPI, length Lp, and wire diameter Wd on combustion characteristics, flame stability, and heat transfer are experimentally and numerically studied. The results demonstrate that the key equivalence ratio affecting combustor thermal performance is Φ = 1.6, and the inserted PM significantly improves flame stability and heat transfer. When the PM length is Lp = 15 mm, the inserted PM effectively enhances combustor radiation temperature. Additionally, among the tested PM parameters, PPI 40 and Wd = 0.20 mm yield higher wall temperatures and improved combustor thermal performance. Furthermore, the employment of gradient multi-layer PM with porosity arrangement of ε = 0.94 + 0.9 + 0.86 improves energy conversion and efficiency, where the maximum radiation power of 44.79 W is achieved at Vf = 700 mL/min, while the largest radiation efficiency of 36.53% is gained at Vf = 650 mL/min. For the generator employed the measured wall temperatures and InGaAsSb photovoltaic cells model, the calculated electrical output and system efficiency respectively reach 1.76 W and 1.41% at Vf = 700 mL/min. These findings provide guidelines for the design and optimization of zero-carbon micro power generators.

title: Enhanced properties of poly(iminodibenzyl-co-terphenyl piperidinium)-based anion exchange membranes enabled by alkoxy containing crosslinkers
abstract: To achieve highly conductive and chemically stable anion exchange membrane electrolytes for renewable energy devices of green hydrogen, we introduce rigid iminodibenzyl to prepare quaternized poly (p-terphenyl-co-iminodibenzyl N-methylpiperidine) (QPTIP). Then, three flexible crosslinkers possessing different alkoxy groups are employed to fabricate linear or star crosslinked membranes. The alkoxy groups benefit the formation of interconnected ion conducting channels according to the results of morphology analysis and theoretical calculation. The crosslinked membranes with a tensile stress at break above 40 MPa exhibit the OH− conductivity of 113.0 to 133.7 mS cm−1 in water with a water swelling ratio less than 25% at 80 °C. The conductivity of over 83% is retained by the proposed membranes after aging in 2 mol L−1 KOH at 80 °C for 2000 h. The membrane QPTIP-PTM10 crosslinked by branched 2, 2′, 2’’-((propane-1,2,3-triyltris(oxy)) tris(methylene))-tris(oxirane) (PTM) shows better comprehensive performance than those crosslinked by linear crosslinkers. This membrane-based single fuel cell demonstrates a peak power density of 946 mW cm−2 at 80 °C without back pressure; and a water electrolytic cell assembled with the QPTIP-PTM10 membrane reaches a current density of up to 2.5 A cm−2 at 2.0 V and can stably work for 100 h at a current density of 500 mA cm−2.

title: Online optimization of operating parameters for PCM-based ocean thermal engines: Numerical and experimental study
abstract: Phase-change-material–based ocean thermal engines offer a promising pathway toward long-endurance ocean observation by harvesting in-situ thermal energy for self-powered operation. However, existing systems rely primarily on fixed, experience-based operating parameters or offline optimization and therefore cannot adapt their profiling strategies to changing temperature–depth conditions. In this study, we propose a cycle-to-cycle online optimization framework that jointly updates the maximum diving depth, descent and ascent velocities, and surface and bottom residence times to maximize the cycle-averaged net output power. Because each optimization run requires repeated evaluation of the phase-change dynamics, a physics-informed surrogate model is employed as a fast evaluator. The particle swarm optimization algorithm is adopted to optimize the operating parameters of the engine. Under the same thermal conditions and prototype configuration, the optimized strategy improved the simulated net output power by 345.5% relative to a conventional fixed profiling strategy. Finally, the proposed online optimization framework was validated through lake trial. After acquiring the local temperature–depth profile, the optimization algorithm identified the optimal operating parameters within 11 min, and the optimized cycles achieved an average measured net output power of 0.56 W, higher than that obtained using the conventional operation strategy.

title: Modeling and operating characteristics of open-cathode air-cooled proton exchange membrane fuel cells under high-altitude conditions
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) demonstrate great potential for logistics operations in complex terrains. Air-cooled proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) have become the preferred power source for small-to-medium-sized UAVs, yet they are highly sensitive to high-altitude conditions because cathode air serves as both reactant and cooling medium. This work develops a multi-physics PEMFC model coupled with an atmospheric environment model, and rigorously validates it through high-altitude field experiments, to clarify the effects of atmospheric pressure and oxygen concentration. Pressure reduction destroys the uniformity of internal multi-physics fields and impairs mass transport, reaction kinetics, and thermal management. When pressure decreases from 101325 Pa to 78256 Pa and 61165 Pa, the stack peak power density drops by 24.9% and 37.6%, respectively. Moreover, reduced oxygen volume fraction severely lowers the oxygen concentration at the cathode catalyst layer, aggravating local starvation and thermal non-uniformity. This induces a distinct striated current density distribution, significantly degrades peak power, and shifts the peak power toward lower current densities. Ultimately, oxygen starvation dominates high-altitude performance decay, accounting for 72.2% and 79.2% of peak power attenuation at 78256 Pa and 61165 Pa. The findings provide valuable insights and technical guidance for the optimal design and control of air-cooled PEMFCs.

title: Prediction of transient heat exchange performance of energy pile groups using a physics-constrained DeepONet
abstract: Rapid prediction of transient heat exchange performance of energy pile groups becomes particularly challenging when thermal interference among piles, groundwater seepage, and intermittent operation act simultaneously. Numerical simulations are computationally expensive, whereas previous data-driven studies have mainly focused on the quasi-steady-state response of an isolated pile. This study developed an integrated framework of an analytical model and a physics-constrained deep operator network for transient thermal performance of energy pile groups under groundwater seepage and intermittent operation. The analytical model for pile groups was based on the moving finite cylindrical source theory, thermal resistance model, and spatiotemporal superposition principles. After validation against numerical and experimental results, the analytical model was used to generate 15,000 cases comprising 3000 independent physical-parameter sets evaluated under five operation strategies. Three machine-learning models were developed to predict the time-dependent heat exchange response and were evaluated over five runs with different random seeds. The physics-constrained deep operator network generally showed superior performance in the test set, and an ablation study was conducted to quantify the contribution of each embedded constraint. Independent examples further demonstrated that the machine-learning model can reproduce the transient thermal performance of individual piles and pile groups over a 90-day period within 1 s. SHAP analysis identified the relative importance of ten input features, and initial ground temperature and operation strategy were dominant for thermal performance of energy pile groups. The proposed framework provides a physically credible and computationally efficient surrogate model for preliminary design and operation optimization of energy pile groups.

title: Analysis of Startup Dynamics Characteristics in Air-Cooled PEMFCs Using a 3D Transient Non-Isothermal Two-Phase Flow Model
abstract: Air-cooled open-cathode proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) are lightweight candidates for unmanned aerial vehicle portable power, yet suffer from inherent trade-offs between heat dissipation and membrane hydration during dynamic cold startup. Most existing numerical models published rely on steady-state single-phase frameworks with incomplete cell components, lacking insights into full transient multi-physics coupled evolution and local field characteristics throughout galvanostatic startup. To address these critical research gaps, this work develops a fully coupled three-dimensional transient non-isothermal two-phase air-cooled PEMFC model integrating all 11 core components. The simulation quantitatively reveals several novel transient phenomena unreported in prior journal studies: cathode rib-channel geometry dominates species distribution in the late startup stage; membrane water content exhibits obvious transport time lag in ionomer domains; current density uniformity continuously deteriorates and reaches minimum when the cell stabilizes. PEM ohmic polarization dominates dynamic voltage fluctuation, with a 28.4 mV variation exceeding the 22.4 mV change of cathode catalyst layer overpotential. This study clarifies the intrinsic multi-field coupling mechanisms unique to room-temperature startup, and delivers targeted theoretical support for transient performance optimization and dynamic water-heat control of aviation air-cooled fuel cell power systems.

title: A novel BIPV weave curtain wall for synergistic solar-thermal-electric regulation in public buildings
abstract: Large-area glass curtain walls are widely adopted in modern public buildings for their integrated aesthetic and functional merits. However, they inherently induce excessive secondary solar heat gain, which substantially elevates the cooling load of buildings. To address these two critical issues, this study proposes a novel building-integrated photovoltaic (BIPV) weave curtain wall. The proposed system enables passive regulation of solar radiation in response to seasonal variations in solar altitude and azimuth angle, integrates photovoltaic power generation with solar thermal regulation effectively. A comprehensive transient model coupling optical, electrical, and heat transfer analyses is established and experimentally validated. With the validated model, the performance of the BIPV weave curtain wall with various geometric parameters are evaluated for Harbin and Shenzhen. Furthermore, the regional applicability of the optimized configuration is analyzed across 32 provincial administrative regions in China. The results reveal that the curtain wall achieves optimal energy performance in low-to-mid latitude and low-altitude regions. In hot climate zones, the simulated building cooling load can be reduced by up to 151.9 kWh/m2. By contrast, in severe cold regions, it may increase the heating demand in winter. Even so, the annual power generation in severe cold regions still reaches 89.0 kWh/m2. Additionally, the power generation capacity is positively correlated with local direct solar radiation and negatively correlated with the solar heat gain coefficient. This study demonstrates that the proposed curtain wall offers an efficient, aesthetically pleasing, and climate-adaptive solution for energy-efficient building envelopes, possessing broad application potential across diverse climatic regions.

title: Investigation on degradation nonuniformity among single cells of the PEMFC stack based on I-V curve and nonlinear least square model
abstract: The factors affecting performance nonuniformity among cells and the durability of proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) stacks are complex and difficult to measure experimentally. In this work, we conducted a 3000 h durability test and periodic performance tests on a PEMFC stack. Based on the nonlinear least-squares (NLS) method, we propose a novel model to estimate the membrane electrode assembly (MEA) parameters of individual cells within the stack. By combining the model with measured current–voltage (I–V) curves, we investigated the evolution characteristics of MEA parameters and the degradation nonuniformity among cells and quantified their respective contributions to voltage degradation. The main conclusions are as follows: the polarization curves and voltage evolution curves fitted using the proposed model agreed well with the measured data, with errors of less than 2.5%; degradation nonuniformity among cells is attributed to differences in the decrease in MEA parameters, primarily the electrochemical surface area, which accounted for more than 85% of the voltage degradation; and the contribution of hydrogen permeation current was below 1%. The study demonstrates the reliability and effectiveness of the proposed model and method, providing a useful mathematical tool for assessing cell degradation within a stack and a foundation for potential online applications.

title: Climate-dependent performance of a rooftop radiative cooling and latent heat storage system for building cooling in China
abstract: Radiative cooling (RC) can provide low-grade cooling for buildings, but its application is limited by the mismatch between nighttime cooling availability and daytime cooling demand. To address this challenge, this study proposes an integrated cooling system combining a rooftop RC-based water-cooling unit, latent heat thermal energy storage (LHTES), and radiant ceiling panels (RCPs), such that cooling harvested at night can be utilized for daytime cooling. An integrated simulation framework was developed and was applied to representative climates across China. Parametric analysis identified a moderate storage configuration with 15 modules as the preferred design. Under this configuration, annual cooling electricity savings reach 9.8 kWh·m−2 in Chengdu and 14.3 kWh·m−2 in Hong Kong. The daytime runtime is strongly climate dependent, remaining high throughout the cooling season in Urumqi and Kunming, but dropping sharply in hotter climate areas. When heating penalties are considered, the system provides the most balanced net annual performance among the investigated configurations, yielding net savings of 7.3 kWh·m−2 in Chengdu and 14.1 kWh·m−2 in Hong Kong. Nationwide simulations further indicate that the system can provide positive net savings in parts of the hot-summer/cold-winter area, although the magnitude and seasonal availability remain strongly dependent on local weather and geographic conditions.

title: Heat extraction characteristics of CO2-based closed-loop U-shaped deep geothermal wells under natural circulation
abstract: Density-difference-driven natural circulation using CO2 offers a potential pathway for pump-free heat extraction from closed-loop U-shaped geothermal wells. However, its dynamic operational characteristics are less understood. In this paper, a coupled wellbore-formation heat transfer model is developed considering the balance between the thermal buoyancy and the flow resistance along the wellbore. The heat extraction characteristics of closed-loop U-shaped geothermal wells based on CO2 natural circulation are analyzed. The effects of geothermal gradient, well depth, and wellbore structural parameters on heat extraction performance are evaluated. The results indicate that the natural-circulation flow rate of CO2 in the closed-loop U-shaped well is significantly higher than that of H2O owing to its greater buoyancy driving pressure and lower flow resistance. CO2 maintains a natural-circulation mass flow rate of approximately 35.7 kg/s on Day 120, with cumulative heat extraction of approximately 1.35 × 104 GJ over the 120-day operation period. Geothermal gradient and well depth exert the strongest effects on circulation and heat-extraction performance, whereas pipe diameter primarily controls circulation intensity and horizontal-section length mainly affects the effective heat-exchange capacity. These results demonstrate the thermohydraulic potential of CO2 natural circulation and provide a theoretical basis for the design and performance assessment of pump-free closed-loop geothermal wells.

title: Mediterranean offshore wind spatial potential: Focusing on national targets of Italy, Greece and Cyprus for electricity and hydrogen production
abstract: Offshore wind and green hydrogen are expected to play a central role in Mediterranean decarbonisation, yet deep waters, intense coastal uses, and visual-acceptance constraints make siting and system design challenging. This study develops an integrated geospatial and techno-economic framework that combines marine spatial-planning layers, long-term wind reanalysis, offshore wind-farm design, and power-to-x valuation to assess where offshore wind can support electricity supply and hydrogen production. Spatial exclusions, bathymetric limits, and a visual-impact index reduce the basin to about 6.6 ⋅ 1 0 5 km 2 of eligible sea space (about 24% of the Mediterranean). For each grid cell, multi-year wind series are coupled with precomputed performance and cost tables for fixed-bottom and floating concepts, multiple turbine ratings, layouts, and spacings, producing spatially resolved indicators for annual electricity yield and levelised costs for electricity and hydrogen. For Italy, Greece, and Cyprus, 2030 electricity and hydrogen targets can be met using less than 8% of the eligible area, while export-oriented 2050 cases require up to about 55% in Italy and 75% in Greece and Cyprus, with avoided emissions on the order of several tens of MtCO 2 yr −1 .

title: Impacts of concentrator optical factors on array performance of dense-array concentrated photovoltaic systems
abstract: Dense-Array Concentrated Photovoltaic systems can concentrate low energy density solar radiation onto a small area via high concentration technology to substantially improve the conversion efficiency of photovoltaic cells. For the dish type concentrated system, this paper establishes a dish concentrator optical model coupled with Series-Parallel, Total-Cross-Tied, and Quartered-Rotational-Symmetry array simulation models. By constructing an electrical model, the effects of specular reflectivity, surface slope error and tracking error on system performance are quantitatively analyzed. Optical simulation results demonstrate that specular reflectivity only changes the magnitude of energy flux on the receiver surface. The peak concentration ratio under error-free conditions is 1.75 times that under the 10 milliradian surface slope error condition, and the light spot shifts by 0.05 m with loss of irradiance distribution symmetry when the tracking error rises to 10 milliradian. Electrical results indicate that the maximum output power of the three arrays decreases synchronously by 9.58% as specular reflectivity falls from 100% to 90%. Increasing optical errors decrease irradiance uniformity, and partial cells of series-parallel and total-cross-tied arrays become reverse biased under the 10 milliradian system tracking error condition. The quartered-rotational-symmetry array achieves the best overall performance across all simulated operating conditions; compared with series-parallel and total-cross-tied configurations, its maximum output power, photoelectric conversion efficiency and fill factor are enhanced by 5.26%-36.28%, 5.27%-36.32% and 6.76%-64.29%, respectively, and all its cells maintain forward biased status even under harsh operating conditions.

title: Tuning physicochemical properties of magnetic biochar to enhance semi-thermophilic anaerobic digestion
abstract: Semi-thermophilic anaerobic digestion (STAD, 41–49 °C) has emerged as a promising alternative to mesophilic and thermophilic systems. However, the application of magnetic biochar (MB) in STAD remains underexplored, and the combined mechanisms by which its key properties influence STAD are poorly understood. In this study, tunable MBs (K0–K3) with different specific surface area (SSA), electron-donating capacity (EDC), and zero-valent iron (ZVI) loading were synthesized to evaluate their effects on STAD performance. MB addition accelerated volatile fatty acid depletion, and the optimal MB (K2) increased methane yield by 112%. Microbial and metagenomic analyses showed that K1–K3 promoted the enrichment of syntrophic acetate-oxidizing bacteria (SAOB) such as Syntrophaceticus, thereby enhancing the potential for the syntrophic acetate oxidation coupled with hydrogenotrophic methanogenesis (SAO-HM) pathway and supported a functionally complementary syntrophic network. K1–K3-amended reactors also exhibited a higher relative abundance of populations with potential for direct interspecies electron transfer (DIET) (e.g., DTU014), while K2 uniquely enriched MAG.176 (order Desulfotomaculales), a putative DIET-capable bacterium harboring a DIET-related gene set. Partial least squares path modeling indicated that SSA and EDC were the main factors explaining the enhanced methanogenic performance, with ZVI playing a complementary role. Overall, MBs enhanced STAD mainly through indirect chemical and microbial regulation rather than direct abiotic catalysis. These findings provide mechanistic insight into the rational design of functional MB for improving STAD.

title: Editorial Board
Experimental study on dynamic response characteristics of proton exchange membrane fuel cells under different anode gas supply modes
abstract: The dynamic performance of proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) is essential for its efficient and stable operation. This work compares PEMFC dynamic behaviors under three anode supply modes: dead-end anode (DEA), peristaltic pump circulation anode (PCA), and ejector circulation anode (ECA). The influences of current-variation amplitude, anode inlet pressure, cathode stoichiometric ratio, cathode humidity and operating temperature on dynamic performance are explored, where key metrics including voltage leap (VL), transient voltage minimum (TVM), steady-state voltage (SSV), voltage undershoot (VU), dynamic response time (DRT) and energy loss (E-loss) are analyzed. A printed circuit board (PCB) technology is adopted to capture local current density (LCD) under cyclic-load conditions. Results show that elevated anode inlet pressure improves steady-state voltage and dynamic response. Larger cathode stoichiometric ratio causes unevenly distributed liquid water and delays membrane rehydration. 80% cathode inlet humidity is the threshold of cell dynamic response. Higher cathode humidity brings no obvious enhancement in dynamic performance. The operating temperature substantially boosts dynamic performance, and temperature is strongly correlated with VL. The ECA mode delivers the best dynamic and steady-state performance among the three configurations. Compared to DEA and PCA, ECA shortens the average DRT and yields 0.75 V output at 600 mA/cm2. Furthermore, the ECA mode incurs no direct electrical parasitic power for the PEMFC system.

title: Household-level biogas technology adoption within an extended UTAUT model: Sustainable energy transition pathway
abstract: Although green energy technologies have rapidly advanced sustainable development goals, household adoption of biogas technology remains strikingly low. Therefore, this study investigated the factors affecting biogas technology adoption within the unified theory of acceptance and use of technology. Data from 300 Pakistani households in Chakwal city of Upper Punjab province were analyzed using partial least squares-based structural equation modeling. Findings showed that performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence, facilitating conditions, seasonal functioning, fragmented landholdings, and unavailability of natural gas infrastructure predicted behavioral intention, which in turn significantly mediated their impact on biogas technology adoption. The relative significance evaluation of key predictors indicated that effort expectancy was the main driver, while fragmented landholdings emerged as the primary barrier to biogas technology adoption. A novel multigroup analysis revealed that social influence promoted biogas adoption among individuals with low and medium education but was neutral among the highly educated, whereas facilitating conditions encouraged adoption among the medium- and highly educated but had little effect on those with low education. Eventually, the estimated model provided innovative insights to boost the adoption and implementation of biogas technology to fulfill sustainable development goals, especially SDG7.

title: Direct electrification and hydrogen-based pathways in EU passenger transport: Energy, environmental, and material implications
abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrogen-based passenger transport pathways are increasingly considered as potential decarbonization options in the European Union’s (EU) energy transition, particularly for long-distance and high-utilization applications where direct electrification may face operational constraints. However, their representation in Integrated Assessment Models (IAMs) and their system-wide energy, environmental, and material implications remain insufficiently assessed. This study extends the IAM WILIAM by incorporating hydrogen-based passenger transport pathways for light-duty vehicles, buses, and rail, together with electrolytic hydrogen production, storage, distribution, refueling infrastructure, greenhouse gas (GHG) and pollutant emissions, and critical material requirements. We assess EU policy-aligned scenarios focused on passenger transport, combining direct electrification, fuel cell electric vehicle (FCEV) deployment, renewable electricity expansion, and demand-side sufficiency assumptions. Results show that direct electrification plays the central role in reducing liquid fuel demand, primary energy (PE) consumption, and GHG and pollutant emissions. Adding hydrogen-based pathways further reduces liquid fuel demand and several emissions, especially VOC, CO, and CO 2 , but delivers smaller additional reductions than direct electrification alone and negligible additional reductions for CH 4 . In the most hydrogen-intensive scenario, FCEV deployment requires 137 GW of electrolyzer capacity, 44200 refuelling stations, and up to 196 GW of additional electricity generation capacity, while increasing PE consumption relative to the direct electrification pathway. Material trade-offs also emerge, with reduced pressure on some battery-related materials but increased demand for platinum and iridium, potentially exceeding the corresponding reserve benchmarks. Demand-side sufficiency substantially alleviates these pressures, delivering the strongest reductions in total energy demand and emissions while requiring lower infrastructure deployment requirements.

title: Thermally enhanced co-digestion of sugarcane bagasse and organic fraction of municipal solid waste for compressed biogas: From pilot-scale optimization to life cycle assessment for net-zero mobility
abstract: Decarbonizing mobility requires scalable renewable fuel pathways that integrate feedstock valorization, process efficiency, and system-level sustainability. This study presents a first-of-its-kind integrated assessment of compressed biogas (CBG) production from thermally enhanced co-digestion of sugarcane bagasse and the organic fraction of municipal solid waste, linking laboratory optimization with long-term pilot-scale validation (700 L reactor, 208 days). Optimization study identified optimal substrate-to-inoculum and mixing ratios (60:40 for BG:OFMSW), while thermal pretreatment (Dry heating mode) (110 °C, 60 min) effectively overcame lignocellulosic recalcitrance, achieving a maximum methane yield of 379.4 mL/g-VS. These results were validated at continuous pilot-scale reactor. Operation in Anaerobic bi-phased baffled reactor (ABBR) established an optimal organic loading rate of 1.5 kg VS/m3/day and biogas yield of 0.86 m3/kg VS for pretreated biomass compared to 0.64 m3/kg VS for untreated systems. A life cycle assessment for the vehicular use demonstrates that only methane yield enhancement does not ensure environmental sustainability. Instead, the carbon intensity of the energy used for thermal pretreatment rules overall performance. Renewable source (solar PV) integration significantly reduces the additional thermal pretreatment impacts. A cradle-to-grave LCA was conducted using 1 ton of mixed substrate as the functional unit. Environmental impacts were assessed using the ReCiPe 2016 (H) midpoint and endpoint methods across seven impact categories, including global warming, eutrophication, ecotoxicity, toxicity, fossil resource scarcity, and water consumption. The study highlights the need for integrated optimization across feedstock, conversion, and energy systems to enable scalable, low-carbon CBG pathways. These findings contribute to advancing renewable fuels for net-zero mobility under real world operational constraints.

title: A High-Performance Parallel Computing Model for Linear Fresnel Reflectors
abstract: Conventional ray tracing for linear Fresnel reflectors (LFRs) is computationally expensive, limiting annual optical evaluation and multi-parameter optimization. This study develops a parallel optical model using a multi-process architecture. Unlike previous LFR studies that mainly focus on geometric and structural optimization, this study develops a high-performance multi-process parallel optical model for LFRs, enabling efficient large-scale annual optical evaluation and multi-parameter optimization. Large-scale incident rays are divided into independent task blocks and processed in parallel by multiple workers. Validation against SolTrace at transverse incidence angles of 45° and 90° gives normalized root mean square errors of 0.08 and coefficients of determination of 0.98 and 0.99, respectively, indicating acceptable agreement for engineering optical analysis. Compared with literature data, the mean absolute percentage error ranges from 0 to 0.74%, confirming the model’s high accuracy. At 5.0 × 107 traced rays, the standard deviation of repeated calculations decreases to 0.0019%, demonstrating high computational stability. For 2.5×108 rays, the model achieves a speedup of 21.5× over SolTrace and 357.7× over a serial program. For 108 rays, computation time is reduced by 14.7× compared with a reported method. The model is applied to daily and annual optical performance analyses at different latitudes. Results indicate that the proposed model substantially reduces computational expense, and daily average optical efficiency is closely related to latitude, solar elevation angle, and direct normal irradiance.

title: Numerical evaluation of a complex fenestration system with solar optics and photovoltaic cells for building energy efficiency and daylight autonomy
abstract: Dielectric crossed compound parabolic concentrator-photovoltaic (CCPC-PV) windows represent an attractive building-integrated photovoltaic (BIPV) fenestration solution, capable of harvesting solar energy for electricity generation while admitting daylight into occupied spaces. Nevertheless, conventional whole-building simulation tools cannot natively reproduce the complex optical, thermal, and electrical behaviours of CCPC-PV windows, and holistic building-scale evaluations considering diverse window design scenarios and climatic conditions remain insufficient. This study presents a coupled multi-physics simulation workflow based on the Equivalent Layer Fenestration Model (ELFM). It converts ray-tracing and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) outputs of complex CCPC-PV window geometry into equivalent-layer thermal/optical datasets compatible with EnergyPlus. Parametric simulations are conducted across different concentrator spacing layouts, window-to-wall ratios (WWRs), and climatic conditions. The simulation results reveal that densely arranged CCPC-PV configurations deliver the best overall system performance. At WWR = 64%, the optimal layout achieves net energy savings of 56.86% in London, 67.63% in Barcelona, and 33.93% in Stockholm. Under all simulated conditions, CCPC-PV windows achieve higher useful daylight illuminance (UDI 500-2000 ) than conventional double-glazed windows and mitigate visual discomfort due to over-illumination. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of the coupled simulation framework for evaluating complex BIPV fenestration systems, and quantifies the energy and daylight benefits of CCPC-PV windows across different design and climate contexts.

title: Advanced exergy analysis of an innovative solar-driven system for sustainable hydrothermal liquefaction: Experimental validation and topology optimization
abstract: Integrating renewable energy sources into thermochemical processes offers a viable pathway to reducing environmental impacts associated with conventional heat-intensive systems. Hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) represents a promising technology for biomass conversion, but large-scale implementation faces constraints from the substantial enthalpy required to achieve subcritical conditions and the need for specialized reactor designs that maintain uniform thermal environments. To address these challenges, a novel solar-driven HTL configuration is introduced in this study, heating a batch reactor with a photovoltaic-powered thermal collar. The system is experimentally and analytically evaluated using conventional energy and exergy analyses, advanced exergy methodologies, and a topology optimization framework to improve reactor–collar thermal integration. The experimental results demonstrate the capability of the solar-powered configuration to reliably attain the temperature and pressure conditions required for HTL, with a maximum exergy efficiency of 36%. Moreover, advanced exergy analysis reveals that nearly all irreversibilities within the photovoltaic field originate from endogenous sources, while the converter, charge regulator, and battery exhibit significant exogenous and avoidable components. As a result, system-level interactions, rather than intrinsic photovoltaic limitations, dominate overall performance losses. In addition, topology optimization of the heating collar improves the configuration, reducing exergy destruction and increasing the HTL system efficiency from 36% to 42%.

title: Feasibility of variable flow regulation in distributed air source heat pump heating systems
abstract: To verify the feasibility and advantages of variable flow regulation in distributed air source heat pump space heating systems, this study proposed a regulation method called “optimal thermal condition regulation” for dual-pipe radiant floor heating systems. A field experiment was conducted in a distributed air source heat pump space heating system in Hebei Province, China. Compared with no-regulation and quality regulation, the proposed method increased the time-averaged coefficient of performance to 2.83, corresponding to improvements of 14.95% and 4.88%, while reducing total system energy consumption by 15.58% and 9.88%, respectively. For the monitored representative end users, the indoor temperature distribution became more concentrated, with 74.55% of the data within 20.0 – 21.0 °C, compared with 63.93% under quality regulation, indicating an increase of 10.62 percentage points. The maximum deviations of supply and return water temperatures from the calculated values were reduced to 0.72 and 0.41 °C, respectively, compared with 2.38 and 1.35 °C under quality regulation. In addition, partial intermittent control and branch isolation control were proposed to address insufficient unit flow under low system flow conditions. The results demonstrated that the proposed method improved system thermal balance and exhibited significant energy-saving potential.
keywords: Distributed air source heat pump space heating system

title: Incentive effects of small-scale flow separation structures on low-speed hydrokinetic energy harvesting of cylinder-array oscillators
abstract: Vortex-induced vibration (VIV) energy conversion systems are promising for low-speed flows, but the synergistic gains from coupling surface geometry with cylinder array configuration remain poorly understood. This paper studies a rigidly coupled three-cylinder VIV system with small-scale square/arc-shaped grooves and bumps, examining how geometric form and attachment angle affect vibration response, wake evolution, and energy harvesting. Bumps at 30° and 60° shift boundary layer separation forward from 80° to 90°, intensifying wake vorticity and generating high-energy “2P"/"2T” patterns that broaden the galloping lock-in range. The square bump at 30° performs best, raising average energy harvesting by 22.76% and extending the high-efficiency range to Ur = 6–13, while the arc-shaped bump at 120° suppresses vibration amplitude by 69.33%. These findings support the design of VIV-based energy harvesters and vibration control of marine structures.

title: Performance and tribological reliability of low-sulfur fuel oil/biofuel oil blends in a low-speed marine diesel engine
abstract: To support the compatible use of renewable marine fuels in in-service main propulsion systems, this study used low-sulfur fuel oil (LSFO) as the baseline fuel and compared four LSFO/biofuel oil blends (B15, B24, B30 and B50) in a two-stroke low-speed marine diesel engine. Emissions, fuel economy, exhaust temperature, vibration response and tribological reliability were evaluated. Compared with LSFO, the load-averaged HC emissions of B15-B50 decreased by 6.7-75.0%, whereas NOx, exhaust CO2 and BSFC increased by 3.6-7.5%, 0.9-2.1% and 0.8-3.7%, respectively. B24 and B30 reduced the load-averaged cylinder-head RMS response by 15.3% and 13.5%, respectively. B50 showed pronounced 4.1 kHz responses at both 50% and 75% load, but whether these responses represent a risk signal requires equal-duration validation. Under the specified equal-weight screening, B24 ranked first and was selected for long-term validation, while B30 remained an HC-oriented alternative because its greater HC reduction involved higher NOx, CO2 and BSFC penalties.

title: Investigation on the energy-saving and thermal performance of telecommunication base station with radiative sky cooling and phase change materials
abstract: Radiative cooling and phase change technology on building envelope have significant potential for reducing energy consumption. However, their thermal management performance for the 5G telecommunication case station (TBS) in China characterized by high IT heat dissipation and year-round cooling requirements remains unclear. To address this gap, this study numerically investigated the energy-saving and thermal performance of a novel TBS envelope combining radiative sky cooling and phase change materials (PCM + RSC) with natural ventilation. Traditional, RSC, PCM and PCM + RSC TBS models were established using EnergyPlus and experimentally validated. The key parameters such as location and spectral reflectivity of RSC were optimized. A comparative analysis of energy-saving and thermal performance was conducted among the different TBS models. The optimal location and spectral reflectivity for minimizing cooling consumption were south-facing and 0.96. The results indicate the combination of PCM and RSC to enhance heat dissipation, and the improvement was most significant in winter, mild in transitional seasons and minimal in summer. The ventilated PCM + RSC TBS achieves energy-saving rate up to 31.48%, compared to the traditional TBS. Furthermore, the energy-saving potential of PCM + RSC TBS was explored in five Chinese cities with different climatic conditions, indicating that ambient temperature exerts a greater influence than solar radiation.

title: Spillover effects and transmission channels of carbon price volatility
abstract: abstract Studies have shown that carbon markets influence financial markets, commodity prices, and overall uncertainty. However, the impacts of carbon price volatility on these areas remain underexplored. This study addresses this gap by analyzing the relationships between carbon price volatility, renewable energy assets, financial volatility, uncertainty, financial markets, and oil markets using weekly data, Vector Autoregressive and Global Vector Autoregressive models, and Granger causality tests. The shock identification assumes that carbon price volatility spreads through financial markets and uncertainty, eventually affecting oil markets. The results indicate that a carbon price volatility shock is potentially linked to increased financial volatility and uncertainty, while corresponding to declines in stock market performance for two to four weeks. After this period, the shock's effect dissipates. The variance decomposition reveals that carbon price volatility has a greater influence on volatility and uncertainty than on spot prices: carbon price volatility does not directly impact oil prices; instead, it affects only oil price volatility. The estimates also show that the potential primary drivers of carbon price volatility are renewable energy assets and financial volatility. These findings highlight (i) the spillover effects of carbon price volatility on financial markets, uncertainty, and oil markets, (ii) the potential transmission channels of carbon price volatility, and (iii) the connectedness of carbon price volatility with volatility indices, where higher carbon price volatility is associated with greater volatility in financial and oil markets.

title: Beyond daily average irradiance: Instantaneous homogeneous light distribution unlocks higher productivity in fixed-tilt agrivoltaics
abstract: Agrivoltaic systems integrate photovoltaic electricity generation with agriculture, enabling dual land use. However, conventional fixed-tilt systems can reduce crop productivity because opaque photovoltaic modules create non-uniform irradiance beneath the array. To address this, this study presents an even solar sharing agrivoltaic system using linear-diverging Fresnel optics to redistribute transmitted sunlight into shaded regions, producing a more homogeneous instantaneous light distribution than a conventional checkerboard layout. A 1.1 kWp rooftop pilot agrivoltaic plant was developed by replacing 50% of the photovoltaic modules with diverging optics and compared with a checkerboard agrivoltaic system having the same photovoltaic coverage and with open-field cultivation. The three-day average photosynthetic photon flux density was 831, 246 and 231 μmol m−2 s−1 for the open field, checkerboard and even solar sharing systems, respectively. Hydroponically cultivated spearmint (Mentha spicata) showed a 13% higher yield under the even solar sharing agrivoltaic system than under the checkerboard agrivoltaic system, despite comparable daily average photon flux density, highlighting the importance of instantaneous light uniformity. The land equivalent ratio reached 1.81 relative to full rooftop photovoltaic coverage and 2.04 relative to ground-mounted photovoltaics for even solar sharing agrivoltaics. These findings establish that instantaneous light uniformity should be considered alongside daily average irradiance as a key design criterion for fixed-tilt agrivoltaics and demonstrate that linear-diverging Fresnel optics improve crop productivity and land-use efficiency.

title: Comparative assessment of three all-sky photometry systems for the local characterization of daylight climates
abstract: Characterizing the angular distribution of sky luminance is crucial for solar applications; however, traditional sky-scanner technology presents important limitations that motivate the use of alternative instrumentation. This study evaluates the sensitivity of sky-type classification to alternative instrumentation (a high dynamic range imaging system and a photodiode array) and how consistent they are compared to sky-scanners regarding the measurement of local solar radiation patterns. A methodology was developed to determine sky type from the measurements of alternative instruments, and the instrument potential to obtain results comparable to that of sky-scanners was assessed under various sky conditions. For sky characterization, the Tregenza method was applied to all three instruments; however, given the significant differences among the luminance detectors, differing data processing pipelines were employed. Results indicate that the assessed instruments are suitable for sky classification, but the imaging system exhibited the most balanced statistics. Particularly, under clear-sky conditions the other instruments showed greater uncertainty, which is interpreted as higher deviation from theoretical sky classes. The assessment suggests that full-sky imaging presents lower RMS values and more classification stability under the evaluated experimental conditions, which encompass a single location and a temporal period limited to three months during spring-summer season.

title: Machine learning approaches in solar forecasting across different climate types: A unified evaluation framework
abstract: With the continuous development of solar energy technology, solar forecasting has become increasingly important. Accurate short-term solar forecasting could help maintain grid stability and provide reliable power. It is also critical for scheduling in intra-day electricity markets and grid operations. Compared to Deep Learning models, Machine Learning models offer the advantages of faster computation and better adaptability to small datasets. However, there is a lack of a unified evaluation framework to evaluate Machine Learning models due to the diversity of datasets, time step, forecasting horizon, set up and evaluation metrics. This work addresses this gap by evaluating six validated Machine Learning methods including Linear Regression, Polynomial Regression, Support Vector Regression, Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting and Artificial Neural Network for hourly solar irradiance forecasting across five different geographical regions: Canberra, Shanghai, Miami, Amherst and Kitakyushu. Results reveal that all Machine Learning models outperform the Smart Persistence Model (SPM) at the one-hour horizon; tree-ensemble methods, specifically Random Forest (RF) and XGBoost, achieve the highest overall accuracy and provide predictive performance competitive with DL models at the one-hour-ahead horizon. In stable-sky locations such as Canberra, the RF model achieved a normalized Root Mean Square Error (nRMSE) of 48.97% and a coefficient of determination ( R 2 ) of 0.8859, whereas the nRMSE increased to 61.47% in the highly variable conditions of Kitakyushu. This work helps establish a consistent framework for future studies, facilitating better comparison and improvement of Machine Learning models in solar forecasting.

title: A piezoelectric wind energy harvester with a sealed interference shell based on coupled vortex-induced vibration and galloping
abstract: This study proposes a novel sealed interference shell-based piezoelectric wind energy harvester designed to overcome the persistent challenges of poor output-voltage stability and performance degradation in vortex-induced vibration (VIV)–galloping coupled harvesting systems under complex flow conditions. The proposed design leverages a special sealed interference shell to achieve synergistic vortex-induced vibration–galloping coupling and physical protection, integrating power generation enhancement, environmental isolation, and compact structural integration into a single system. It greatly improves the energy harvesting capabilities and the stability of the harvester. Through integrated theoretical modeling and experimental validation, three distinct vibration response states are identified and characterized: the unsteadiness state, the inter-well state, and the intra-well state, among which the inter-well state proves most effective for power generation. The fabricated prototype achieves a maximum average power of 2.39 mW, an output voltage 25 times that of the unsealed counterpart at 8 m/s, and maintains an average output power above 0.43 mW over a broad wind speed range of 2–10 m/s. By proposing a sealed interference shell-type wind energy harvesting scheme based on VIV-galloping coupling, this work offers a promising pathway for traditional piezoelectric fluid energy harvesters to address the environmental adaptability issues, specifically their susceptibility to failure and significant performance degradation in complex fluid environments.

title: An integrated surrogate-based optimization framework for the preliminary design of laboratory-scale two-body point absorber wave energy converters
abstract: This work presents an early-stage parametric design optimization framework for a laboratory-scale two-body point absorber wave energy converter, tailored to the operational constraints of the University of New Hampshire wave tank. Design of experiments approach over six design variables is employed generating 66 configurations evaluated through boundary element method simulations. The Power-to-Mass ratio is selected as the performance metric, normalizing the mean absorbed power by the total structural mass to provide a cost-effective indicator suitable for laboratory-scale prototype comparison. A quadratic surrogate model is fitted to the defined metric results of the design of experiment configurations, which achieves high predictive fidelity. Analysis of Variance and Pareto analysis identified the floater diameter as the dominant individual variable, and the interaction between spar-plate diameter and the power take-off damping as the most influential coupled effect. Differential evolution algorithm over the surrogate model found 60 candidate configurations that achieve a Power-to-Mass ratio of 9.5, the upper limit defined for the confidence region of the surrogate model, selecting one of them for construction at the university wave tank, expecting a mean absorbed power, normalized by wave amplitude, of 960 [W/m] with 105 [kg] of overall mass. The proposed framework is open-source and transferable to any wave tank facility. Beyond the laboratory-scale application, the methodology can be adapted to alternative performance indices and extended to full-scale wave energy converter design by updating the design-variable bounds and environmental inputs

title: Numerical and experimental investigation of heat transfer in photothermal liquid films for parametric analysis of their applicability in photovoltaic-thermal (PV/T) systems
abstract: Falling-film cooling for photovoltaic (PV) systems is employed in warm climates to boost electrical efficiency. However, few studies have addressed thermal energy recovery from PV panels by recycling liquid films over their surface. In this paper, experiments involving thin liquid film cooling a sun-heated surface were conducted, along with a numerical investigation of heat transfer between the liquid film, the surrounding air, and a PV panel. The liquid film was modeled using the volume-of-fluid (VOF) approach and numerical simulations were performed to parametrically analyze film cooling as a foundation for a simplified photovoltaic-thermal (PV/T) concept. Several PV cooling scenarios were examined. For the investigated open falling-film configuration, water exhibited low thermal performance, below 50%, due to evaporation. In contrast, a heat-transfer fluid with reduced evaporation (40 °C, 1 bar) is an interesting alternative to water. Although limited by other operational characteristics, a simulated organic oil exhibited 71% total efficiency.

title: Tunable spectral beam-splitting performance of CuO–ZnO hybrid nanofluids and its enhanced heat transfer in a photovoltaic/thermal system with internal fins
abstract: Spectral beam-splitting photovoltaic/thermal systems require coordinated light transmission, heat capture and removal to improve solar utilization. This study investigated the coupled effects of nanofluid formulation, flow rate and internal fins on combined thermal-electrical performance. Single-component nanofluids and nanofluids with copper oxide-to-zinc oxide mass ratios of 5:5 and 7:3 were prepared at 0.005 wt% total nanoparticle concentration (with dispersion stability evaluated by zeta-potential measurements and dynamic light scattering) and tested in non-finned and internally finned channels under irradiances of 600 and 1000 W m−2 and flow rates of 0–1.5 mL min−1. The results showed that the 5:5 formulation exhibited the highest average transmittance of 81.46% over 650–1050 nm and favored electrical generation, whereas the 7:3 formulation provided higher thermal efficiency. Internal fins enhanced heat extraction and reduced photovoltaic-cell temperature, while flow-rate regulation influenced thermal and electrical benefits. At 1000 W m−2 and 1 mL min−1, the finned 7:3 system achieved the highest thermal efficiency of 43.1% and an electrical efficiency of 6.04%. Its exergy efficiency reached 7.98%, and its corresponding merit function was 2.77. The weighted energy efficiency index was introduced and applied to assess the trade-off between thermal efficiency and channel pressure drop. Although fins increased pressure drop, the index indicated that, except at 1.5 mL min−1 under 1000 W m−2, the performance gains outweighed the hydraulic penalty under the evaluated flowing conditions.
