These findings highlight the importance of matching nanofluid formulation, internal-fin configuration, and operating flow rate in photovoltaic/thermal systems, providing guidance for engineering applications.

title: Energy cascaded utilization and performance improvement in internal-reforming molten carbonate fuel cells via thermionic-enhanced thermophotovoltaic converters
abstract: Molten carbonate fuel cells (MCFCs) exhibit high electrochemical conversion efficiency but release substantial high-grade waste heat. This study theoretically investigates a cascaded system integrating an MCFC with a thermionic-enhanced thermophotovoltaic (TIPV) converter. In the proposed configuration, the TIPV converter simultaneously exploits thermionic emission and thermophotovoltaic effects, enabling efficient conversion of MCFC waste heat into supplementary electrical power. A steady-state, zero-dimensional model couples MCFC electrochemical polarization, TIPV electron-photon transport, and the system energy balance. An effective active-area ratio is introduced as a key design parameter to ensure thermal matching between two subsystems. Numerical results indicate that the hybrid system achieves a maximum power density of 0.188 Wcm−2 and an energetic efficiency of 34.8% at 923 K when the semiconductor bandgap is 0.36 eV, representing increases of 13.9% and 22.1% compared with a standalone MCFC. Parametric analyses further reveal that optimizing the semiconductor bandgap, reducing the emitter work function, and increasing the MCFC operating temperature can significantly enhance the system performance. Under the common idealized assumptions and geometric constraints used here, the TIPV configuration provides a higher peak power density than the corresponding thermionic-generator and TPV configurations. These findings provide theoretical insights into performance optimization and multi-parameter co-design of MCFC–TIPV hybrid systems and establish a solid foundation for future integrated energy conversion architectures coupling electrochemical power sources with solid-state photoelectric converters.

title: Geographical and Ecological Measurements of China’s Photovoltaic Power Deployment via Spatially Explicit Modeling
abstract: The utilization of photovoltaic power is regarded as a critical strategy for low-carbon energy transition. However, land-intensive photovoltaic deployment may pose a series of challenges and risks, particularly regarding resource allocation and ecological consequence. Combined with multi-source geospatial datasets and spatial statistical methods, this study develops an integrated spatially explicit framework to depict geographic trends, examine evolution determinants and evaluate ecological responses alongside photovoltaic deployment across China. From the results, photovoltaic deployment across China presents an evident northwest-southeast spatial pattern with an annual expansion rate exceeding 70% between 2010 and 2022. Regional photovoltaic distribution shows strong heterogeneity, with resource endowments and proximity to power infrastructure as the dominant drivers. Counterfactual assessment confirmed an evident decline in ecosystem quality during the construction of photovoltaic power stations, whereas the additional recovery associated with power station operation was limited, with most of the three-year post-construction recovery being consistent with the baseline ecological trend represented by matched controls. Despite accounting for over 2% of photovoltaic land use, protected areas can still be regarded as an effective barrier against photovoltaic expansion. By unveiling geographic trends, evolution determinants and ecological responses of China's photovoltaic deployment, some rational and feasible policy implications are proposed including strengthening region-specific governance strategies and implementing ecological conservation assessments before large-scale photovoltaic deployment worldwide.

title: Flexible, superhydrophobic phase-change composites with high photothermal efficiency for humid outdoor solar energy harvesting
abstract: How to improve solar energy utilization efficiency is an urgent priority for decreasing fossil energy usage and alleviating the present energy shortage crisis. As effective carriers for solar energy utilization, photothermal conversion materials are severely restricted in practical applications by key factors such as low photothermal conversion efficiency and limited-service scenarios in outdoor humid environments such as natural rainfall. In this study, a novel flexible PCM with both efficient photothermal conversion performance and superhydrophobicity was successfully fabricated by spraying a superhydrophobic coating onto the surface of the MF/MWCNT/PEG. The prepared superhydrophobic MF/MWCNT/PEG (SH-MF/MWCNT/PEG) exhibited a high water contact angle of 142.3°. The SH-MF/MWCNT/PEG could maintain a stable floating state after being immersed in water for 24 h, while MF/MWCNT/PEG quickly settled within 2s. Quantitative hygroscopic experiments revealed that upon moisture uptake, the melting enthalpy of uncoated MF/MWCNT/PEG decreased significantly from 168.85 to 140.67 J/g, while the SH-MF/MWCNT/PEG maintained its enthalpy at 168.64 J/g even after water immersion. The composite demonstrated an average photothermal conversion efficiency of 88.4%, which surpassed the 62.2% efficiency exhibited by the water-saturated MF/MWCNT/PEG. In the water thermal insulation performance test, the MF/MWCNT/PEG modified with a single-sided superhydrophobic coating showed comparable heat storage performance to the unmodified sample, with the final temperatures of deionized water in the two groups reaching 55.7 °C and 55.1 °C, respectively. In contrast, the maximum temperature of deionized water in the group with double-sided superhydrophobic (DSH) coating modification reached 58.7 °C, which was higher than the above two groups. This study provides a new technical approach and experimental basis for the efficient utilization of solar energy under outdoor humid working conditions.

title: Multistage stochastic bidding of hydrogen-enabled virtual power plants with off-taker commitments
abstract: Hydrogen refuelling stations equipped with on-site renewable generation, electrolysers, hydrogen storage and optional reconversion can operate as hydrogen-enabled virtual power plants, arbitraging across electricity markets while meeting contracted hydrogen demand. This paper proposes a multistage stochastic mixed-integer linear program to co-optimise hydrogen procurement with day-ahead bidding and sequential recourse in reserve, intraday and imbalance markets. The model represents electrolyser and fuel cell on, standby, and off states, warm and cold starts, and degradation, while battery ageing is captured through cycle-dependent costs. A case study with real-world data compares four portfolios built around a photovoltaic-driven station: fuel cell with reserve, no reserve, battery replacing the fuel cell, and optional hydrogen sales. Results show that reserve remuneration is the main profitability driver and materially reshapes operating states. The fuel cell rarely generates electricity and is used mainly to support reserve provision, whereas the electrolyser concentrates production to limit starts and degradation. Replacing the fuel cell with a battery provides the strongest profit uplift, while hydrogen sales deliver a smaller, episodic benefit.

title: Process-based Monte Carlo cost simulation for offshore wind farm decommissioning: A scenario analysis for the German North Sea
abstract: : We estimate the probability distribution of the net costs of decommissioning a first-generation offshore wind farm in the German North Sea. The process-based Monte Carlo model covers a 288 MW reference wind farm with 80 monopile-founded 3.6 MW turbines and ten scenarios. The model is based on expert judgments and market data from a multi-year research project with industry partners. It models dependence among cost rates and among process durations and quantities. It links offshore removal to onshore processing costs and material revenues. Expected net costs, defined as gross expenditures less material revenues, range from €242,000 to €545,000 per MW in 2022 prices. Correlation among inputs raises the upper tail far more than the mean. The 95th percentile of the baseline lies 34% above the mean, versus 23% for independent inputs. The decommissioning concepts filed with the German regulator include risk surcharges of up to 30%. Such a surcharge covers the 95th percentile only for independent inputs. Material revenues fall short of onshore costs in 15% of the baseline simulations. Leaving the scour protection in situ lowers expected costs by 18%, and cutting the foundation above the seabed lowers them by a further 9 percentage points. Feeder logistics raise costs by 48% for foundations and by 65% for foundations and turbines, conditional on the fleet, the 2022 vessel market, and the implicit treatment of weather. For the 3.6 MW reference case, the scenario ranking is the same under all stochastic specifications tested. The results provide a benchmark for financial provisioning.

title: Performance investigation of a novel valve-integrated ejector-enhanced CO2 cycle for heating and cooling
abstract: The application of electric vehicles is considered an effective measure to promote the consumption of renewable energy and reduce pollutant emissions. The air conditioning system is an important component of the energy consumption of electric vehicles, and CO2 is one of its environmentally friendly alternative refrigerants. However, existing research on CO2 air conditioning for electric buses mainly focuses on the basic vapor compression cycle, and further exploration is needed to improve the cycle efficiency by integrating ejectors. Furthermore, the inherent unidirectional flow characteristic of the ejector poses a challenge for mode switching between heating and cooling. This study proposes a novel valve-integrated ejector-enhanced CO2 cycle. By introducing an eight-port valve that coordinates with a four-way valve, the proposed cycle enables the efficient utilization of the ejector and the complete sharing of cycle components in both modes, thereby achieving significant efficiency improvements without compromising compactness. Thermodynamic comparisons demonstrate that the proposed cycle achieves coefficient of performance improvements of 20.1% to 33.6% over the basic cycle under cooling conditions (28 °C–45 °C), and 9.4% to 11.5% under heating conditions (−30 °C–11 °C). Annual simulations for ten representative cities indicate that the annual performance factor of the proposed cycle is improved by 10.9%–27.9% over that of the basic cycle, with life cycle carbon emissions lowered by up to 21.7% in hot climates. Economic analysis shows payback periods of 1.2–10.1 years for all investigated cities except Sydney.

title: Experimental investigation of a multi-buoy cooperative point-absorber wave energy
abstract: This study presents a proof-of-concept experimental investigation of a multi-buoy cooperative point-absorber wave energy converter (WEC). The proposed concept consists of an array of surface-penetrating buoys connected through a shared closed-loop hydraulic power take-off (PTO) system. Energy is extracted through the collective motion of the buoy array, where pressurised flow generated by individual buoys drives a turbine within the hydraulic circuit. A 1:40 scale model was tested in the wave tank facilities at the University of Oslo. Experiments with regular and irregular long-crested waves at two different incident angles were conducted to assess power absorption, wave period response, and interaction effects. Two array configurations were investigated: an eight-buoy array with an axis-to-axis spacing of 1.5 buoy diameters, and a four-buoy array with a 3.0 diameter spacing. Although piston head leakage affected the power measurements, our results demonstrate that the WEC absorbs incoming wave energy and produces measurable power. The eight-buoy configuration achieved the highest power output per buoy compared to the four-buoy configuration, but exhibited increased sensitivity to wave period and wave heading, due to buoy-buoy interactions, such as collisions. This study highlights buoy count and internal buoy spacing as key design parameters for cooperative point-absorber wave energy systems. The results indicate that higher buoy counts enhance hydraulic cooperation, and increased buoy spacing improves robustness to wave heading and reduces destructive interaction effects. We also suggest that a lower system inertia can improve responsiveness to shorter waves. These insights provide a foundation for further optimisation and future full-scale development.

title: Development of low-cost AC–MnO2–Fe3O4/PVDF and binder-free AC–Fe3O4 electrodes for high-power microbial fuel cells
abstract: To further improve the electric power generation performance of the microbial fuel cell (MFC), activated carbon (AC) and two metal oxides (MnO2 and Fe3O4) were doped as catalysts to the air cathode and a polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) membrane was attached (referred to as AC-MnO2-Fe3O4/PVDF air cathode). The AC-MnO2-Fe3O4/PVDF air cathode significantly improved electrical performance, water resistance, and stability. An anode electrode was also modified, in which AC and Fe3O4 were attached to a carbon brush by ultrasonic treatment without using a binder (referred to as binder-free AC-Fe3O4 carbon brush anode). The MFC equipped with the newly fabricated air cathodes and anodes achieved a maximum power density of 4.1 W m−3, 4.1 times higher performance than the MFC with AC air cathodes and normal carbon brush anodes. Furthermore, the modified MFC was integrated with a low-voltage booster (LVB). The integrated MFC-LVB system successfully harvested sufficient power from 133 mL and 13.3 mL of municipal wastewater (average COD = 377 ± 66 mg L−1) to operate an LED headlight for over 12 min and a temperature/humidity sensor for more than 6 h continuously, respectively. This simple and cost-effective electrode modification strategy enables markedly enhanced power output, demonstrating the practical applicability.

title: Effects of splitter blades on S-characteristics and low-frequency pressure fluctuations in a low-head pump-turbine
abstract: When pump-turbines enter the S-characteristics region, unstable flow phenomena, including flow separation, backflow, and rotating stall, intensify and induce pronounced low-frequency pressure fluctuations, thereby compromising operational stability. To investigate the effects of splitter blades on the S-characteristics and low-frequency pressure fluctuations, nine splitter-blade runner configurations were developed using an orthogonal experimental design. The unit-discharge–unit-speed characteristic curves were reconstructed using piecewise cubic Hermite interpolation, and Pareto analysis was applied to assess the trade-off between the S-characteristics and bidirectional efficiency. Frequency-domain and circumferential modal analyses were then performed to compare the pressure fluctuations of the original model, Model 6, and Model 9 under knee and braking operating conditions. Across the tested factor levels, the mean unit-speed span of the S-characteristics region varied most with the wrap-angle ratio, whereas mean bidirectional efficiency varied most with blade number. Model 6 achieves a favorable compromise between S-characteristics and efficiency, whereas Model 9 exhibits the most pronounced S-characteristics. At the knee operating condition, both splitter-blade configurations reduce the energy of low-frequency pressure fluctuations, but affect their circumferential organization differently. Model 6 primarily attenuates the fluctuation amplitude while retaining a coherent low-order circumferential structure, whereas Model 9 weakens the coherent circumferential propagation of pressure fluctuations by redistributing modal energy. Under braking, the Original model and Model 6 exhibit dominant peaks and retain coherent low-frequency circumferential structures, whereas Model 9 retains a subsynchronous component without stable phase progression. These findings provide guidance for the parameter optimization and stability-oriented design of splitter-blade runners for low-head pump-turbines.

title: Mapping Colombia's green hydrogen potential: A nationwide geospatial suitability and cost screening assessment
abstract: This study develops a comprehensive geospatial framework to identify and evaluate suitable locations for green hydrogen production in Colombia, integrating renewable energy potential, infrastructure readiness, and environmental constraints. The framework combines high-resolution Geographic Information System (GIS) modeling with a screening-level cost assessment of Levelized Costs of Electricity (LCOE) and Hydrogen (LCOH), applied to solar PV, onshore wind, and offshore wind technologies. Results reveal that approximately 5.1% of Colombia’s land area is eligible for solar PV, 1% for onshore wind, and 2.1% of its maritime Exclusive Economic Zone for offshore wind once environmental, technical, and legal restrictions are applied. Among the assessed regions, La Guajira emerges as the most promising hub, achieving LCOE values as low as 41 $/MWh for onshore wind and corresponding LCOH values of 6–8 $/kg. The study applies an oversizing factor methodology for renewable–electrolyzer systems, adapted from and consistent with previous studies, improving accuracy compared with conventional 1:1 capacity assumptions. Sensitivity analysis shows that renewable-resource utilization and electrolyzer specific electricity consumption are major technical drivers of LCOH, while the dominant economic drivers vary across renewable pathways. Institutional barriers, such as land-use restrictions under ANH concessions and grid infrastructure gaps, remain key bottlenecks. The findings inform policy design, investment prioritization, and spatial planning for Colombia’s Green Hydrogen Roadmap and provide a replicable framework for other emerging economies pursuing renewable-based hydrogen strategies.

title: Retraction notice to “Integration of renewable energy, environmental policy stringency, and climate technologies in realizing environmental sustainability: Evidence from OECD countries” [RENE 196, (2022), 1376--1384]
Optimizing heat flux density for solar tower power plants: A novel HFLCAL linearization approach
abstract: Slow structural drift misaligns heliostats, and the tracking loop cannot remove it. In a surround field, the displaced aim-points of heliostats on opposite sides can converge onto one meridian of a cylindrical receiver, creating hot spots above its allowable flux density (AFD). Linearizing the Heliostat Field Layout CALculation (HFLCAL) flux model about the misaligned field makes aim-point correction a convex quadratic program with a hard per-pixel AFD limit, solved offline to global optimality for the linearized problem. In a 2650-heliostat Gemasolar-class model, worst-case convergence on the North meridian raises the peak flux 14.8% above the AFD at spring-equinox noon. Computed in 88 s, the correction lowers the peak to 23% below the AFD and cuts the uncorrected field’s non-uniformity (coefficient of variation) by 55%. Maximum uniformity costs 6.3 percentage points of interception efficiency versus the aligned plant, whereas restoring only the plant’s 5% margin below the AFD costs 1.6 points, so the trade-off is tunable. At equal computational time, grouped ant-colony and genetic-algorithm baselines barely bring the peak below the AFD and leave almost twice the correction’s non-uniformity. Neither finer grouping nor tenfold computational time closes this gap. The correction remains effective across seasons, times of day, and a clear-sky year, and the flux model agrees with a ray-tracing round-robin to within about 15% for typical geometries. The analysis specifies the tracking loop’s required pointing accuracy.

title: Retraction notice to “The influence of grid connectivity, electricity pricing, policy-driven power incentives, and carbon emissions on renewable energy adoption: Exploring key factors” [RENE 232, (2024), 121108]
Hydroelastic performance and energy conversion of a flexible annular tubular WEC equipped with PTO arrays
abstract: Wave energy harvesting in multifunctional floating systems can support offshore renewable energy supply while improving marine-space utilization. This study evaluates the energy capture performance of a flexible annular tubular wave energy converter equipped with distributed bottom-mounted power take-off units. A two-way coupled numerical model is used to predict wave-induced structural response and mechanical energy absorption by the power take-off system. The capture factor is adopted to quantify the overall energy performance. The effects of power take-off number and arrangement, sea-side/lee-side damping distribution, structural flexibility, and tube cross-sectional geometry are systematically examined. Among the tested configurations, 40 power take-off units provide the most favorable balance between structural motion and energy extraction. A uniform arrangement increases the highest tested capture factor by approximately 84–128% compared with concentrated layouts, while balanced sea-side/lee-side damping maintains higher energy capture under long-period waves. Structural flexibility increases the highest tested capture factor to approximately 2.5 times that of the rigid configuration and broadens the high-capture range. Increasing the tube diameter by approximately 67% further enhances energy capture over intermediate wave periods. The largest-diameter configuration reaches its highest tested capture factor of 0.238, approximately 3.9 times that of the smallest configuration. These results show that energy capture is governed by the coordinated effects of structural deformation, power take-off distribution, and tube geometry. The open annular configuration also provides potential for integration with aquaculture cages and other multifunctional marine facilities.

title: Enhancing Photovoltaic Power Generation through the Cooling/Purification Effects of Green Roofs: Impacts of Meteorological Conditions and Vegetation Design on Renewable Energy Utilization Efficiency
abstract: Mitigating both thermal stress and particulate soiling is essential for improving the power generation efficiency and long-term operational stability of photovoltaic systems. Rooftop vegetation offers a passive and renewable-energy-compatible solution by regulating the local microclimate and reducing airborne particle deposition. However, the combined effects of vegetation-induced cooling and particulate matter removal on photovoltaic performance remain insufficiently investigated. To address this research gap, this study develops and validates a multi-physics model for rooftop photovoltaic-vegetation systems by coupling airflow, heat-moisture transfer, vegetation canopy energy balance, PM10 transport and deposition, and photovoltaic thermoelectric conversion models. The results show that, compared with the non-vegetated case, the optimized shrub-lawn vegetation configuration increases the midday power output of a single photovoltaic module from 182 W to 193 W. Increasing the leaf area density of shrubs and lawns from 2.0/1.0 to 4.0/2.0 further improves the optical absorptance from 0.624 to 0.640 and raises the power output from 191.6 W to 196.6 W. The long-term pollution exposure prediction indicates that, after 90 days, the composite vegetation reduces dust accumulation by approximately 14% and increases the daily total energy output of the photovoltaic array from 109 kWh to 119 kWh. These findings demonstrate that rooftop vegetation can serve as an effective passive strategy for soiling mitigation, module cooling, and renewable energy performance optimization in polluted urban and industrial environments.

title: Numerical Study on Dynamic Wake Characteristics of Floating Offshore Wind Turbines Under Six Degree of Freedom Motions using the SPDMD Method
abstract: Wake effects strongly influence fatigue loading and power output in floating offshore wind turbines, while platform motion introduces additional unsteady wake scales. This study used large-eddy simulation coupled with an actuator line model under neutral atmospheric boundary layer inflow to examine a floating turbine subjected separately to surge, sway, heave, roll, pitch, and yaw. Two thousand wake snapshots sampled at 0.1 s were analyzed with Dynamic Mode Decomposition and its sparsity-promoting variant. The prescribed motion frequencies were 0.062, 0.080, and 0.102 Hz, and the mean wind speed at hub height was 11.4 m/s. Firstly, Dynamic Mode Decomposition and sparsity promoting Dynamic Mode Decomposition were comparatively evaluated for dominant mode extraction and reduced order reconstruction. Reconstruction loss generally decreased with shallow plateaus, with surge showing a change of only 0.21 percentage points between the compact and expanded settings. Subsequently, sparsity promoting Dynamic Mode Decomposition modes at the prescribed platform motion frequency were found to indicate that imposed six-degree-of-freedom motions mainly modify near wake dynamics, with the most differences generally confined to the near wake (x ≲ 4D). Moreover, dynamic wake characteristics are strongly dependent on motion type. Finally, at equal retained mode counts, the sparsity-promoting models generally produced lower reconstruction errors because they selected a more effective subset of dynamic modes. The results provide quantitative guidance for reduced-order modelling and load-oriented analysis of floating wind turbines.

title: A multimodal method for ultra-short-term photovoltaic power forecasting with irradiance information constraints
abstract: Accurate ultra-short-term photovoltaic power forecasting is essential for grid dispatch, reserve allocation, and renewable energy integration. However, conventional data-driven models rely on statistical relationships in historical data and thus struggle to characterize plane-of-array irradiance fluctuations induced by cloud formation and dissipation. These fluctuations drive non-stationary variations in photovoltaic power output, thereby limiting forecasting accuracy. To address this issue, this paper proposes an ultra-short-term photovoltaic power forecasting method with irradiance information constraints. The proposed method constructs a dual-channel forecasting framework that integrates sky images and historical power information, and introduces a cross-modal attention mechanism to strengthen the interaction between visual features and temporal features, thereby improving the characterization of photovoltaic power fluctuations caused by cloud evolution. Two physically interpretable irradiance-related quantities are further introduced into the learning process of visual features at different layers, enabling the model to better distinguish the overall irradiance background from local rapid disturbances. Additionally, a gradient coordination strategy is used to coordinate the main forecasting task and irradiance information constraints, thereby enhancing forecasting accuracy and model stability. The results of five independent runs on the primary test set show that DIPF reduces the MAE by approximately 23.20% while maintaining an MSE comparable to that of the best-performing baseline model and the same FS, and exhibits smaller performance variations under different random initializations. Independent training and testing on another dataset further indicate that DIPF has a certain degree of cross-site applicability under site-specific training.

title: Numerical study on the thermal characteristics of large-area perovskite solar cells
abstract: Perovskite solar cells offer the advantages of high efficiency and low cost, while commercial cells with large area commonly suffer from significant impact of thermal effects compared with small ones in labs. In this study, thermal characteristics of typical perovskite solar cells with different structures were analyzed as well as the effect of environmental conditions. A thermal simulation model was developed, and an experiment was conducted to validate the reliability of the model. The results showed that the maximum thermal stress reached 63.1 MPa and the maximum thermal deformation was 9.904 × 10−8 m at an operating temperature of 46.2 °C. As ambient temperature increased from 20 °C to 80 °C, the maximum thermal stress and deformation of the perovskite layer increased by 289% and 303%, respectively. As irradiance increased from 200 W/m2 to 1200 W/m2, the maximum thermal stress and thermal deformation increased by 181% and 177%, respectively. As cell area increased from 0.04 cm2 to 9 cm2, the maximum thermal stress increased by 42.9%, and the maximum thermal deformation increased by approximately 15 times. A thermal stress prediction model was further established for perovskite solar cells with single-layer SnO2 and bilayer C60/SnO2 electron transport layers. An assessment method based on driving strain energy was proposed to evaluate the fracture risk of large-area cells. This study is expected to improve commercial large-area perovskite solar cells.

title: Thermal analysis of a ground-mounted photovoltaic system coupled with the crop of a metal-hyperaccumulating plant using multiple modelling approaches
abstract: Understanding the operating temperature of photovoltaic (PV) modules is crucial for assessing their electrical performance, yet most agrivoltaic models focus on crop yield rather than PV thermal behaviour. This study addresses this gap by proposing a one-dimensional dynamic thermal model based on a nodal approach to simulate the PV modules’ temperatures. The model was validated using PV back-surface temperatures measured during a two-year experiment and integrate soil and vegetation surface temperatures and meteorological parameters. This model (Model 3) was evaluated against two simplified thermal models: the Ross thermal model (Model 1) and the Normal Operating Cell Temperature model (Model 2). Model 3 showed the greatest precision with a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) down to 1.6°C and a Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency coefficient (NSE) > 92 %, outperforming Models 1 and 2 by 20 % in NSE and 50-80 % in RMSE reduction. Model 1 performed better under cloudy conditions (RMSE 3.6-4.5°C; NSE 72-80 %), while Model 2 slightly improved sunny-day predictions (NSE up to 82 %). Model 3 consistently provided the best results (NSE > 92 %). Comparing simulated and measured electrical energy production of an opaque module, Models 1 and 2 overestimated output (+2 % to +3 %, more under sunny conditions), while Model 3 exhibited the closest agreement (deviation < 1 %). Parametric simulations with Model 3 also highlighted the potential of brownfield sites in southern France for ecovoltaic deployment. This work provides a robust thermal modelling framework for ecovoltaic systems, improving performance predictions and supporting sustainable energy integration.
